units.la: CAPVT IV. De Trinitate Personarum in Divina Essentia.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV. On the Trinity of Persons in the Divine Essence.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: QUotquot hodie dispersi vivunt Judæi, negant omnes ore præfracto divinæ Essentiæ Trinitatem, quam ɯɥ nominant, à Majoribus discedentes, summæ veritatis Doctoribus, tum ante Messiam ex Prophetarum vaticiniis, tum post Messiæ adventum ex antiqua residua Catechesi, cognitionisque Clavi, observantibus bene multis, maxime Raymundo in Pugione Fidei per Voysinium edito, & Galatino læpe cum Hebræorum scriptis conferendo, quod aliquando cespitet, in Arcanis veritatis Religionis Catholicæ; Detestanturque Posteri præposteri Prisonarum voces, accusantque Christianos, quod legem pervertant sacrosanctam, quod יהוה Essentiæ Unitatem destruant, tollantque, quod tres habeant, quos venerentur. tur Deos; Hinc quotidie ex articulo fidei secundo clamant, boantque Deum unum, unicum, solum, cui nihil sit simile; Et שמע ישראל יהוה אלהינו יהוה אחד Audi Israel, Iehova, Deus noster, Iehova unus est, Deut. cap. 6. verl. 4. Et ואלמי תומיני ואשוה cui assimilabitis me, aut aequalis essem, Jef. cap. 40. verl. 25. Sed sicut unam constituunt Essentiam divinam, ita unam, solamque venerantur & colunt Personam, quam unam, solamque appellant Jehova, Deum, Deum Deorum, Creatorem coeli & terrae, Deum Israelis, Deum Magnum, Potentem, facientem mirabilia, &c.
units.tr: All the Jews who live dispersed today deny, with stubborn mouths, the Trinity of the divine Essence, which they call [שלוש, shalosh]. In doing so they depart from their forefathers, who were teachers of the highest truth, both before the Messiah from the prophetic oracles and after his coming from the ancient surviving catechesis and the key of knowledge. Many have observed this, above all Raymundus in the Pugio Fidei edited by Voisin, and Galatinus, who often compared the Hebrew writings with the secrets of the truth of the Catholic Religion, and sometimes stumbled. The later generations detest the perverse voices of the Prophets and accuse the Christians of perverting the most sacred law, of destroying and removing the unity of the essence of Jehovah [יהוה], because they have three gods whom they worship. Hence every day, from the second article of faith, they cry out and proclaim one God, the only one, the sole one, to whom nothing is like: "Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God, Jehovah is one" [שמע ישראל יהוה אלהינו יהוה אחד], Deut. ch. 6, v. 4; and "To whom will you liken me, or who would be my equal?" [ואל מי תדמיוני ואשוה], Isa. ch. 40, v. 25. But just as they affirm one divine Essence, so they worship and honour one Person only, whom they alone call Jehovah, God, God of gods, Creator of heaven and earth, God of Israel, the great, mighty God who does wonders, and so on.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Rident, calumniantur que constantem omnium seculorum doctrinam de Sacro Sancta Trinitate, oblatrantque multa de Trinitatis in Unitate impossibilitate, quod fit ex ייחוד, rebus quae fieri nunquam possunt, sic Judaeus Anonymus apud Coccejum in Considerationibus Quaestionum Judaicarum, cap. 61. Quifit ut Christiani omnia fidei sua fundamenta superstruant rebus impossibilibus, captum omnem exsuperantibus & rationi adversis, ut sint unus & tres, Deus & homo, virgo & puerpera, panis & caro, vinum & sanguis, unum corpus in multis diversis locis uno eodemque temporis articulo; Non considerantes hanc propositionem veram esse in Essentia finita, creacreataque, salsissimam vero in infinita, increataque; Quod secum ipsa pugnet, ac intellectui contrarietur humano, sicuti loquitur Rabbi Isaac Bar Abraham in Chiluk Emuna, pag. 115, 116. At Deus Benedictus solus vere unus est, nec aliud praeter eum vere unum existit; cumque solus vere unus sit, sieri non potest, ut ex duobus aut tribus componatur, qui enim ex duobus aut tribus componitur, non est vere unus. Tanto igitur magis illorum opinio, qui credunt unum esse tria, & tria esse unum, quoniam secum ipsa pugnat, mendax est, ac humano intellectui adversatur; Quod Trinitas unitatis imperfectionem dicat, quodque sit contra divinam omnipotentiam, nam si una persona est omnipotens, duæ sint supervacuæ, imo quod contra ipsam Dei sit immensurabilitatem, cum una Persona alterius sit mensura, referente Judæo Anonymo in Considerationibus Quastionum Jud. cap. 3. Hæc simplicissima Dei unitas demonstratur quoque manifestis rationibus, quarum etsi multæ sint numero, tres tantum adferemus. 1. Si in divina Essentia diversitas personarum existeret, suppositum aliquod esse oporteret quod eas distingueret, idque necessario in una persona reperiri deberet, in alia non. Iam alterutrum necessarium est, ut suppositum hoc perfectionem in se habeat vel imperfectionem. Si perfectionem, tum personæ quæ illo carent sunt imperfectæ. Si imperfectionem, ea ubi reperitur imperfecta est persona, Verum in Deo nulla potest test esse imperfectio. Ergo nec diversitas personarum. II. Aut qualibet personarum quas in Essentia divina esse asserunt, habet omnipotentiam ex se ipsa, ita ut non indigeat aliarum auxilio, aut non potest omnia absque aliarum auxilio & opera. Si primum statuas, nempe quod qualibet persona sit omnipotens, jam dua alia persona non necessaria sunt & supervacua. Si secundum, quod qualibet persona auxilio aliarum indigeat, inde sequitur nullam istarum ex sese infinitam & omnipotentem esse, cum tamen divina Essentia non possit esse supervacua: Sed re ipsa infinita ac omnipotens esse debeat. Non ergo est in ea diversitas personarum. III. Quicquid actu est infinitum, ei nequit dari mensura qua mensurari possit. Deus est actu infinitus. Nequit ergo ei dari mensura qua mensuretur. At si diversæ essent personæ in Essentia divina, jam una esset mensura aliarum & sic nulla earum esset infinita.
units.tr: They mock and slander the doctrine of the most Holy Trinity, which has been constant in every age, and they loudly object that the Trinity within unity is impossible, because it concerns things that can never happen, which is what the yichud [ייחוד] is about. So the anonymous Jew, quoted by Coccejus in his Considerations of Jewish Questions, ch. 61, says: "It comes about that the Christians build all the foundations of their faith on impossible things, which exceed every grasp and are opposed to reason: that they are one and three, God and man, virgin and mother, bread and flesh, wine and blood, one body in many different places at one and the same moment of time." They do not consider that this proposition is true of a finite and created essence, but most absurd of an infinite and uncreated one; that it contradicts itself and is contrary to the human intellect, as Rabbi Isaac Bar Abraham says in the Chizzuk Emuna, pp. 115, 116: "But God, blessed be he, alone is truly one, and nothing exists besides him that is truly one; and since he alone is truly one, it cannot be that he is composed of two or three, for whatever is composed of two or three is not truly one." Therefore the opinion of those who believe that one is three and three is one is all the more false, since it contradicts itself and is opposed to the human intellect. Further, the Trinity declares the imperfection of the unity, and it is against the divine omnipotence, for if one Person is omnipotent, two are superfluous; indeed it is also against the very immensity of God, since one Person would be the measure of another, as the anonymous Jew reports in the Considerations of Jewish Questions, ch. 3: "This most simple unity of God is also demonstrated by plain reasons, of which, although there are many, we shall bring forward only three. 1. If there were a diversity of persons in the divine Essence, there would have to be some supposit that distinguishes them, and this would necessarily have to be found in one person and not in another. Now one of two things must be the case: either this supposit has perfection in itself or imperfection. If perfection, then the persons who lack it are imperfect. If imperfection, then the person in whom it is found is imperfect. But in God no imperfection can be. Therefore neither can there be a diversity of persons. 2. Either each of the persons who are said to be in the divine Essence has omnipotence from itself, so that it does not need the help of the others, or it cannot do all things without the help and work of the others. If you assert the first, namely that each person is omnipotent, then the other two persons are neither necessary nor useful. If the second, namely that each person needs the help of the others, it follows that none of them is infinite and omnipotent from itself, although the divine Essence cannot be superfluous but must in fact be infinite and omnipotent. Therefore there is no diversity of persons in it. 3. Whatever is actually infinite cannot be given a measure by which it can be measured. God is actually infinite. Therefore no measure can be given to him by which he is measured. But if there were diverse persons in the divine Essence, then one would be the measure of the others, and so none of them would be infinite."

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Quod doctrina hæc ex ipsis novi Instrumenti libris non possit probari, ipseque JEsus Messias noster aperte profiteatur se filium hominis esse, non Numen divinum, uti rursus loquitur Rabbi Isaac pag. 117, 118. Sic quoque multa reperire est apud Scriptores Novi Testamenti, quæ doctrinam de Trinitate destruunt, quorum aliqua adducam. Matth. 12. v. 32. legitur: Si quis locutus quid fuerit adversus filium hominis, id remittetur ei; quisquis autem locutus fuerit adversus Spiritum Sanctum non idei remittetur, neque in hoc seculo, neque in seculo venturo. Hactenus ibi. Idem hoc dictum repetitur apud Marcum cap. 3. v. 28. Et Lucam cap. 12. v. 10. Ecce e verbis istis homines illi manifesto convincuntur, Spiritum Sanctum & filium non esse unum, ut proinde tanto minus tres unum esse queant. Amplius liquet hinc, Iesum filium hominis, nequaquam vero, ceu falso ipsis creditum, Numen esse, nec quisquam sapiens in dubium hoc vocaverit. Insuper scriptum apud Marcum c. 13. v. 32. Diem illum & horam illam non est qui sciat, nec Angeli quidem qui in coelo sunt, neque ipse filius, sed tantum pater. Hactenus ibi. Ecce ex hoc loco quoque evincitur, patrem & filium unum non esse, cum filius cognita non habeat quae novit pater: quin & illud consequitur filium Deum non esse, cum ea quae futura sunt ignoret. Adde, quod in universo Evangelio nullum evidens ejus quam Christiani tenent, Trinitatis, reperitur testimonium. Quin nec ullo in loco deprehendes Iesum se ipsum Deum vocare, sed potius divinitatem, robur ac potentiam Deo Benedicto tribuit, ipse vero se Dei ministrum appellat. Vti in illo Matth. cap. 10. v. 40. Qui recipit vos, me recipit, & qui me recipit, recipit eum qui misit me. Hactenus ibi. Sic quoque de se ipso enunciat se hominem esse, nam apud Iohannem c. 8. v. 40. legitur: Nunc autem studetis vos interimere hominem qui veritatem loquitur vovobiscum. Et Paulus Epistola ad Romanos cap.5.15. de illo ait: Per gratiam hominis IESU Messiae exunda-vit in multos. Pari ratione in aliis locis ipsum filium hominis dicit. Vti Matth.20.v.18. Ecce ascendimus Hierosolymas, & filius hominis tradetur sacerdotibus. Sequitur ibidem v.28. Sicut filius hominis non venit ut sibi ministretur, sed venit ad ministrandum: prout res haec suo loco explicabitur. Tandem perspicue totum hoc negotium quoque intelligitur ex oratione quam Iesus discipulos suos docuit, quamque Pater ipsi vocant, descripta apud Matth.c.6. nec enim praecepit invocare Trinitatem, sed tantum Deum unum, eundemque Deum caeli, cum ex ipsa oratione constat.
units.tr: This doctrine cannot be proved from the books of the New Testament itself, and Jesus our Messiah openly professes that he is the Son of Man, not a divine Power, as Rabbi Isaac again says (pp. 117, 118). Many passages in the writers of the New Testament destroy the doctrine of the Trinity, and I will adduce some of them. Matthew 12:32 reads: "Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the age to come." Thus far there. The same saying is repeated in Mark 3:28 and Luke 12:10. From these words those men are manifestly refuted: the Holy Spirit and the Son are not one, and so much less can three be one. It is further clear from this that Jesus is the Son of Man and by no means God, as falsely believed by them, and no wise person would call this into doubt. Moreover, it is written in Mark 13:32: "Of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels who are in heaven, nor the Son himself, but only the Father." Thus far there. From this passage too it is proved that the Father and the Son are not one, since the Son does not have the knowledge that the Father has; indeed it follows also that the Son is not God, since he does not know the things that are to come. Add that in the whole Gospel no clear testimony is found to that Trinity which Christians hold. Nor will you find in any place that Jesus calls himself God; rather he attributes divinity, strength and power to the blessed God, while he himself calls himself the minister of God, as in that passage of Matthew 10:40: "Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives him who sent me." Thus far there. Likewise he declares of himself that he is a man, for in John 8:40 we read: "But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth." And Paul, in his Epistle to the Romans 5:15, says of him: "By the grace of the man Jesus Messiah it has abounded to many." By the same reasoning he calls himself the Son of Man in other places, as in Matthew 20:18: "Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests." It follows in the same place, verse 28: "Just as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve," as this matter will be explained in its place. Lastly, this whole business is also plainly understood from the prayer which Jesus taught his disciples, and which they call the Lord's Prayer, described in Matthew 6. For he did not command them to invoke a Trinity, but only the one God, the same God of heaven; this is clear from the prayer itself.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Non tantum efflagitant a Christianis Trinitatis demonstrationem, quod doctrina sit, non divina, sed de novo reperta, teste Judaeo Anonymo in Considerationibus Quaestionum Judaicarum, cap.3. Quomodo probatur, in Deo non posse esse tres personas in una Essentia? Nullum est dubium, quin si hic Interrogator boni Dialectici munus implere vellet, laborem ipsemet praestare deberet probandi, quod a nobis probari postulat. Omnia siquidem de novo reperta dogmata obligationem perspicuae demonstrationis secum adferunt; Verum promptas paratasque ad divinas rationes, suas habent exceptiones, cavillationesque, uti appa-paret paretex Rabbi LipmanniCarmine Memoriali,quo se munire solent adversus Christianos : Ecquid respondebo Epicureo, qui adventat ad perden-dum & destruendum legem sacrosanctam fidelium, atque Dei unitatem cum superbiloquentia impugnat! Objicit primum illud Genes. 1. verf. 1. In principio creavit אלהים Elohim. Ex plurativo numero vocis אלהים petens subsidium. Sed enim parata est Haereticis responsio: Sane quidem verbum אלהים multitudinem significat: At vox ברא creavit appositè statim unitatem arguit. Nimirum quia non scriptum est ברא crearunt. Ideo Dei unius nomen, unicè celebrandum. Est vero haec Scriptura consueta loquendi ratio, ut in encomiis, & cum dominatus alicujus designatur, in plurativo numero verborum fiat constructio. Nam sic Gen. 39. verf. 20. herus Iosephi vocatur אדוני יוסף, & Exod. 22. v. 14. de Domino rei commodatae dicitur בעליו, atque prorsus omnino simili ratione Deut. 10. v. 17. Deus unus & solus, qui-que mox unitatis numero, האל הגדול הגבור והנורא Deus maximus, fortissimus, summeque formidabilis audit, idem etiam האלהים / אדוני pluralis numeri vocibus appellatur. Porro debachantur Adversarii nostri, objectando verba Genes. 1. verf. 26. Faciamus hominem ad imaginem nostram. Istis quoque suam de Deo opinionem confirmare volentes. Ac etiam ibi confessim è latere adscripta responsio: Etenim sic habet commasequens 27. Et creavit Deus hominem, creaturam exilem, carneam & sanguinolentam. Ejus vero nomine quid opus erat instituere consultationem.
units.tr: Christians are not only pressed to demonstrate the Trinity, on the ground that the doctrine is not divine but newly invented, as the anonymous Jew in the Considerations of Jewish Questions, chapter 3, testifies: How is it proved that in God there cannot be three persons in one essence? There is no doubt that if this questioner wished to perform the office of a good dialectician, he himself ought to supply the proof of what he demands we prove. For all newly invented dogmas bring with them the obligation of a clear demonstration; but they have ready and prepared answers and cavils against the divine arguments, as appears from Rabbi Lipmann's Memorial Poem, with which they are accustomed to fortify themselves against Christians: What shall I answer to the Epicurean who comes to destroy and overthrow the holy law of the faithful, and with arrogant speech attacks the unity of God! He first objects that verse of Genesis 1:1, "In the beginning God created [אלהים] Elohim, seeking support from the plural number of the word [אלהים]. But the Heretics have a ready answer: it is true that the word [אלהים] signifies a multitude; but the verb [ברא] created immediately and fittingly argues unity, namely because it is not written [ברא] they created. Therefore the name of the one God is to be celebrated uniquely. Indeed it is the customary manner of speaking in Scripture, when a dignity or lordship is designated, that the construction of the verb is in the plural number. For thus in Genesis 39:20 the master of Joseph is called adonai Yosef [אדוני יוסף], and in Exodus 22:14 of the owner of a borrowed thing it is said baalav [בעליו]; and in an entirely similar way in Deuteronomy 10:17, God, one and alone, who is then also named in the singular, ha-El ha-gadol ha-gibbor veha-nora [האל הגדול הגבור והנורא], God the great, mighty and most formidable; likewise the same God is called by plural words, ha-Elohim [האלהים] / adonai [אדוני]. Further, our adversaries rage, objecting the words of Genesis 1:26, "Let us make man in our image," wishing to confirm their opinion of God by these words too. And there, at once, an answer is added in the margin: for the following verse 27 reads thus: "And God created man," a slight, fleshly and bloody creature. What need was there to hold a consultation in his name?

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Apparebit multo magis, si Nizzachon Vetus consulamus, quod ad objectiones Christianas sequentibus respondet verbis, pag. 4, 5. In principio creavit אלהים. Si dicant Apostata, sive Iudai baptizati: Quare scriptum est אלהים numeroplurativo? Utique scribendum erat אלוה numerounitatis, si nulla locum in Divinis haberet pluralitas. Cum ergo hoc postremum factum non sit, manifeste infertur, duo esse principia, Patrem & Filium. Respondendum: אלהים interdum de uno solo usurpatur, prout infra amplius explicabitur; atque hoc sensu adhibita vox in illo Exod. 7. vers. 1. Ecce constitui te אלהים Pharaoni. Amplius dicendum, esse honoris expressionem. Nam Principes, qui meri homines sunt, tamen in hanc usque diem in more habent, ut de se solitarius pluralivum numerum adhibeant: Nos ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Θεὸς. Quanto igitur magis convenit, ut de Deo loquentes, hoc utamur elogio? Nihilominus aeternum Deus unus est, & nomen ejus unum, prout ex mox sequentibus patescit, nam commate 21, & 27. & creavit, dicitur, non ויברא & crearunt: Scriptum quoque est Es. 44. vers. 24. Extendo caelos solus, expando terram per me ipsum. Faciamus hominem. Respondet Apostatis: Dixit Deus telluri: Faciamus ego & tu inter nos hominem. Da tu mihi, ex tuo pulverem; atque ego ex meo suppeditabo spiri- tum, unde porro sequitur in textu commate 7. Et finxit Dominus Deus hominem ex pulvere terrae. Ecce hoc e tellure est: Sufflavitque in nares ipsius halitum vitae: Ecce tibi, quod Spiritus Deum authorem habet. Quapropter significanter dicitur commate 26. admaginem nostram secundum similitudinem nostram, hoc est, secundum tuam imaginem & similitudinem, esto pulvis: & ego efficiam, ut secundum meam imaginem & similitudinem habeat Spiritum. Hanc obrem dicitur cap. 3. verf. 19. In sudore vultus tui vescitor cibo, donec revertaris in humum, cum ex ea defumtus fueris. Salomo quoque ait Eccles. c. 12. v. 7. Redeunte pulvere in terram quemadmodum fuerat: Spiritu autem redeunte ad Deum, qui dederat illum.
units.tr: It will appear much more clearly if we consult the Old Nizzachon, which answers the Christian objections in the following words (pp. 4, 5): "In the beginning created God [אלהים]. If the apostates, or Jews who have been baptized, say: Why is God written with a plural form [אלהים]? Surely it ought to have been written in the singular [אלוה], if plurality had no place in the divine nature. Since this has not been done, it is plainly inferred that there are two principles, the Father and the Son. The answer must be that אלהים is sometimes used of one alone, as will be explained more fully below. In this sense the word is used in that passage of Exod. 7. vers. 1: 'Behold, I have made you אלהים to Pharaoh.' Further, it must be said that it is an expression of honour. For princes, who are mere men, nevertheless to this day have the custom of using the plural of themselves alone: 'We, ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Θεὸς [the God and God].' How much more fitting, then, is it that we use this title when speaking of God? Nevertheless the eternal God is one, and his name is one, as becomes clear from what follows. For in verses 21 and 27 it says וַיִּבְרָא [and he created], not וַיִּבְרְאוּ [and they created]. It is also written in Isa. 44. vers. 24: 'I alone stretch out the heavens; I spread out the earth by myself.' 'Let us make man.' They answer the apostates: God said to the earth, 'Let you and me make man among us. Give me dust from yours, and I will supply the spirit from mine.' Hence the text goes on in verse 7: 'And the Lord God formed man from the dust of the earth.' Here is what is from the earth; 'and he breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.' Behold, here is what the spirit has as its author. Therefore it is significantly said in verse 26, 'in our image, after our likeness,' that is, 'after your image and likeness, be dust; and I will bring it about that he has the spirit after my image and likeness.' For this reason it is said in Gen. 3. vers. 19: 'In the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken.' Solomon also says in Eccles. 12. vers. 7: 'The dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.'"

units.la: Faciamus hominem. Dicunt Haeretici, verbum Faciamus, duos innuere, nempe Patrem & Filium. Paria habent Rabbi Isaac Bar-Abraham in Chiluk Emuna, pag. 107, 108, 109. Menasseh Ben-Israel in Conciliatore, Quaestione 6. Aben Esra, Ralchi, Kimchius, aliisque ad sua quaeque loca, conferendi cum Rabbi Mose Nachmanide in disputatione cum Fratre Paulo, pag. 58, 59.
units.tr: Faciamus hominem. The heretics say that the word Faciamus signifies two, namely Father and Son. Rabbi Isaac Bar-Abraham has the same in Chiluk Emuna, pp. 107, 108, 109; Menasseh Ben-Israel in Conciliator, Question 6; Aben Ezra, Rashi, Kimchi and others in their own places, to be compared with Rabbi Moses Nachmanides in his disputation with Brother Paul, pp. 58, 59.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Laudant Anti Trinitarios, pessimae doctrinae socios, maxime Socinianos, Servetianos, Arianos rianos, quod argumentis validis, tum ex scri-ptura, tum depromtis ex ratione, asserant solius Dei Unitatem, confutentq; Trinitatis opinio-nem, sicuti patet in Munimine Fidei, quod ca-lamo composuit virulento erga Christianos Rabbi Isaac Bar Abraham, cum sic loquitur pag. 119. Accedit his, quod nostra aetate pridem multi ex Sapientibus ipsorum, quos Sectam Ebionitarum, Sectam Servetianorum, & Sectam Arianorum ipsi vocant, Sectas Romano Catholicorum & Lutheranorum in hoc impugnarunt, Dei unitatem asserentes, & evertentes dogma de Trinitate. Huc pertinent quae disserit Doctissimus Nicolaus Prut a in libro quem latino idiomate de Dei unitate composuit, & qui de uno vero Deo inscribitur, estque meditatio ac explicatio divina unitatis. Similiter Eruditissimus Martinus Zachvvit[?] Polonica lingua Dialogos edidit, ubi Dialogo secundo opinionem eorum qui Trinitatis dogma amplectuntur, argumentis validis ex Scriptura & ratione depromptis, confutat. Idem in libro cui nomen fecit, sermo trium dierum a folio 28. usque ad folium 69. refellit omnes probationes Trinitatis dogma amplectentium, quas ex Novo Testamento arcessunt. Eodem modo multi Sapientum e sectis quas supra memoravimus, omnia fundamenta Trinitatem credentium, in suis quibusdam libris radicitus destruxerunt.
units.tr: They praise the Anti-Trinitarians, companions of a very bad doctrine, chiefly the Socinians, Servetians and Arians, because they assert the unity of God alone with strong arguments, both from Scripture and drawn from reason, and refute the opinion of the Trinity. This is clear in the Munimen Fidei, which Rabbi Isaac Bar Abraham wrote with a virulent pen against the Christians, when he speaks thus at p. 119: Moreover, in our time many of their wise men, whom they call the sect of the Ebionites, the sect of the Servetians and the sect of the Arians, have attacked the sects of the Roman Catholics and the Lutherans on this point, asserting the unity of God and overthrowing the dogma of the Trinity. To this belongs what the most learned Nicolaus Prut(z)a discusses in the book he composed in Latin on the unity of God, entitled On the One True God, which is a meditation and explanation of divine unity. Likewise the most erudite Martin Zachvvit[?] published Dialogues in the Polish language, in which, in the second dialogue, he refutes the opinion of those who embrace the dogma of the Trinity with strong arguments drawn from Scripture and reason. In the book he named Sermo trium dierum, from folio 28 to folio 69, he refutes all the proofs that those who embrace the dogma of the Trinity draw from the New Testament. In the same way many of the wise men of the sects we mentioned above have utterly destroyed, in certain of their books, all the foundations of those who believe in the Trinity.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Adgrediuntur maxime JEsum Nazarenum, Divum Servatorem nostrum, negantes cum Patribus ex odio inveterato, Jesum Personam fuisse divinam, possidentem cum Patre Spirituque Sanƈto unam, eandemque Essentiam, extitisse Filium Dei æternum, duasque potuisse possidere naturas, divinam, humanamque, sed nudum fuisse hominem, mortuum deinde, inque cadaver mutatum, qui nullam potuerit liberare rem, sicuti loquitur RabbiLipmannus inCarmineMemoriali: Num suspensus aliquis, sepultus, inque cadaver mutatus, rem nullam liberare posset? Num id praftaret, qui ipsemet in die mortis suæ liberationem nullam invenit, clamitansDeus mi, Deus mi, quare deferuisti me? Qui alias diserte professus est: Annon filius hominis ego sum? Quemque summa egestate pressum, omnibus rebus destitutum constat questum futffe, quorsum reclinabo caput meum?
units.tr: They attack chiefly Jesus of Nazareth, our divine Saviour. From an ancient hatred, and with the Fathers, they deny that Jesus was a divine Person possessing one and the same essence with the Father and the Holy Spirit, that the eternal Son of God existed, and that he could possess two natures, divine and human; they say he was a mere man, who then died and was changed into a corpse, and who could free nothing. So says Rabbi Lipmann in the Carmen Memoriale: Could someone who was hanged, buried and changed into a corpse free anything? Could he do this, who himself on the day of his death found no deliverance, crying "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" who otherwise plainly professed, "Am I not the son of man?" and who, pressed by the greatest want and destitute of all things, is known to have complained, "Where shall I lay my head?"

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Negant Jesum Nazarenum Deum fuisse, quod Deus Benedictus ex divinitate & humanitate nullo modo possit componi, quia id quod compositum est, Deus esse nequit, sic ratiocinatur Rabbi Ifaac Bar Abraham inChifsuk Emuna, pag. 116. quem propriis audire verbis juvabit: Pari ratione illud etiam quod perfua-sum sum habent, Creatorem componi ex divinitate & corpore, nullo modo in Numine æterno locum invenit. Compositum enim opus habet componente, atque omne compositum, ob compositionem creatum est, habetque cum aliis creaturis corporeis similitudinem, ac subjicitur multiplicationi, divisioni, & mutationi. Quamobrem id quod compositum est, Deus esse nequit, quia Deus nihil quicquam sibi par habet, cum nec multiplicetur, nec dividatur, nec immutetur. Unde scriptum apud Esaiam cap. 40. Cui ergo assimilabitis Deum, & quam similitudinem comparabitis ei? Neque vero Deo tribuendum est, ut possit ipse seipsum componere, aut ad corpus se redigere, prout nec potest alium ex omni parte sibi parem aut similem procreare, id enim nullam in Deo perfectionem poneret, & absit ut tale quid ei conveniat, ceu sapientibus ea res perspecta est.
units.tr: They deny that Jesus of Nazareth was God, because the Blessed God cannot in any way be composed of divinity and humanity, since what is composed cannot be God. So reasons Rabbi Isaac Bar Abraham in the Chizzuk Emuna, p. 116, whose own words it will be helpful to hear: By the same reasoning, that which they are also persuaded of, that the Creator is composed of divinity and body, finds no place at all in the eternal Godhead. For what is composed has need of a composer, and every composite is created on account of its composition, and has a likeness to other corporeal creatures, and is subject to multiplication, division, and change. Wherefore what is composed cannot be God, because God has nothing equal to himself, since he is not multiplied, nor divided, nor changed. Hence it is written in Isaiah ch. 40: "To whom then will you liken God, and what likeness will you compare to him?" Nor is it to be attributed to God that he could compose himself, or reduce himself to a body, just as he cannot beget another who is in every respect equal or like to himself, for that would place no perfection in God, and far be it that such a thing should belong to him, as is clear to the wise.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Inficiantur Jesum Nazarenum Deum unquam extitisse, quod illud Majoribus Judæorum persuadere neutiquam potuerit, sed falsitatis crimine notatus fuerit, si vero Deus fuisset, majorem debuisset fidem verbis suis conciliasse, ut illud crederent, sicuti objicit Rabbi Moses Nachmanides in Disputatione, quam habuit cum Fratre Paulo Christiani, & Fratre Raymundo Martini, pag. 58. Atenim magnum mirum, Iesum ipsum Majoribus nostris probationes attuattulisse, ut offenderet se Deum esse, atque hos illi acer-rime contradicere, & falsitatem asserti demonstrare ausos fuisse. Caterum, erat utique in illius potestate verbis suis majorem fidem conciliare, quam a Rege id praestari potest, si Deus is erat, ceu vobis videtur. Quod si vero illi qui cum vivo ipso conversabantur, morem ei non gesserunt, quomodo nos Regi credemus, ejusque dictis obtemperabimus, qui nullam rei habet notitiam, sed omnia hausit ex levi fama eorum homi-num, qui nec viderunt Iesum, nec vixerunt in regione illius, pro ut Majores nostri, qui omnia ista perspecta habuerunt, & rebus ipsis testes intervenerunt.
units.tr: They deny that Jesus of Nazareth was ever God, because this could in no way have been persuaded to the ancestors of the Jews; rather he was marked with the crime of falsehood. For if he had been God, he ought to have won greater faith for his words, so that they would believe it. So objects Rabbi Moses Nachmanides in the Disputation he held with Brother Paul the Christian and Brother Raymund of Martini, p. 58: But it is a great wonder that Jesus himself brought forward proofs to our ancestors so that he might show that he is God, and that they most fiercely contradicted him and dared to demonstrate the falsity of the assertion. Moreover, it was certainly in his power to win greater faith for his words than a king can secure, if he was God, as it seems to you. But if those who lived with the living man himself did not comply with him, how shall we believe the King and obey his words, who has no knowledge of the matter, but drew everything from the light report of those men who neither saw Jesus nor lived in his region, as our ancestors did, who had all these things thoroughly in view and were witnesses to the things themselves.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Negant Messiam nostrum Personam divinam fuisse, quod in carne apparuerit, neque palam venerit, quod in aprico non patraverit miracula sua, quod foeminae ventrem immunditie plenum ingressus fuerit, inquinatus, sordensque in lucem fuerit editus, sicuti scribit Judaeus Anonymus, Autor Nizzachon Veteris, pag. 6,7. Si Deus erat, quare ipsum se carne obtexit, & cur non palam venit ad Legem suam innovandam, & publice promulgandam, ne homines illius aetatis circa eum errarent, atque cespitarent mortales? In aprico edere debebat opera sua, ut innotescerent, atque sic omnes in illum crediturí erant. At vero, en tibi maximam jacturam! Namplures hac dissimulatione latione perdidit, quam quos ejus redemtio ser vavit. Nimirum, ob hanc dissimulationem, secessum ab illo fecerunt, qui in ipsum credere debebant, quia sanctitatem & puritatem a se segregavit, & ius impuritatibus, quibus nulla in Lege divina graviores sunt, adhaesit. Vide mihi, quid Exod. 19. verf. 15. de Legislatione antiqua scriptum sit: Estote parati in diem tertium, & ne accedite ad uxores. Die enim tertio descendit Deus, inspectante omni populo, ideoque illos sanctificabat. Quomodo igitur iste Deus esse posset, qui foeminam plenum immunditie ventrem habentem, ingressus est? & quem toties mater illius, novem graviditatis mensibus, eo detulit, quo satura itabat? quique tempore nativitatis editus est inquinatus, & sordens, involutus secundinis, & abominabilis sanguine partus ac profluvii? Atqui jussit Lex, sollicite cavere foeminas τὰ ἐμμηνα & fluxum patientes, itemque puerperas, de quibus scriptum est Levit. 12. verf. 4. Triginta tres dies maneto in sanguinis purgatione, nullam rem sacram tangito &c. donec completi fuerint dies purgationis suae. Ecce tibi, puerperam sanctitatis recipiendae incapacem esse; Et pag. 40. Quanto magis vos torquebit ignis inextinguibilis & in ima inferni descendetis, qui errore vestro prolabimini, ut dicatis rem sanctam intrasse foeminam, per locum tam obscaenum? Neque enim in orbe universo res magis foeda est muliebri utero, qui plenus sordibus, immunditie, ac saccatis humoribus, sanguinis nis & mensium excretiam effluviaque patitur, ac fe-men virile recipit.
units.tr: They deny that our Messiah was a divine Person because he appeared in the flesh, because he did not come openly, because he did not perform his miracles in public, and because he entered a woman's womb full of filth, was conceived in uncleanness, and was born in squalor, as the Jewish anonymous author of the Nizzachon Vetus writes (pp. 6, 7): If he was God, why did he cover himself with flesh, and why did he not come openly to renew his Law and proclaim it publicly, so that the people of his time would not err about him and stumble? He ought to have performed his works in public, so that they would become known, and thus all would have believed in him. But see the great loss he caused! By this concealment he lost more people than his redemption saved. Indeed, because of this concealment, those who ought to have believed in him withdrew from him, since he separated himself from holiness and purity and clung to the impurities, than which no defilements are worse in the divine Law. Consider what Exodus 19:15 says about the old legislation: Be ready for the third day, and do not approach your wives. For on the third day God descended, in the sight of all the people, and therefore he sanctified them. How, then, could that God be one who entered a woman's womb full of filth, which his mother carried for nine months, until she was sated, and who at his birth came forth unclean and filthy, wrapped in the afterbirth and in the abominable blood and discharge of childbirth? Yet the Law commanded that women having their periods [τὰ ἐμμηνα] and women suffering a flow, and likewise women after childbirth, be carefully kept apart, as is written in Leviticus 12:4: She shall remain thirty-three days in the purification of blood; she shall touch nothing holy, etc., until the days of her purification are complete. Behold, a woman after childbirth is incapable of receiving holiness. And at p. 40: How much more will the unquenchable fire torment you, and you will descend into the depths of hell, you who through your error go so far as to say that a woman entered the holy place through so obscene a passage? For in the whole world there is nothing more foul than the womb of a woman, which is full of dregs, impurity, and clotted humours, suffers the discharge of blood and of the monthly flow, and receives the male seed.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Negant Jesum Nazarenum Deum fuisse, quia mortuus, & ex arbore suspensus fuit, nec comedit de arbore vitae, ne orbem deciperet universum, sic calumniatur more suo Anonymus Judaeus, qui vetus compositui Nizzachon, cum pag. 10. scribit: Scilicet vidit Deus, venturum Iesum, & decepturum orbem, dicendo se esse Deum; hinc Deus cogitabat: Vtile est ut homines moriantur, & ut Iesus ex arbore suspendatur, nec de arbore vita comedat, ut omnibus in orbe viventibus constet, illum minime Deum esse; Quia facies Jesu nullo praedita splendore, sicuti Moses Magistri nostri, qui tamen merus fuit homo, sicuti rursus debachatur idem Judaeus, compilator veteris Nizzachon, pag. 40, 41. Ecce enim Moses Magister noster f. m. qui homo merus erat, quia Deus de facie ad faciem cum eo locutus erat, vultum tam lucentem retulit, ut vererentur Iudaei accedere. Quanto igitur magis de ipsa Divinitate hoc tenere oportet, atque Iesu faciem ab uno orbis cardine ad alterum fulgorem diffundere conveniebat. At non praeditus erat ullo splendore, sed reliquis mortalibus fuit simillimus. Quamobrem constat, non esse in eum credendum, & quicquid fecit, peractum est abeo ope Magia.
units.tr: They deny that Jesus of Nazareth was God because he died and was hanged on a tree, and because he did not eat of the tree of life, lest he deceive the whole world. So the Jewish anonymous author, who compiled the old Nizzachon, slanders him in his usual way, writing on p. 10: Surely God saw that Jesus was to come and would deceive the world by saying that he is God. Hence God reasoned: it is useful that men should die, and that Jesus should be hanged on a tree and not eat of the tree of life, so that it would be plain to all living in the world that he is by no means God. Because the face of Jesus bore no splendour, unlike that of Moses, our Master, who nevertheless was a mere man, the same Jew, compiler of the old Nizzachon, raves again on pp. 40, 41: For behold, Moses our Master, peace be upon him, who was a mere man, because God spoke with him face to face, brought back a countenance so shining that the Jews were afraid to approach. How much more, then, ought one to hold this concerning Divinity itself, and it would have been fitting for the splendour of Jesus' face to spread from one end of the world to the other. But he had no splendour at all, and was most like the rest of mortals. Therefore it is clear that one should not believe in him, and whatever he did was done by means of magic.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Negant Jesum Deum fuisse, quod non unam cum Patre suo habuerit voluntatem, sed diversam, distinctamque, ipsoque Jesu teste in sua Lege nova, quodque nullam habuerit potentiam propriam, sed totam ex manu Patris mutuatam, ipso rursus judice, sicuti loquitur alius Judaeus Anonymus apud Buxtorfium in Synagoga Judaeorum, Quaestione 18. & 19. Quaero, si est Filius Dei, & si Pater & Filius unum tantum sunt, necessario etiam eadem est eorum voluntas. Ipse tamen, quum oraret ante Patrem suum, (Matth. 26.) dixit: Pater mi, si fieri potest ut non bibam calicem hunc, fac sin minus, fac ut est bonum in oculis tuis: non fiat secundum voluntatem meam, sed secundum voluntatem tuam. Ergo non sunt eorum voluntates similes. Quaero, si ille fuit Deus, quare dum oraret dixit Patri suo, ut faceret voluntatem suam? Hinc apparet, quod non habuerit potentiam in manu sua, qua quidquam posset facere: sed tantum faciebat ex voluntate Patris sui, non autem ex potentia sua.
units.tr: They deny that Jesus was God, because he did not have one and the same will with his Father but a different and distinct will. They appeal to Jesus' own words in his so-called New Law, and also say that he had no power of his own but received all of it from the Father's hand. Here again the judge is another, anonymous Jew, as quoted by Buxtorf in Synagoga Judaeorum, Questions 18 and 19: I ask, if he is the Son of God, and if the Father and the Son are only one, then their will must necessarily be the same as well. Yet he himself, when he prayed before his Father (Matth. 26.), said: "My Father, if it is possible that I should not drink this cup, do it; but if not, let it be as is good in your eyes. Let it not be done according to my will, but according to yours." Therefore their wills are not alike. I ask, if he was God, why did he, when praying, tell his Father to do his will? From this it appears that he did not have power in his hand by which he could do anything; he acted only from the will of his Father, not from his own power.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Credunt Jesum Nazarenum merum fuisse hominem, sed seductorem, Magum, Blasphematorem, qui in Terra Sancta ante eversas vixerit Hierosolymas, matrem habuerit Mariam, aufugerit in Aegyptum, in templo apparuerit, non sine applausu populum docuerit Judaïcam daicum, diversa per Schem Hammephorasch patraverit miracula, inter discipulos Matthæum, Jacobum, Thaddæum, Paulum, aliosque numeraverit, quod à Synedrio maximo Hierosolymis fuerit condemnatus, inque ipsa vespera Paschatis crucifixus, hincque infinita in gentem propriam derivata fuerint mala; Quæ omnia licet calumniis, convitiisque variis in scriptis sint exposita Judaicis, sunt nihilominus certissima, fidissimaque negatæ veritatis Evangelicæ argumenta sæpe atque documenta.
units.tr: They believe that Jesus of Nazareth was merely a man, but a seducer, a magician, and a blasphemer. They hold that he lived in the Holy Land before Jerusalem was overthrown, had Mary as his mother, fled into Egypt, appeared in the temple, taught the Jewish doctrine to the people, not without applause, performed various miracles by means of the Shem Hamephorash, and counted among his disciples Matthew, James, Thaddaeus, Paul, and others; that he was condemned by the Great Sanhedrin at Jerusalem and crucified on the very evening of the Passover, and that from this infinite evils flowed down upon his own nation. Although all these things are set out in Jewish writings with various slanders and insults, they are nevertheless most certain, and are often and abundantly the most trustworthy proofs of the denied Gospel truth.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Appellant Mesiam nostrum Benedictum יש Iefchu, & Iesum Nazarenum, ab urbe habitationis, testibus Talmudicis, in Tractatibus Berachot, Sanhedrin, Sota, Gittin, Avoda Zara, allegatis operose per Vorstium in observationibus ad Rabbi Davidis Gantzii Chronologiam pag. 257. sequentibusque, negantibus licet Judæis perpaucis Talmudistarum consensum, asserentibusque nil de nostro memorari Jesu in Talmude, sed alium quendam intelligi Jesum, de quo pessima quæque referantur, sicuti testantur Rabbi Jechiel in disputatione cum Nicolao pag. 15, 16, 17. Rabbi Lipmannus Mulhusinus in Nizzachon pag. 191. Rabbi Gedalja in Schalschelet Hakkabala pag. 24. Et Rabbi Salomo Zevi Offenhausensis, qui decem arargumentis voluit probare nullam omnino de Servatore nostro in Talmude extare mentionem, nuspiamque ei magistros dixisse contumelias, consulendus in Theriaca Judaica per Humanissimum, Doctissimumque Wulferum nuper recusa; Et ex Christianis Galatinus de Arcanis Catholicae veritatis lib. 1. cap. 7. pag. 25. Paulus Riccius in Epitome Doctrinae Talmudicae, & Schickardus in Tarich pag. 84. Cum tamen hoc a Judaeis his fit negatum, vel ex metu cruciatuum, afflictionum, ipsiusque mortis saepe propterea tolerandae, quod coram Regibus, Principibus, Personisque sacris essent constituti, quibus calumniam Talmudistarum objicien- tibus sic erat respondendum, vel ex astutia, calliditateque genti propria, ut Christianis magis placerent, pacatioresque inter ipsos vivere possent; Imo contrarium restentur non solum Judaei antiquiores, qui expresse Talmudica haec de nostro exponunt Jesu, quales sint Abrahamus Zacutus in Juchasin, pag. 16. Aben-Esra ad Danielis cap. 11. verf. 14. Abraham Ben Dior in Megillath Taanith, pag. 27. Abarbanel in Daniel p. 101. aliique plurimi; verum etiam recentiores, quorum concors pro recepta opinione suffragium fit, uti egregie haec omnia probat Illustris, Magnusque Wagenseilius noster in Sota sua nunquam declinante, pag. 1057. Sed tamen magis inclino in illam Seldeni, sive communem, tam veterum, quam recentiorum eruditorum sententiam, non de alio, quam de nostro Domino Deoque IEsu Christo Talmudistas loquutos esse, atque redditurosillos olim in decretorio die, gravem rationem, mendaciorum & maledictorum, quae adversus Sacrosanctam ejus majestatem sceleratissime effuti-verunt. Atque, huc non admodum me impellit, illorum, (cui Seldenum tamen quid tribuisse appareat,) authoritas, qui Basileenses Talmud expurgarunt, nam Christiani erant, nec satis suam mihi probant industriam, etiam in perficiendo labore, quem fuere aggressi. Illud multo maximum est, ipsos Iudaeos, ultro, in Codicibus quibusdam En Iacob, multa quae de Iesu dicenda occurrebant omisisse, nunquam id facturi, si alium quam nostrum Servatorem innui credidissent. Accedit deinde, concors Iudaeorum nostra aetatis, pro recepta opinione suffragium, nec memini me unquam cum quoquam contulisse, qui aliter fuerit animatus. Tum vero ex antiquioribus, eos quoque in eandem rem allegare possumus testes, qui magna pollent authoritate, & adversus quos non R. Salomo Zevi tantum, sed nec ipse R. Gedalia, autor libri Schalaschelet Hokkabala, si darentur, auderent hicere.
units.tr: They call our Messiah, Blessed be he, Jeschu [יש], and Jesus of Nazareth, from the town where he lived, on the testimony of the Talmudic writings in the tractates Berachot, Sanhedrin, Sota, Gittin, and Avoda Zara, which Vorstius has laboriously cited in his observations on the Chronology of Rabbi David Gantz, p. 257 and following. Although a few Jews deny that the Talmudists agree on this, and assert that nothing about our Jesus is mentioned in the Talmud, but that some other Jesus is meant, about whom all manner of wicked things are related, as Rabbi Jechiel testifies in his disputation with Nicholas, pp. 15, 16, 17; Rabbi Lipmann of Mühlhausen in the Nizzachon, p. 191; Rabbi Gedaliah in the Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah, p. 24; and Rabbi Solomon Zevi of Offenhausen, who undertook to prove with ten arguments that there is no mention whatever of our Saviour in the Talmud, and that the masters nowhere spoke insults against him (he should be consulted in the Jewish Theriaca, recently reprinted by the most learned and erudite Wülfer); and among Christians, Galatinus, On the Secrets of the Catholic Truth, book 1, chapter 7, p. 25; Paulus Riccius in his Epitome of Talmudic Doctrine; and Schickard in the Tarikh, p. 84. Yet this denial by the Jews is made either from fear of torments, afflictions, and even death, which they often had to endure precisely because they were brought before kings, princes, and sacred persons, to whom they had to answer thus when the Talmudists' slander was laid against them; or from the cunning and craftiness proper to their nation, so that they might please Christians more and live more peaceably among them. Indeed, not only the older Jews, who expressly interpret these Talmudic passages of our Jesus, maintain the opposite, such as Abraham Zacuto in the Yuchasin, p. 16; Ibn Ezra on Daniel 11:14; Abraham ben Dior in the Megillat Taanit, p. 27; Abarbanel on Daniel, p. 101; and very many others; but also the more recent writers, whose agreement supports the accepted opinion, as our illustrious and great Wagenseil excellently proves in his Sota, which never wavers, p. 1057. Yet I incline more to the view of Selden, that is, the view common to the learned men of both older and recent times, that the Talmudists spoke of none other than our Lord and God Jesus Christ, and that on the Day of Judgment they will render a heavy account for the lies and curses which they have wickedly uttered against his most holy majesty. Nor does the authority of those who purged the Basel Talmud move me much (though it appears they ascribed something to Selden); for they were Christians, and they do not prove their diligence to me, even in completing the labour they undertook. What is by far the greatest point is that the Jews themselves, of their own accord, have omitted in certain codices, such as the En Jacob, many things that ought to be said about Jesus, which they would never have done had they believed that someone other than our Saviour was meant. Furthermore, there is the agreement of the Jews of our own age in support of the accepted opinion, and I do not remember ever having conversed with anyone who thought otherwise. Moreover, from the older authorities we can cite as witnesses on this same matter men of great weight, against whom not only Rabbi Solomon Zevi, but not even Rabbi Gedaliah himself, the author of the Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah, would dare to raise his voice, if they were available.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Appellant per contumeliam Servatorem nostrum ישו, non ישו, quod ipsum verum esse Ser-
units.tr: By way of insult they call our Saviour Jeschu [ישו], not Jeschua [ישוע], which

units.la: Servatorem negent, teste Rabbi Elia Levita in Lexico Tisbi ad vocem Jeschu: Et quia Iudaei non credunt quod ipse sit servator ille, idcirco nolunt ipsum vocare יש׳ sed tollunt א׳ין literam, & pronunciant יש׳ Ieschu; Sed hominem nequam, mendacem, malum, abominandum credant, cujus proinde memoria expungenda, exponentes ex impio Cabbalae mysterio, tres literas nominis Jeschu per tres voces, ימח שמו וזכרו, Est mendacium & malum, vel ימח שמו וזכרו, Est mendacium & abominatio, vel ימח שמו וזכרו, Deleatur nomen ejus & memoria ejus, non diffitentibus nobis quandoque Judaeis familiaribus, sic pariter Buxtorfio, Westphalorum in Hebraicis Eruditissimo, in Lexico triginta annorum, pag. 992; Et in Toledot Jeschu, pag. 6. Sic Judaei hodierni vocant Messiam nostrum בן נזר, Ben Nezer, vel Talmudicorum famosissimum latronem intelligentes, cujus mentio fit in Tractatu Cetubhot, vel Messiam cum ipso comparantes, quod non melioris fuerit conditionis, vel forte ad aliud quid alludentes, sic Abarbanel Insignis Commentator in Danielem, visus nobis Bafileae, in linguam translatus latinam per Buxtorfium, cum ita loquitur sol. 66. Diligenter adverte, qua ratione exponant cornu illud ultimum parvum de Ben Nezer, qui est Iesus Hannozeri, & juxta seriem contextus cum eo conjungunt regnum impium, pium, quod est regnum Edom: Edom vero est populus Iesu. Nam illud regnum est ipsius populus; Sic in Aruch manuscripto apud Buxtorfium in Lexico Talmudico, p. 1383. Nezer est etiam Nozeri maledictus ille. Praeterea Rabbini quandoque Messiam nostrum ne nomine quidem suo exprimere volunt, sed ex malitia nominant, Aliquem, Virum illum, innominatum, ita Rabbi Aben Esra in Genes. cap. 27. vers. 40. Fuerunt homines pauci qui crediderunt in Virum, quem constituerunt Deum, quando credidit Roma tempore Constantini, qui innovavit totam religionem et posuit in vexillo suo figuram Viri ipsius.
units.tr: they deny to be the Saviour's name, as witnessed by Rabbi Elijah Levita in his Lexicon Tishbi under the word Jeschu: "And because the Jews do not believe that he is that Saviour, they therefore refuse to call him Jeschua, but remove the letter aleph and pronounce it Jeschu." They regard him as a wicked, lying, evil, and abominable man, whose memory must therefore be blotted out. They explain the three letters of the name Jeschu from the impious mystery of the Cabbalah by three words, ימח שמו וזכרו [yimach shemo vezichro]: either "It is a lie and an evil," or "It is a lie and an abomination," or "Let his name and his memory be blotted out." We do not deny that some familiar Jews sometimes do this; Buxtorf, the most learned of the Westphalians in Hebrew matters, agrees in his Lexicon of Thirty Years, p. 992, and in the Toledot Jeschu, p. 6. In this way the Jews of today call our Messiah Ben Nezer [בן נזר], either understanding by him the most famous Talmudic robber, who is mentioned in the tractate Ketubot, or comparing the Messiah with him, because he was not of better condition; or perhaps alluding to something else. So Abarbanel, the distinguished commentator on Daniel, whom we saw at Basel translated into Latin by Buxtorf, speaks thus on fol. 66: "Pay close attention to the reason why they explain that last small horn as Ben Nezer, who is Jesus of Hannozeri, and according to the sequence of the context they join with him the impious kingdom, which is the kingdom of Edom; Edom indeed is the people of Jesus, for that kingdom is his people." So also in the manuscript Aruch cited by Buxtorf in his Talmudic Lexicon, p. 1383: "Nezer is also that accursed Nozeri." Moreover, the rabbis sometimes do not even wish to express our Messiah by his own name, but out of malice call him "Someone," "That man," "the Nameless One." So Rabbi Ibn Ezra on Genesis 27:40: "There were few men who believed in the Man whom they set up as God, when Rome believed in the time of Constantine, who renewed the whole religion and placed on his standard the figure of that very Man."

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Nominant patrem Jesu Nazareni Pandiram, vel Pantherem, matrem Stadam, quandoque Mariam, hinc Jesum Filium Pandirae, & Filium Stadae, ita enim legimus in Tractatu Talmudico Sanhedrin cap. 7. sol. 67. Sic fecerunt filio Stadae in Lydda, et suspenderunt eum in vespera Paschatis, Filius autem hic Stadae fuit Pandirae filius. Dixit quidem Rafchasda, maritus Stadae Pandira, Paphus filius Iehudae est. Dico nihilominus: Mater ejus fuit Stada, Maria nimirum illa plicatrix capillorum mulierum, de qua dicunt Pombeditha: declinavit ista a marito suo; Sic in Tract. Talmudico Schabbat cap. 12. sol. 104. In Tract. Talm. Chagiga sol. 4. In Talmude HieHierofolymitano Tractatu Sanhedrin.c. 7. In Beth Jacob,sol.127. Nominant Mesiae Patrem תנחומא Iosephum Panderam, referuntque fuisse ganeonem, qui nullius fuerit frugis, oriundus ex tribu Juda, sic loquuntur in pestilentissimo libello, Toledot Jeschu, de generatione Jeschu, pag. 3. Prodiit enim quidam ganeo, vir nequam nulliusque frugis, ex trunco succisio tribus Iuda, cui nomen Iosephus Pandera. Iserat statura insignis, manu fortis, & eximia pulchritudine, maximamque aetatis partem in adulteriis, sceleribus, rapinis item ac violentia exegerat. Domicilium ei Bethlehemi Iuda, habitabatque in illius vicinia vidua quadam, cui filia Mirjam nomine, esque hac illa Mirjam, ornatrix capillorum muliebrium, cujus aliquoties in Talmude mentio injicitur. Cum quo paria faciunt, quae referuntur in manuscripto nostro virulento Judaei Anonymi, quod תולדות ישו Historiam suspensi ore appellare voluit maledico, quando sic calumniatur, p.1. Et ecce, fuit vir quidam nomine Iosephus ganeo, malus, nulliusque frugis, deleatur nomen ejus, ex trunco Iuda, cognominatus Pandera. Erat bellicosus, & maxima praditus statura, verum qui totam fere vitae partem transigebat in rapina, violentia, adulterio & sceleribus. Habitabat autem Bethlehemi Iehuda, habebatque in vicinia habitantem viduam aliquam, cuius filia erat nomine Mirjam.
units.tr: They call the father of Jesus of Nazareth Pandira or Panthera, and his mother Stada, and sometimes Maria. Hence they call Jesus the son of Pandira and the son of Stada. For so we read in the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, chap. 7, sol. 67: So they did to the son of Stada in Lydda, and they hanged him on the eve of the Passover. Now this son of Stada was the son of Pandira. Rafchasda, the husband of Stada, indeed said that Pandira was Pappus, the son of Judah. I nevertheless say: his mother was Stada, that Maria who dressed women's hair, of whom Pombeditha says that she turned aside from her husband. So also in the Talmudic tractate Shabbath, chap. 12, sol. 104; in the Talmudic tractate Chagiga, sol. 4; in the Jerusalem Talmud, tractate Sanhedrin, chap. 7; and in Beth Jacob, sol. 127. They name the Messiah's father Tanchuma [תנחומא] and Joseph Pandera, and they say that he was a debauched fellow, good for nothing, descended from the tribe of Judah. So they speak in the most pestilent little book, the Toledot Jeschu [תולדות ישו], on the generation of Jeschu, p. 3: For there appeared a certain debauched man, a wicked fellow good for nothing, from the stock of the tribe of Judah, whose name was Joseph Pandera. He was remarkable in stature, strong of hand, and of extraordinary beauty, and he spent the greater part of his life in adulteries, crimes, robberies, and likewise in violence. His home was at Bethlehem of Judah, and in its neighbourhood there lived a certain widow, who had a daughter named Miriam, and this was that Miriam, the hairdresser of women's hair, of whom mention is made several times in the Talmud. Agreeing with this are the things reported in our virulent manuscript of an anonymous Jew, which the malicious author chose to call the History of the Hanged One [תולדות ישו], where he slanders thus, p. 1: And behold, there was a certain man named Joseph, a debauched fellow, wicked and good for nothing; let his name be blotted out; from the stock of Judah, surnamed Pandera. He was warlike and endowed with very great stature, yet he spent almost the whole of his life in robbery, violence, adultery and crimes. Now Jehuda dwelt at Bethlehem, and he had as a neighbour a certain widow, whose daughter was named Miriam.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Calumniantur audacter, Servatoris nostri matrem fuisse זונה Adulteram, a marito suo Jochanan declinantem, & cum Josepho Pandera, ganeone magno, rem habentem, sic rursus in libello impio Toledot Jeschu, pag. 4. Hinc Messiam ממזר Spurium, nothumque proclamant, pag. 6,7. Calumniantur Mariam fuisse נדה Pollutam, Menstruatamque, טמאה Impuram, capillorum muliebrium plicatricem, & quae non alia, testimoniis in Talmude obviis, ut ita contra propriam mentem locutus sit Rabbi Jechiel, in ea quam habuit disputatione cum quodam Nicolao, quando p. 18. scribit: AEquum omnino dixisti, non convenit nobis eam conviciari, quid enim ipsa peccavit, aut quid deliquit? Adde, quod ex ossibus nostris carne, nostra oriunda (cognata nobis & consanguinea est.) Sed vero nec totum Talmud, nec omnes Historici libri uspiam de ea loquuntur: nam ea, quam ipse indicavit, longe alia fuit, atque ecce vobis rei testimonia; Cum persuasum fere omnibus hodie sit, Judaeos sacrilegos, sicuti in Gemara Talmudica Redemtori nostro unice sunt conviciati, ita quoque data opera in Mariae opprobrium quaedam per summam scripsisse calumniam, sicuti ex ipsis Judaeis quam egregie demonstrat Optimus Buxtorfius in Lexico Talmudico, p. 1460, 1461, quem proinde
units.tr: They boldly calumniate the mother of our Saviour, calling her an adulteress [זונה], who turned aside from her husband Jochanan and had intercourse with Joseph Pandera, a great debauchee. So again in the impious booklet Toledot Jeschu, p. 4. From this they proclaim the Messiah a bastard [ממזר], an illegitimate child, p. 6, 7. They calumniate Mary as unclean [נדה], polluted and menstruous, impure [טמאה], one who plaits women's hair, and nothing else, according to testimonies found in the Talmud. So Rabbi Jechiel spoke against his own mind in that disputation he had with a certain Nicolaus, when on p. 18 he writes: You have said altogether fairly; it is not right for us to revile her, for what did she do, or what fault did she commit? Add that she is of our flesh, sprung from our bones (she is related and kin to us). But neither the whole Talmud nor all the historical books speak of her anywhere; for the one he pointed to was quite different, and here is the evidence for the matter: ... Since it is now almost universally believed that the Jews, who in the Talmudic Gemara have reviled our Redeemer alone, have also deliberately written certain things in the greatest calumny to Mary's disgrace, as the most excellent Buxtorf shows very clearly from the Jews themselves in his Talmudic Lexicon, pp. 1460, 1461, whom therefore

units.la: de audire non parum juvabit: Utut enim Rabbini in Additionibus Talmudicis contendant, non intelligi Iesum Nazarenum, & malitiam suam conentur tegere, tamen fraus ipsorum multipliciter pellucet, & de illo ipso eos haec omnia scribere & intellegere, varia evincunt. Nam primo vocatur quoq; Ben Pandira. Sic autem vocatur quoq; ab ipsis Iesus Nazarenus, ut aliquot testimoniis infra in פנדירא ostendetur. Deinde haec Stada dicitur fuisse Maria, & haec Maria Mater Ploni ת N. quo sine dubio Christus intelligitur. Sic enim nomen ejus reticere solent, quia exprimere verentur. Manuscripta exemplaria, si ad manus essent, forte ejus rei fidem facerent. Et hoc quoq; fuit nomen matris Iesu Nazareni. Tertio dicitur fuisse Seductor populi. Pro tali habitum fuisse olim Christum a Iudaeis, testatur historia Evangelica, & hodieq; adhuc ab ipsis haberi, scripta hodierna, vide Sanhedr. sol. 107. col. 2. edit. Veneta. Quarto dicitur fuisse suspensus, quod manifeste refertur ad crucifixionem Christi, praesertim cum circumstantia temporis addatur, in vespera Sabbathi, quae cum tempore crucifixionis Christi convenit. Et sic scribunt in Sanhedr. sol. 43. col. 1. בערב פסח תלאוהו לישו In vespera Paschatis suspenderunt Iesum. Quinto, quod in Talm. Hierosol. de duobus discipulis sapientum, tanquam testibus scilicet in insidias ipsi collocatis, & deinde contra ipsum productis, scribitur; id refero ad duos illos ψευδομάρτυρες, quorum mentionem facit cit Evangelista Matth. c. 26. 60, 61. vel ad illud, quod Lucas dicit c. 20. v. 20. παρατηρήσαντες· ἀποστείλαντες ἐγκα- θέτως ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι, ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου, &c. Sexto, quod de eodem Ben Stada scribunt, eum in cæsura carnis jus eduxisse magicas artes ex Ægypto. Simile quid enim de Christo scribunt in virulentissimo scripto ישו תולדות. Vide infra in radice שמ, in שמ״ו. Septimo denique tempus quoque convenit. Nam dicitur hic Ben Stada vixisse diebus Pappi filii Jehuda, qui fuit contemporaneus R. Akiva. Akiva autem vixit tempore ascensionis Christi, & adhuc postea: Maria etiam ista dicitur vixisse sub templo secundo. Ex quibus omnibus patet, tecte & blasphemè eos hic per Filium Stada intelligere Filium Mariæ, Iesum Christum; quam ipsorum fraudem & malitiam hoc loco, ex occasione hujus vocis ישו in transitu prodere & detegere voluimus: Inprimis cum historia Evangelica per illam potius illustretur, quam obscuretur. Quod alia quædam circumstantia discrepent, nihil obest. Nihil enim novi hoc est in libris Iudæorum: sed studio id faciunt, ut tanto minus a Christianis impostura animadvertatur.
units.tr: it will greatly help to hear. For although the rabbis in their Talmudic Additions contend that Jesus of Nazareth is not meant, and try to hide their malice, nevertheless their fraud shines through in many ways, and several things prove that they wrote and understood all this about that very man. For first, he is also called Ben Pandira. Jesus of Nazareth is also called this by them, as will be shown by several testimonies below under פנדירא. Next, this Stada is said to have been Mary, and this Mary the mother of Peloni [ת N.], by which Christ is undoubtedly meant. For they are accustomed to keep his name unspoken, because they fear to pronounce it. Manuscript copies, if they were at hand, would perhaps confirm the fact, and this too was the name of the mother of Jesus of Nazareth. Third, he is said to have been a seducer of the people. That Christ was once regarded as such by the Jews is attested by the Gospel history, and that he is still held so by them today is shown by their modern writings; see Sanhedrin, fol. 107, col. 2, Venetian edition. Fourth, he is said to have been hanged, which clearly refers to the crucifixion of Christ, especially since the circumstance of time is added, on the eve of the Sabbath, which agrees with the time of Christ's crucifixion. So they write in Sanhedrin, fol. 43, col. 1: [בערב פסח תלאוהו לישו] "On the eve of the Passover they hanged Jesus." Fifth, what is written in the Jerusalem Talmud about two disciples of the wise, namely as witnesses set to lie in wait for him and then produced against him, I refer to those two false witnesses whom the Evangelist mentions, Matth. c. 26, 60, 61, or to that which Luke says in c. 20, v. 20: [παρατηρήσαντες· ἀποστείλαντες ἐγκαθέτως ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι, ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου] "watching him, they sent spies pretending to be righteous, that they might catch him in a word," etc. Sixth, what they write of the same Ben Stada, that by the incision of his flesh he drew magical arts out of Egypt. For they write something similar about Christ in the most virulent writing, the Toledot Jeschu. See below under the root שמ, in שמ״ו. Seventh and finally, the time also agrees. For this Ben Stada is said to have lived in the days of Pappus the son of Judah, who was a contemporary of R. Akiva. Akiva lived at the time of Christ's ascension and for some time afterwards. This Mary too is said to have lived under the second temple. From all these things it is plain that they here, covertly and blasphemously, mean by the son of Stada the son of Mary, Jesus Christ. We have wished to lay bare and expose this their fraud and malice in passing, on the occasion of this word [ישו], especially since the Gospel history is thereby illuminated rather than obscured. That certain other circumstances differ does no harm. For there is nothing new in this in the books of the Jews, but they do it deliberately, so that the imposture is less noticed by Christians.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Pergunt calumniari Iesum discipulum fuisse Iosuæ, Filii Perachiæ, cum quo in Ægyptum aufugerit, ubi artibus magicis fuerit imbutus, quas inde mira eduxerit astutia, quibusque que populum deinceps fascinaverit, & ad idololatriam seduxerit, hinc יושב Maleficus, Praestigiator, Magusque appellatus, sicuti petulanter loquuntur ex Tractatu Talmudico Sanhedrin, cap. 11, quod Cheleck inscribitur, translatumque in linguam fuit Germanicam per Gersonem Judaeum conversum, sol. 107. Cum Rabbi Iosua filio Perechia quid factum? cum occidisset Rex Iannaeus Rabbinos, abiit Rabbi Iosua filius Perechia, & cum eo Iesus in Alexandriam Aegypti. Pace vero restituta misit ad eum Simeon Ben Schotach & sic scripsit: Ex me Hierosolyma urbe Sanctā ad te in Alexandriam in Aegypti soropem meam S. P. maritus meus moratur apud te, & ego sedeo desolata. Surrexit itaque Rabbi Iosua & exiit in Alexandria, venit in quoddam diverso, ubi affecerunt eum honore magno. Dixit: quam pulchrum hospitium! Respondit Iesus (existimans ipsi sermonem esse de hospitatione, cum vox ambigua sit, & tam hospitium quam hospitam denotare possit,) Pulchra utique est Magister; oculi ejus sunt teretes. Dixit: Scelesté, haeccine tibi curae sunt? Atque adduxit quadringentas buccinas & excommunicavit eum. Redibat vero ille aliquoties, dicens: Recipe. Sed Rabbi Iosua non curavit eum. Alia die, cum legeret textum Deut. 6. Audi Israel, venit Iesus coram eo, & sperravit se receptum iri. Annuit ipsi manu sua Rabbi Iosua; sed cum putaret se repelli, abiit & erexit lapidem & adoravit.
units.tr: They go on to calumniate Jesus as a disciple of Joshua, son of Perachiah, with whom he fled into Egypt, where he was steeped in magic arts, which he afterwards brought out with wonderful cunning, and by which he then bewitched the people and led them into idolatry. Hence he is called [יושב] a sorcerer, a deceiver, and a magician, as they wantonly say from the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, chapter 11, called Chelek, which was translated into German by the Jew Gerson, who was converted, fol. 107: What happened to Rabbi Joshua son of Perachiah? When King Jannaeus had killed the rabbis, Rabbi Joshua son of Perachiah left, and with him Jesus went to Alexandria in Egypt. When peace was restored, Simeon ben Shetach sent to him and wrote thus: From me, from the holy city of Jerusalem, to you in Alexandria in Egypt, my sister S. P. Your husband is staying with you, and I sit desolate. So Rabbi Joshua got up and went out to Alexandria; he came to a certain inn, where they honoured him greatly. He said: What a beautiful lodging! Jesus answered him (supposing that he spoke of lodging, since the word is ambiguous and can denote both an inn and a hostess): Certainly, Master, her eyes are round. He said: Wicked man, is this what you care about? And he brought four hundred trumpets and excommunicated him. But Jesus came back several times, saying: Receive me. Yet Rabbi Joshua took no notice of him. Another day, as he was reading the text of Deut. 6, Hear, O Israel, Jesus came before him and hoped to be received. Rabbi Joshua nodded to him with his hand; but when he thought he was being repulsed, he went off, set up a stone and worshipped it.

units.la: 1 vit eum. Dixit ipsi Rabbi Iosua : Reditus sit concessus. Respondit : Itaa te traditum accepimus : Qui-cunque peccat & plures ad peccandum impellit, non concessum est ipsi pœnitentiam agere. Verum Mar dixit: Iesus fuit præstigiator & seduxit & ad lapsum impulit Israel; Etlicet Rabbi Jechiel, Rabbi Salomo Zevi, cum Rabbi Gedalja inficientur nostrum intelligi JEsum,cum Jannæus illi coævus esse non poslit, quod centum & plurimis annis ante ad plures abierit, manet tamen firmum hæc de nostro dici JEsu, quod non solum illud Gerson Ex Judæus in Præfatione Chelek testetur, sed ipse Rabbi Abraham Zacutus in Juchasin pag. 16. Vera est Traditio Majorum, illum Virum, (quem nominare nolo) discipulum fuisse Iosuæ Perachidæ. Atque hæc est Secta..... Tenendum igitur, omnino Virum illum natum esse, anno quarto regni Jannæi secundi, qui & Alexander dicitur, hoc est, anno ante excisum templum CCLXIII. & anno LI. regiminis Chasmonæorum, qui est annus orbis conditi supra ter millesimum sexcentesimus septuagesimus & unus, (Nec discedendum ab hac opinione,) etiamsi ii (qui ejus nomen profitentur perhibent) ipsum imperante Herode, servo illo Chasmonæorum, anno post orbem conditum (ter millesimo) & supra septingentesimum sexagesimo natum esse, fuisseq; suspensum annis XXXV. ante templi excidium, cum ageret ætatis annum XXXII.(Nam hæc ipsi ita effinxerunt) eum in finem, ut nobis illudant, dicantque, objcelus quod adversus eum patravimus, illico quadragesimo anno post, templum nostrum fuisse excisum. Necrem conficiet omnino, quod Jannæus Rex & Pontifex Judæorum longo tempore ante natum nostrum fuerit Jesum, proindeque aliium in Talmude indigitari, cum notante Clarissimo Seldeno libro 4. de Jure Naturæ & Gentium juxta discipli- nam Hebræorum cap. 9. earum non sit, tempora illius sæculi Hebræis confundi, aliterque multo atque a Christianis putari, hocque eos scire, qui Chronica eorum salutaruntj imo dicendum sit Hebræos vel studio, ex summa malitia, rationem temporum pervertisse, quo sic facilius fucum facerent, & aliorum oculis offunderent caliginem; vel ex ignorantia, nimiaque oscitantia quandoque plurima falsa, metachtonismosque ridicularioss narrationibus admiscuisse Historicis, ut vel pueris nostris desipere viderentur. Sed expedita esse omnia illa, quæ de Jesu nostro referuntur in Talmude, ostendunt maxime ea, quæ legimus in Tractatu Talmudico Schabbat cap. 12. sol. 104. Dixit Rabbi Eliezer Sapientibus: Annon Filius Stadæ eduxit magias ex Ægypto per casuram carnis suæ? Responderunt ipsi: Stultus est & non petimus probationem a stultis.
units.tr: 1 ...him. Rabbi Joshua said to him: Return is permitted. He answered: Thus we have received the tradition: whoever sins and drives many to sin, it is not permitted to him to repent. But Mar said: Jesus was a sorcerer, who seduced and drove Israel to apostasy. Although Rabbi Jechiel, Rabbi Solomon Zevi and Rabbi Gedaliah deny that our Jesus is meant, since Jannaeus cannot have been his contemporary, he having lived more than a hundred years earlier, it nevertheless remains certain that these things are said of our Jesus. This is attested not only by Gerson the Jew in the Preface to Chelek, but by Rabbi Abraham Zacutus himself in Juchasin, p. 16: The tradition of our forefathers is true, that that man (whom I do not wish to name) was a disciple of Joshua the son of Perachiah. And this is the sect... It must therefore be held that that man was born in the fourth year of the reign of Jannaeus the Second, who is also called Alexander, that is, in the year 263 before the temple was destroyed, and in the 51st year of the Hasmonean rule, which is the year of the world 3671. (Nor should one depart from this opinion,) even if those who profess his name report that he was born in the time of Herod, that servant of the Hasmoneans, in the year of the world 3760, and was hanged 35 years before the destruction of the temple, when he was 32 years old. (For they invented these things thus) to the end that they might mock us, and say that the crime we committed against him was punished forty years later, when our temple was destroyed. Indeed, it must be concluded that King and High Priest Jannaeus of the Jews lived long before our Jesus was born, and therefore another person is indicated in the Talmud; as the most distinguished Selden observes in book 4 of De Jure Naturae et Gentium iuxta disciplinam Hebraeorum, chapter 9, it is not that the Hebrews confuse the times of that century, and they think otherwise than Christians do, and those who know their chronicles know this. Or rather it must be said that the Hebrews, either deliberately, from extreme malice, have perverted the reckoning of times, so as to make the deception easier and cast a mist over the eyes of others; or else from ignorance and great carelessness they have mixed very many false things and ridiculous transpositions of events into their historical narratives, so that they might seem foolish even to our children. But that all those things which are related of our Jesus in the Talmud are idle is shown above all by what we read in the Talmudic tractate Shabbat, chapter 12, fol. 104: Rabbi Eliezer said to the sages: Did not the son of Stada bring magic out of Egypt through the incision of his flesh? They answered him: He is a fool, and we do not ask proof from fools.

units.la: Oggánniunt Verpæ Jesum Nazarenum artefua magica ad templi Hierololymitani penetrasse interiora, inde nomen Jehova abstulisse, & miracula multa deinde patrasse, sicut Rabbini in Toledot Jeschu, libello de Genealogia Jesu pestilentissimo, pag. 7. Cum innotuisset rumor Jesum spurium esse, deseruit Galilæam superiorem, & cum clam venisset Hierosolymas, ingressus est templum, didicitque literas sacras, nomenque ineffabile membrana inscripsit, quo prolato, ne dolorem sentiret, caesuram in sua fecit carne, membranam cum myrrhis inibi recondens. Mox cum nomen illud rursus elocutus fuisset, rediit caro in locum suum. Et arte magica & incantationibus ingressus est templum, si enim aliter fuisset, non permisissent Sacerdotes sancti filii Aaronis, ut ingrederetur. Quare manifestum est eum per impurum nomen & artem magicam omnia ista effecisse. Cum vero per januam egrederetur, allatrarunt ipsum leones, & oblitus est hujus nominis. Tunc exivit urbe, effodit carnem suam, & eduxit scripturam, literas bene perpendit, & ita rursus hoc nomen didicit. Oblatrant pariter Judæi Jesum Nazarenum perversam docuisse doctrinam, non Mosi, non Prophetis congruam, sed è diametro contrariam, accusantes graviter Jesum quod Legem Mosis æternam per propriam novam abolere omni modo voluerit, quod edulium lium suum publice adulterit, id est ex mente Talmudistarum, quod doctrinam corruperit, & ad haeresin, idololatriamque desciverit, quod tetrum de se odorem miserit, veluti cibus nimium adustus, sicut loquuntur in Tractatu Berachot sol. 18. Edit. Venetæ: In Plateis nostris, ne sit nobis filius aut discipulus, qui adurit edulium suum publice, veluti Nazaræus; Et in Sanhedrin sol. 103. Et plaga non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo, non erit tibi filius aut discipulus, qui corrumpit decoctum seu edulium suum publice, sicuti Iesus Nazaræus.
units.tr: The Jews babble that Jesus of Nazareth, by magical arts, penetrated into the inner parts of the Temple of Jerusalem, thence took away the name Jehovah, and afterwards performed many miracles. So the rabbis say in the Toledot Jeschu, that most pestilential little book on the genealogy of Jesus, p. 7: When the rumour became known that Jesus was illegitimate, he left upper Galilee, and having come secretly to Jerusalem, entered the temple and learned the sacred letters, and wrote the ineffable name on a parchment; and when he had pronounced it, so that he would not feel pain, he made an incision in his flesh and hid the parchment there with myrrh. Soon, when he had uttered that name again, his flesh returned to its place. By magical art and incantations he entered the temple, for otherwise the holy priests, the sons of Aaron, would not have allowed him to enter. It is therefore clear that he accomplished all those things through the unclean name and magic art. But when he was going out by the gate, the lions barked at him, and he forgot this name. Then he left the city, dug up his flesh, drew out the writing, weighed the letters well, and so learned the name again. Likewise the Jews rail that Jesus of Nazareth taught a perverse doctrine, agreeing neither with Moses nor with the Prophets but diametrically opposed to them. They gravely accuse Jesus of wishing in every way to abolish the eternal Law of Moses by his own new one; that he publicly spoiled his own food (that is, in the mind of the Talmudists), that is, corrupted the doctrine and fell away into heresy and idolatry; and that he gave off a foul odour of himself, like food burnt too much. So they speak in the tractate Berachot, fol. 18, Venice edition: In our streets, may we not have a son or disciple who publicly burns his food, like the Nazarene; and in Sanhedrin, fol. 103: And a plague shall not come near your tabernacle; you shall have no son or disciple who spoils his boiled food or his food publicly, as Jesus the Nazarene did.

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: Vocant JEsum blasphemia vulgari Jeshu-Jpensum, quod tanquam blasphemus & seductor populi ob ignominiosa facinora & delicta in cruce fuerit suspensus, ita enim legimus in Tractatu Talmudico Sanhedrin cap. 6. sol. 43. Vespera Paschatis suspenderunt Iesum.
