They say that the King Messiah must judge the whole world in justice and equity, whereas the Nazarene had few followers, not from the leading men of the people but from the obscure common folk. They say that the Messiah ought to confirm the Mosaic Law, whereas the Nazarene taught things contrary to the Law, and therefore displeased the Jewish people; so speaks the Jew Isaac Orobio in his conference with Limborch, page 150: "I answer that it is not hard for us to know why the Fathers living at that time did not give faith to Christ and the Apostles. First, they did not believe because no sufficient foundation appeared to them for believing; for if they had found one, there would have been no reason for them to deny and reject him, and not only the learned and elders but also the people of Jerusalem would have admitted him. Second, because they did not see the earthly king who had been promised as such, and whom Israel, taught by the same God over so many ages, had been expecting." The doctrine displeased them more, as contrary to the divine Law, which it preached to be for the most part vain and useless, and no longer pleasing to God. They did not recognise him as the Messiah, because he taught that he was equal to God, indeed God himself, whom they had previously believed to be incorporeal, immortal and impassible; nor did they think there was any way by which God, through his omnipotence, could make himself in the opposite manner, just as we now think it impossible that God should become bread, or bread become God, either by transmutation or by the assumption of nature. Such was the teaching in which the Jews had been instructed by God; but afterwards a corporeal, passible and mortal being was proposed for adoration, the hypostatic union of the two natures not yet having been devised, nor ever announced by Christ or by the Apostles. And although it had been announced beforehand, it would by no means have been admitted by the Jews, as impossible and contrary to their divine dogma.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Hinc nos vocant blasphemos, qui purum putumque hominem, unum cum Patre esse credimus, ajuntque Judæi nos nullis demonstrare posse argumentis in Messia duplicem esse naturam, divinam unam, alteram humanam, cum si verum hoc esset, scriptura illud innumeris in locis debuisset testari, quod quia non fecerit, rem se aliter habere, sic enim cavillatur Judæus apud Doctissimum Coccejum, considerantem Responsionem Judaicam ad Quæstionem quartam de duplici natura in Christo: Quibus argumentis demonstratur Messiam purum hominem esse debere & non simul Deum ac hominem? ad primam quæstionem jam diximus juxta dialecticorum canones eum qui nova quædam introducit dogmata teneri rationem istorum reddere, non ab aliis ut ea refellat exigere. Idem ei qui hæc interrogat faciendum incumbit, ut qui nobis proponit doctrinam scripturæ sacræ non comprehensam ac rationi ipsi adversam. Nam rationem poscere cur Messias non possit simul esse Deus & homo, perinde est quasi interrogeres, cur non Centaurus, hoc est, ex dimidio homo ex dimidio equus, aut vir pariter & fœmina esse possit. Verum nos facilius rationibus adductis refellemus id quod quaeritur, quam ut quis hujusmodi commenta demonstrare valeat. Primum Propheta Ezechiel ait: Ezech.37: 24, 27. Eruntque mihi in populum, & ego ero illis in Deum, & servus meus David Rex eorum. Hic statim apparet differentia inter Deum & servum ipsius Davidem. Nam unus Deus erit, alter Rex populi: non vero dicitur Davidem fore Deum. Secundo Esaias de Messia sic loquitur: Esa.11: 2. adfuturum eit timorem Domini. In prima quaestione simplicem Dei unitatem adstruximus; at si Messias Deus simul ac homo existeret, jam necesse esset eundem Deum illum unum esse, nec tum convenienter de eo diceretur quod se-metipsum timeret. Atq; haec pro responso ad praesentem quaestionem sufficiant: praeterquam quod hinc solide demonstretur. Si talis nobis exspectandus fuisset Messias, sacram scripturam innumeris locis hoc debuisse testari ac docere.
units.tr: Hence they call us blasphemers, we who believe that a plain and simple man is one with the Father. The Jews also say that we cannot demonstrate by any arguments that the Messiah has a twofold nature, one divine and the other human; for if this were true, Scripture should have attested it in countless places. Since it does not, the matter must stand otherwise. So the Jew cavils, as reported by the most learned Coccejus, who considers the Jewish Response to the Fourth Question on the twofold nature in Christ: By what arguments is it demonstrated that the Messiah must be a mere man and not at once God and man? To the first question we have already said that, according to the canons of the dialecticians, one who introduces some new doctrines is bound to give an account of them, and cannot demand that others refute them. The same duty lies on the one who asks these questions, since it is he who puts forward a doctrine not contained in holy Scripture and contrary to reason itself. For to ask for a reason why the Messiah cannot be at once God and man is just as if you asked why a Centaur, that is, a creature half man and half horse, or a man and woman together, cannot exist. Yet we would more easily refute by the arguments adduced what is asked than anyone could prove such inventions. First, the Prophet Ezekiel says: Ezek. 37:24, 27. They shall be my people, and I will be their God, and my servant David shall be their King. Here the difference between God and David, the servant of God, appears at once. For there will be one God, and the other will be King of the people; it is not said that David will be God. Secondly, Isaiah speaks of the Messiah thus: Isa. 11:2. The fear of the Lord shall rest upon him. In the first question we asserted the simple unity of God; but if the Messiah were at once God and man, it would then be necessary for that same one God to be him, and it would not be fitting to say of him that he feared himself. Let these things suffice as the answer to the present question, besides which it is solidly demonstrated from this that, if such a Messiah had been awaited by us, Holy Scripture ought to have attested and taught this in countless places.

units.la: Quod quia non facit, sequitur rem aliter se habere.
units.tr: Since it does not do so, it follows that the matter stands otherwise.

units.la: CAPUT XIII. De Justificatione & Conversione Hominis Peccatoris ex Operibus propriis, aliisq; mediis.
units.tr: CAPUT XIII. Concerning the Justification and Conversion of the Sinful Man from His Own Works, and Other Means.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Sic repudiata rupe salutis unica, susque deque Messiæ habita redemptione spirituali, necesse fuit alios animarum quærere duces, aliosque Justificationis suæ apud Deum excogitare modos, quare toti hactenus in eo fuerunt, hocque onus, hicq; labor Judæis unicus fuit, ut per opera sua, Legisve Mosaicæ observantiam, tum à perpetratis absolverentur peccatis, Deoque reconciliarentur, tum perfectam seculi futuri adipiscerentur beatitudinem, & hinc inani externorum privilegiorum opinione, ceremoniarumque nocivaInfatuati pompa, suam Conversionem, Justificationemq; coram Deo benedicto, non doloribus & operibus Messiæ,sed externis suis operibus, meritis propriis, confessionibus, perpessionibus, aliisque humanis mediis tribuerunt, uti clare patet & ex scriptis Judæorum passim obviis, & ex unanimi Magistrorum, vulgique contestatione; Interrogati quippe de Justificationis apud Deum mediis & modis,respondebunt semper, se justificari non Messiæ merito,cum nondum venerit,sed operibus bonis ad Legem Mosaicam formatis, maxime pœnitentia,afflictionibus,calamitatibus,jejuniis, precibus, eleemosyna, ipsa denique morte, quæ malorum sit ultimum; Quin etiam non raro ad Dei solius, non Messiæ, confugiunt misericordiam, eamque salutis apprehenduntanchoram, clamantes: Domine, Deus misericors, benigne, longanime, & gratia abundantissime, concede libens, volens, ut vincant miserationes tuæ iram tuam adversus liberos tuos, eripe populum tuum ab omni malo, quod est in mundo, remitte nobis omnem pravitatem operum nostrorum, sufficiat nobis noster contemptus & captivitas, in qua ob peccata nostra per quatuor mundi plagas sumus dispersi, & quod domus magna & sancta ob peccata nostra est destructa, quodque civitas sanctitatis tuæ devastata jacet propter peccata nostra.
units.tr: Thus, with the one rock of salvation rejected and the spiritual redemption through the Messiah held in light regard, it was necessary for them to seek other leaders of souls and to devise other ways of obtaining their justification before God. For this reason they have, until now, all been intent on this, and this burden and labour has been theirs alone: that by their own works, and by observance of the Mosaic Law, they might be absolved both from the sins they had committed and be reconciled to God, and that they might obtain the perfect blessedness of the age to come. From this vain opinion of external privileges, and from the pomp of ceremonies that harms them, they have ascribed their conversion and justification before the blessed God not to the sufferings and works of the Messiah, but to their own external works, their own merits, confessions, sufferings, and other human means. This is plain both from the Jewish writings that are everywhere to be found and from the unanimous testimony of their teachers and their common people. For when they are asked about the means and methods of justification before God, they will always answer that they are justified not by the merit of the Messiah, since he has not yet come, but by good works formed according to the Mosaic Law, above all repentance, afflictions, calamities, fasts, prayers, alms, and finally death itself, which is the last of evils. Indeed, not infrequently they flee to the mercy of God alone, not of the Messiah, and seize it as the anchor of salvation, crying out: "Lord, merciful, kind, long-suffering, and most abundant in grace, grant freely and willingly that your mercies may overcome your anger against your children. Deliver your people from every evil that is in the world. Forgive us all the perversity of our works. Let our contempt and captivity suffice us, in which, on account of our sins, we have been scattered to the four quarters of the world, and let the great and holy house, destroyed on account of our sins, suffice us, and the city of your holiness, which lies laid waste on account of our sins."

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Credunt ergo firmiter Judæi nostri, hominem coram Deo justificari, non per Messiæ redemptionem, sed ex Legis Mosaicæ operibus, ipsaque divina misericordia, ita loquuntur in Catechesi Judaica, Responsione ad Quæstionem undecimam: Non dubium est, quin tam ante quam post adventum redemptoris, homo probus, legisq; & præceptorum sedulus observator perfectionem & beatitudinem animæ suæ comparare queat; Et ad Quæstionem: Quid autem nobis faciendum incumbit, ut istarum rerum fiamus compotes? Responsione decima quinta: Idquod servus Domino & filius Patri præstant. Hi enim, si quicquam à Domino suis sibi expectant, in id primum incumbunt, ut ad placitum eorum res actiones suas componant, deinde preces & sollicitationes admovent. Ita nostrarum quoque partium est, indies ea quæ voluntati divinæ congruant, exequi, quo spectant præcepta, & opera bona, legi Mosis tam scripta, quam tradita conformia. Quibus si addamus supplicationes & preces, dubitandum non est, quin votis nostris ipse benignus affluat. His succedit fiducia, quæ nos instar firmi fundamenti cujusdam, Deo simul aspirante, sustinens, animam corpusq; reficit, & insigne in iis, quæ vel legem, vel res seculi concernunt, adjumentum præbet. Qui enim in Jehova spherat, illum misericordia circum-dabit. dabit undiquaq;, nec declinabunt crura ejus, prout illis, qui rebus aliis confidunt, evenit. De quo ita decinit unctus Dei Jacob: Spera in Jehova, & fac bonum: inhabita terram, & pasce veritatem, & dele- ita te in Jehova, & dabit tibi petitiones cordis tui. Volve super Jehovam viam tuam, & spera in eo, & ipse faciet; Ita quoque nuper Judaeus Ifacus Orobius in Collatione cum L mborchio, p. 57. Siquidem in omnibus afflictionibus a Prophetis admonebatur (Israel) quod legem divinam servaret, quod erat unicum medium, quo in Dei gratiam restitueretur; nunquam vero dixere, quod in futurum Messiam ipsem haberet, sed in Deum, ut ab inimicis liberaretur, & in sui gratiam restitueretur; Et pag.70. In hoc secundo sensu nullo Messia, nulla redemptione indiget, nec aliquando opus habuit ad salutem aeternam consequendam: sufficit quidem lex divina quam ut unicum medium ad salutem Dominus Israeli praecepit. Et post aliqua interjecta pergit Judaeus Orobius: At Israelis individua nullam aliam gloriam sibi propositae praeter Deum ipsum, cui si Israel legem observans placuerit, credit & sperat infallibiliter eo in aeternum fruitu-rum: Sed ubi, & quomodo, nec scit, nec scire usquam affectavit, neque pro hoc divino, & summo bono consequendo, Messia, aut alterius redemptionis, interventionem admittunt Judaei, aut necessariam esse credidinunt, sola divina misericordia, & lege contenti.
units.tr: Our Jews therefore firmly believe that a man is justified before God not through the redemption of the Messiah but by the works of the Mosaic Law and by the divine mercy itself. They speak thus in the Jewish Catechism, in the answer to the eleventh question: There is no doubt that a upright man, and one who diligently observes the law and precepts, can procure the perfection and blessedness of his soul, both before and after the coming of the Redeemer. And to the question: What then must we do, so that we may become partakers of these things? the fifteenth answer runs: What a servant renders to his Lord and a son to his Father. For if they expect anything from their Lord, they first apply themselves to arranging their affairs and actions according to his pleasure, and then they add prayers and entreaties. So it is also our part to carry out daily those things that agree with the divine will, by which the precepts and good works conformable to the Law of Moses, both written and handed down, are fulfilled. To these, if we add supplications and prayers, there is no doubt that the kind God himself will flow abundantly to our wishes. To these is joined confidence, which, like a firm foundation, sustains us, with God breathing upon us at the same time, refreshes soul and body, and gives remarkable help in those matters that concern either the Law or the affairs of the age. For he who hopes in Jehovah, mercy shall surround him on every side, and his legs shall not stumble, as happens to those who trust in other things. Concerning this the anointed of God, Jacob, thus spoke: "Hope in Jehovah and do good; dwell in the land and feed on truth; delight yourself in Jehovah, and he will give you the petitions of your heart. Commit your way to Jehovah, and hope in him, and he will act." Likewise the Jew Isaac Orobio recently wrote in his Conference with Limborch, p. 57: For in all afflictions Israel was admonished by the Prophets that it should keep the divine law, which was the only means by which it could be restored to the grace of God. But they never said that it would have the Messiah in the future, but that it should look to God, so that it might be freed from its enemies and restored to his favour. And on p. 70: In this second sense, it has no need of any Messiah or any redemption, nor ever had need of one to obtain eternal salvation. The divine law, which the Lord commanded Israel as the only means to salvation, is indeed sufficient. And after some intervening matter, the Jew Orobio goes on: But the individual Israelite proposes to himself no other glory than God himself, and if Israel, observing the law, pleases him, he believes and hopes that he will enjoy him infallibly for ever. But where and how this will be, he neither knows nor has ever sought to know. Nor do the Jews admit the intervention of the Messiah or of any other redemption for obtaining this divine and supreme good, nor do they believe it to be necessary, being content with the divine mercy and the law alone.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Constituunt, quotquot vivunt Judæi; homi-nis justitiam, peccatorumque remissio-nem, non in Meffiæ Justitia, sed in propria,in factis,operibusque humanis,tum malis omit-tendis, tum bonis faciendis, longe aberrantes à Jehova Justitia nostra, à sole Justitiæ, à fervo justo, qui justificat multos, non induti pallio justitiæ, uti liquet ex Judæo Anonymo, interro-gante Quæst. 7. apud Coccejum in Confi-derat. Refponf. Judaic. Quomodo Judæi hoc tem-pore remissionem peccatorum consequuntur, fine qua salvi esse non possunt? modi quibus remissio pec-catorum obtinetur, sunt isti, quos Lex & Prophetæ multis in locis nobis indicant, quorum duos fpecia-tim proponemus. Primum dicit Efaias. Impro-bus viam suam deferet & vir injustitiarum cogita-tiones suas, & convertent fe ad Dominum, & Deus noster miserebitur ejus & peccata remittet illi. Si-militer Propheta Ezechiel cap. 18. verf. 20. Si con-vertit fe homo malus ab omnibus peccatis quæ fecit, & fervat omnia mea præcepta faciens judicium ac justitiam, vivendo vivet & non morietur. Omnium malitiarum ejus quæ fecit non recordabor: in justitia quam fecit vivet. An voluntas mea est mors impiorum dicit Dominus, ac non potius ut convertatur à viis suis & vivat? atqui hæc propitiatio multo erit facilior, addita vi & peculiari privilegio quod Deus Deus concessit diei expiationis, quemadmodum ait in Levitico cap. 16. vers. 29. 30. Et hoc erit vobis in sempiternum: septimo mense decima die mensis affligetis animas vestras, nec opus ullum facietis sive indigena sive advena qui peregrinatur inter vos. Hoc die expiatio & purificatio vestri erit, ab omnibus peccatis vestris coram Domino purificabimini. Et quamvis jam nulla sint sacrificia, quæ mediante rant ad tanto facilius impetrandam remissionem peccatorum, eadem tamen per pœnitentiam ac resipiscentiam declinando a vitiis malis impetratur: juxta dictum Psalmista: Ps. 50. Contritus Spiritus Deo est Sacrificium: ac confractum & humiliatum animum tu o Deus non despicies: Idque ideo quia hodie victimas offerre non possumus destituti medijs ad hoc necessarijs, quæ quando obtinebimus, tum remissio illa tanto facilior reddetur.
units.tr: All Jews who are alive hold that a person's justice and the forgiveness of his sins are found not in the justice of the Messiah but in his own deeds and works, both in refraining from evil and in doing good. In this they stray far from Jehovah our Justice, the Sun of Justice, the righteous Servant who justifies many, and do not put on the garment of righteousness. This is clear from the anonymous Jew who asks question 7 in Cocceius, in his Considerations on Jewish Answers: How do the Jews at this time obtain the forgiveness of sins, without which they cannot be saved? The ways by which the forgiveness of sins is obtained are those which the Law and the Prophets indicate to us in many places; we will set out two of them in particular. First, Isaiah says: "Let the wicked forsake his way, and the man of iniquities his thoughts, and let them return to the Lord, and our God will have mercy on him and will pardon him." Likewise the prophet Ezekiel, chapter 18, verse 20: "If a wicked man turns from all the sins that he has committed, and keeps all my precepts, doing judgment and justice, he shall live by living and shall not die. I will not remember any of the wickednesses that he has done; he shall live in the justice that he has done. Is my will the death of the wicked, says the Lord, and not rather that he turn from his ways and live? Yet this atonement will be much easier, with the added force and the peculiar privilege which God granted to the Day of Atonement, as he says in Leviticus, chapter 16, verses 29 and 30: "And this shall be for you a statute forever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and do no work, whether native or stranger who sojourns among you. On this day shall your atonement be made, and you shall be purified from all your sins before the Lord." And although there are now no sacrifices, which were offered through the priests to obtain the forgiveness of sins more easily, the same forgiveness is nonetheless obtained through repentance and conversion, by turning away from evil vices, according to the saying of the Psalmist: "A contrite spirit is a sacrifice to God; a broken and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise" (Ps. 50). And this is so because today we cannot offer victims, being deprived of the means necessary for this; when we shall obtain them, that forgiveness will then be made much easier.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Extollunt quam maxime bona sua Opera, clamantes hominem perpetua frui ac gaudere beatitudine virtute, meritoque suorum operum; Esse illa ex se meritoria futuræ gloriosæ vitæ, Hinc variis laudibus opera deprædicant bona, ad cœlumque evehunt; Hinc mirum in modum pietatis, bonorumque operum urgent studium, incitantque vehementer non suæ Religionis solum homines, sed quandoque nostros, ipsasque gentes, sponspondentes,quod si bonum opus fecerint in-primis Judæis, mercedem pariter accepturi sint, vel temporalem, vel partem aliquam in Resurrectione mortuorum, quod Deus ex veterum Magistrorum sententia nullam creaturam sua fraudet mercede; Hinc egregiis passim inculcant monitis hospitalitatem, humilitatem, liberalitatem, parentum honorem, manuetudinem, patientiam, misericordiam, concordiam, dehortantes suos a vitiis, furto, superbia, odio, mendacio, libidine, ira, invidia, ingratitudine, ebrietate, calumnia, adulterio, avaritia, hypocrisi, adulatione, aliisque innumeris; Et de his bonis operibus, decantatis illis salutis, vitæque æternæ mediis, adminiculisque, non solum ora abundant Judaica, libriqué morales sunt pleni, verum ipsi fidei articuli his exornati, inter quos numero undecimus sic se habet: Fundamentum undecimum, quod Deus nemini præmium sit denegaturus, sed retributurus mercedem iis, qui præcepta servant, & delinquentes multaturus pœna; Sic quoque Rabbi Josephus Albo, Fundamentorum lib. 4. Etenim fides qua quis credit mercedem, necessaria est cuivis credenti in legem divinam, adeo, ut qui eam negaverit, fundamentum negaverit.
units.tr: They extol their good works as far as possible, crying out that man enjoys and rejoices in perpetual blessedness by the virtue and merit of his own works; that these works are in themselves meritorious of a future glorious life. Hence they proclaim good works with various praises and exalt them to heaven. Hence they press most strenuously the zeal for piety and good works, and vehemently urge not only men of their own religion but sometimes ours too, and even the nations, promising that if they do a good work, above all Jews, they will likewise receive a reward, either temporal or some part in the resurrection of the dead, since God, according to the opinion of the ancient masters, will defraud no creature of its reward. Hence everywhere they inculcate with excellent admonitions hospitality, humility, liberality, honour of parents, gentleness, patience, mercy, and concord, dissuading their own people from vices: theft, pride, hatred, lying, lust, anger, envy, ingratitude, drunkenness, calumny, adultery, avarice, hypocrisy, flattery, and countless others. And not only do Jewish mouths overflow with these good works, sung up as the means and aids of salvation and eternal life, and not only are their moral books full of them, but the very articles of their faith are adorned with them; among these the eleventh article reads thus: The eleventh foundation: that God will deny the reward to no one, but will repay wages to those who keep the precepts, and will punish with penalty those who transgress. Likewise Rabbi Joseph Albo, in the fourth book of the Fundamentals: For the faith by which a man believes in reward is necessary for everyone who believes in the divine law, so that whoever denies it has denied the foundation. ## V.

units.la: V.

Commendant cum operibus Fidem, per quam in futuro vivant seculo, docentes fidem donum esse Dei, quod mentibus superne sit inditum, uti legimus in Catechesi Judaica, Responsione ad Quæstionem tertiam: Iustus in fide sua & fiducia in Deum, atq; subeundo jugum legis ejus, quod imposuit Moses filius Israel, vivet in isto seculo, futuro scilicet; Et ad Quæstionem: Quænam autem est illa fides, cujus principium & fundamentum exposuisti? Responsio sexta: Fides illa est donum, quod Deus mentibus nostris indidit, quo mediante credimus omnia illa, quæ nobis per Prophetas servos suos dixit; Sed licet fidem subinde commendent valde, non explicant interim, quomodo donum illud Dei consistere possit cum viribus arbitrii humani, quas nimis quam par est amplificant, ex earundem bono usu salutem sibi fabricantes propriam, nec fidem intelligunt salvificam, quæ in Mesfiam sit directa, negantes eam in sacris commendari literis, verum vel de notitia, vel de fiducia in Deum Creatorem, quod evincitur ex Catechesi rursus Judaica, ad Quæstionem quartam: Quodnam est igitur fundamentum fidei & legis? Responsione: Quod Deus Benedictus, qui est Ens supremum, creaverit ex nihilo mundum, eumque pro voluntate sua fecerit, neq; ullus impedire possit, quin illum iterum sive totum sive per partes immutet; Vel de fide & integritegritate intelligunt, quæ in commerciis, contractibusque sancta sit servanda, ut adeo sana pauca de fide à gente exspectanda sint Judaica; Explodunt interim omnem fidem carbonariam, asserentes cognitionem necessarium esse fidei requisitum, cum sine cognitione nihil credi possit, nemoque rei ignotæ posse assentiri, teste Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Sepher Emunah, libro fidei, sol. 4. col. 3. Fides est, cum cor qualitatem rei alicujus cognitæ apprehendit, quam cognitionem excipit intellectus, eamque bene comprehensam cordi studiose imprimit, ut sic homo rem objectam credat, sibique in usum commodum reservet, ut dicitur Proverb. cap. 10. verf. 14. Sapientes recondunt scientiam. Et post quædam: Fides vera in eo consistit, ut quis cognoscat rem qualis sit, quod multum multum, parum parum, album album, nigrum nigrum, existens existens. Et Rabbi Maimonide in More Nevochim, Part. 1. c. 50. Scias Lector candide, quod fides non sit id, quod ore profertur, sed res concepta & figurata in anima: quando nempe credimus, rem ita se habere, prout illam in animo conceptam habemus. Quando ergo de dogmatibus Religionis, vel aliis, quæ pro veris & indubitatis habes, ore tantum differs, sine vera illorum intelligentia & fide, vel examinatione, nimis hoc est exiguum, neque sufficit. Ita enim reperimus, multos homines stolidos & inceptos quædam observare & credere, quorum rationem nullam in animo suo tenent; Et post pauca interjecta pergit Maimonides: Et non est fides, nisi post formalem rei conceptionem: fides etenim est de eo, quod in animo formatum & conceptum habemus credere, quod ita se habeat extra intellectum, prout formatum est in intellectu. Quod si jam cum ista fide conjuncta sit certa fiducia ac persuasio, rem illam aliter se habere non posse, nec vel minimum ei adhaereat, quod illam expellere vel labefactare queat, tum demum vera est fides.
units.tr: They commend faith together with works, by which they live in the future age, teaching that faith is a gift of God, which is implanted in minds from above, as we read in the Jewish Catechism, in the answer to the third question: The righteous man, in his faith and trust in God, and in undertaking the yoke of His law, which Moses son of Israel imposed, shall live in this age, that is, the future one. And to the question: But what is that faith, the beginning and foundation of which you have set out? The sixth answer: That faith is a gift which God has placed in our minds, through which we believe all those things which He, through His servants the Prophets, has spoken to us. But although they commend faith very highly at times, they do not in the meantime explain how that gift of God can consist with the powers of human free choice, which they amplify more than is fitting, fabricating for themselves their own salvation by the good use of these powers; nor do they understand saving faith, which is directed toward the Messiah, denying that it is commended in the sacred letters. Rather they understand it either of knowledge or of trust in God the Creator, as is shown again from the Jewish Catechism, to the fourth question: What, then, is the foundation of faith and of the Law? Answer: That the Blessed God, who is the supreme Being, created the world out of nothing, and made it according to His will, and that no one can prevent Him from changing it again, whether wholly or in parts. Or they understand it of faith and integrity, which is to be kept holy in business and contracts, so that indeed few sound things about faith are to be expected from the Jewish nation. Meanwhile they reject every blind faith, asserting that knowledge is a necessary requisite of faith, since nothing can be believed without knowledge, and no one can assent to a thing unknown; so Rabbi Saadia Gaon in the Sepher Emunah, the book of faith, page 4, column 3: Faith is when the heart apprehends the quality of some known thing, which knowledge the intellect receives, and, having comprehended it well, impresses it diligently on the heart, so that a man believes the object and reserves it for his own useful purpose, as it is said in Proverbs, chapter 10, verse 14: The wise lay up knowledge. And after some things: True faith consists in this, that a man knows a thing as it is: that much is much, little is little, white is white, black is black, what exists exists. And Rabbi Maimonides in the More Nevochim, part 1, chapter 50: Know, kind reader, that faith is not what is uttered by the mouth, but a thing conceived and formed in the soul: namely, when we believe that a thing is as we have it conceived in our mind. Therefore, when you differ only in word about the dogmas of religion, or about other things which you hold to be true and undoubted, without true understanding and faith in them, or examination, this is too little and is not sufficient. For we find many foolish and ignorant men who observe certain things and believe them, and hold no reason for them in their mind. And after a few intervening words Maimonides continues: And there is no faith unless after the formal conception of the thing: for faith is about what we have formed and conceived in the mind, to believe that it is so outside the intellect as it is formed in the intellect. If then this faith is joined with certain confidence and persuasion that the thing cannot be otherwise, and nothing adheres to it which could expel or weaken it, then at last faith is true.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Suadent, persuadentque frequentes distribuendas Eleemosynas, tum Gentibus, tum maxime popularibus, fronte hilari, ex Vajikra Rabba, Sect. 34. sol. 204. Quando facturus est homo eleemosynam, faciat eam corde hilari; Non tantum in publico, verum quoque in occulto ex Tract. Talmudico, Bava Bafra, cap. 1. Major est eleemosynam dant in occulto, Mose Doctore nostro; Appellantes Eleemosynam צדקה justitiam, quod per hanc in conspectu Dei justificentur; Deprædicantesque miras eleemosynarum virtutes, quod harum vi, efficaciaque homines ab æterno liberentur exitio, ex Tract. Talm. Gittin, sol. 7. Quicunque demit aliquid de facultatibus suis, & eleemosynas ex illis facit, liberatur a iudicio Gehennæ; Quod Eleemosynarum ope mortui suscitentur, ex Pirke Rabbi Elie-feris,cap.33. Rabbi Simeon inquit: Efficacia eleemosyna mortui suscitabuntur; Quod appropinquare faciant redemptionem, inque pari cum Lege sint gradu, ex Tract. Talm. Hierosol. Peah,cap.1. Eleemosyna & beneficentia exaequant totam legem; Quod virtute eleemosynae Spiritus Sanctus cum aliquo habitet, ex Pirke Rabbi Elieseris,cap.33. Rabbi Azaria dicit: Ut animadvertas vim eleemosynae, veni & vide de Sallom filio Tikva, qui erat ex magnatibus ipsius aetatis, & quotidie eleemosynas erogabat. Quid fecit? Implevit hydriam aqua, & consedit ad portam urbis, atque cuilibet venienti ex itinere potum praebuit, & reduxit animum illius ad ipsum. Ob meritum autem eleemosynae hujus habitavit Spiritus Sanctus cum uxore ejus; Quod hominem custodiat a periculis, ex Tract. Talm. Hierof. Peah, cap. 1. Si dederis e marsupio tuo eleemosynam, Deus custodiet te a lasionibus, a damnis, a tributis, & vestigalibus; Quod Deus eleemosynarum datorem abunde remuneret, ex Vajikra Rabba, Sect. 34. sol. 204. Quicunque obolum unum dat pauperi, et Deus reddit obolos multos; Nec privatas solum suadent Eleemosynas, verum publicas quoque, in Synagogis, Scholisque collectas, in Synagogae usum, captivorum liberationem, pauperum sustentationem, filiarum egeneram. narum elocationem, fratrumque Hierosolymitanorum ac Palæstinorum solamen, subsidiumque, ut pro salute dispersorum orent, mittendas quoque Traphat, Tiberiadem, Hebronem, ad sepulchra Patriarcharum, Abrahami, Ifaci, Jacobi; ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi, in libello de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum, Part. I. c.14. Undiq; Judæi Hierosolymam versus Eleemosynas mittunt, ad succurrendum inopiæ istorum, qui illic versantur, precesque fundunt pro salute omnium, quin & alia Palæstinæ loca, verbi gratia, Joppen, Tiberiada & Hebronem, ubi Patriarchæ, Abrahamus, Ifacus & Jacobus, una cum uxoribus suis, sepulti jacent, beneficiis suis beare, & invisere solent; Hinc quoque in Festo Purim Eleemosynas mittunt Judæis pauperioribus, quo & ipsi pro sua conditione festum celebrare digne possint.
units.tr: They urge and persuade the frequent distribution of alms, both to Gentiles and especially to their own people, with a cheerful face, from Vayikra Rabba, section 34, p. 204: When a man is about to give alms, let him give it with a cheerful heart. Not only in public but also in secret, from the Talmudic tractate Bava Bathra, chapter 1: Greater is he who gives alms in secret, according to our teacher Moses. They call alms צדקה [tsedaqah], that is, justice, because by it people are justified in the sight of God. They proclaim the wonderful virtues of alms, that by their power and efficacy people are freed from eternal destruction, from the Talmudic tractate Gittin, p. 7: Whoever takes something from his wealth and makes alms from it is freed from the judgment of Gehenna. That by the help of alms the dead are raised, from Pirke Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 33: Rabbi Simeon says: By the efficacy of alms the dead will be raised. That they bring near the redemption and stand on a level with the Law, from the Talmudic tractate of Jerusalem, Peah, chapter 1: Alms and beneficence equal the whole Law. That by the virtue of alms the Holy Spirit dwells with someone, from Pirke Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 33: Rabbi Azariah says: That you may perceive the power of alms, come and see Sallom the son of Tikva, who was among the great men of his age and gave alms every day. What did he do? He filled a water jar and sat down at the city gate, and offered a drink to each person who came in from the road, and so brought back their soul to them. And on account of the merit of this alms the Holy Spirit dwelt with his wife. That it guards a man from dangers, from the Talmudic tractate of Jerusalem, Peah, chapter 1: If you give alms from your purse, God will keep you from injuries, from losses, from tributes and taxes. That God richly rewards the giver of alms, from Vayikra Rabba, section 34, p. 204: Whoever gives one obol to the poor, God gives back many obols. Nor do they urge only private alms, but also public collections in the synagogues and schools, for the use of the synagogue, the ransoming of captives, the support of the poor, the marriage of poor daughters, and the relief and help of the brethren in Jerusalem and Palestine, and that they should send to Tiberias, Hebron and Tiberias, to the tombs of the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, from Rabbi Leo of Modena, in his little book on the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part I, chapter 14: From everywhere the Jews send alms towards Jerusalem, to relieve the want of those who dwell there, and pour out prayers for the welfare of all; and they are wont to bless and visit other places of Palestine, for example Joppa, Tiberias and Hebron, where the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob lie buried with their wives. Hence also at the feast of Purim they send alms to the poorer Jews, so that they too may be able to celebrate the feast worthily according to their condition.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Collaudant, commendantque pari pietatis affectu ʼʼʼɥ Jejunia, abstinentes quam rigide non a certis, sed omnibus cibis, celebrantes tum percelebre illud Jejunium, in Festo Expiationis, decimo die Tisri, seu Septembris, Levit. cap. 23. verf. 32. tum quatuor illa vetera maxime solennia, publica, ordinaria, ʼʼʼɥ Jejunia Ecclesiæ, Zachar. cap. 8. verf. 19. Jejunium scilicet Decembris, die decimo, quod isto die
units.tr: With the same feeling of piety they commend and praise fasts [תַּעֲנִית], abstaining as strictly not from certain foods but from all foods. They celebrate especially that most famous fast on the Feast of Atonement, the tenth day of Tishri, or September, Leviticus chapter 23, verse 32; and also those four ancient and most solemn fasts, public and ordinary, fasts of the Church, Zechariah chapter 8, verse 19: namely the fast of the tenth day of December, when King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it most closely;

units.la: Rex Babyloniæ Nebucadnezar Hierosolymam accesserit, arctissimaque cinxerit obsidione; Jejunium Junii mensis, decimo septimo die, quod hoc die legis tabulæ confractæ, sacrificium juge sub priori templo abrogatum, liberque legis fuerit crematus; Jejunium Julii, seu mensis Abh, nono die, quod eo die utrumque templum, tam prius, quam posterius fuerit desolatum, urbs munitissima Bether, sedes Pseudo Messiæ Bar Cochab fuerit expugnata, fundamentum templi aratro per Rufum belli ducem fuerit proscissum, decretumque divinum in deserto contra Israelitas emanaverit, quod terram sanctam non essent ingressuri; Jejunium Septembris, tertio die, quod isto die in primo excidio Hierosolymorum per Nebucadnezarem, occisus fuerit Gedaljas; Tum extraordinaria, publica tamen, propter ingruentes calamitates, propter gladium & afflictionem hostium Israelem arctantium, pestem, bestiam malam, locustam & bruchum propter adustionem legetum, propter morbos, propter annonæ caritatem, pluviam, aliaque, teste Rabbi Maimonide Tractatu de Jejuniis, c. 2. Tum privata יום צום Jejunia unici appellata, singulis diebus Lunæ & Jovis, pridie omnium Noviluniorum, vel quoties infausti aliquid somniarunt, vel ob diem emortualem patris, vel aliam ob causam, prout majorem pietatis speciem affectant, recitantes sequentem precatiunculam: Mi Deus, quo tempore stabat sanctuarium, si quis peccatum committebat, offerebat coram te oblationem, & expiabatur. Nunc quando propter peccata nostra sanctuarium est eversum, nil habemus praeter jejunia & preces nostras. Placeat itaque tibi Domine Deus mi, & Deus Patrum nostrorum, ut pinguedo, & langues ille meus, qui hoc meo jejunio diminuitur, perinde coram te sit, ac si oblationem obtulissem, & gratiosus mihi esto. Hinc varia jejuniorum praescribunt praecepta, jejunimque perfecte observantem ʾnn sanctum appellant, volentem vero & non servantem ʾmn peccatorem; Negantes interim in Colbo sol.68.col.4. Et apud Maimonidem, Tract. de Jejuniis, cap.5. Jejunia ad finem mundi duratura, sed tempore Messiae cessatura, quod tunc omnes dies futuri sint boni, dies convivorum, gaudiique, sicut legitur apud Zachar. cap.13.vers.19.
units.tr: the fast of the month of June, on the seventeenth day, because on this day the tablets of the law were broken, the continual sacrifice was abolished in the former temple, and the scroll of the law was burned; the fast of July, or the month of Av, on the ninth day, because on that day both temples, the former as well as the latter, were laid waste, the most fortified city of Bethar, the seat of the false Messiah Bar Kokhba, was taken, the foundation of the temple was ploughed up by the plough by Rufus the commander of the war, and the divine decree was issued in the wilderness against the Israelites, that they should not enter the holy land; the fast of September, on the third day, because on that day Gedaliah was killed in the first destruction of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar. Then the extraordinary, public fasts, on account of impending calamities, on account of the sword and the affliction of enemies pressing upon Israel, plague, evil beast, locust and caterpillar, the burning of crops, diseases, dearth of grain, drought, and other causes, as Rabbi Maimonides testifies in his Treatise on Fasts, chapter 2. Then the private fasts, called יום צום [yom tsom] single fasts, on each Monday and Thursday, on the day before all new moons, or whenever they have dreamed something unlucky, or on the anniversary of a father's death, or for some other reason, as they aim at a greater show of piety, reciting the following short prayer: My God, at the time when the sanctuary stood, if anyone committed sin, he offered an oblation before you and was atoned. Now, since our sanctuary has been overthrown on account of our sins, we have nothing but our fasts and our prayers. May it therefore please you, Lord my God and God of our fathers, that the fat and the blood of mine, which is diminished by my fasting, be as if I had offered an oblation before you, and be gracious to me. Hence they prescribe various rules for fasting, and they call one who observes the fast perfectly holy [חָסִיד, chasid], but one who wishes to fast and does not keep it a sinner [חוטא]. Meanwhile they deny, in the Kol Bo, p. 68, col. 4, and in Maimonides, Treatise on Fasts, chapter 5, that the fasts will last until the end of the world, but will cease in the time of the Messiah, because then all days will be good, days of feasting and joy, as is read in Zechariah chapter 13, verse 19.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Collaudant, inculcantque inter opera Preces, in Minhagim five ritualibus obvias, matutinas, vespertinas, nocturnasque, tum publicas in Synagogis, tum privatas, in se, cellu privato, maxime usitatam formulam Audi Israel, ceu Symboli Judaici compendium, dium, non omittentes Amen in fine precū, cui multum tribuunt, quod majorille sit qui dicit Amen, quam qui benedictionem recitat; Per- agunt vero preces more antiquo stantes, capite tecto incurvatoque, oculis depressis, cingulo cincti, facie loti, totoque ad devotionem compósito corpore, ex Tractat. Talmud Jevamot, sol. 19. col. 2. Qui orat, demittere debet faciem suam deorsum, & corsuum elevare sursum; Et ex Tractat. Talmud. Berachot. cap 5. Non stant ad precandum, nisi cum gravitate capitis, hoc est, capite demisso; Requiruntex precantibus intentionem cordis, quod precario sine intentione, sit sicut corpus sine anima, ex Rabbi Aben Esra in Psalm. 78. Praecipuum in precatione est intentio cordis; Commendant preces frequentes, benedictionesque, quas non ad octodecim solum singulis diebus restringunt, sed ad מאה ברכות ad centum preces, benedictionesque extendunt, referentes, quod quicunque multiplicet orationem suam, exaudiatur a Deo Benedicto; Commendant quoque precum virtutes, ex Rabbi Bechai, in Cad Hakkemach, sol. 80. col. 2. Nulla quippe est pulchrior virtus hac ipsa, utpote quae major est omnibus oblationibus, sicut dicitur: Ad quid mihi multitudo sacrificiorum vestrorum; Et ex sol. 79. Magna est vis precationis etiam ad mutandam naturam, ad liberationem è periculis, & ad avertendas pœnas divinas; Dirigunt preces suas ad Deum solum, Creatorem cœli & terræ, excludentes omnes דיינא Advocatos, Mediatores, inter Deum & homines, tam Angelos, quam defunctos, ex cap. 8 §. 19. Et ex Rabbi Menalleh Ben Israel in Conciliat. Part. II. pag. 180. In verbis: Non satiatis mecum Deos argenteos, & Deos aureos non faciatis vobis: Prohibetur, constituere Intercessores inter Deum & hominem. Id enim si maxime concedatur causa prima, est idololatriæ species. Atque integer contextus habet: Vos vidistis quod de cœlo vobis locutus sum. Non faciatis mecum. Aram terream mihi facies, atque super illa sacrificabis &c. Quasi diceret; li qui quærunt Intercessores in mundo apud Principes, id ideo faciunt, quia non facile possunt impetrare eos alloquendi potestatem. At, hæc ratio, apud me non obtinet. Vidistis, quod de cœlo vobis locutus sum, ideo non faciatis mecum alios intercessores. Id est, non adjungatis mihi alia media, verum enim medium, quod habetis ad favorem meum obtinendum, est solum illud sacrificiorum. Facite igitur aram, & sacrificate &c. Spem unice in me reponentes, nec in aliam ullam creaturam; Licet interim inficiandum non sit, Judæos nostros sepulchra adire demortuorum, vespera rum novi anni, tum diei Expiationis, tum ingruente calamitate, ut velut mortuos suam coram Deo ostendant humilitatem, Deumque sibi reddant propitium ob defunctorum merita, uti loquitur Rabbi Isac Abarbanel in Capite Fidei, cap. 12. Neque praesfrate negandum, Judaeos conari defunctos sibi reddere benevolos, uti demonstrat Wagenseilius noster, in Sota, pag. 332. Judaei enim, non unquam defunctos sibi propitiare conantur, nisi in ipsis locis, ubi corpora illorum requiescunt, alibi vero ad eos conceptas preces, inutiles esse arbitrantur. Colligitur id tam ex Gemara nostra, quam ex aliis quae adduximus Scriptorum verbis evidentissime, ipsa insuper accedit experientia, & communis omnium Judaeorum, si de ea re quaerantur, confessio: Addendum quibus tamen, ipsos dissentire Judaeos in modo, quo defuncti preces viventium habeant perspectas.
units.tr: Among the works they commend and press upon the people are prayers: the morning, evening and night prayers found in the Minhagim, or ritual books, both the public ones in the synagogues and the private ones each person says in his own room. The formula they use most of all is Hear, O Israel, which they regard as a summary of the Jewish creed. At the end of their prayers they do not omit Amen, to which they attach great weight, holding that he who says Amen is greater than he who recites the blessing. They say their prayers in the ancient manner, standing, with the head covered and bowed, eyes lowered, girded with a belt, face washed, and the whole body composed for devotion. From the Talmud, tractate Jevamot, folio 19, column 2: He who prays must lower his face towards the ground and lift his heart upwards. And from the Talmud, tractate Berachot, chapter 5: They do not stand to pray except with the head bowed, that is, with the head hung down. They require of those who pray an intention of the heart, since prayer without intention is like a body without a soul, as Rabbi Aben Ezra says on Psalm 78: The chief thing in prayer is the intention of the heart. They commend frequent prayers and blessings, and they do not restrict them to the eighteen to be said each day, but extend them to a hundred blessings [מאה ברכות], reasoning that whoever multiplies his prayer shall be heard by God the Blessed. They also commend the virtues of prayer, citing Rabbi Bechai in Kad Hakkemach, folio 80, column 2: Indeed there is no more excellent virtue than this, since it is greater than all offerings, as it is said: What is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? And from folio 79: Prayer has great power, even to change nature, to deliver from dangers, and to avert divine punishments. They direct their prayers to God alone, the Creator of heaven and earth, and exclude all advocates [דיינא] and mediators between God and men, whether angels or the dead, as stated in chapter 8, §19. And from Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel in Conciliator, Part II, page 180: In the words, "You shall not make with me gods of silver, nor gods of gold for yourselves," it is forbidden to appoint intercessors between God and man. For even if the first cause were granted, this would be a kind of idolatry. And the whole context says: "You have seen that I spoke to you from heaven. You shall not make with me. You shall make me an altar of earth, and upon it you shall sacrifice," and so on. As if he were saying: those who seek intercessors among princes in the world do so because they cannot easily obtain the right to address them. But this reasoning does not hold with me. You have seen that I spoke to you from heaven, so do not make other intercessors with me. That is, do not join other means to me; the only true means you have of obtaining my favour is that of sacrifices. Make therefore an altar and sacrifice, and so on, placing your hope in me alone and in no other creature. Yet it must not be denied that our Jews do go to the graves of the dead on the evenings of the new year, and on the day of Atonement, and when calamity threatens, so that by showing their humility before God as though they were dead, and by the merits of the departed, they may make God propitious to them, as Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel says in the Book of Principles, chapter 12. Nor is it to be denied altogether that the Jews try to make the dead favourable to them, as our Wagenseil shows in Sota, page 332: For the Jews never try to propitiate the dead except in the very places where their bodies rest, and they think that prayers addressed to them elsewhere are useless. This is evident both from our Gemara and from the words of the other writers we have cited, and moreover experience itself confirms it, and the common confession of all Jews, if they are asked about the matter. It should be added, however, that the Jews differ among themselves as to the manner in which the dead have knowledge of the prayers of the living.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Eximunt ex bonorum operum numero vitam Monasticam, credentes vitam Monasticam absurdam esse, magisque bestiarum moribus, quam hominum congruam, sicuti testatur Rabbi Saadia Gaon, vitam Monasticam damnans, variisque argumentis dissuadens, in Sepher Emuna, sol. 45. Sic vitam Monachalem, abstinentiam ab esu carnium, & caelibatum judicant vitam peccaminosam, apud Rabbi Maimonidem in Tractatu de Moribus, cap. 3. Forte dicat quis quispiam: siquidem invidia, concupiscentia, honor, & similia, via malæ sunt, quæ hominem e mundo ejiciunt, longius ab illis & in alteram partem discedam: Ita ut carnem non edat, nec vinum bibat, nec uxorem ducat, nec in domo splendida habitet, nec vestepulchra, sed sacco & rudi lana induatur, instar sacrificulorum Edom; Etiam hæc via mala est, in qua incedere vetitum; Accusant Monachos, Capucinos pariter, quod, quamvis perfectionem simulent Christianam, intus vera destituantur spiritualitate, uti loquitur Judæus Isacus Orobius in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag. 67. Si tamen ego omnes Christianos Monachos Capucinos factos vidissem, tunc libenter fatererer, eam habere Evangelicam perfectionem in totius mundi, & terrestrium contemptu stabilitam: Interim neque in vita compositione, neque in cordis affectibus, neque in cœlestibus unice disquirendis Christianos cæteris gentibus majori videospiritualitate gaudere, quantumvis de ea maxime glorientur. Potius nulla Religio, quæ tot vitiis, sectis, præcipue idololatria pro majore ejus parte scateat, & conspurcata sit, ac semper fuerit; Accusant Monachos, quod infinita divorum fingant miracula, maxime aggrediuntur Avianum Capucinum, sanctissimum impostorem, uti patet ex Judæo Isaco Orobio, in citata Collat. cum Limborchio, pag. 14. 15. Adhuc nostro sæculo sinfingunt, & semper finxere Monachi Divorum infinita miracula, quibus populi fidem adhibuere: credit satis pie, & pia hac fraude miserè deceptus, quisque filios erudit, & isti alterius nationis homines, donec in toto Christianismo Papistico illa impostura de fide habeatur, ut qui negaverit, igne sua infidelitatis poenas luat. Sic nostro tempore Pater Javianus Capucinus miraculis claret, populos, & principes decipit, ut sanctissimus impostor.
units.tr: They exclude monastic life from the number of good works, believing monastic life to be absurd and more fitting to the ways of beasts than of men, as Rabbi Saadia Gaon testifies, condemning monastic life and dissuading from it with various arguments, in Sepher Emunah, folio 45. Likewise they judge the monastic life, abstinence from eating meat, and celibacy to be a sinful life, according to Rabbi Maimonides in the Treatise on Morals, chapter 3: Perhaps someone may say: since envy, lust, honour and the like are evil ways which drive a man out of the world, I will go far from them to the other extreme, so that he eats no meat, drinks no wine, takes no wife, lives in no splendid house, wears no fine clothes, but is clothed in sackcloth and coarse wool, like the priests of Edom. This too is an evil way, and it is forbidden to walk in it. They also accuse the monks, and the Capuchins likewise, that although they feign Christian perfection, they lack true spirituality within, as the Jew Isaac Orobio says in his Conference with Limborch, page 67: Yet if I had seen all Christian monks made into Capuchins, I would gladly confess that they had evangelical perfection, established by contempt of the whole world and of earthly things. But in the composure of their life, in the affections of their hearts, and in seeking only heavenly things, Christians do not rejoice in greater spirituality than other peoples, however much they may boast of it. Indeed no religion is more full of vices and sects, and above all of idolatry for the greater part, and has always been so and polluted, than that one. They accuse the monks of inventing endless miracles of their saints, and they attack above all Avianus the Capuchin, a most holy impostor, as is clear from the Jew Isaac Orobio in the Conference cited with Limborch, pages 14 and 15: Even in our own century the monks have invented, and have always invented, endless miracles of the saints, to which the people have given credence. Each one, who is wretchedly deceived by this pious fraud, believes it quite piously and teaches it to his sons, and these men of another nation, until in the whole Papist Christianity that imposture is held as a matter of faith, so that whoever denies it shall pay the penalty of his unbelief by fire. So in our time Father Avianus the Capuchin is famous for miracles, and deceives the people and the princes, as a most holy impostor.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Commendant, laudantque maximè תשובה Poenitentiam, inculcantes ex Psalm. 34. verf. 15. סור מרע ועשה טוב Recede à malo, & fac bonum, longe removentes desperationem, per quam quis gratiae diffidet divinae, quasi peccatores ad gratiam recipere non posset Deus, cum ipsa sit misericordia, ex Catechesi Judaica, Responsione ad Quaest. 19. Secundum Desperatio, (quod Deus odit) dum aliquis gratiae Dei diffidet, instar alterius Elisaei cujusdam, quasi poenitentes Deus in gratiam recipere non possit, nec cogitat, quanta sit Dei erga peccatores misericordia, cujus omnes homines, etiamsi quis omnium delictorum reus esset, si modo sincera poenitentia, & venia petitio intervenerit, participes facit, teste Propheta Ezech. cap. 18. verf. 32. Quia non delectatur mortem morientis, sed ut revertatur à viis suis & vivat. Quis enim nostrum Menasse irritatore gravius peccant? cant ? At de illo legitur 2. Paral. cap. 33. verf.13. Et orabat & precabatur eum, & audivit preces ejus; Repudiantes pariter Pœnitentiam, cum fide in Messiam conjunctam, ex Judæo Isaco Orobio in Collat. cum Limborchio, num.7. pag.94. Quod Israeli præfixa a Deo pœnitentia, ut ad Deum reflpisceret, non eam habuit conditionem, ut Messiam crederet, sed quod legem Moss integrè servaret; Extollunt Pœnitentiam tum ab Origine & antiquitate, quod mundo condito sit vetustior, ex Tr. Talm. Pesach., f.54.col.1. Nedarim f.39.col.2. Septem res creatæ sunt prius, quam mundus conderetur, nempe hæ: Lex, Pœnitentia, Hortus Eden, Gehenna, Solium Gloriæ, Domus Sanctuarii, & Nomen Messiæ; Non quasi Pœnitentia revera extitisset ante mundum conditum, hoc enim qui prudentiores sunt, non agnoscent, sed quod in Dei voluntate & decreto ante creationem rerum omnium fuerit, quodque unum ex iis fuerit, quæ maxime in mundo debuerint exerceri, vel quod etiam cum mundo pœnitentia in Adamo post lapsum extiterit; Tum extollunt pœnitentiam a necessitate, utilitate, & virtutibus, quod multis parasangis ipsam superet pietatem; Quod magna sit virtus eorum, qui pœnitentiam egerunt, ita ut nulla creatura in septo illorum consistere queat, ex Rabbi Maimonide in Tract. de Pœnitentia nitentia, cap.7. Ipso, ut videtur Luca teste, in Evangelio cap.15.verf.7. Quod omnia pervadat, ex Catechesi Judaica ad Quæst.33. Responsione: Magna equidem vis est pœnitentia, quæ precibus & bonis operibus stipata omnia pervadit, manusq; ad excipiendum redeuntes nunquam non extensas habet; Quod pœnas tollat divinas, ex Tract. Talmud. Pirke Avoth, c.4. Pœnitentia & opera bona sunt veluti clypeus contra pœnas divinas; Quod Pœnitentia sit fundamentum mundi, & columna ejus, nec consistat mundus, nisi propter pœnitentiam; Quod per Pœnitentiam liberati ex Ægypto, ex Rabbi Eliefer in Pirke c.43.in fine: R. Juda inquit: Si Israelitæ non egissent resipiscentiam, non fuissent liberati ex Ægypto; Quod per Pœnitentiam Rex Israelitarum Achabus ad Deum fuerit reversus, & שובן בעל Dominus Pœnitentiæ, seu Pœnitens factus fuerit; Quod Menasse filius Hiskiæ per Pœnitentiam Deo fuerit reconciliatus; Quod Rex Ægypti Pharao, qui valde rebellavit Rupi supremæ, egerit pœnitentiam, ex Rabbi Eliesferis Pirke, cap.43. Præscribunt quin etiam diversas Pœnitentiæ formulas, hominemque pluribus ad seriam pœnitentiam instruunt monitis, ne pœnitentiam differat, sed statim quam primum incipiat, ex Pirke Avoth, cap.2. §.16. Resipisce diem unum ante ante mortem tuam; Ut propriis viribus dignam agant refipiscentiam, expectentque tunc certum a Gratia divina adjutorium; Enumerant denique varias poenitentiae species, quae recensitae sunt in Tractatu Talmudico Joma, quaeque ratione effectuum dicuntur תשובה תשובות Poenitentiae majores, quarum alia sit, quae mundo sanitatem conciliat, ex Jerem. cap. 3. verf. 22. Revertimini filii aversantes, curabo aversiones vestras; Alia quae appropinquare facit redemptionem, ex Jesai. cap. 56. verf. 1. Observati jus, exerceto justitiam, nam proximo salus mea ventura est; Alia quae peccata superbe & studio commissa convertere potest in peccata errorum; Alia quae vitam hominis prolongat; Omnium autem maxima ratione nobilissimi effectus illa, quae hominem usque ad solium gloriae seu divinae majestatis appropinquare facit, ex Hos. cap. 14. verf. 1. Convertere Israel usque ad Dominum Deum tuum; Caeterum, qui totam de Judaeorum Poenitentia doctrinam cognoscere desiderat, evolvere potest Rabbi Jonam Gerundensem, in שער התשובה in Portis Refipiscentiae.
units.tr: They commend repentance [תשובה] above all and urge it from Psalm 34:15, "Depart from evil, and do good" [סור מרע ועשה טוב]. They strongly reject despair, by which a person distrusts divine grace, as if God could not receive sinners back into grace, since he is mercy itself. This is from the Jewish Catechism, the answer to question 19: "Despair is the second thing (which God hates), when someone distrusts the grace of God, like another Elisha, as if God could not receive the penitent into grace. Such a person does not consider how great God's mercy towards sinners is. He makes all people share in it, even if someone were guilty of every crime, provided that sincere repentance and a request for pardon intervene. The prophet Ezekiel 18:32 is witness: 'For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, but that he turn from his ways and live.' For who of us sins more gravely than Manasseh the provoker? Yet of him it is read in 2 Chronicles 33:13: 'And he prayed unto him, and he was entreated of him, and heard his supplication.'" They likewise reject repentance joined with faith in the Messiah. Isaac Orobio the Jew, in his Collatio with Limborch, §7, p. 94, says: "The repentance set before Israel by God, that they might turn back to God, did not have the condition that they believe in the Messiah, but that they keep the law of Moses entirely." They also exalt repentance by its origin and antiquity, that it is older than the created world, from the Talmud, Pesachim f. 54 col. 1, and Nedarim f. 39 col. 2: "Seven things were created before the world was made, namely these: the Law, repentance, the Garden of Eden, Gehenna, the Throne of Glory, the House of the Sanctuary, and the Name of the Messiah." They do not mean that repentance actually existed before the world was made (the more sensible among them do not acknowledge this), but that it was in God's will and decree before the creation of all things, and that it was one of those things which ought most to be exercised in the world; or that repentance existed together with the world in Adam after the fall. They also exalt repentance for its necessity, usefulness and virtues, saying that it surpasses piety by many parasangs; that the virtue of those who have repented is so great that no creature can stand within their enclosure. This is from Rabbi Maimonides, Treatise on Repentance, ch. 7. Luke, as it seems, bears witness to this in the Gospel, ch. 15:7. They say it pervades all things, from the Jewish Catechism, question 33, answer: "Indeed, repentance has great power; supported by prayers and good works, it pervades all things, and always has its hands stretched out to receive those who return." It removes divine punishments, from the Talmudic tractate Pirke Avoth, ch. 4: "Repentance and good works are like a shield against divine punishments." Repentance is the foundation and pillar of the world, and the world does not stand except on account of repentance. Those freed from Egypt were freed through repentance, from Rabbi Eliezer in Pirke ch. 43, at the end: "Rabbi Judah says: If the Israelites had not repented, they would not have been freed from Egypt." Achab, king of Israel, returned to God through repentance, and became "the Lord of Repentance" [שובן בעל], or was made a penitent. Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, was reconciled to God through repentance. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who rebelled greatly against the Supreme Rock, repented, from Rabbi Eliezer's Pirke, ch. 43. They even prescribe various formulas of repentance and instruct the person with many admonitions for earnest repentance, so that he does not postpone it but begins at once, as soon as possible, from Pirke Avoth, ch. 2, §16: "Repent one day before your death." So that they may perform a repentance worthy by their own powers, and then await the sure help of divine grace. Finally they enumerate the various kinds of repentance, which are listed in the Talmudic tractate Yoma, and which, according to their effects, are called "repentances" [תשובות], the greater repentances. One of these brings health to the world, from Jeremiah 3:22: "Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings." Another makes redemption draw near, from Isaiah 56:1: "Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come." Another can turn sins committed proudly and deliberately into sins of error. Another prolongs the life of a man. But the most noble of all effects, in reason, is that which brings a person near to the throne of glory, that is, to the divine majesty, from Hosea 14:1: "O Israel, return unto the Lord thy God." Moreover, whoever wishes to know the whole Jewish doctrine of repentance may read Rabbi Jonah of Gerona, in the Shaar ha-Teshuvah [שער התשובה], the Gate of Repentance.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Commendant simul מועדי Lachrymas, feriae Poenitentiae indices, perpetuosque comites, quae efficiant, ut Deus praecedentium non recordecordetur peccatorum, acceptumque devotum habeat pœnitentem, Urgent quoq; ⁊n Peccatorum Confessionem, Pœnitentiæ comitem, signumque, referentes quod Confessio peccatorum vitam mereatur æternam, ex Berachit Ketanna ad cap. 49 Omnis enim qui confitetur actus suos, dignus est futuro seculo; Et postaliqua: Qui abscondit scelera sua, non dirigetur, qui autem confitetur & relinquit ea, misericordiam consequetur; jubentes, ut in diebus Jejuniorum cum precibus jungant peccatorum Confessiones, ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum, Part. III. cap. 8. Ut, sicut semper, ita certis annis temporibus, inprimis in die, qui antecedit Expiationem magnam, confessionem recitent cum affectu singulari, & contusione pectoris, ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi, Part. III. cap. 6. Quælibet natio more patrio multum precatur, immixtis Confessionibus ad declarandum contritionem, animique sui submissionem & humilitatem; Hancque Confessionem præscribentes: Obsecro, o Domine; Peccavi, inique egi, & prævaricatus sum coram te; Sic & sic feci. Ecce pœnitet me, & pudet me operum meorum; Nunquam revertar ad rem illam; Distinguunt Confessionem in publicam & privatam, seu in communem & particularem, enumeranmerantes in Confessione gravissima & frequentiora peccata, ipsis Rabbinis minima quoque commissa peccata, fi in memoriam veniant. Deo confitentibus, excitato libello Rabbi Mutinenfis, Part.V. cap. 6. Nullum aliud apud illos confessionis genus obtinet quam illud, quo supplices a Deo peccatorum veniam deprecantur. Communi quadam, & juxta ordinem fyllabicum composita gaudent confessione, quam insigniunt nomine ין Confessionis. Quaelibet litera summum aliquod graviffimumq; pra fe fert ac dicit delictum, quod fapius nempe committi solet, sed qui eruditi & prudentes sunt, ordine ac sigillatim peccata commissa enumerant, nec reticent eorum & species & circumstantias. In more quoque positum est, diebus Luna & Jovis peccatorum edere confessiones, omnibusque praeterea inedia diebus: fapiffime, at singulari ratione, idem facerrimum negotiu peragere suevere die jejunii expiatorii, qua de re monui Part.2.cap.6. Ulterius qui morbo sunt affecti, aut in quocunque alio periculo fatis evidenti constituti, qualibet vespera, priusquam fe adfomnum componunt, & omni mane, dum nempe evigilant, iterum peccata agnoscunt & deflent. XII. Inter salutis opera, vitaeque aeternae media, constituunt pariter ינוד Castigationes, Afflictiones, docentes, quod castigationes tempora-les les sint quasi fax accensa in manu hominis, ad cognoscendum statum ejus cum Creatore suo; Quod male homini fit, si ex hoc mundo discedat sine ullis tribulationib9, & castigationib9 ex Tr. Talmudico, Avoda Sarah, t.10. Va navi, quae abit absque vectigali; Et ex Devarim Rabba, sol.290. Va navi, quae solvit, & non dat tributum; Hinc crebras patiuntur castigationes, maxime in die Expiationis, ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judaeorum, Part.III. cap.6. Multi aqua se perfundi, pectusque suum 39 vicibus virgis percuti permittunt, ictusque ita numerati nomine מנה ipsis veniunt: Distinguunt quin etiam Castigationes in Necessarias, & Spontaneas, tradentes, illos homines vel a Deo, vel ab alio castigari; Hi homines se ipsos castigare ac affligere, scilicet abstinere ab omni opere, a cibo & potu, a lotione, ab unctione, a calceorum inductione, ab usu lecti conjugalis, corpus frigida frequenter abluere, flagellare, aliisque modis excruciare; Castigationes Dei vero duplices esse, vel יסורי אהבה Castigationes amoris, vel יסורי תוכחות Castigationes redargutionis; Has infligi propter iniquitatem, quam patravit homo; Illas immitti justo ob iniquitates saeculi sui, ex Berelchit Rabba, Sect. 92. Nullus homo est absque castigationibus. Beatus est ille, cui castigatiogationes obtingunt ex lege, sicut dicitur: Et ex lege tua doce me. Dixit Rabbi Jehofchua, Ben Levi, omnes castigationes quæ veniunt super hominem, & cessare eum faciunt à verbis legis, sunt castigationes redargutionis: sed castigationes quæ veniunt super hominem, & non cessare faciunt eum à verbis legis, sunt castigationes amoris; Commendant autem silentium in castigationibus, ut patienter eas ferant, nulloque modo desperent, cùm in æ-ternum non sint duraturæ, ex Berefchit Rab-ba, Seɛt.38. Nulla calamitas obvenit homini, in qua tandem non sit aliqua respiratio.
units.tr: They also commend the appointed seasons of tears [מועדי], days of repentance and their constant companions, which bring it about that God does not remember earlier sins and accepts the penitent as devout. They also press the confession of sins, the companion and sign of repentance, asserting that confession of sins earns eternal life, from Berachit Ketanna on chapter 49: For everyone who confesses his deeds is worthy of the world to come. A little later it says: He who hides his wicked deeds will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy. They order that in the days of fasting prayers be joined with confessions of sins, from Rabbi Leo of Modena, On the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part III, chap. 8. So that, as always, and at certain fixed times of the year, especially on the day before the Great Atonement, they recite the confession with particular feeling and beating of the breast, from Rabbi Leo of Modena, Part III, chap. 6: Every nation, in its ancestral manner, prays much, mixing in confessions to declare contrition and the submission and humility of its soul. They prescribe this confession: "I beseech you, O Lord; I have sinned, I have acted wickedly, and I have transgressed before you; I have done such and such. Behold, I repent and I am ashamed of my works; I will never return to that thing." They distinguish confession into public and private, or into common and particular. In confession they enumerate the most grave and most frequent sins, and even the smallest sins committed, if they come to mind, when confessing to God. Citing the book of Rabbi Leo of Modena, Part V, chap. 6: No other kind of confession prevails among them than that by which suppliants beg God for forgiveness of sins. They have a common confession, composed according to alphabetical order, which they mark with the name ין of Confession. Each letter carries and names some very grave sin, which is usually committed most often; but those who are learned and prudent enumerate the sins committed in order and one by one, and do not omit their kinds and circumstances. It is also the custom to make confessions of sins on Monday and Thursday, and besides on all fasting days: very often, and with special care, they are accustomed to perform this same most serious business on the day of the expiatory fast, concerning which I have warned in Part II, chap. 6. Furthermore, those who are sick, or who are in some other evidently dangerous situation, acknowledge and lament their sins again every evening before they lie down to sleep, and every morning when they wake. XII. Among the works of salvation and the means of eternal life they likewise set castigations and afflictions [ינוד], teaching that temporal castigations are like a torch lit in a man's hand, to let him know his state with his Creator. It goes badly for a man if he leaves this world without any tribulations and castigations, from the Talmudic tractate Avoda Sarah, chap. 10: Woe to the ship that departs without paying tax. And from Devarim Rabba, fol. 290: Woe to the ship that sets sail and does not pay tribute. Hence they frequently suffer castigations, especially on the day of Atonement, from Rabbi Leo of Modena, On the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part III, chap. 6: Many allow themselves to be drenched with water and to have their breasts struck 39 times with rods, and the blows thus counted come to them under the name מנה. They also distinguish castigations into necessary and spontaneous, teaching that those men are castigated either by God or by another; these men castigate and afflict themselves, namely by abstaining from all work, from food and drink, from washing, from anointing, from putting on shoes, from the use of the marriage bed, by frequently washing the body in cold water, by flogging, and by tormenting themselves in other ways. The castigations of God, moreover, are of two kinds: either יסורי אהבה castigations of love, or יסורי תוכחות castigations of rebuke. The former are inflicted on account of the iniquity which a man has committed; the latter are sent upon the just for the iniquities of their age, from Berelchit Rabba, Sect. 92: No man is without castigations. Blessed is he to whom castigations come from the law, as it is said: And teach me from your law. Rabbi Jehoshua ben Levi said: all the castigations which come upon a man and cause him to cease from the words of the law are castigations of rebuke; but castigations which come upon a man and do not cause him to cease from the words of the law are castigations of love. They commend silence under castigations, so that they bear them patiently and in no way despair, since they will not last for ever, from Berelchit Rabba, Sect. 38: No calamity befalls a man in which at last there is not some respite.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Inter divinum Numen placandi media referunt longum illud exilium, quod extra terram sanctam tolerant sub gentium dominio; Referunt sic inter illa labores, quos impendunt in scribendo, publicandoque libro, ex Autore Halichot Olam, qui initio sui loquitur libri: Fortassis Jehova intuebitur exilium meum, atque erunt mihi Halichot Olam loco oblationis & muneris mei ad expiandum reatum meum, & pro piaculo peccati mei, Amen; Referunt pariter inter media contemptum, quem tolerant dispersi per mundi plagas, ita quippe magnis elatisque clamoribus vociferantur in Darke Zion, Porta 2. cum stant in monte, cui domus sacra fuerat inædificata: Sufficit nobis noster contemptus temptus & captivitas, in qua ob peccata nostra per quatuor mundi plagas sumus dispersi. Referunt ad illa mutationem nominis, mutationemque operum, tremores, tristitiam, aliaque minoris commatis plurima, quae si omnia simul conglobentur, non tamen unquam offensae divinae aequalia evadent, cum peccata offendant infinitam Dei Majestatem, proindeque infinitam incurrant indignationem divinam.
units.tr: Among the means of appeasing the divine Power they count that long exile which they endure outside the holy land under the dominion of the nations. They likewise count among these the labours they expend in writing and publishing a book, following the author of Halichot Olam, who at the beginning of his book says: Perhaps Jehovah will look upon my exile, and Halichot Olam will serve me in place of an offering and gift to atone for my guilt and as expiation for my sin, Amen. They also count among the means the contempt which the dispersed endure throughout the regions of the world. For so, with great and loud cries, they shout in Darke Zion, Gate 2, when they stand on the mountain on which the sacred house had been built: Our contempt is enough for us, and the captivity in which, on account of our sins, we have been scattered through the four regions of the world. To these they refer the change of name, the change of works, trembling, sadness, and very many other things of lesser note. Yet even if all of these were gathered together, they would never equal the offence against God, since sins offend the infinite Majesty of God and therefore incur infinite divine indignation.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Credunt diem Expiationis יום כפורים cum praeviis novem Poenitentiae diebus expiare commissa peccata, hominemque divino reconciliare Numini, statuentes summam diei hujus necessitatem, quod mundi sit columna, gravia & levia expians peccata, in hoc & futuro seculo, ex monitu Rabbi Eliezeris in Pirke, cap. 46. Nisi autem esset dies Cippurim, expiationum, mundus non subsisteret: dies enim expiatorius in hoc & futuro seculo expiat, sicut dicitur, Levit. cap. 16. vers. 30. Sabbathum Sabbathorum hoc vobis. Sabbathum hujus seculi, Sabbathorum in futuro seculo. Licet autem omnia festa transsirent vel abolerentur, dies tamen expiatorius non transibit, quia dies expiatorius levia & gravia peccata expiat; Hinc dicitur vers. 31. Quia ipso die expiabit vos ab omnibus peccatis vestris; Non est hic scriptum, a peccatis vestris, sed ab omnibus peccatis vestris; Quod diabolus illo die nullam in ipsos habeat potestatem, cum peccatis careant, quod ipso die similes sint Angelis, nec cibum, nec potum capientes, sed toto stent die, sicuti Angeli Ministerii, uti rursus loquitur Rabbi Eliefer in allegato libro, cap. 46. Isto die, quo Lex fuit lata, dixit Sammael coram Sancto Benedicto: Domine mundi, super omnes populos mundi dedisti mihi potestatem, non vero in Israelitas. Respondit illi: En, habes in illos potestatem die expiationis, si habuerint peccatum, si vero non, in illos non habebis potentiam. Idcirco dant illi munus die expiatorio ne irritum reddat Israelitarum sacrificium, hinc dicitur Levit. cap. 16. verf. 8. Una sors pro Domino, altera sors pro Hazazel (seu capro emissario. Sors Sancti Benedicti est sacrificium holocausti; Sors vero Hazazel est hirci peccati, atque omnes iniquitates Israelis super illum sunt, juxta illud verf. 22. Et feret hircus ille super se omnes iniquitates illorum. Animadvertit autem Sammael, nullum peccatum in iis deprehendi die expiatorio. Dixit coram Domino mundi: Habes unicum populum in terra, similem Angelis ministerii in coelis. Quid Angeli ministerii? Non habent poplites; Sic & Israelitae die expiatorio stant super pedes suos. Quid Angeli ministerii? Non habent cibum nec potum; Sic & Israelitae die expiationis non habent cibum, neque potum. Quid Angeli ministerii? Puri sunt ab omni peccato; Sic quoq; Israelita die expiatorio mundi sunt ab omni peccato. Quid Angeli ministerii? Pax inter illos est intima; Ita etiam die expiationis pax est in medio Israelitarum; Hinc sublatis sacrificiis, Gallum gallinaceum, quem zeru virum appellant, in locum substituunt, ac pro peccatis suis offerunt, dicentes: Hic gallus sit permutatio pro me, hic in locum meum succedat, hic sit expiatio pro me, huic gallo mors afferetur, mihi vero & toti Israeli vita fortunata, Amen; Obtinetque hic ritus apud Judæos in Germania, Polonia, Moravia, Bohemia, aliisque in locis, testibus Doctoribus, ipsaque experientia, licet in Italia & Oriente obliteratus sit, quod mera subsit vanitas, ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi de Ceremoniis Judæorum, Part. III. c. 6. Solenni quodam antiquitus delectabantur ritu, sub ipsis nempe Festi hujus vigiliis. Gallum vivum tribus vicibus capiti allidebant, dicendo adiectum quemlibet: Sit mei loco immolatus. Actus iste appellabatur כפרה Expiatio. At consuetudo haec in Italia ac Oriente hodie plane obliterata est, ac esse desiit, posteaquam meram ei subesse vanitatem & superstitionem, neque ulli vero fundamento superstructam esse, deprehensum est.
units.tr: They believe that the Day of Atonement [יום כפורים], together with the nine preceding days of repentance, expiates committed sins and reconciles the man to the divine Power. They hold the great necessity of this day, which is the pillar of the world, expiating grave and light sins in this age and in the age to come, according to the admonition of Rabbi Eliezer in Pirke, chap. 46: Unless there were the day of Kippurim, the day of expiations, the world would not endure; for the day of expiation expiates in this age and in the age to come, as it is said, Lev. chap. 16 verse 30: "a sabbath of sabbaths to you." A sabbath in this age, sabbaths in the age to come. Although all the festivals should pass away or be abolished, the day of expiation will not pass, because the day of expiation expiates light and grave sins. Hence it is said in verse 31: "For on this very day he will atone for you from all your sins." It is not written here "from your sins" but "from all your sins."
