On that day the devil has no power over them, since they are free from sin; on that day they are like the Angels, neither taking food nor drink, but standing the whole day like the Angels of ministry. So again speaks Rabbi Eliezer in the book cited, chap. 46: On this day, when the Law was given, Sammael said before the Holy One, blessed be he: "Lord of the world, you have given me power over all the peoples of the world, but not over the Israelites." He answered him: "Behold, you have power over them on the day of atonement, if they have sinned; but if they have not, you will have no power over them." Therefore they give him a portion on the day of expiation, so that he may not render void the sacrifice of the Israelites. Hence it is said in Lev. chap. 16 verse 8: "One lot for the Lord, the other lot for Hazazel (that is, the scapegoat)." The lot of the Holy One, blessed be he, is the burnt offering; but the lot of Hazazel is the goat of sin, and all the iniquities of Israel are upon it, according to that verse 22: "And that goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities." Sammael, however, observed that no sin was found in them on the day of expiation. He said before the Lord of the world: "You have one unique people on earth, like the Angels of ministry in heaven. What of the Angels of ministry? They have no knees; so too the Israelites on the day of expiation stand upon their feet. What of the Angels of ministry? They have no food or drink; so too the Israelites on the day of expiation have no food or drink. What of the Angels of ministry? They are pure from all sin; so too the Israelites on the day of expiation are free from all sin. What of the Angels of ministry? Peace among them is intimate; so too on the day of expiation there is peace in the midst of the Israelites." Hence, with the sacrifices removed, they substitute a cock, which they call a zeru man, and offer it for their sins, saying: "Let this cock be a substitute for me; let it take my place; let it be an expiation for me. Let death come to this cock, but to me and all Israel a fortunate life, Amen." This rite prevails among the Jews in Germany, Poland, Moravia, Bohemia and other places, as the teachers attest and experience itself shows, although it has been dropped in Italy and the East, because it rests on sheer vanity, according to Rabbi Leo of Modena, On the Ceremonies of the Jews, Part III, chap. 6: "In ancient times they delighted in a certain solemn rite, namely on the eve of this festival. They would strike a live cock three times against the head, saying each time: 'Let him be sacrificed in my place.'" This act was called kapparah, Expiation. But this custom has now been entirely abandoned in Italy and the East, and has ceased, since it was found to rest on mere vanity and superstition, and to be built on no true foundation.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Credunt mortem temporalem in fidelibus malorum esse ultimum, pretiumque esse re-demdemptionis, quod univerla expiet peccata, hinc vulgatum istud moribundorum Judæorum: Sit mors mea cunctarum transgressionum mearum expiatio; Et Judæorum adstantium: Sit mors ejus expiatio pro ipso & pro toto Israel; Solent quippe cum morte luctantes sequentem recitare precatiunculam, quæ in precum Judaicarum libellis passim obvia est: Quod si adest tempus visitationis mea ad moriendum, sit quæso mors mea expiatio omnium peccatorum, scelerum, & delictorum, quæ peccavi, commisi, perpetra vi coram te, inde ab illo die, quo primum natus sum, & concede mihi partem in horto Edenis; Solent quoque hanc fidei confessionem recitare, præsentibus ad minimum decem Judæis, inter quos adsit Magister, ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi, de Ceremoniis Judæorum, Part. V. c. 7. Cum quis de vita sua sanitateque pristina recuperanda desperat, decem minimum advocat viros, quos inter Magister quidam adsit necesse est, coram hus, in genere tamen, errata patefacit, de qua confessione modo verba feci; mox precibus suis a Deo sanitatis restaurationem supplex contendit; vel animam suam, sin ita Domino visum fuerit, provida ipsius cura commendat, unaque precatur, dignetur summum Numen morte expiari peccata unquam a se commissa; Sic facinorosi, quibus violenta a carnifice imminet mors, non intermittunt exclaexclamare: Sit mors mea expiatio pro omnibus peccatis meis, putantes hanc nudam confessionem sibi satis posse sufficere, ut de salute persuasi essent reddantur.
units.tr: They believe that temporal death is the last of evils for the faithful, and that it is the price of redemption, which expiates all sins. Hence the common saying of dying Jews: May my death be the expiation of all my transgressions; and of the Jews standing by: May his death be an expiation for him and for all Israel. Those who struggle with death customarily recite the following short prayer, which is found everywhere in Jewish prayer books: If the time of my visitation for dying has come, may my death, I beg you, be the expiation of all the sins, crimes, and offences which I have committed, perpetrated, and done before you, from the day on which I was first born, and grant me a place in the garden of Eden. They also customarily recite this confession of faith in the presence of at least ten Jews, among whom there must be a teacher, from Rabbi Leo of Modena, On the Ceremonies of the Jews, Part V, ch. 7: When someone despairs of recovering his former life and health, he calls at least ten men, among whom some teacher must be present, before whom he reveals his errors, in general terms, concerning which confession I have just spoken; soon after, with his prayers, he earnestly seeks from God the restoration of his health; or, if it has seemed good to the Lord, he commends his soul to his watchful care, and at the same time prays that the highest Power would deign that sins ever committed by him be expiated by death. So too wicked men, whose death is imminent by violence from the executioner, do not cease to cry out: May my death be an expiation for all my sins, thinking that this bare confession can be enough to persuade them that they are restored to salvation.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Credunt Demortuorum opera magnum habere pondus, egregiumque praebere adjutorium vitam operantibus aeternam, quod Deus preces exaudiat propter innocentiam & justitiam defunctorum, ex Rabbi Isaco Abarbanele, in libello de Capite Fidei, cap. 12. Quare tempore angustiae eximus ad sepulchra? Respondet: Ad indicandum, nos esse tanquam mortuos, atque hoc fit propter humiliationem. Istud etiam responderunt ad negotium de indumento sacci, nos videlicet esse instar bestiarum; Vel ut preces effundamus ad Deum, ut nostri memor esse velit, propter illorum innocentiam ac justitiam, quae semper permanserat. Atque hoc intendit alius sapiens, cum ait in responsione ad commemoratam quaestionem; Ut effl agitent mortui commiserationem pro nobis; Quare ad Sanctorum confugiunt merita, tam antiquorum, quam recentium, consolantes se in constructione Isaci super aram ab Abrahamo extructam, dum divino mandato parere, & victima fieri paratus erat; Atque hoc obsequium trahunt in peccatorum suorum expiationem, sicuti quam clare patet, &c
units.tr: They believe that the works of the dead carry great weight and offer an excellent help to those working for eternal life, since God hears prayers on account of the innocence and righteousness of the departed. So Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel, in the booklet On the Articles of Faith, ch. 12: Why do we go out to the graves in time of distress? He answers: to show that we are like the dead, and this is done for the sake of humility. They gave this same answer on the matter of wearing sackcloth, namely that we are like beasts; or so that we may pour out prayers to God, that he may be willing to remember us, on account of the innocence and righteousness of those dead, which always endured. Another wise man aims at this too, when in answer to the question mentioned he says: that the dead may stir up compassion for us. Hence they take refuge in the merits of the saints, both ancient and recent, comforting themselves with the binding of Isaac on the altar built by Abraham, when he was ready to obey the divine command and become a victim. And they draw this obedience into the expiation of their sins, as is clearly evident, etc.

units.la: Ec
units.tr: Ec

units.la: ex Tractatu Talmudico Schabbat,sol.89. Ex Targum in Cantic.cap. 2.verf.17.cap.3.verf.6. Et ex precum quotidianarum Ritualibus: Deus noster, Deus Patrum nostrorum, memento ligationis, qua ligavit Abraham filium super altare; Consolantes pariter fe in probitate & justitia piorum, non longe demortuorum, quod nos non unus Judaeorum tantum docuit Magister, sed maxime confirmavit Wagenfeilius noster, in Carminis Lipmanni confutatione, quando lessum Judaicum, in obitum Lipmani alterius, exhibet pag. 496,497.
units.tr: From the Talmudic tractate Shabbat, fol. 89. From the Targum on Song of Songs 2:17 and 3:6. And from the ritual daily prayers: Our God, God of our fathers, remember the binding with which Abraham bound his son upon the altar; likewise comforting themselves in the probity and righteousness of the pious dead. Not only one Jewish teacher taught us this, but our Wagenseil especially confirmed it, in his refutation of Lipmann's Song, where he presents the Jewish lament on the death of another Lipmann, pp. 496, 497.

units.la: Recitavi tantum Lipmanni hujus bona opera,
units.tr: I have recited only the good works of this Lipmann,

units.la: Ut Deus Benedictus nobis Messiam mittat in diebus nostris.
units.tr: That the blessed God may send us the Messiah in our days.

units.la: Hora noctis tertia
units.tr: The third hour of the night

units.la: Miserrimus casus contigit,
units.tr: A most wretched accident has happened,

units.la: Excellentissimusque Rabbinus & Sacerdos Lipmannus, pappus optimus,
units.tr: And the most excellent Rabbi and Priest Lipmann, a very good grandfather,

units.la: Morte sua cessit in sacrificium.
units.tr: By his death has passed into a sacrifice.

units.la: Ejus pietas nobis semper subveniat.
units.tr: May his piety always help us.

units.la: Ita fiat ut pietatis ejus fructus semper percipiamus.
units.tr: So may it come about that we always receive the fruit of his piety.

units.la: Pietas ejus ubique nobis sit auxilio.
units.tr: May his piety always be our help.

units.la: Ob pietatem ejus procul a nobis sit desolatio.
units.tr: Through his piety may desolation be far from us.

units.la: Ob pietatem illius nemo ante diem suum moriatur. Pie-
units.tr: Through his piety may no one die before his day. Pie-

units.la: Pietas ejus averruncet omne periculum. Pietas ejus in omnibus adversitatibus nos tueatur.
units.tr: May his piety avert every danger. May his piety protect us in all adversities.

units.la: Deus porro iram suam avertat, Ob pietatem viri hujus probissimi.
units.tr: May God moreover turn away his anger, for the sake of this most upright man.

units.la: Optimus noster Interpres apud Deum fuit in hoc mundo; Sed nunc ante thronum gloriae est constitutus, Ibi advocatum nostrum agere debet, Et pro omnibus nobis preces fundere: Ut Deus nos a malo custodiat, Et ex captivitate liberet, Idque propere & in diebus nostris, Itaque omnes succinamus Amen.
units.tr: Our best interpreter was among us before God in this world; but now he is set before the throne of glory. There he ought to act as our advocate and pour out prayers on behalf of us all: that God may guard us from evil and free us from captivity, and that speedily and in our days. So let us all add our Amen.

units.la: Sed de his, brevi, pluribus, Celeberrimus Wagenseilius, in Opere, Judicium Sanguinis inscribendo, demonstraturus ex Tractatu Talmudico Moed Katon, sol. 28. quod Judaei credant, hominum justorum ac pietate praestantium, quales Aharon & Mirjam, obitum expiare & ipsorum, & totius populi peccata, uti patet ex illius operis Ichnographia, quae in nupera Dissertatione Epistolica ad Clarissimum Fechtium est obvia; Hinc quoque est, quod martyrum memoriam habeant in veneratione maxima, appellantes hos sanctos, uti liquet ex Bibliis Hebraicis Atthianis, in quibus Joseph AtAtthias nominatur filius Sancti Abrahami Atthiae.
units.tr: But on these matters, briefly and at greater length, the most celebrated Wagenseil, in a work to be entitled Judicium Sanguinis, will demonstrate from the Talmudic tractate Moed Katon, fol. 28, that the Jews believe the death of just men and those outstanding in piety, such as Aaron and Miriam, expiates both their own sins and those of the whole people; as is evident from the outline of that work, which is available in the recent Epistolary Dissertation addressed to the most distinguished Fechtius. Hence also it is that they hold the memory of the martyrs in the greatest veneration, calling these saints, as is clear from the Hebrew Bibles of Athias, in which Joseph Athias is named the son of Saint Abraham Athias.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Constituunt bonorum operum varios gradus, ut rite inter opera salutem possint operari propriam, enumerantes decem, quorum unus alio sit superior, taciliorque manuducat ad operis gradum difficiliorem, quo ita per illos ascenderent, donec ad supremum omnium pertingerent, divinaque potirentur majestate, quorumque haec sequens sit nomenclatura: Admonitio, promptitudo, abstinentia, innocentia, mudicia, sanctitas, humilitas, timor peccati, beneficentia, & majestas divina, ex Rabbi Machir, in Abkat Rochel, Part. I. Lib. 1. pag. 4, 5. Edit. Hulsianae: Primus itaque gradus est Admonitio, qua homo indiget, ut sibi caveat a peccato omnique re ad transgressionem impellente, atque hoc medio alacris efficietur ad praeceptum, beneficiorum retributionem, bona opera, & bonos mores; quod si vero ad praeceptorum observationem & bona opera alacrem sese offenderit & legi operam dederit, mundus inde & immunis evadet ab omni peccato, ab omni immunditie, improbitate & delicto purgatus; & si ita fuerit mundus paulatim subsistet coram Deo, innocens manibus & purus; si vero ita mundus fuerit, eo tandem deveniet, ut sanctus & magnus sit habendus coram creatore suo; & si fuerit erit sanctus, timens Deum quoq; erit, humilis & submissus spiritu coram possessore suo; & si humilis fuerit, Deum timebit Deoq; dilectus erit; & si ita fecerit, beneficus quoq; evadet, & beneficia rependens omni creaturæ; & si talis fuerit, majestas divina super ipso quiescit, & hic gradus supremus est, neque datur superior eo. Justus ergo adscendit de gradu in gradum donec ad supremum hunc & omnium maximum pertingat.
units.tr: They set out various degrees of good works, so that a man may rightly work out his own salvation among the works. They enumerate ten, each of which is higher than the one before it and leads more easily to the next, more difficult, degree. By these they would climb until they reached the highest of all and obtained the divine majesty. The list runs as follows: admonition, readiness, abstinence, innocence, cleanness, holiness, humility, fear of sin, beneficence, and divine majesty. This is from Rabbi Machir, in Abkat Rochel, Part I, Book 1, pages 4-5, Hulsius edition: The first degree, then, is admonition, by which a man needs to guard himself against sin and every thing that drives him to transgression. By this means he will become eager for the commandment, for the repayment of benefits, for good works and good morals. But if he has presented himself eager for the observance of the precepts and good works, and has applied himself to the law, he will thereby become clean and free from every sin, purged of every uncleanness, wickedness and offence. And if he has been made clean in this way, he will gradually stand before God, innocent in hands and pure. If he has become so clean, he will at last come to be regarded as holy and great before his Creator. And if he has been holy, he will also fear God, be humble and submissive in spirit before his possessor. And if he has been humble, he will fear God and be beloved of God. And if he has done so, he will also become beneficent, repaying benefits to every creature. And if he is such, the divine majesty rests upon him, and this is the highest degree, and there is none above it. The just man therefore ascends from degree to degree until he reaches this highest and greatest of all.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Describunt pariter, commendantq; prolixe bonorum operum Effecta, enarrantes quæ merces quemlibet boni operis excipiat gradum, ut ita ad bonorum operum, pietatisque studium magis inflammarent contribules, uti rursus patet ex Rabbi Machir, in Abkat Rechel, Part.1. Libr.1. pag.5,6. Si igitur cautus fuerit, quanam erit merces ejus? Liberabit eum Deus ab omni angustia & anxietate & ab omnibus perditionis & pœnarum generibus, juxta illud Ezech. 34. verf.5. Qui monitum acceperit animam suam eripiet. Et si ad servanda præcepta fuerit alacrus, quæ merces ejus? Deus dilatabit cor ipsius, & lumine legis oculos ipsius illuminabit, dicitur enim Psalmo 119. verf.32. Viam præceptorum tuorum percurram, cum dilataveris animum meum. Et si abstinens fuerit, quæ merces ejus? Deus faciet eum peculium suum, quia dicitur Lev.20. verf.26. Separavi ravi vos a populis ut sitis mei. Et si innocens fuerit, quae merces ejus? Deus confringet hostes ipsius coram ipso, & exhilarabit ipsum in ruina eorum, nam dicitur Job 22. verf. 19. Videbunt recti & laetabuntur, & innocens subsannabit eos. Quod si fuerit mundus quae merces ejus? Vocabitur amicus Dei, dicitur enim Proverb. 22. verf. 11. Qui amat mundiciem cordis, pro gratia labiorum ejus, Rex amicus ejus futurus est. Quod si fuerit sanctus, quae merces ejus? Deus illum disponit ad vitam futuri mundi, quia dicitur Esai. 4. verf. 3. Erit enim ut qui relictus fuerit Sione & residuus Jeruschalaimis, sanctus ipsi dicitur, quisquis adscriptus fuerit vitae Jeruschalaimis. Quod si fuerit humilis, quae merces ejus? Deus intelligere faciet eum arcana legis, & explanabit ipsi thesauros sapientiae suae, quia dicitur Psal. 25. verf. 14. Arcanum Jehovae adest timentibus ipsum. Quod si fuerit beneficus, quae merces ejus? Deus habitare faciet super ipso Spiritum sanctum, ipsi loquetur ad modum omnium Prophetarum, quia dicitur Psalm. 89. verf. 20. Tunc per visionem allocutus es beneficum tuum.
units.tr: They likewise describe and commend at length the effects of good works, relating what reward each degree of good work receives, so as to inflame their fellow tribesmen all the more to the zeal of good works and piety. This again appears from Rabbi Machir, in Abkat Rochel, Part I, Book 1, pages 5-6: "If, then, a man is cautious, what will be his reward? God will deliver him from every distress and anxiety, and from all kinds of destruction and punishments, according to that saying in Ezek. 34.5: 'He who has received warning will save his soul.' And if he is eager to keep the precepts, what is his reward? God will enlarge his heart and illuminate his eyes with the light of the law, for it is said in Psalm 119.32: 'I will run the way of your precepts, when you have enlarged my mind.' And if he is abstinent, what is his reward? God will make him his peculiar people, for it is said in Lev. 20.26: 'I have separated you from the peoples, that you may be mine.' And if he is innocent, what is his reward? God will break his enemies before him and gladden him in their ruin, for it is said in Job 22.19: 'The righteous shall see and rejoice, and the innocent shall mock them.' But if he is clean, what is his reward? He shall be called the friend of God, for it is said in Prov. 22.11: 'He who loves purity of heart, for the grace of his lips, the king shall be his friend.' But if he is holy, what is his reward? God will dispose him for the life of the future world, for it is said in Isa. 4.3: 'He who is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy, everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem.' But if he is humble, what is his reward? God will make him understand the secrets of the law and will explain to him the treasures of his wisdom, for it is said in Psalm 25.14: 'The secret of Jehovah is with those who fear him.' But if he is beneficent, what is his reward? God will make the Holy Spirit dwell upon him, and will speak to him after the manner of all the prophets, for it is said in Psalm 89.20: 'Then you spoke by vision to your beneficent one.'

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Efflagitant tandem bona opera, amoris potius impulsu suscipienda, quam intuitu lucri, mercedisque, ex antiquo magistri Antigoni monito, in Pirke Abhot, cap. 1. §. 3. Ne sitis tanquam servi, qui serviunt Domino ea conditione ut recirecipiant mercedem, sed estote tanquam servi, qui serviunt Domino, non ea conditione ut recipiant mercedem, sitque timor Dei super vos; Hinc in Catechismo Iudaico, ad Quæstionem secundam, qua interrogant: Deus tibi propitius sit, mi fili, dic quaso, in quem finem te Deus in hac forma eximia creavit? Respondent: Omnia in gloriam suam creavit. Atque ego conditus sum, ut Domino meo serviam, eum diligam, gloriamque ejus timeam, ac quae ipsi placuerint, praestem, idque non mercedis adipiscendae causa, quamquam praemium tandem habiturus sum, cum perveniam in seculum aeternum, & vivam coram eo in deliciis aeternis.
units.tr: At last they demand good works, to be undertaken from the impulse of love rather than with a view to gain or reward, following the old saying of the teacher Antigonus in Pirke Abhot, ch. 1, §3: Be not like servants who serve the Lord on condition of receiving a reward, but be like servants who serve the Lord not on condition of receiving a reward, and let the fear of God be upon you. Hence in the Jewish Catechism, at the second question, where they ask: May God be gracious to you, my son. Tell me, I pray, for what end did God create you in this excellent form? They answer: He created all things for his own glory. And I have been made so that I may serve my Lord, love him, fear his glory, and do what pleases him, and that not for the sake of obtaining a reward, although I shall indeed have the prize in the end, when I come into the eternal age and live before him in eternal delights.

units.la: CAPUT XIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIV.

units.la: De Legis Mosaicæ Observantia, mercede, præceptisq; sexcentis & tredecim.
units.tr: On the Observance of the Mosaic Law, its Reward, and the Six Hundred and Thirteen Precepts.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: CRedunt unanimes hominem coram Deo justificari ex operibus Legis Mosaicæ, quæ
units.tr: All agree that a man is justified before God by the works of the Law of Moses, which

units.la: non iolum temporariam promittat felicitatem, sed certissimas pariter vitæ æternæ promissiones completatur, proinde Deum observantibus præcepta legis mercedem vitæ æternæ in futuro retributurum seculo, ex articulo fidei undecimo, in Catechesi Judaica: Fundamentum undecimum, quod Deus nemini præmium sit denegaturus, sed retributurus mercedem iis, qui præcepta servant, & delinquentes multaturus pœna, vel in hoc seculo vel in futuro, vel in utroque, prout præcepti delictorumq; gravitas exegerit. Summa vero retributio erit post mortem in futuro seculo, summaque punitio; Ex Tractatu Talmudico Avoda Zara, sol. 2. In futuro seculo Sanctus Benedictus allaturus est in gremio suo librum Legis & dicturus: Quicunq; Legi huic operam dedit, venire debet & tollere mercedem suam; Ex Pirke Avot, cap. 6. §. 9. Ea hora qua homo decedit ex hac vita, non comitantur eum argentum, aurum, lapides pretiosi, margaritaque, sed Lex & bona opera solummodo, sicut dicitur Proverb. cap. 6. verf. 22; Ex Rabbi Bechai in Commentario ad Genesin, pag. 3. Observatio præceptorum duas completitur utilitates, utilitatem corporis in hac vita, & utilitatem animæ in altera vita, atque hoc est quod generaliter commemorat Moses, Deuteron. cap. 6. verf. 24. Ex Rabbi Isaco Abarbanele in Nachalat Avot, cap. 6. sol. 93. Jam memoravi, quod quod adductus fuerit sermo iste ad declarandum à nobis magnitudinem legis, quæ largitur vitam facientibus eam in futuro seculo; Et paulo post: Et infert Rabbi Jose probationem, si quis consequatur vitam æternam, fieri id beneficio Legis, & bonorum operum; Et ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, de Resurrectione mortuorum, Lib. i. cap. 13. pag. 100, 101. Quod autem dicunt Patriarchas nullam alterius vitæ rationem habuisse, neque Isaacum, cum Jacobo filio suo benediceret, alia bona ei promisisse, quam caduca & temporalia, in eo vehementer fallun-tur atque errant: nam idcirco Abrahamus vitam suam, filiique sui, susque deque habuit, & omnia bona temporalia, à Deo sibi promissa posthabuit; quin imo idcirco in animum induxit filium sua manu necare, ut æternæ vitæ fieret particeps. Adde, quod Isaacus benedicens filio suo promisit ei spiritualia bona: quod ex eo deprehendere licet, quia ante benedictionem corporalem, bis positum legitur, יברכהו & benedixit illi.
units.tr: not only promises temporal happiness but also fulfils the most certain promises of eternal life. Therefore God, they say, will reward those who keep the precepts of the law with the wage of eternal life in the future age, as the eleventh article of faith in the Jewish Catechism states: The eleventh foundation is that God will never deny a reward to those who keep the precepts, but will repay those who keep them with a wage, and will punish transgressors with punishment, either in this age or in the future, or in both, as the gravity of the precept and of the transgression requires. The full repayment will come after death, in the future age, and the full punishment likewise. From the Talmudic tractate Avoda Zara, fol. 2: In the future age the Holy One, blessed be he, will bring the book of the Law in his bosom and say: Whoever has laboured at this Law, let him come and take his wage. From Pirke Avot, ch. 6, §9: At the hour when a man departs from this life, neither silver, nor gold, nor precious stones, nor pearls accompany him, but only the Law and good works, as is said in Prov. 6:22. From Rabbi Bechai in his Commentary on Genesis, p. 3: The observance of the precepts brings two advantages: the advantage of the body in this life, and the advantage of the soul in the other life; and this is what Moses generally recalls in Deut. 6:24. From Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel in Nachalat Avot, ch. 6, fol. 93: I have already mentioned that this saying was brought forward to declare to us the greatness of the Law, which gives life to those who keep it in the future age. And a little later: Rabbi Jose also draws the proof that if anyone attains eternal life, this comes about by the benefit of the Law and of good works. And from Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, On the Resurrection of the Dead, bk. 1, ch. 13, pp. 100–101: As for those who say that the patriarchs had no regard for any other life, and that Isaac, when he blessed his son Jacob, promised him no other goods than fleeting and temporal ones, they are greatly mistaken and in error. For Abraham therefore held his own life and the life of his son as nothing, and set aside all the temporal goods promised him by God; indeed, he resolved to slay his son with his own hand so that he might become a partaker of eternal life. Add that Isaac, blessing his son, promised him spiritual goods; this can be gathered from the fact that before the bodily blessing the word yebarekhehu [יברכהו], "he blessed him," is found twice.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Crepent licet Amorem Dei אהבת המקום, Amorem hominum אהבת הבריות maxima, primaria-que Legis Mosaicæ esse præcepta, quæ totam absolvant legem, quæque ad consum-matam felicitatem obtinendam unice requiran-tur, non intermittunt interim plurima hinc emanantia, hisque superstructa inculcare præ-cepta, cepta, totam legem, tum ad meliorem intel‐ligentiam, tum ad faciliorem observantiam, in sexcenta & tredecim distinguere praecepta, quorum 248 sint Jubentia seu Affirmativa, 365 vero sint Negativa seu Prohibitiva, uti patet & ex dictis cap.2.§.18. Et ex Catechesi Judaica, in qua ad Quaestionem 21. Explicasti duo illa, amorem Dei & hominum, annon praeter illa adhuc quicquam ad consummatam illam beatitudinem obtinendam requiritur? Respondetur: Duobus ipsis primaria totius legis regula absolvitur. Illud nam Deuteron. cap. 6. verf. 5. Et diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, & ex tota anima tua, & ex omnibus viribus tuis, complectitur omnia illa, quae Deo Benedicto cum homine intercedunt, praecepta, nimirum omnia tam affirmantia quam negantia. Illud autem Levit. cap. 19. verf. 18. Et diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum, comprehendit omnia ea praecepta, quibus homines inter se invicem continentur, sive affirmativa sive negativa; quo pertinent res pecuniarias & injuriarum, judicia criminalia, item lex de sponsalium & primogenitura, quibus omnibus lex ipsa & societas humana superstructa est. Quaenam vero nobis alia Deo placendi via est, quam ut omnia 613 praecepta hinc emanantia observemus? Et ex Tractatu Talmudico Maccoth, cap. 3. f. 23. Praecepta 613 dicta fuerunt Mosi in Sinai, 365 negativa, juxta numerum dierum solarium, 248 affirmativa, juxta membra hominis. Dixit Rabbi Menunna, qua Scriptura id probatur? חוה Legem praecepit nobis Moses hereditariam, Deuteron. cap. 33. verf. 4. Ubi חוה in numeris est 613, si duo scilicet priora Decalogi praecepta adjiciantur.
units.tr: Although they boast that the love of the Omnipresent [אהבת המקום] and the love of men [אהבת הבריות] are the greatest and chief precepts of the Law of Moses, which comprise the whole law and are alone required to obtain perfect happiness, they nevertheless do not cease to press upon us the many precepts that flow from these and are built upon them. They divide the whole law, both for better understanding and for easier observance, into six hundred and thirteen precepts, of which 248 are Commanding or Affirmative and 365 are Negative or Prohibitive, as is also clear from what was said in ch. 2, §18. And in the Jewish Catechism, in answer to question 21: You have explained those two, the love of God and of men; is nothing further required to obtain that perfect blessedness? The answer is: The whole primary rule of the Law is fulfilled by these two. For that saying, Deut. 6:5, And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, embraces all those precepts that lie between God, blessed be he, and man, namely all of them, both affirmative and negative. But that saying, Lev. 19:18, And you shall love your neighbour as yourself, comprehends all those precepts by which men are bound to one another, whether affirmative or negative; to this belong matters of money and injuries, criminal judgments, likewise the law of betrothal and of the firstborn, on all of which the law itself and human society are built. And what other way is there for us to please God than to observe all the 613 precepts that flow from these? From the Talmudic tractate Makkoth, ch. 3, fol. 23: The 613 precepts were told to Moses at Sinai: 365 negative, according to the number of the days of the sun, and 248 affirmative, according to the members of the human body. Rabbi Menuna said: By what Scripture is this proved? The word torah [תורה], "law," which Moses commanded us as an inheritance, Deut. 33:4, where the word torah has the numerical value of 613, if the two first precepts of the Decalogue are added.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Docent sexcenta haec tredecimq; praecepta nucleum comprehendere, compendiumque totius Theologiae Judaicae, enumerantes illa ordine ex Mose, uti abunde patet ex Hebraeorum monumentis, praetereaq; liquet ex Rabbi Abraham, Bar Ketanni in Voce Dei, ex versione Exjudaei Poloni, Philippi Ferdinandi, quae Cantabrigiae Anno 1597. impressa, & hinc inde aliqua observatione est illustrata:
units.tr: They teach that these six hundred and thirteen precepts contain the kernel and summary of the whole Jewish theology, listing them in order from Moses, as is abundantly clear from the Hebrew monuments; moreover, it is evident from Rabbi Abraham Bar Ketanni, in his entry on the Name of God, from the version of the Polish Jew Philip Ferdinand, printed at Cambridge in the year 1597, and illustrated here and there with some annotation:

units.la: GENESIS.
units.tr: GENESIS.

units.la: Observ. 1 Primum praeceptum est de matrimonio, hoc praeceptum maxime Hebraei observant, & scribunt in suis commentariis si quis excesserit viginti annos & non duxit uxorem vel si duxerit uxorem sterilem aeque peccat ac si hominem interfecisset & meretur poenam Onam, quem Deus interfecit. Tamen qui additus &tus est studio legis ut uxorem non curet habere is nihil peccat, si vero senserit cupiditatem illam invalescere debet uxorem ducere.
units.tr: Observation 1. The first precept concerns marriage. The Hebrews observe this precept carefully and write in their commentaries that if a man has passed twenty years of age and has not taken a wife, or if he has taken a barren wife, he sins just as much as if he had killed a man, and he deserves the punishment of Onan, whom God slew. Yet a man who is devoted and wholly given to the study of the law, so that he does not care to have a wife, sins not at all; but if he perceives that this desire is growing strong, he ought to take a wife.

units.la: Ne comedant nervum muta-tionis. i. nervum in femore prorup-tum. Observant Hebraei hoc praeceptum, nec edunt posteriorem partem bestiae dum nervos illi adimunt. Hoc praeceptum traditum est in monte Sinai, tamen in memoria luctae Jacobi cum Deo hic collocatur.
units.tr: Do not eat the sinew of dislocation, that is, the sinew in the thigh that was put out of joint. The Hebrews observe this precept and do not eat the hind part of the beast, since they remove its sinews. This precept was given on Mount Sinai, yet here it is placed in memory of Jacob's wrestling with God.

units.la: EXODUS.
units.tr: EXODUS.

units.la: Est de Calendario Judaico se-cundum motus Lunares, ut sciant rationem dierum festivorum. Hoc observant Hebraei, tamen vacillant de suo numero, ergo festum celebrant unius diei duobus excepto Sabbatho: Saducaei hoc non faciunt: ergo Pharisaeos illud observantes deridendos proponunt.
units.tr: There is a Jewish calendar based on the lunar motions, so that they may know the reckoning of the festival days. The Hebrews observe this, yet they waver about their count, and therefore they keep a festival of one or two days, excepting the Sabbath. The Sadducees do not do this, and therefore they put forward the Pharisees, who observe it, as objects of ridicule.

units.la: 4 Ut mactent Paschae suo tempo.re non observatur, nam stante Ecclesia non potuerunt, nunc non licet: cet: sic ubicunq; videris, Non observ. scias hoc non ex Judæorum pravitate sed ex temporum mutatione accidere.
units.tr: 4 That they sacrifice the Passover at its proper time is not observed. For while the Church stood they could not, and now it is not lawful. So wherever you see Non observ., know that this comes about not from the perversity of the Jews but from the change of times.

units.la: 5 Ut edant carnem paschatis nocte decima quinta.
units.tr: 5 That they eat the flesh of the Passover on the fifteenth night.

units.la: 6 De non edendo agnum crudum.
units.tr: 6 Concerning not eating the lamb raw.

units.la: 7 De non relinquendo aliquid de Carne Paschali.
units.tr: 7 Concerning not leaving any of the Passover flesh over.

units.la: 8 Debes tollere fermentatum panem nocte decima quarta ex domo tua.
units.tr: 8 You must remove leavened bread from your house on the fourteenth night.

units.la: 9 Azimi iunt edendi prima nocte paschatis.
units.tr: 9 Unleavened bread is to be eaten on the first night of the Passover.

units.la: 10 Totis septem diebus paschatis ne reperiatur apud te panis fermentatus.
units.tr: 10 For all seven days of the Passover, leavened bread must not be found with you.

units.la: 11 Non debes aliquid cum fermento mixtum edere.
units.tr: 11 You must not eat anything mixed with leaven.

units.la: 12 Ne edat aliquis Apostata Judæ in societate eorum de Paschate.
units.tr: 12 Let no apostate of Judah eat of the Passover in their company.

units.la: 13 Inquilinus & mercenarius non edant de Paschate.
units.tr: 13 A sojourner and a hired servant shall not eat of the Passover.

units.la: 14 Non educas carnem Paschatis e domo societatis.
units.tr: 14 You shall not carry the flesh of the Passover out of the house into the company.

units.la: 15 Non debes frangere ossa in Paschate.
units.tr: 15 You must not break a bone at the Passover.

units.la: Ff
units.tr: Ff

units.la: 16 Præputiatus non debet edere carnem Paschalem.
units.tr: 16 An uncircumcised person must not eat the Passover flesh.

units.la: 17 Non debes edere fermentum per omnes dies paschatis.
units.tr: 17 You must not eat leaven throughout all the days of the Passover.

units.la: 18 Ne appareat aliquid fermentatum per totos septem dies.
units.tr: 18 Let nothing leavened appear throughout the seven days.

units.la: 19 De recensendo historiam de exitu Ægyptiaco prima nocte paschatis, hac nocte paschatis legunt hanc historiam, & bibunt quatuor cyathos vini in gratiarum actionem & post cœnam frangunt panem & dant patresfamilias unicuique in mensa cum tanta sanctitate ac si ipsum pascha mactassent.
units.tr: 19 Concerning the recounting of the history of the Egyptian exodus on the first night of the Passover: on this night of the Passover they read this history, and drink four cups of wine in thanksgiving, and after the supper they break bread and give it to each householder at the table with such holiness as if they had themselves slaughtered the Passover.

units.la: 20 Ne egrediare civitatis termi-nos die Sabbathi. Saducæi male hoc intelligunt, nec e domo sua die sabbathi exeunt vel ad preces, Pharisæi autem probant ex ultimo capite Esaiæ versu penult. quod licitum est ire ad preces.
units.tr: 20 You shall not go out beyond the borders of the city on the Sabbath day. The Sadducees understand this wrongly, and do not go out of their houses on the Sabbath, even to prayers. The Pharisees, however, prove from the penultimate verse of the last chapter of Isaiah that it is lawful to go to prayers.

units.la: 21 Credere in Deum in hoc præcepto continetur tota lex. In decem præceptis sunt tot literæ quot sunt præcepta in bibliis, id est, 613 & septem literæ sunt præterea quæ oftendunt septem plagas quæ debentur legis transgressoribus, Levit. 26. 28. Et hoc est quod dixit Moses. Ecce ego proposui vobis vitam & mortem, id est, 613 præcepta ad vitam, & septem plagas ad mortem.
units.tr: 21 In this precept, to believe in God, the whole law is contained. In the ten precepts there are as many letters as there are precepts in the Bible, that is 613; and there are besides seven letters which show the seven plagues owed to transgressors of the law, Lev. 26. 28. And this is what Moses said: Behold, I have set before you life and death, that is, 613 precepts for life and seven plagues for death.

units.la: Observ. 22 Non habebis Deos alienos coram me.
units.tr: Observ. 22 You shall have no other gods before me.

units.la: Observ. 23 Non facies sculptile neque tibi neque aliis: neque factum in usum tuum emas.
units.tr: Observ. 23 You shall not make a graven image for yourself or for others, nor buy one made for your own use.

units.la: Observ. 24 Ne incurves vel prosternas te coram idololatris nullo modo.
units.tr: Observ. 24 You must not bow down or prostrate yourself before idolaters in any way.

units.la: Observ. 25 Non est serviendum idololatris eo modo quo solent cultores eorum illis deservire.
units.tr: Observ. 25 One must not serve idolaters in the manner in which their worshippers are accustomed to serve them.

units.la: Observ. 26 Ne sumito nomen ejus in vanum, id est, sine necessitate.
units.tr: Observ. 26 You shall not take his name in vain, that is, without necessity.

units.la: Observ. 27 De sanctificatione diei Sabbathi.
units.tr: Observ. 27 Concerning the sanctification of the Sabbath day.

units.la: Observ. 28 Die Sabbathi non est laborandum.
units.tr: Observ. 28 On the Sabbath day no work is to be done.

units.la: Observ. 29 Honora patrem & matrem.
units.tr: Observ. 29 Honour your father and mother.

units.la: Observ. 30 Non debes innocentem interficere.
units.tr: Observ. 30 You must not kill the innocent.

units.la: Observ. 31 Ne furere animam ex fratribus tuis, id est, Israeliticis. Numer. Præceptor. Cap. VI. Observ. 32 De falso testimonio. ib. 16 Observ. 33 Ne desideres rem fratris tui ut ib. 17 iam, &c. Observ. 34 Non facies formas Ethnicis ib. 23 etiam si non adorent illas. N.obs. 35. Non ædificies altare ex lapidibus ferro rasis. ib. 25 N.obs. 36 Non debes ascendere per gradus ad altare, ut revelentur pudenda tua. 20 ult. N.obs. 37 Observabis statuta cum Hebræi servo, secundum regulas traditas. 21. 2 observ. 38 De desponsando ancillam Hebræam. ib. 8,9 Observ. 39 De redimendo Hebræam. ib. 8 Observ. 40 Non vendes ancillam Hebræam alii Hebræo. ib. 8 Observ. 41 Alimentum, operimentum, habitationem ne auferas etiam ancillæ desponsatæ. ib. 10 Observ. 42 Ne percutias patrem vel matrem. ib. 15 Observ. 43 Ne maledicas patri vel matri. ib. 17 Observ. 44 Judicibus licet uti gladio. ib. 20 Observ 45 Qui damnum facit multetur pecunia. ib. 22 Observ. 46 Ne habeas utilitatem de car- ne bovis labidati. ib. 28 47 PuNum. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Observ. 31 You shall not steal a soul from your brethren, that is, from the Israelites. Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI. Observ. 32 Concerning false witness. ib. 16. Observ. 33 You shall not covet your brother's property, as ib. 17, etc. Observ. 34 You shall not make images for the Gentiles, ib. 23, even if they do not worship them. N. obs. 35. You shall not build an altar of stones dressed with iron. ib. 25. N. obs. 36 You must not ascend to the altar by steps, lest your nakedness be uncovered, 20 last. N. obs. 37 You shall observe the statutes concerning the Hebrew servant, according to the rules handed down. 21. 2. Observ. 38 Concerning betrothing a Hebrew maidservant. ib. 8, 9. Observ. 39 Concerning redeeming a Hebrew woman. ib. 8. Observ. 40 You shall not sell a Hebrew maidservant to another Hebrew. ib. 8. Observ. 41 Do not withhold food, clothing or dwelling even from a betrothed maidservant. ib. 10. Observ. 42 You shall not strike your father or mother. ib. 15. Observ. 43 You shall not curse your father or mother. ib. 17. Observ. 44 Judges may use the sword. ib. 20. Observ. 45 He who causes loss shall be fined in money. ib. 22. Observ. 46 You shall not profit from the flesh of an ox that has been gored. ib. 28. 47 Pun. Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Observ. 47 Puniatur homo pro damno quod alteri obvenerit de effossione foveæ
units.tr: Observ. 47 A man shall be punished for the loss that comes to another from the digging of a pit.

units.la: Observ. 48 Puniatur homo cujus jumen tum alicui faciat damnum.
units.tr: Observ. 48 A man whose beast causes loss to anyone shall be punished.

units.la: Non 49 Fur puniendus vel [s]olvendo pecuniam, vel morte.
units.tr: Non 49 A thief is to be punished either by repaying money or by death.

units.la: Observ. 50 De reponendo, si quis depascens agrum alterius, immiserit que pecus suum.
units.tr: Observ. 50 Concerning restitution, if anyone grazing in another's field lets in his own flock.

units.la: Observ. 51 De rependendo, si quid damni ex igne contingat.
units.tr: Observ. 51 Concerning repayment, if any loss arises from fire.

units.la: Observ. 52 De depósito & de pastione grata.
units.tr: Observ. 52 Concerning a deposit and grazing for hire.

units.la: Observ. 53 De depósito per mercedem, vel propter mercedem.
units.tr: Observ. 53 Concerning a deposit for wages, or on account of wages.

units.la: Observ. 54 De jure quod debet observari inter accusantem & negantem.
units.tr: Observ. 54 Concerning the law that must be observed between the accuser and the denier.

units.la: Observ. 55 De mutuo bestiæ vel vesti-menti.
units.tr: Observ. 55 Concerning a loan of a beast or of a garment.

units.la: Observ. 56 Si quis pellexerit ancillam de-bet quinquaginta siclis puniri.
units.tr: Observ. 56 If anyone seduces a maidservant, he must be punished with fifty shekels.

units.la: Non 57 Præstigiatricem ne finito vive-re.
units.tr: Non 57 You shall not let a sorceress live.

units.la: Observ. 58 Ne injuriam facias Profylitæ justo qui accessit religionis ergo in verbis, i.e. ne fallas, vel decipias.
units.tr: Observ. 58 You shall not wrong a proselyte who has come to the religion, that is, in words: do not deceive or mislead him.

units.la: Observ. 59 In emendo vel vendendo ne ta-lem circumvenias.
units.tr: Observ. 59 In buying or selling, do not overreach such a person.

units.la: Ff 3 60
units.tr: Ff 3 60

units.la: Num.Præceptor. Cap.VI.
units.tr: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Observ. 60 Ne affligas viduam aut Or-phanum.
units.tr: Observ. 60 You shall not afflict a widow or orphan.

units.la: Observ. 61 Mutuum oportet des paupe-ri & indigenti.
units.tr: Observ. 61 You ought to lend to the poor and needy.

units.la: Observ. 62 Ne quæras tuum debitum abegente.
units.tr: Observ. 62 You shall not demand your due from a debtor.

units.la: Observ. 63 Ne fis testis inter illos, qui promutuo accipiunt usuram & dant.
units.tr: Observ. 63 Do not be a witness among those who take and give usury in a loan.

units.la: Observ. 64 Judici ne maledicas.
units.tr: Observ. 64 Do not curse a judge.

units.la: Observ. 65 Ne maledicas principi vel tem-porali vel spirituali. Hoc observant & pro rege sub quo vivunt precantur in suis precibus, & ita illum honorant ac si ex proprio genere esset oriundus.
units.tr: Observ. 65 Do not curse a prince, whether temporal or spiritual. They also observe this, and pray in their prayers for the king under whom they live, and honour him as if he were born of their own stock.

units.la: Observ. 66 Frugum tuarum primitias da-bis secundum ordinem constitutum ne des hysteron proteron.
units.tr: Observ. 66 You shall give the firstfruits of your produce according to the established order, not putting the last first.

units.la: Observ. 67 Ne edas rem discerptam.
units.tr: Observ. 67 Do not eat a torn animal.

units.la: Observ. 68 Non debet judex aurem unisermoni temere adhibere, eiq; credere nisi penitus perspecta re, & cognita etiam alterius oratione.
units.tr: Observ. 68 A judge must not rashly lend his ear to one speech, nor believe it unless the matter has been thoroughly examined and the other side's speech also heard.

units.la: Observ. 69 Ne fis testis impius.
units.tr: Observ. 69 Do not be an impious witness.

units.la: 70 In judiciis sanguinis non debesaequum majorem partem si minorem excedat plus quam in duobus.
units.tr: 70 In capital judgments, one must not, if the majority exceeds the minority, go beyond two.

units.la: 71 Ju-
units.tr: 71 Ju-

units.la: Num. Præceptor. Cap.VI.
units.tr: Num. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Judex & testis non possunt homine reum facere rei capitalis quem primo innocentem fecerunt.
units.tr: A judge and a witness cannot make a man guilty of a capital crime whom they first made innocent.

units.la: Cum majore parte debes ire in controversiam de pecunia.
units.tr: You must go to dispute about money with the greater part.

units.la: Justitia requirit ne pauperum miseresceas injustitia.
units.tr: Justice requires that you not show pity to the poor by an unjust judgment.

units.la: Si videris asinum ofloris tui succumbentem omnino deponito illud.
units.tr: If you see the ass of your enemy lying under its burden, you shall surely unload it.

units.la: Ne pervertito justitiam pauperis in lite sua. Hinc ajunt Rabbini non debemus judicare hominem in aliquo facto ex antegressi peccato.
units.tr: Do not pervert the justice owed to the poor man in his suit. Hence the rabbis say that we ought not to judge a man for any deed on account of an earlier sin.

units.la: Non debemus ferre judicium in re aliqua ex opinione testium nisi res sit pro certo cognita, ut quod illam rem factam conspexerit.
units.tr: We ought not to pass judgment in any matter on the opinion of witnesses unless the thing is known for certain, as when one has seen the deed done.

units.la: Munus a judice non accipiendum.
units.tr: A gift is not to be accepted from a judge.

units.la: Septimo anno, terra relinquenda est inculta, & fructus quem produxit.
units.tr: In the seventh year the land is to be left uncultivated, and so is the fruit it produces.

units.la: Ut acquiescas die sabbathi.
units.tr: That you rest on the day of the Sabbath.

units.la: Non jurandum est per idolola triam contra illum qui inservit illi, nec facies eum jurare.
units.tr: You must not swear by an idol, nor make the one who serves it swear.

units.la: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Num. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Non debemus incitare Israeli-tam ad idololatriam.
units.tr: We ought not to incite an Israelite to idolatry.

units.la: Celebrentur tria festa in anno.
units.tr: Three feasts are to be celebrated in the year.

units.la: Ne ascendas ad festum sine sacrificio.
units.tr: Do not go up to the feast without a sacrifice.

units.la: Necesse est ut omnes comparent ante dominum ter in anno.
units.tr: It is necessary that all appear before the Lord three times a year.

units.la: Non macta bis pascha, dum fermentum est in domo.
units.tr: Do not sacrifice the Passover while leaven is in the house.

units.la: Non relinques extra pascha tuum, quia abominatio est Deo.
units.tr: Do not leave any of your Passover offering over until the next day, for it is an abomination to God.

units.la: Primitias omnium quæ ex terra enascuntur Jerusalem mam adferres.
units.tr: You shall bring the firstfruits of everything that grows from the ground to Jerusalem.

units.la: Non debes edere carnem in lacte. Saducæi edunt quia prohibitum est ne facias in proprio lacte matris suæ.
units.tr: You must not eat flesh in milk. The Sadducees do eat it, since it is forbidden to do so in its mother's milk.

units.la: Orabis singulis diebus, quia dum est in textu inservies Deo tuo corde tuo, & nulla servitus est cordis nisi per orationem, pro Anathematæ habent qui opus sive &c. sine oratione aggreditur, orantque ter in die, & mane & hora quarta pomeridiana, & ante cubitum.
units.tr: You shall pray every day, for you serve your God with your heart, and there is no service of the heart except through prayer. They hold as anathema those who begin a work without prayer, and they pray three times a day: in the morning, at the fourth hour in the afternoon, and before going to bed.

units.la: Non fines apud te habitare[?] qui colunt deos perigrinos vel ster-coreos.
units.tr: Do not let those who worship foreign or dung gods dwell among you [?].

units.la: Est : ut ædificent tabernacu-lum.
units.tr: It is: that they build the tabernacle.

units.la: Non debes tollere veétes arcæ exannulis suis vel foraminibus.
units.tr: You must not take the poles of the ark out of their rings or holes.

units.la: Sacerdotes parent panem pro-positionis & Thus.
units.tr: The priests prepare the showbread and the incense.

units.la: Ut parent candelas & lucer-nas singulis diebus. Observatur in synagogis in memoriam templi.
units.tr: That they prepare candles and lamps every day. This is observed in the synagogues in memory of the temple.

units.la: Ut sacerdotes in fungendo of-ficio induant fe vestibus facerdota-libus.
units.tr: That the priests, in performing their office, put on the priestly vestments.

units.la: Ne separetur pectorale ab E-phod. i. humerali.
units.tr: The breastplate is not to be separated from the ephod, that is, the shoulder-piece.

units.la: Ne laceretur illa tunica fupe-rior,
units.tr: That upper tunic is not to be torn.

units.la: Edant illam carnem quæ fa-crificium est pro peccatis.
units.tr: They shall eat that flesh which is the sacrifice for sins.

units.la: Non debet alienus edere carnem ex sancto sanctorum.
units.tr: No stranger may eat the flesh of the Holy of Holies.

units.la: Ut suffitum faciat sacerdos bis in die.
units.tr: The priest is to burn incense twice a day.

units.la: Non debes suffitum facere lu-per altare aureum suffumigatione aliena.
units.tr: You must not burn incense on the golden altar with strange incense.

units.la: Ff 5 192 UNum. Præceptor. Cap. V. Unusquisque dabit singulis annis dimidium sicli pro Elemosyna: observant hoc secundum facultatem: quia nesciunt quid fuit siclus.
units.tr: Num. Praeceptor. Cap. V. Everyone shall give half a shekel each year as alms; they observe this according to their means, because they do not know what a shekel was.

units.la: Sacerdos lavabit manus suas obs. & pedes in tempore cultus divini.
units.tr: The priest shall wash his hands and feet at the time of divine worship.

units.la: Sit unctio sacerdotum magnorum regumq; cum oleo sancto.
units.tr: Let the anointing of priests and of great kings be with holy oil.

units.la: Ne ungas alienum cum illo oleo.
units.tr: Do not anoint anyone else with that oil.

units.la: Ne facito oleum huic simile.
units.tr: Do not make oil like it.

units.la: Nec suffitus, quales sacerdotes fecerunt, facies.
units.tr: Nor shall you make incense such as the priests made.

units.la: Redimes primogenitum & pecuniam redemptionis dabis sacerdoti.
units.tr: You shall redeem the firstborn and give the redemption money to the priest.

units.la: Si non vis redimere primogenitum appendis illum.
units.tr: If you do not wish to redeem the firstborn, you shall pay its equivalent.

units.la: Ceslabis a cultu terræ.
units.tr: You shall cease from working the land.

units.la: Carnem in lacte coquere de bet nullus Judæus.
units.tr: No Jew shall boil flesh in milk.

units.la: Non interficies reum die Sabbathi.
units.tr: You shall not put a guilty man to death on the day of the Sabbath.

units.la: LEVITICUS.
units.tr: LEVITICUS.

units.la: Observandus est ordo oblatio- nis ex mandato Dei.
units.tr: The order of the offerings is to be observed as God commanded.

units.la: Nul-
units.tr: No-

units.la: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Num. Precepts. Chap. VI.

units.la: 114 Nullum suffitum ex melle vel fermento adolebitis.
units.tr: 114 You shall offer no incense of honey or leaven.

units.la: 115 Non debet abesse sal in sacrificiis.
units.tr: 115 Salt must not be lacking from the sacrifices.

units.la: 116 Sale salientur omnia sacrificia.
units.tr: 116 All sacrifices shall be seasoned with salt.

units.la: 117 Si cætus Israeliticus vel synedrium erraverit & non docuerit secundum legem tum offerat pro se.
units.tr: 117 If the Israelite congregation or the Sanhedrin has erred and not taught according to the law, let it offer for itself.

units.la: 118 Obligatus est qui scit aliquod testimonium contra legem peccantis.
units.tr: 118 He is bound who knows of some testimony against one who sins against the law.

units.la: 119 Sacrificabit peccator pro peccatis sibi cognitis secundum facultatem suam.
units.tr: 119 The sinner shall sacrifice for the sins known to him, according to his means.

units.la: 120 Ne discerpas in sacrificando aves: non separabis caput a corpore.
units.tr: 120 Do not tear the birds apart in sacrificing; you shall not separate the head from the body.

units.la: 121 Non pones oleum supra oblationem peccatoris.
units.tr: 121 You shall not put oil upon the sinner's offering.

units.la: 122 Non pones thus supra oblationem.
units.tr: 122 You shall not put frankincense upon the offering.

units.la: 123 Si homo dubitet de suo peccato nihil obstante tamen debet sacrificare, si est tale peccatum ut pro ipso astrictus sum pro illo sacrificare.
units.tr: 123 If a man doubts about his sin, yet nothing stands in the way, he must nevertheless sacrifice, if it is such a sin that I am bound to sacrifice for it.

units.la: 124 Qui dedit oblationem vel eleelevationem debet dare quintam partem plusquam ejus valor est.
units.tr: 124 He who gave an offering or an elevation must give a fifth part more than its value.

units.la: 125 Unusquisque pro errore suo offerre debet cum ex errore peccaverit.
units.tr: 125 Each one must offer for his error when he has sinned through error.

units.la: 126 Restituet rapinam quisque.
units.tr: 126 Each shall make restitution for what he has seized.

units.la: 127 Sacrificabis sacrificium pro rapina, vel si concumbet cum puella.
units.tr: 127 You shall sacrifice a sacrifice for robbery, or if he lies with a girl.

units.la: 128 Holocaustum facies secundum legem.
units.tr: 128 You shall make the burnt offering according to the law.

units.la: 129 Effleres cinerem de altare singulis diebus.
units.tr: 129 You shall remove the ashes from the altar every day.

units.la: 130 Debes accendere ignem in altare holocausti singulis diebus.
units.tr: 130 You shall kindle fire on the altar of burnt offering every day.

units.la: 131 Non extingues ignem.
units.tr: 131 You shall not extinguish the fire.

units.la: 132 Reliquias oblationis possunt edere sacerdotes.
units.tr: 132 The priests may eat the remnants of the offering.

units.la: 133 Ex reliquiis non facies fermentatum.
units.tr: 133 You shall not make leaven from the remnants.

units.la: 134 Sacerdos magnus singulis diebus sacrificabit oblationem.
units.tr: 134 The high priest shall offer the offering every day.

units.la: 135 Nulli edant ex oblationibus vel sacrificiis istis sacerdotes, i. de Minicha.
units.tr: 135 Let no priests eat of these offerings or sacrifices, that is, of the Minchah.

units.la: 136 Facies opus sacrificii peccati secundum legem. i. Cataht.
units.tr: 136 You shall do the work of the sin offering according to the law, that is, the Chatat.

units.la: 137 Non Num.Præceptor. Cap.VI.
units.tr: 137 Not

units.la: 137 Non edant sacerdotes carnem sacrificii peccati quod factum erat intus.
units.tr: 137 The priests shall not eat the flesh of the sin offering which was burned inside.

units.la: 138 Facies sacrificium reatus secun dum præceptum Dei.
units.tr: 138 You shall make the guilt offering according to God's precept.

units.la: 139 Facies opus Eucharistici sacrificii secundum legem.
units.tr: 139 You shall do the work of the thank offering according to the law.

units.la: 140 Non edes carnem abominabilem.
units.tr: 140 You shall not eat abominable flesh.

units.la: 141 Nō edes de sanctis contaminatis.
units.tr: 141 You shall not eat of the holy things that are defiled.

units.la: 142 Carnem sanctam pollutam debes comburere.
units.tr: 142 You must burn defiled holy flesh.

units.la: 143 Sacerdos pollutus non debet edere sancta.
units.tr: 143 A defiled priest must not eat holy things.

units.la: 144 Adipem comedere non debent, hoc observant maxime nec edunt carnem nisi adipe sublata.
units.tr: 144 They must not eat fat; they observe this most strictly, nor do they eat flesh unless the fat has been removed.

units.la: 145 Non sanguinem, nullam carnem edunt nisi posita sit hora una in aqua, alia in sale.
units.tr: 145 They eat no blood, and no flesh unless it has lain one hour in water and another in salt.

units.la: 146 Ne egrediatur sacerdos templum dum fungatur officio suo.
units.tr: 146 The priest shall not leave the temple while he is performing his office.

units.la: 147 Velato capite sanctuarium ne ingrediatur sacerdos.
units.tr: 147 The priest shall not enter the sanctuary with his head uncovered.

units.la: 148 Ne ingrediatur sacerdos templum laceris vestibus.
units.tr: 148 The priest shall not enter the temple in torn garments.

units.la: 149 Non debet ingredi ebrius temtemplum, neque ebrius debet docere alium.
units.tr: 149 A drunken man must not enter the temple, nor may a drunken man teach another.

units.la: ObserV. 150 Distingues inter animalia munda & immunda: ibi prohibetur caro porcina, lepus, &c.
units.tr: Obs. 150 You shall distinguish between clean and unclean animals: there the flesh of the pig, the hare, and so on, is forbidden.

units.la: Observ. 151 Ne edas immundam bestiam.
units.tr: Obs. 151 You shall not eat an unclean beast.

units.la: Observ. 152 In piscibus distinguantur mundi ab immundis.
units.tr: Obs. 152 Among fish, the clean are to be distinguished from the unclean.

units.la: Observ. 153 Non edes reptile aliquid ex aqua.
units.tr: Obs. 153 You shall not eat any creeping thing from the water.

units.la: Observ. 154 Non edes piscem immundum.
units.tr: Obs. 154 You shall not eat an unclean fish.

units.la: Observ. 155 Non avem immundam.
units.tr: Obs. 155 Not an unclean bird.

units.la: Observ. 156 Non reptile avium edes.
units.tr: Obs. 156 You shall not eat a creeping bird.

units.la: Observ. 157 Distingues locustam mundam ab immunda.
units.tr: Obs. 157 You shall distinguish the clean locust from the unclean.

units.la: N.obs. 158 Observabis & reptilia contaminare hominem dum tangit illa.
units.tr: N.obs. 158 You shall also observe that creeping things defile a man when he touches them.

units.la: N.obs. 159 Etiam cibus 8 horum reptilium polluit hominem.
units.tr: N.obs. 159 Even food of these creeping things defiles a man.

units.la: N.obs. 160 Tangens cadaver bestiae immundus est.
units.tr: N.obs. 160 Whoever touches the carcass of an unclean beast is unclean.

units.la: Observ. 161 Non edes reptile quod reptat supra terram.
units.tr: Obs. 161 You shall not eat a creeping thing that crawls upon the earth.

units.la: Observ. 162 Non edes vermem qui tetigit aliquando terram.
units.tr: Obs. 162 You shall not eat a worm that has ever touched the ground.

units.la: Observ. 163 Non edes reptile supra terram. Hoc appellatur renelh.
units.tr: Obs. 163 You shall not eat a creeping thing upon the earth. This is called renelh.

units.la: Numer. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Numbers. Precepts. Chap. VI.

units.la: 164 Mulier pariens prolem in separatione sua erit immunda, & immunda sunt vestimenta quæ tangit. Observant: mulier dum peperit filiam immunda erit 80 dies, neque cumbet cum viro, neque tanget illum cum digito, sin filium, tum 40 dies & finito hoc tempore lavet se bis, & immergat in aquam postea cumbet cum viro.
units.tr: 164 A woman who bears offspring shall be unclean in her separation, and the garments she touches are unclean. They observe: a woman who has borne a daughter shall be unclean for 80 days, and shall not lie with her husband nor touch him even with a finger; but if she has borne a son, then 40 days. When this time is over she shall wash herself twice and immerse herself in water; afterwards she may lie with her husband.

units.la: 165 Circumcidatur filius die octavo nisi fuerit ægrotus.
units.tr: 165 The son shall be circumcised on the eighth day unless he is sick.

units.la: 166 Mulier sacrificium offeret purificationis suæ.
units.tr: 166 The woman shall offer the sacrifice of her purification.

units.la: 167 Ne tondas pilum faciei.
units.tr: 167 You shall not shave the hair of the face.

units.la: 168 Observabis in lepra regulas ejus & canones.
units.tr: 168 You shall observe in leprosy its rules and canons.

units.la: 169 Ut sit leprosus notus omnib cum iis signis constitutis in lege.
units.tr: 169 That the leper be known to all by those signs appointed in the law.

units.la: 170 Vestimenta infecta lepra sunt immunda & immundos facient alios.
units.tr: 170 Garments infected with leprosy are unclean and will make others unclean.

units.la: 171 Purificetur leprosus cum Cedro & hysopo.
units.tr: 171 The leper shall be cleansed with cedar and hyssop.

units.la: 172 Leprosus tondeat suos pilos.
units.tr: 172 The leper shall shave his hair.

units.la: 173 Leprosus sacrificabit pro mundatione sua.
units.tr: 173 The leper shall sacrifice for his cleansing.

units.la: Cap. VI.
units.tr: Chap. VI.

units.la: 174 Leprosi domus erit immun-da & alios etiam faciet.
units.tr: 174 The house of a leper shall be unclean, and will make others unclean as well.

units.la: 175 Qui habet fluxum feminis, immundus est, & alios etiam facit.
units.tr: 175 He who has a discharge of seed is unclean, and makes others unclean as well.

units.la: 176 Qui mundabit se in aquam le immergat, & mundabitur tan-tum per aquam.
units.tr: 176 He who cleanses himself shall immerse himself in water, and he is cleansed only by the water.

units.la: 177 Post mundationem sacrificet.
units.tr: 177 After cleansing he shall sacrifice.

units.la: 178 Semen quod exit ab homine immundas facit res alias.
units.tr: 178 Semen that comes out of a man makes other things unclean.

units.la: 179 Mulier quæ profluit profluvio vio sanguinis diebus præter sepa-rationem suam, omnibus diebus pro-fluvii immunditiæ luæ sit immunda.
units.tr: 179 A woman who has a flow of blood on days outside her separation, all the days of her flow, shall be unclean in her impurity.

units.la: 180 Ut ipsa etiam in profluvio immunda sit, & omnia alia facit im-munda.
units.tr: 180 She herself is unclean in the flow, and makes all other things unclean.

units.la: 181 Ut pro munditia sua sacrificet.
units.tr: 181 She shall sacrifice for her cleansing.

units.la: 182 Ne ingrediatur sacerdos ma-gnus omni tempore in sanctum san-ctorum.
units.tr: 182 The high priest shall not enter the holy of holies at all times.

units.la: 183 Sacerdos magnus faciet ossi-cium uniuscujusque diei tempore constituto.
units.tr: 183 The high priest shall perform the service of each day at the appointed time.

units.la: 184 Non debes macture sacrifi-cium extra Hierosolymam.
units.tr: 184 You shall not slaughter a sacrifice outside Jerusalem.

units.la: 185 Teges sanguinem Animalis & & avis pulvere cum mactabis hæc.
units.tr: 185 You shall cover the blood of an animal or bird with dust when you slaughter these.

units.la: {a}186 Non facies aliquid quod cau-sa esse poterit ut retegatur nuditas mulieris. i. vel osculari, vel cum illa saltare, vel manum tangere.
units.tr: {a}186 You shall not do anything that could be a cause of uncovering a woman's nakedness, that is, either kiss her, or dance with her, or touch her hand.

units.la: 187 Non reteges nuditatem pa-tris.
units.tr: 187 You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father.

units.la: 188 Neque matris tuæ.
units.tr: 188 Nor of your mother.

units.la: 189 Neque uxoris patris tui.
units.tr: 189 Nor of your father's wife.

units.la: 191 Neque sororis vel paternæ velmaternæ.
units.tr: 191 Nor of your sister, whether paternal or maternal.

units.la: 192 Neque filiæ filii tui.
units.tr: 192 Nor of your son's daughter.

units.la: 193 Neque filiæ, filiæ tuæ.
units.tr: 193 Nor of your daughter's daughter.

units.la: 194 Neque nuditatem filiæ tuæ. est à majore ad minus.
units.tr: 194 Nor the nakedness of your daughter; it is from the greater to the lesser.

units.la: 195 Neque nuditatem filiæ uxo-ris patris tui.
units.tr: 195 Nor the nakedness of your father's wife's daughter.

units.la: 196 Neque nuditatem sororis pa-ternæ.
units.tr: 196 Nor the nakedness of your father's sister.

units.la: 197 Neque nuditatem sororismaternæ.
units.tr: 197 Nor the nakedness of your mother's sister.

units.la: 198 Neque nuditatem patruitui.
units.tr: 198 Nor the nakedness of your father's brother.

units.la: 199 Neque nuditatem uxoris fra-tris patris tui.
units.tr: 199 Nor the nakedness of your father's brother's wife.

units.la: 200 Neque nuditatem uxoris filiætuæ.
units.tr: 200 Nor the nakedness of your daughter's wife.

units.la: Numer. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Numbered Precepts. Chapter VI.

units.la: Obserw. 201 Neque nuditatem uxoris fratris tui.
units.tr: Precept 201. Neither shalt thou uncover the nakedness of thy brother's wife.

units.la: Observ. 202 Neque concumbes cum matre, & cum filia.
units.tr: Precept 202. Thou shalt not lie with a mother and her daughter.

units.la: Observ. 203 Neque nuditatem filiæ uxoris, & neptis ejus à filio.
units.tr: Precept 203. Neither shalt thou uncover the nakedness of a wife's daughter, or of her granddaughter through a son.

units.la: Observ. 204 Neque nuditatem uxoris & neptis ejus à filio.
units.tr: Precept 204. Neither shalt thou uncover the nakedness of a wife and of her granddaughter through a son.

units.la: Observ. 205 Non accipies sororem uxoris tuæ dum ipsa adhuc est in vivis: sed post mortem potes.
units.tr: Precept 205. Thou shalt not take a wife's sister while your wife is still alive, but after her death you may.

units.la: Observ. 206 Ne retegas nuditatem fæmi-næ in profluvio.
units.tr: Precept 206. Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of a woman during her flux.

units.la: Observ. 207 Non mœchaberis.
units.tr: Precept 207. Thou shalt not commit adultery.

units.la: Observ. 208 Non offeres de semine tuo Deo Molec.
units.tr: Precept 208. Thou shalt not offer any of thy seed to Molech.

units.la: Observ. 209 Non concumbes cum masculo.
units.tr: Precept 209. Thou shalt not lie with a male.

units.la: Observ. 210 Non concumbes cum bestia.
units.tr: Precept 210. Thou shalt not lie with a beast.

units.la: Observ. 211 Nec mulier coibit cum bestia.
units.tr: Precept 211. Nor shall a woman stand before a beast to lie down with it.

units.la: Observ. 212 Time matrem & patrem.
units.tr: Precept 212. Ye shall fear every man his mother and his father.

units.la: Observ. 213 Ne vertas te ad Idola.
units.tr: Precept 213. Thou shalt not turn thyself to idols.

units.la: Observ. 214 Nec aliis facies Deos fictiles: nec tibi.
units.tr: Precept 214. Thou shalt not make for thyself or for others gods of molten metal.

units.la: N.obs. 215 Combures reliquias sacrificio-rum.
units.tr: Precept 215. Thou shalt burn the remnants of the sacrifices.

units.la: N.obs. 216 Non edes quod residuum est.
units.tr: Precept 216. Thou shalt not eat what is left over.

units.la: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Num. Præceptor. Chapter VI.

units.la: N.obf. 217 Relinques angulum agri tui ib. 9 pauperibus.
units.tr: N. obs. 217 You shall leave the corner of your field for the poor. ib. 9

units.la: N.obf. 218 Relinques acinos vineæ tuæ. ib. 10
units.tr: N. obs. 218 You shall leave the gleanings of your vineyard. ib. 10

units.la: N.obf. 219 Relinques spicilegium in terra ib. 10 vestra pro pauperibus.
units.tr: N. obs. 219 You shall leave the gleanings on the ground of your land for the poor. ib. 10

units.la: N.obf. 220 Non vindemiabis acines vi- ib. 10 neæ tuæ, si pauper non racem abit.
units.tr: N. obs. 220 You shall not gather the grapes of your vineyard, if the poor man does not take them. ib. 10

units.la: Obferv. 221 Relinques etiam racemos ib. 10 etiamsi nemo colliget.
units.tr: Obs. 221 You shall also leave the clusters, even if no one gathers them. ib. 10

units.la: N.obf. 222 Non colliges racemos vineæ. ib. 10
units.tr: N. obs. 222 You shall not gather the clusters of the vineyard. ib. 10

units.la: Obferv. 223 Non furaberis rem ullam. ib. 10
units.tr: Obs. 223 You shall not steal anything. ib. 10

units.la: Obferv. 224 Non abnegabis pecuniam fo- ib. 11 cio tuo.
units.tr: Obs. 224 You shall not deny money to your companion. ib. 11

units.la: Obferv. 225 Non jurabis falsum in pecu- ib. 11 nia.
units.tr: Obs. 225 You shall not swear falsely about money. ib. 11

units.la: Obferv. 226 Non transgredieris supra ib. 12 verbum quod jurasti.
units.tr: Obs. 226 You shall not break your word, what you have sworn. ib. 12

units.la: Obferv. 227 Non opprimes proximum ib. 13 tuum.
units.tr: Obs. 227 You shall not oppress your neighbour. ib. 13

units.la: Obferv. 228 Non depræcaberis illum. ib. 13
units.tr: Obs. 228 You shall not defraud him. ib. 13

units.la: Obferv. 229 Noli sinere ut merces mer- ib. 13 cenarii tecum pernoctet.
units.tr: Obs. 229 You shall not let the wages of a hired man stay with you overnight. ib. 13

units.la: Obferv. 230 Ne maledicas fratri tuo. ib. 14
units.tr: Obs. 230 You shall not curse your brother. ib. 14

units.la: Obferv. 231 Non pones offendiculum vel ib. 14 animo corporive fratris tui.
units.tr: Obs. 231 You shall not put a stumbling block before your brother, either in mind or in body. ib. 14

units.la: Obferv. 232 Non injuriam facies injudi- ib. 15 cio.
units.tr: Obs. 232 You shall not do injustice in judgment. ib. 15

units.la: Gg 2 233 Non
units.tr: Gg 2 233 Not

units.la: Observ. 233 Non honorabis majorem in ib. 15 lite.
units.tr: Obs. 233 You shall not favour the greater man in a suit. ib. 15

units.la: Observ. 234 Juste judicabis & litem committes, priusquam lege experiare.
units.tr: Obs. 234 You shall judge justly and shall bring the suit before the judge, before you try it by law.

units.la: Observ. 235 Non debes esse detractor. ib. 16
units.tr: Obs. 235 You must not be a slanderer. ib. 16

units.la: Observ. 236 Non instabis contra sanguinem fratris tui. ib. 16
units.tr: Obs. 236 You shall not stand against the blood of your brother. ib. 16

units.la: Observ. 237 Non odio prosequeris fratrem tuum in corde. ib. 17
units.tr: Obs. 237 You shall not hate your brother in your heart. ib. 17

units.la: Observ. 238 Corriges & castigabis illum. ib. 17
units.tr: Obs. 238 You shall reprove and rebuke him. ib. 17

units.la: Observ. 239 Non facies illum erubescere ib. 17 dum objicias ei peccatum coram hominibus.
units.tr: Obs. 239 You shall not make him blush by charging him with sin before men. ib. 17

units.la: Observ. 240 Non debes ulcisci te de homine. i. par pari referre.
units.tr: Obs. 240 You must not take revenge on a man, that is, return like for like.

units.la: Observ. 241 Non allervabis malum apud ib. 18 te, i. non objicies suum malum illi, & in benefaciendo aderis fratri tuo in quo tibi adesse voluerit.
units.tr: Obs. 241 You shall not bear a grudge against your people, that is, you shall not throw his evil in his face; and in doing good you shall be with your brother, in whatever he wishes you to be with him. ib. 18

units.la: Observ. 242 Amabis fratrem tuum ut te ib. 18 ipsum.
units.tr: Obs. 242 You shall love your brother as yourself. ib. 18

units.la: Observ. 243 Non fines duo genera jumentorum coire. ib. 19
units.tr: Obs. 243 You shall not let two kinds of cattle mate. ib. 19

units.la: Observ. 244 Non seres duo genera semi ib. 19 num in uno loco.
units.tr: Obs. 244 You shall not sow two kinds of seed in one place. ib. 19

units.la: Nob. 245 Non edes praeputiatum arboris fructum, i. ante triennium finitum non edetis de illis. 246
units.tr: Nob. 245 You shall not eat the fruit of an uncircumcised tree, that is, you shall not eat of them until three years are finished. 246

units.la: Numer. Præceptor. | Cap. VI.
units.tr: Numer. Præceptor. | Chapter VI.

units.la: N. obf. 246 Fructus quarti anni erit sanctus. | ib. 24
units.tr: N. obs. 246 The fruit of the fourth year shall be holy. | ib. 24

units.la: Obferv. 247 Ne utamini conjectationibus. | ib. 26
units.tr: Obs. 247 You shall not use divinations. | ib. 26

units.la: Obferv. 248 Neque uti licet præstigiis. | ib. 26
units.tr: Obs. 248 Nor is it lawful to use enchantments. | ib. 26

units.la: Obferv. 249 Ne circumcidito pilos ad latus capitis. | ib. 27
units.tr: Obs. 249 You shall not round off the hair at the sides of your head. | ib. 27

units.la: Obferv. 250 Non rades totam barbam. | ib. 27
units.tr: Obs. 250 You shall not shave off the whole beard. | ib. 27

units.la: Obferv. 251 Non facies stigma in corpore tuo. | ib. 28
units.tr: Obs. 251 You shall not make any mark on your body. | ib. 28

units.la: N.obf. 252 Timebitis sanctuarium meum. | ib. 30
units.tr: N. obs. 252 You shall revere my sanctuary. | ib. 30

units.la: Obferv. 253 Ne convertas te ad Pytho-nes. | ib. 31
units.tr: Obs. 253 Do not turn to mediums. | ib. 31

units.la: Obferv. 254 Non consuletis ariolos. | ib. 31
units.tr: Obs. 254 Do not consult soothsayers. | ib. 31

units.la: Obferv. 255 Honorabis doctores & le-nes. | ib. 32
units.tr: Obs. 255 You shall honour teachers and elders. | ib. 32

units.la: Obferv. 256 Non facies injuriam in mensura & judicio. | ib. 35
units.tr: Obs. 256 You shall do no wrong in measure and in judgment. | ib. 35

units.la: Obferv. 257 Habebis trutinas justas & ponderajusta. | ib. 36
units.tr: Obs. 257 You shall have just balances and just weights. | ib. 36

units.la: N.obf. 258 Morte plectantur adulter & adultera, i. suspendantur. | 20. 10
units.tr: N. obs. 258 Adulterer and adulteress shall be put to death, that is, hanged. | Lev. 20. 10

units.la: N.obf. 259 Judex comburet eos. | ib. 14
units.tr: N. obs. 259 The judge shall burn them. | ib. 14

units.la: N.obf. 260 Non sequeris mores gentium. | ib. 23
units.tr: N. obs. 260 You shall not follow the customs of the nations. | ib. 23

units.la: Obferv. 261 Non polluet se sacerdos cir-cum. | 21. 1 ca mortuos non habent templum tamen volunt omnes ex tribu Aaronis abstinere à cadavere. Sed pro proximo suo potest lugere & le polluere.
units.tr: Obs. 261 The priest shall not defile himself for the dead, since they have no temple; yet all of the tribe of Aaron wish to abstain from a corpse. But for his kinsman he may mourn and defile himself. | Lev. 21. 1

units.la: Sacerdos qui interdiu munda-vit se aqua non fungatur suo officio usque ad vesperam.
units.tr: A priest who has washed himself with water during the day shall not perform his office until evening.

units.la: Non accipiet sacerdos meretricem pro uxore.
units.tr: The priest shall not take a harlot for a wife.

units.la: Nec profanatam.
units.tr: Nor a profaned woman.

units.la: Non repudiatam.
units.tr: Nor a divorced woman.

units.la: Semini Aaronis honorem tribues.
units.tr: You shall give honour to the seed of Aaron.

units.la: Non debet sacerdos magnus se polluere apud propinquos suos.
units.tr: The high priest must not defile himself among his kinsmen.

units.la: Nec ingrediatur ubi est mortuus.
units.tr: Nor shall he enter where a dead body is.

units.la: Sacerdos magnus ducet virginem.
units.tr: The high priest shall take a virgin.

units.la: Non accipiet viduam.
units.tr: He shall not take a widow.

units.la: Nec concubinam.
units.tr: Nor a concubine.

units.la: Non inserviet sacerdos nec ib. 17 erit qui habet maculam.
units.tr: The priest shall not minister, nor shall anyone who has a blemish. | ib. 17

units.la: Nec inserviet qui habuit ali- quando maculam.
units.tr: Nor shall one who has at some time had a blemish minister.

units.la: Sa-
units.tr: Sa-

units.la: Theologia Judaica.
units.tr: Theologia Judaica.

units.la: 275 Sacerdos maculatus ne ingrediatur templum vel altare.
units.tr: 275 A priest who is blemished shall not enter the temple or the altar.

units.la: 276 Non inserviet sacerdos pol-lutus.
units.tr: 276 A defiled priest shall not minister.

units.la: 277 Non edit pollutam elevatio-nem.
units.tr: 277 He shall not eat of the defiled heave-offering.

units.la: 278 Privatus nec Israëliticus edetde istis.
units.tr: 278 Neither a layman nor an Israelite shall eat of these things.

units.la: 279 Inquilinus & mercenarius sisit sacerdos non edet.
units.tr: 279 A sojourner or a hired servant of a priest shall not eat.

units.la: 280 Non edet filia sacerdotis deistis si fit prophanata.
units.tr: 280 The daughter of a priest shall not eat of these things if she has been profaned.

units.la: 281 Non edet sanctum præputia-tus, hoc probant ex paschate, hoc non faciunt, ergo non hoc.
units.tr: 281 No uncircumcised person shall eat of the holy thing. They prove this from the Passover; they do not do this, therefore not this.

units.la: 282 Non debet edere fructum non decimatum.
units.tr: 282 He ought not to eat fruit that has not been tithed.

units.la: 283 Non offerent bestiam macu-latam in sacrificio.
units.tr: 283 They shall not offer a blemished beast in sacrifice.

units.la: 284 Non sacrificabis bestiam ma culatam ad altare.
units.tr: 284 You shall not sacrifice a blemished beast on the altar.

units.la: 285 Omne sacrificium ex bestia integra & perfecta.
units.tr: 285 Every sacrifice must be from a whole and perfect beast.
