units.la: 286 Non facienda est macula in bestia sanctificata, vel devota.
units.tr: 286 No blemish is to be made in a beast that is sanctified or devoted.

units.la: 287 Ne aspergas sanguinem ad al-tare bestiæ maculatæ.
units.tr: 287 You shall not sprinkle blood on the altar from a blemished beast.

units.la: 288 Non
units.tr: 288 Not

units.la: Num. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Num. Praeceptor. Chapter VI.

units.la: 288 Non facies suffitum ex intestinis bestiarum maculatarum.
units.tr: 288 You shall not make a fumigation from the entrails of spotted beasts.

units.la: 289 Non facies lpadonem exa liquo masculo.
units.tr: 289 You shall not make an ephod from a male.

units.la: 290 Non sacrificabis oblationes maculatas quas ab Ethnicis mañan- das accepisti.
units.tr: 290 You shall not offer blemished oblations that you have received from the Gentiles.

units.la: 291 Sacrificium non erit de bestia nisi erit octo dierum.
units.tr: 291 The sacrifice shall not be from a beast unless it is eight days old.

units.la: 292 Non mastabis bestiam & pul- lum & e contra in uno die.
units.tr: 292 You shall not slaughter a beast and its young on the same day.

units.la: 293 Non manebit de sacrificio usque ad cras.
units.tr: 293 No part of the sacrifice shall remain until morning.

units.la: 294 Non debes profanare nomen Dei.
units.tr: 294 You shall not profane the name of God.

units.la: 295 Sanctificabis nomen ejus.
units.tr: 295 You shall sanctify his name.

units.la: 296 Acquiesces in primo die pa- schatis.
units.tr: 296 You shall rest on the first day of the Passover.

units.la: 297 Non facies opus illo die.
units.tr: 297 You shall do no work on that day.

units.la: 298 In septimo die paschatis ces- sabis.
units.tr: 298 On the seventh day of the Passover you shall cease from work.

units.la: 299 Non facies opus eo die.
units.tr: 299 You shall do no work on that day.

units.la: 300 Sacrificabis unum agnum cum una mensura, id est, guomer.
units.tr: 300 You shall sacrifice one lamb with one measure, that is, the omer.

units.la: 301 Non edes panem frumenti novi ante Pascha.
units.tr: 301 You shall not eat bread of new grain before the Passover.

units.la: 302 Non edes panem tostum de no- vo frumento ante pascha. 303 Num.Præceptor. Cap.VI.
units.tr: 302 You shall not eat toasted bread made of new grain before the Passover. 303 Num. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Non comedes aristam ante pascham.
units.tr: You shall not eat an ear of grain before the Passover.

units.la: Debes numerare septem fc-ptimanas à pafchate usque ad Pentecosten.
units.tr: You shall count seven weeks from the Passover until Pentecost.

units.la: Offeres duos panes cum sacrificiis Agitationis in die intermissionis.
units.tr: You shall offer two loaves with the sacrifices of waving on the day of the intermission.

units.la: Acquiesce quinquagesimo die post pascha.
units.tr: You shall rest on the fiftieth day after the Passover.

units.la: Non facies opus eo die.
units.tr: You shall do no work on that day.

units.la: Non metes totum agrum tuum sed relinques angulum.
units.tr: You shall not reap your whole field but shall leave a corner.

units.la: Non colliges spicas quæ cadunt inter metendum.
units.tr: You shall not gather the ears of grain that fall while reaping.

units.la: Die primo mensis septimi quiesces. i. primo die anni. i. in Septemb.
units.tr: You shall rest on the first day of the seventh month, that is, the first day of the year, that is, in September.

units.la: Non facies opus eo die.
units.tr: You shall do no work on that day.

units.la: Quiesces decimo die septimi mensis, hic dies, dies expiationis.
units.tr: You shall rest on the tenth day of the seventh month; this is the day of atonement.

units.la: Jejunabis eo die. Manent viginti quatuor horas in synagoga & putant Deum illis remittere omnia peccata præterita superioris anni.
units.tr: You shall fast on that day. They remain for twenty-four hours in the synagogue and think that God forgives them all the sins of the previous year.

units.la: Non facies opus in eo.
units.tr: You shall do no work in it.

units.la: Non edes non bibes illo die.
units.tr: You shall neither eat nor drink on that day.

units.la: naculorum, id est, decimo quarto die septimi mensis.
units.tr: ...nacles, that is, on the fourteenth day of the seventh month.

units.la: Non facies opus in eo.
units.tr: You shall do no work in it.

units.la: Quiescès octavo die tabernaculorum.
units.tr: You shall rest on the eighth day of the tabernacles.

units.la: Non laborabis in eo.
units.tr: You shall not labor in it.

units.la: Accipies palmas cum fructu. Accipiunt palmas & cidron gratiasque agunt Deo pro fructu terræ.
units.tr: You shall take palm branches with fruit. They take palm branches and citron and give thanks to God for the fruit of the earth.

units.la: Sedebis septem dies in tabernaculis.
units.tr: You shall dwell seven days in booths.

units.la: Ne maledicas Deo.
units.tr: You shall not curse God.

units.la: Non putabis arborem in sefeptimo anno.
units.tr: You shall not prune a tree in the seventh year.

units.la: Non coles terram eodem anno.
units.tr: You shall not till the land in that same year.

units.la: Non debes sponte natum metere.
units.tr: You shall not reap what grows of itself.

units.la: Non debes colligere fructum arboris sponte natæ anno septimo.
units.tr: You shall not gather the fruit of a tree that grew of itself in the seventh year.

units.la: Numerabis Jubilæum & annum cessationis terræ.
units.tr: You shall count the Jubilee and the year of the land's rest.

units.la: Perlonet clangor tubæ annuntiando libertatem servorum.
units.tr: The sound of the trumpet shall ring out, proclaiming liberty to the servants.

units.la: Sanctificabitis annum Jubilei in cessare à satione lemente & mese.
units.tr: You shall sanctify the Jubilee year by ceasing from sowing, reaping and harvest.

units.la: 329 Non putabis in anno Jubilæi arborem, nec terram excoles.
units.tr: 329 You shall not prune a tree in the Jubilee year, nor shall you till the land.

units.la: 330 Non metes Iponte natum in anno Jubilæi.
units.tr: 330 You shall not reap what grows of itself in the Jubilee year.

units.la: 331 Non congregabis in Jubilæo frustum de arbore.
units.tr: 331 You shall not gather in the Jubilee a piece of fruit from the tree.

units.la: 332 Obiervabis iustitiam inter mercatores.
units.tr: 332 You shall observe justice among merchants.

units.la: 333 Non circumvenies hominem in pecuniis.
units.tr: 333 You shall not defraud a man in money matters.

units.la: 334 Neque in verbis.
units.tr: 334 Nor in words.

units.la: 335 Non vendes agrum in terra sancta in æternum.
units.tr: 335 You shall not sell a field in the holy land forever.

units.la: 336 Dabis redemptionem terræ secundum legem.
units.tr: 336 You shall give redemption of the land according to the law.

units.la: 337 Ut sit redemptio domus murorum cinctæ in civitate usque ad annum.
units.tr: 337 A house in a walled city may be redeemed up to a year.

units.la: 338 Agrum suburbanum Levitarum non vendes, & rediment illum sive ante sive post Jubilæum.
units.tr: 338 You shall not sell the suburban field of the Levites, and they may redeem it either before or after the Jubilee.

units.la: 339 Non accipies pecuniam in usuram.
units.tr: 339 You shall not take money in usury.

units.la: 340 Non affliges fratrem tuum duriter.
units.tr: 340 You shall not afflict your brother harshly.

units.la: 341 Non vendes illum venditione perpetua.
units.tr: 341 You shall not sell him by a perpetual sale.

units.la: 342 Ne exerceas in eum dominium per sævitiam.
units.tr: 342 You shall not exercise dominion over him with cruelty.

units.la: Utemini servitute Ethnico rum in æternum, nisi illum violaveris aliquo ex præcipuis ejus membris mutilato.
units.tr: You may use the servitude of the Gentiles forever, unless you have injured him by mutilating one of his principal members.

units.la: Non relinques Hebræum in manu Ethnici cum illum vexat cruciliter.
units.tr: You shall not leave a Hebrew in the hand of a Gentile when he oppresses him cruelly.

units.la: Ne ponito lapidem figuratum ut incurves te super ipsum.
units.tr: You shall not set up a carved stone that you would bow down upon.

units.la: Observabis æstimationem redemptionis, hominis secundum legem.
units.tr: You shall observe the valuation of the redemption of a man according to the law.

units.la: Vi voveris bestiam pro oblatione ne ponito aliam pro illa, vel sufficito in ejus locum.
units.tr: If you vow an animal as an offering, you shall not substitute another for it or exchange it in its place.

units.la: Si feceris tunc alia etiam sub certa, erit itidem sancta.
units.tr: If you have done so, then both shall likewise be holy.

units.la: Æstimabit sacerdos bestiam immundam & reservabit sibi pecuniam.
units.tr: The priest shall value an unclean animal and keep the money for himself.

units.la: Observabis quod æstimatio domus tuæ erit prout æstimabit sacerdos.
units.tr: You shall observe that the valuation of your house shall be as the priest values it.

units.la: Sit æstimatio secundum æstimationem legalem.
units.tr: Let the valuation be according to the legal valuation.

units.la: Primogenitus qui primo datus est Deo sanctus erit & non alius.
units.tr: The firstborn who is first given to God shall be holy and no other.

units.la: 353 Si Num.Præceptor. | Cap.VI.
units.tr: 353 If Num. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: 353 Si aliquis Anathema fecerit possessionis suæ, observet ritus constitutos.
units.tr: 353 If anyone devotes his possession, let him observe the prescribed rites.

units.la: 354 Non vendes agrum anathematizatum.
units.tr: 354 You shall not sell a devoted field.

units.la: 355 Neque redimetur ager ana themathizatus.
units.tr: 355 Nor shall a devoted field be redeemed.

units.la: 356 Separabis decimam partem singulis annis Levitis.
units.tr: 356 You shall set apart a tenth part every year for the Levites.

units.la: 357 Dabis decimas de bestiis secundum legem.
units.tr: 357 You shall give tithes of beasts according to the law.

units.la: 358 Non redimes decimam partem bestiæ.
units.tr: 358 You shall not redeem the tithe of a beast.

units.la: NUMERI.
units.tr: NUMBERS.

units.la: 359 Ejicies e castris omnia polluta s. 2 obs. & immunda.
units.tr: 359 You shall put out of the camp everything polluted and unclean.

units.la: 360 Non ingredietur immundus in atria.
units.tr: 360 The unclean shall not enter the courts.

units.la: 361 Confiteberis omnia tua peccata coram Jehova in tempore sacrificii sui.
units.tr: 361 You shall confess all your sins before Jehovah at the time of your sacrifice.

units.la: 362 Non superfundes oleum oli- væ, in oblationem mulieris declinantis.
units.tr: 362 You shall not pour oil on the offering of a jealous woman.

units.la: 363 Pones super illam thus.
units.tr: 363 You shall put incense upon it.

units.la: 364 Facies illis suspectis mulie- ribus
units.tr: 364 You shall deal with those women who are suspected, according to the law prescribed by Moses.

units.la: Numer. Præceptor. Cap.VI. ribus secundum legem à Mose præscriptam.
units.tr: Numbers. Precepts. Chapter VI. Ribus, according to the law prescribed by Moses.

units.la: Obserυ. 365 Nazaræus non bibet vinum neque aliquid in quo vinum est.
units.tr: 365 The Nazarite shall not drink wine, nor anything in which wine is.

units.la: Obserυ. 366 Non edet humidas uvas.
units.tr: 366 He shall not eat moist grapes.

units.la: Obserυ. 367 Ne aridas.
units.tr: 367 Nor dry ones.

units.la: Obserυ. 368 Non edet de cute uvarum.
units.tr: 368 He shall not eat the skin of grapes.

units.la: Obserυ. 369 Non nucleum in uvis.
units.tr: 369 He shall not eat the seed in grapes.

units.la: Obserυ. 370 Non debet tondere Nazaræ omnes capillos toto tempore voti sui.
units.tr: 370 The Nazarite shall not shave all his hair during the whole time of his vow.

units.la: Obserυ. 371 Faciet crescere capillos suos.
units.tr: 371 He shall let his hair grow.

units.la: N.obs. 372 Non ingredietur domum mortuorum.
units.tr: 372 He shall not enter the house of the dead.

units.la: N.obs. 373 Non debet le mortuis pollue- re.
units.tr: 373 He shall not defile himself with the dead.

units.la: N.obs. 374 Tondet crines tempore sa- crificii sui cum implerit tempus Nazareatus, vel alio tempore si pol- lutus erit.
units.tr: 374 He shall shave his head at the time of his sacrifice, when the period of his Nazariteship is complete, or at another time if he has been defiled.

units.la: Obserυ. 375 Bene dicent sacerdotes Israe- litis.
units.tr: 375 The priests shall bless the people of Israel.

units.la: N.obs. 376 Portabunt Levitæ arcam su- pra humeros suos.
units.tr: 376 The Levites shall carry the ark upon their shoulders.

units.la: N.obs. 377 Facient Pascha secundum fe- cundo menle.
units.tr: 377 They shall keep the Passover in the second month.

units.la: N.obs. 378 Edent agnum paschalem eo mense.
units.tr: 378 They shall eat the paschal lamb in that month.

units.la: N.obs. 379 Non relinquas aliquid de agno in secundo paschate.
units.tr: 379 You shall not leave any of the lamb over until the second Passover.

units.la: N.obs. 380 Non franges aliquid de agno secundo paschate.
units.tr: 380 You shall not break any bone of the lamb at the second Passover.

units.la: N.obs. 381 Personent tibiæ in tempore sacrificii, cum est tribulatio magna.
units.tr: 381 Let the trumpets sound at the time of the sacrifice, when there is great distress.

units.la: N.obs. 382 Dabis placentiam sacerdoti ex prima massa tua, vel Collyrium.
units.tr: 382 You shall give a cake to the priest from your first dough, or a collyrium.

units.la: Observ. 383 Facies phylacteria in ora vestimenti tui.
units.tr: 383 You shall make phylacteries on the borders of your garment.

units.la: Observ. 384 Non ibis post cordis tui cogitationem, ne inquiras de Deitate.
units.tr: 384 You shall not follow the thought of your heart, lest you inquire into the Deity.

units.la: N.obs. 385 Custodient Levitæ domum sanctam secundum vices suas.
units.tr: 385 The Levites shall keep watch over the holy house in their turns.

units.la: N.obs. 386 Ne ingrediantur Levitæ in officia sacerdotum nec e contra.
units.tr: 386 The Levites shall not enter upon the offices of the priests, nor the reverse.

units.la: N.obs. 387 Non interviet idiota in sanctis qui non est sacerdos.
units.tr: 387 No layman who is not a priest shall meddle with holy things.

units.la: N.obs. 388 Non cessabit continua custodia in sancto templo.
units.tr: 388 Continual watch shall not cease in the holy temple.

units.la: Observ. 389 Redimes primogenitum hominis & pecuniam redemptionis dabis sacerdoti. i. trigesimo die a nativitate pater accipit filium suum & dat illum sacerdoti coram popupopulo, dicitque ecce offero primogenitum filium sanctum Deo: aut si mavis redemptionem ejus.
units.tr: 389 You shall redeem the firstborn of man and give the redemption money to the priest. That is, on the thirtieth day after birth the father takes his son and gives him to the priest before the people, and says: behold, I offer my firstborn son, holy to God; or, if you prefer, his redemption price.

units.la: 390. Non redimes bestiam mun-ib. 17 dam.
units.tr: 390 You shall not redeem a clean beast. ib. 17

units.la: 391 Sit Levita semper serviens in sanctuario. ib. 23
units.tr: 391 Let the Levite always serve in the sanctuary. ib. 23

units.la: 392 Levitæ dabunt sacerdoti decimas, de decimis ab Israelitis. ib. 26
units.tr: 392 The Levites shall give the priest tithes of the tithes that they receive from the Israelites. ib. 26

units.la: 393 Accipient invicem vaccam rufam integram ad expiationem peccatorum, &c. ib. 2
units.tr: 393 They shall take together a red heifer without blemish for the expiation of sins, etc. ib. 2

units.la: 394 Scias quod cadaver polluita-lios. ib. 11
units.tr: 394 Know that a corpse pollutes others. ib. 11

units.la: 395 Aqua separationis polluit mundos, & mundabit pollutos, hac de re magna mysteria habent Hebræi, & probant hæc ex duobus versibus. ib. 12
units.tr: 395 The water of separation pollutes the clean and cleanses the polluted; the Hebrews have great mysteries concerning this matter and prove them from two verses. ib. 12

units.la: 396 Debes judicare in controversiis possessionum de hæreditate. 27. 8, &c.
units.tr: 396 You must judge in disputes over possessions and inheritance. 27. 8, etc.

units.la: 397 Sacrificabis duos agnos singulis diebus, qui vocantur Tamidth. ib. 3
units.tr: 397 You shall offer two lambs every day, which are called Tamidth [תָּמִיד]. ib. 3

units.la: 398 Addes sacrificium singulis sabbathis. ib. 9
units.tr: 398 You shall add a sacrifice on every sabbath. ib. 9

units.la: 399 Addes singulis primis diebus mensis. ib. 11
units.tr: 399 You shall add one on every first day of the month. ib. 11

units.la: 400 Addes etiam in festo paschatis. ib. 16
units.tr: 400 You shall add one also at the feast of the Passover. ib. 16

units.la: 401 AdNumer. Praeceptor. Cap.VI. 401 Addes in die interdicto etiam unum sacrificium.
units.tr: 401 You shall add also one sacrifice on the holy day.

units.la: 402 Personent tubae primo die anni.
units.tr: 402 Let the trumpets sound on the first day of the year.

units.la: 403 Addes sacrificium primo die anni.
units.tr: 403 You shall add a sacrifice on the first day of the year.

units.la: 404 Addes etiam sacrificium 10. die mensis septimi.
units.tr: 404 You shall also add a sacrifice on the tenth day of the seventh month.

units.la: 405 Addes sacrificium octavo die interdicto
units.tr: 405 You shall add a sacrifice on the eighth holy day.

units.la: 406 Regulas observabis de absolutione voti secundum legem.
units.tr: 406 You shall observe the rules concerning the release of a vow according to the law.

units.la: 407 Non profanabit verbum suum quod aliquis vir voverit.
units.tr: 407 He shall not profane his word, which any man has vowed.

units.la: 408 Dabis Levitis civitates subsidii habitationi idoneas.
units.tr: 408 You shall give the Levites cities suitable for dwelling as their support.

units.la: 409 Non judicabis hominem ad necem cum propria persona adest in judicio.
units.tr: 409 You shall not condemn a man to death while the accused person is present at the trial.

units.la: 410 Expelles homicidam qui interfecit per ignorantiam.
units.tr: 410 You shall expel the manslayer who killed through ignorance.

units.la: 411 Non valebit testimonium unius viri in lite.
units.tr: 411 The testimony of one man shall not stand in a dispute.

units.la: 412 Non accipies pecuniam ab homicida ut liberes illum.
units.tr: 412 You shall not accept money from the murderer to set him free.

units.la: 413 Non accipies pretium redemptionis ab eo qui effugit in civitatem receptus sui. Hh DEU-
units.tr: 413 You shall not accept a ransom from one who has fled into the city of his refuge, to let him return. Hh DEU-

units.la: DEUTRONOMIUM.
units.tr: DEUTERONOMY.

units.la: Nemo sit judex nisi qui bene doctus est in lege etiam si in structus est in aliis humanioribus scientiis.
units.tr: Let no one be a judge unless he is well instructed in the law, even if he is also versed in the other humane sciences.

units.la: Non debet metuere judex impium hominem.
units.tr: A judge ought not to fear a wicked man.

units.la: Non expectes aliquid proximi tui.
units.tr: You shall not expect anything from your neighbour.

units.la: Debes unum Deum confiteri.
units.tr: You must confess one God.

units.la: Amabis illum.
units.tr: You shall love him.

units.la: Discés legem & alios docebis.
units.tr: You shall learn the law and teach others.

units.la: Leges illud caput, Audi Israel, &c. e singulis diebus bis.
units.tr: You shall read that chapter, Hear, O Israel, etc., twice every day.

units.la: Alligabis oracula manui tuæ.
units.tr: You shall bind the oracles to your hand.

units.la: Alligabis frontalibus tuis.
units.tr: You shall bind them on your forehead.

units.la: Inscribes ea postibus domus tuæ.
units.tr: You shall write them on the posts of your house.

units.la: Ne tentate Jehova.
units.tr: Do not tempt Jehovah.

units.la: Ne pangito fœdus cum gentibus profanis.
units.tr: Do not make a covenant with the profane nations.

units.la: Non habebis misericordiam supra illas.
units.tr: You shall show them no mercy.

units.la: Non facies conubia cum illis.
units.tr: You shall not make marriages with them.

units.la: 428 Ne consternantur milites de inimicis suis, neque fugiant in bello.
units.tr: 428 The soldiers shall not be terrified of their enemies, nor flee in battle.

units.la: 429 Non habebis ad usum tuum aurum & argentum ex sculptilibus.
units.tr: 429 You shall not take for your own use gold and silver from the graven images.

units.la: 430 Nec sint Idolorum instrumenta in usum tuum
units.tr: 430 Nor shall the instruments of idols be for your use.

units.la: 431 Dabis Deo gratias post cibum.
units.tr: 431 You shall give thanks to God after eating.

units.la: 432 Diligas peregrinum.
units.tr: 432 You shall love the stranger.

units.la: 433 Timebis Deum.
units.tr: 433 You shall fear God.

units.la: 434 Adhaerebis Deo.
units.tr: 434 You shall cleave to God.

units.la: 435 Jurabis per nomen ejus in vero.
units.tr: 435 You shall swear by his name in truth.

units.la: 436 Evertes idola & instrumenta eorum.
units.tr: 436 You shall overthrow the idols and their instruments.

units.la: 437 Non evertes templum vel synagogam neque templum Dei tui quamvis vetustum, neque delebis unum ex sanctis nominibus ubicunque scriptum reperies, ut ex hoc versu.
units.tr: 437 You shall not overthrow a temple or a synagogue, nor the temple of your God, however old it is, nor shall you blot out any one of the holy names wherever you find it written, as from this verse.

units.la: 438 Homo debet persolvere vota primo tempore quod occurrit in festis.
units.tr: 438 A man must pay his vows at the first opportunity that arises at the feasts.

units.la: 439 Non eriges aram, nec holocausta offeres extra Hierosolymam.
units.tr: 439 You shall not erect an altar, nor offer burnt offerings outside Jerusalem.

units.la: 440 Sacrificabis omnia sacrificia tua in templo Hierosolymitano.
units.tr: 440 You shall offer all your sacrifices in the temple at Jerusalem.

units.la: N.obs. 441 Redimes bestias maculatas pro usu & esu tuo.
units.tr: N.obs. 441 You shall redeem blemished beasts for your use and for eating.

units.la: N.obs. 442 Non debes edere decimam secundam frumenti extra Hierolo- lymam.
units.tr: N.obs. 442 You must not eat the second tithe of corn outside Jerusalem.

units.la: N.obs. 443 Non edes decimam secun- dam musti.
units.tr: N.obs. 443 You shall not eat the second tithe of must.

units.la: N.obs. 444 Non olei.
units.tr: N.obs. 444 Nor of oil.

units.la: N.obs. 445 Non edes primogenitum in- tegrum extra Hicrofolymam.
units.tr: N.obs. 445 You shall not eat the firstborn whole outside Jerusalem.

units.la: N.obs. 446 Non edet sacerdos sacrificia pro peccato & reatu extra atrium.
units.tr: N.obs. 446 The priest shall not eat the sin offerings and the guilt offerings outside the court.

units.la: Non 447 Non edes carnem holocau- obs. sti extra Hierosolymam.
units.tr: Non obs. 447 You shall not eat the flesh of the burnt offering outside Jerusalem.

units.la: N.obs. 448 Non edes carnem ex sacri- ciis leviter sanctificatis antequam fit aspersio sanguinis.
units.tr: N.obs. 448 You shall not eat the flesh of the lesser holy sacrifices before the sprinkling of the blood.

units.la: N.obs. 449 Non edes primitias fructus extra Hierosolymam.
units.tr: N.obs. 449 You shall not eat the first fruits outside Jerusalem.

units.la: Non 450 Non relinques Levitas sed obs. dabis illis festis solennibus semper sua dona.
units.tr: Non obs. 450 You shall not leave the Levites, but shall always give them their gifts at the solemn feasts.

units.la: Obferv. 451 Mastabis bestiam quam co medes vel ovem.
units.tr: Obferv. 451 You shall not muzzle the beast which you eat, or the sheep.

units.la: Obferv. 452 Non edes membrum ex be- stia quæ adhuc vivit.
units.tr: Obferv. 452 You shall not eat a limb from a beast that is still alive.

units.la: Obferv. 453 Debes laborem suscipere & & afferre sancta tua munera Hierosolymam.
units.tr: Obferv. 453 You must take up labour and bring your holy gifts to Jerusalem.

units.la: 454 Non addes legi sive scriptae sive per os traditae quae est ejus interpretatio.
units.tr: 454 You shall not add to the law, whether written or handed down by word of mouth, which is its interpretation.

units.la: 455 Non detrahes legi.
units.tr: 455 You shall not take away from the law.

units.la: 456 Non audies pseudoprophe tam qui prophetavit in nomine Idoli.
units.tr: 456 You shall not listen to the false prophet who prophesied in the name of an idol.

units.la: 457 Non amabis illum qui pellexit ad idololatriam.
units.tr: 457 You shall not love him who enticed you to idolatry.

units.la: 458 Sed semper hunc odio prosequere.
units.tr: 458 But you shall always pursue him with hatred.

units.la: 459 Non liberabis hunc incitatorem.
units.tr: 459 You shall not spare this inciter.

units.la: 460 Non excusabis illum.
units.tr: 460 You shall not excuse him.

units.la: 461 Non tacebit incitatus si nowerit causam contra incitantem.
units.tr: 461 The one who has been incited shall not keep silent, if he knows the cause against the inciter.

units.la: 462 Non debes incitare Israeli tam contra Deum.
units.tr: 462 You must not incite Israel thus against God.

units.la: 463 Expendas oportet diligenter omnia testimonia.
units.tr: 463 One ought carefully to weigh all the testimonies.

units.la: 464 Debes interficere homines depulsos & combures civitatem.
units.tr: 464 You must put to death the men who have been driven out, and burn the city.

units.la: 465 Non aedificabis civitatem ex qua depulsi sunt homines.
units.tr: 465 You shall not rebuild the city from which the men have been driven out.

units.la: 466 Non habebis usum de facultatibus civitatis depulsae.
units.tr: 466 You shall have no use of the goods of the city that has been driven out.

units.la: 467 Non debetis incidere vos ut gentes faciunt.
units.tr: 467 You shall not cut yourselves as the nations do.

units.la: 468 Ne inducatis calvitium pro pter mortuum.
units.tr: 468 You shall not make baldness for the dead.

units.la: 469 Non edes sanctaa abominata, quæ homo sponte rejecit, & abominanda fecit.
units.tr: 469 You shall not eat holy things that are abominable, which a man has rejected of his own accord and made abominable.

units.la: 470 Inquiras in aves quæ mundæ sunt quæ immundæ.
units.tr: 470 Inquire concerning the birds which are clean and which are unclean.

units.la: 471 Non edes morticinium.
units.tr: 471 You shall not eat carrion.

units.la: 472 Dabis decimam fecundam dominis suis.
units.tr: 472 You shall give the second tithe to their lords.

units.la: 473 Dabis decimam fecundam in anno tertio in loco fecundi.
units.tr: 473 You shall give the second tithe in the third year, in the place of the second tithe.

units.la: 474 Relinques argentum & omnia mutuo data post septimum annum.
units.tr: 474 You shall release the silver and all that was lent by loan after the seventh year.

units.la: 475 Non quæres debitum tuum post septimum annum.
units.tr: 475 You shall not demand your debt after the seventh year.

units.la: 476 Quæres debitum de gente post septimum annum.
units.tr: 476 You shall demand the debt from the foreigner after the seventh year.

units.la: 477 Non debes retrahere Elemosynam à paupere.
units.tr: 477 You must not withhold alms from the poor.

units.la: 478 Non debes negare mutuum proximo ante annum septimum.
units.tr: 478 You must not refuse a loan to your neighbour before the seventh year.

units.la: 479 Dabis elemosynam pauperi.
units.tr: 479 You shall give alms to the poor.

units.la: 480 Non emittes servum in libertatem vacuum.
units.tr: 480 You shall not send a servant away into freedom empty-handed.

units.la: Num.Præceptor. Cap.VI.
units.tr: Num. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Observ. 481 Onerando onerabis illum donis tuis.
units.tr: Observ. 481 You shall load him generously with your gifts.

units.la: Observ. 482 Sanctificabis & sacrificabis primogenitum bestiæ mundæ. Sanctificant quidem quia reservant illam usque ad mortem sed in aliquo labore non exercent.
units.tr: Observ. 482 You shall sanctify and sacrifice the firstborn of a clean beast. They indeed sanctify it, because they keep it until it dies, but they do not put it to any labour.

units.la: Observ. 483 Non debes sancta in usum tuum convertere.
units.tr: Observ. 483 You must not turn holy things to your own use.

units.la: Observ. 484 Non debes tondere sancta.
units.tr: Observ. 484 You must not shear holy things.

units.la: Observ. 485 Non edes fermentum post meridiem decimiquarti die Martii.
units.tr: Observ. 485 You shall not eat leaven after noon on the fourteenth day of March.

units.la: Non obs. 486 Non debes servare de agno paschali in diem sequentem.
units.tr: Non obs. 486 You must not keep any of the paschal lamb until the following day.

units.la: Observ. 487 Esto hilaris in solennibus diebus.
units.tr: Observ. 487 Be joyful in the solemn days.

units.la: Observ. 488 Constitues judices & modératores in omni Jubilæo.
units.tr: Observ. 488 You shall appoint judges and governors in every Jubilee.

units.la: Non 489 Non plantabis arborem in sanctuario.
units.tr: Non 489 You shall not plant a tree in the sanctuary.

units.la: N.obs. 490 Non pones statuam.
units.tr: N.obs. 490 You shall not set up a statue.

units.la: N.obs. 491 Non sacrificabis aliquid quod aliquando maculatum fuerit.
units.tr: N.obs. 491 You shall not sacrifice anything that has at any time been blemished.

units.la: Observ. 492 Obtemperabis justitiæ.
units.tr: Observ. 492 You shall obey justice.

units.la: Observ. 493 Non contradices justitiæ.
units.tr: Observ. 493 You shall not contradict justice.

units.la: Non obs. 494 Constitues regem ex Israelitis.
units.tr: Non obs. 494 You shall appoint a king from among the Israelites.

units.la: Num Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Number of the Precept, Chapter VI.

units.la: 495 Non facies peregrinum regem.
units.tr: 495 You shall not set a foreigner over you as king.

units.la: 496 Non multiplicabit rex equos sibi.
units.tr: 496 The king shall not multiply horses for himself.

units.la: 497 Non habitabis in terra Ægypti.
units.tr: 497 You shall not dwell in the land of Egypt.

units.la: 498 Non multiplicabit uxores rex.
units.tr: 498 The king shall not multiply wives.

units.la: 499 Non coacervabit sibi aurum & argentum.
units.tr: 499 He shall not heap up silver and gold for himself.

units.la: 500 Rex habebit legem duplicatam. ter. 1. unum librum sibi emat, alterum sibi scribat.
units.tr: 500 The king shall have the law written out twice (ter. 1.): he shall buy one book for himself and write another for himself.

units.la: 501 Levitæ non habeant partem & hæreditatem cum Israel. Ipsi enim Domini sunt, ubi subjecta erit illis terra Chanaan.
units.tr: 501 The Levites shall not have a portion or inheritance with Israel, for they are the Lord's, when the land of Canaan shall be subject to them.

units.la: 502 Non partem habeant de terra promissionis.
units.tr: 502 They shall not have a portion of the promised land.

units.la: 503 Dabis sacerdoti armos ambos & maxillas ambas.
units.tr: 503 You shall give the priest the two shoulders and the two cheeks.

units.la: 504 Primitias frumenti tui dabis sacerdoti.
units.tr: 504 You shall give the firstfruits of your grain to the priest.

units.la: 505 Primitias velleris etiam dabis ei.
units.tr: 505 You shall also give him the firstfruits of the fleece.

units.la: 506 Inservient sacerdotes per visa ces suas constitutas.
units.tr: 506 The priests shall serve in their appointed courses.

units.la: 507 Non habebis divinatores per sortes.
units.tr: 507 You shall not have diviners by lots.

units.la: 508 NeNum. Praeceptor. | Cap. Vf. Observ. 508 Neque planetarios. | 18. ii Observ. 509 Neque conjectores. | ib. ii Observ. 510 Neque pythoniftam. | ib. ii Observ. 511 Neque ariolum. | ib. ii Observ. 512 Neque habebis qui consulunt mortuos. | ib. ii
units.tr: 508 Nor astrologers. 509 Nor conjecturers. 510 Nor pythons (charmers). 511 Nor soothsayers. 512 Nor shall you have those who consult the dead. (ib. ii Observ. after each, as printed)

units.la: 513 Debes omni Prophetæ obedire non addenti neque subtrahenti aliquid de lege Dei. Non observatur quia Christo repugnant. | ib. ii Observ. 514 Non debes prophetizare falsum in nomine Dei. | ib. 20 Observ. 515 Non debes prophetizare in nomine Idoli.
units.tr: 513 You must obey every prophet who neither adds to nor subtracts anything from the law of God. This is not observed, because they oppose Christ. 514 You must not prophesy falsely in the name of God. 515 You must not prophesy in the name of an idol.

units.la: 516 Obedies prophetæ cujus verba impleta sunt, quæ dixit ventura esse, hoc etiam illos pungit quia debe-rent Christo parere nec parent. | ib. 20 Observ. 517 Non impedies pœnam Pseudoprophetæ nec timebis illum. | ib. 20 N. obf. 518 Sex civitates separato in refugium. | ib. 19·36 Non 519 Non habebis misericordiam cum illo qui interfecit fratrem suum. | ib. 13 Observ. 520 Ne moveto terminum proximi tui quem majores determinaverunt, sive in terræ possessione sive in doctrinæ. | ib. 14
units.tr: 516 You shall obey the prophet whose words are fulfilled, who foretold what would come; this also pricks them, because they ought to obey Christ and do not obey. 517 You shall not spare the punishment of the false prophet, nor fear him. 518 Set apart six cities as places of refuge. 519 You shall show no pity to him who has killed his brother. 520 Do not move your neighbour's boundary, which the forefathers fixed, whether in the possession of land or in doctrine.

units.la: Cap. VI. Observ. 521 Non confirmabit testis unicus rem quam piam.
units.tr: 521 A single witness shall not establish any matter.

units.la: Observ. 522 Facies rectifalsoquod ille mo litus est adversus fratrem suum.
units.tr: 522 You shall do to the false witness just what he had planned to do to his brother.

units.la: Non 523 Unges sacerdotem magnum ut eat cum populo in bellum ut animum militibus addat.
units.tr: 523 You shall anoint the high priest, that he may go with the people to war and encourage the soldiers.

units.la: N.obf. 524 Ut nullum bellum faciat cum populo ullo excepto Chananitico, nisi ante de pace egeris.
units.tr: 524 He shall make no war with any people except the Canaanites, unless you have first offered terms of peace.

units.la: N.obf. 525 Sed Chananitas non vocabis ad pacem quia Deus hoc praecepit bellum, ut non relinquas Animam viventem inter eos.
units.tr: 525 But you shall not call the Canaanites to peace, because God has commanded war against them, that you leave no living soul among them.

units.la: Non 526 Internecioni devovebis gentes Chanaan.
units.tr: 526 You shall devote the nations of Canaan to destruction.

units.la: Non 527 Ne perdito arbores fructifer as in obsidione.
units.tr: 527 You shall not destroy fruit trees in a siege.

units.la: Non 528 Non seminabis nec coles alias quid in valle horrida quae vocatur Aethan.
units.tr: 528 You shall neither sow nor cultivate in the rough valley called Aethan.

units.la: N.obf. 529 Debes decollare vitulam in illa valle.
units.tr: 529 You shall behead a heifer in that valley.

units.la: N.obf. 530 Facies pulchrae faeminae in bello raptae licito (id est in bello a Deo non imperato) secundum legem.
units.tr: 530 You may take a beautiful woman captured in war, lawfully (that is, in a war not commanded by God), according to the law.

units.la: 531 Non vendes illam uxorem quam habuisti in bello, postquam concubes cum illa.
units.tr: 531 You shall not sell that wife whom you had in war, after you have lain with her.

units.la: 532 Non tractabis illam duriter.
units.tr: 532 You shall not treat her harshly.

units.la: 533 Non edes ut commesslatores nec bibes ut ebrii.
units.tr: 533 You shall not eat like gluttons nor drink like drunkards.

units.la: 534 Suspendes illum qui morte dignus est.
units.tr: 534 You shall hang the man who deserves death.

units.la: 535 Suspensus in arbore, ibi non pernoctabit, si aliquis Judæus in crucem agatur a Christianis vel a quopiam tum illi redimendo cadaver sepeliunt in eo ipso die.
units.tr: 535 One hanged on a tree shall not remain there overnight. If any Jew is led to the cross by Christians or by anyone, they bury the body on that same day, to redeem it.

units.la: 536 Sepelies interfectum, vel ipso die quo interficiebatur.
units.tr: 536 You shall bury the one who has been killed, on the very day he was killed.

units.la: 537 Debes reducere ad fratrem tuum omnia perdita.
units.tr: 537 You shall bring back to your brother all things lost.

units.la: 538 Tu non abscondes te a fratre tuo in re perdita sed illi reddes.
units.tr: 538 You shall not hide yourself from your brother in a matter of lost property, but you shall restore it to him.

units.la: 539 Si vides asinum tui locii ja- centem in via quod nimis onustus est sublevabis illum.
units.tr: 539 If you see your neighbour's ass lying in the road because it is overloaded, you shall lift it up.

units.la: 540 Depones onus ejus.
units.tr: 540 You shall unload its burden.

units.la: 541 Non induet mulier vestimen- ta viri. Hinc dicunt Rabbini quod homo non debet in speculum inspicere, quia mos est fæmineus.
units.tr: 541 A woman shall not wear a man's garments. Hence the rabbis say that a man should not look into a mirror, because it is a womanly custom.

units.la: 542 Nec
units.tr: 542 Nor

units.la: Num. Præceptor. Cap.VI.
units.tr: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Observ. 542 Nec vir vestimenta mulie-ib. s ris.
units.tr: Observ. 542 Nor shall a man wear a woman's garments. ib. 5

units.la: Observ. 543 Non accipies matrem cum ib. 4 pullis suis in nido.
units.tr: Observ. 543 You shall not take the mother with her young in the nest. ib. 4

units.la: Observ. 544 Dimittes matrem & postea ib. ʏ accipies pullos.
units.tr: Observ. 544 You shall let the mother go, and afterwards take the young. ib. ʏ

units.la: Observ. 545 Facies loricam ad tectum ib. ⁎ tuum.
units.tr: Observ. 545 You shall make a parapet for your roof. ib. ⁎

units.la: Observ. 546 Non pones homini offendi- ib. ⁎ culum.
units.tr: Observ. 546 You shall not put a stumbling block before a man. ib. ⁎

units.la: Observ. 547 Non conferes vineam tuam ib. ₱ duobus generibus i. mixtura.
units.tr: Observ. 547 You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds, that is, a mixture. ib. ₱

units.la: N. obs. 548 Non edes mixturam quam ib. ϙ severatalique.
units.tr: N. obs. 548 You shall not eat a mixture kept apart in such a way. ib. ϙ

units.la: Observ. 549 Non opus facies disparibus ib. ıı bestiis. i. cum bove vel asino, &c. vel asino & equo.
units.tr: Observ. 549 You shall not work with unlike animals, that is, with an ox and an ass, etc., or an ass and a horse. ib. ıı

units.la: Observ. 550 Accipies mulierem cum do- ib. ıʃ te & sponsaliis & adhæresces illi in sanctitate. Hæc 10. præstanda sunt uxori quam duxeris. 1. Cibum. 2. Indumentum. 3. Concubitum. Hæc ex lege. Septem ex Rabbinis. 1. Æ-grotam curabit. 2. Captivam libera-bit. 3. Mortuam sepeliet. 4. Cibetur bonis ejus. 5. Et sedebit in domo ejus, quam diu vidua est. 6. Filias e-duca-
units.tr: Observ. 550 You shall take a wife with a dowry and a betrothal, and you shall cleave to her in holiness. ib. ıʃ These ten things are to be provided for the wife you have taken: 1. food; 2. clothing; 3. conjugal rights. These are from the law. Seven are from the rabbis: 1. He shall care for her if she is sick. 2. He shall free her if she is captured. 3. He shall bury her if she dies. 4. She shall be fed from his goods. 5. And she shall dwell in his house as long as she is a widow. 6. She shall bring up the daughters until they marry. 7. Sons born of her shall be appointed heirs.

units.la: Numer. Praeceptor. Cap. VI. ducabit usq; dum nubant. 7. Filii ex eageniti erunt hæredes constituti.
units.tr: Numer. Præceptor. Cap. VI. until they marry. 7. The sons born of her shall be appointed heirs.

units.la: 551 Non induesvestimentum va-rie commixtum ex lana & lino.
units.tr: 551 You shall not wear a garment of mixed material, of wool and linen.

units.la: 552 Siquis malam famam protu-lerit contra uxorem suam atq; hoc compertum erit post, erit ei in uxorem in perpetuum.
units.tr: 552 If anyone has spread an evil report against his wife, and this is afterwards proved to be true, she shall be his wife for ever.

units.la: 553 Non repudiabit talis uxoremsuam.
units.tr: 553 Such a husband shall not put away his wife.

units.la: 554 Pœnæ lapidationis sunt judi-cibus licitæ.
units.tr: 554 Penalties of stoning are lawful for judges.

units.la: 555 Non debes punire puellamper vim compressam in agro.
units.tr: 555 You shall not punish a girl who was forcibly violated in the field.

units.la: 556 Cogens puellam accipiet il-lam in uxorem.
units.tr: 556 The man who forced the girl shall take her as his wife.

units.la: 557 Non repudiabit illam.
units.tr: 557 He shall not put her away.

units.la: 558 Eunuchus non accipiet filiamIsraeliticam.
units.tr: 558 A eunuch shall not take an Israelite daughter.

units.la: 559 Spurius non accipiat filiamIsrael: non ad decimam generationem ejus.
units.tr: 559 A bastard shall not take a daughter of Israel, nor shall his descendants, even to the tenth generation.

units.la: 560 Non accipiat Ammonita &Moabita filiam Israel.
units.tr: 560 An Ammonite or Moabite shall not take a daughter of Israel.

units.la: 561 Non quæres pacem Ammonin bello.
units.tr: 561 You shall not seek peace with the Ammonites in war.

units.la: 562 Ne abominare Ædomæumpost. post tres generationes,sed propter religionem & fidem Rabbini lem-per prohibuerunt.
units.tr: 562 You shall not abhor the Edomite after three generations; but on account of religion and faith the rabbis have always forbidden it.

units.la: Non debes abominari Ægyptium post tres generationes.
units.tr: You shall not abhor the Egyptian after three generations.

units.la: Immundus non ingredietur castra Levitarum.
units.tr: The unclean shall not enter the camp of the Levites.

units.la: Habebis spatium extra castra, ut egrediaris illuc foras.
units.tr: You shall have a space outside the camp, to which you shall go out.

units.la: Parabis paxillum ad fodien- dum locum ut sic tegas excrementum.
units.tr: You shall prepare a peg for digging the place, so that you may cover the excrement.

units.la: Ne tradito domino servum fugientem qui habitat extra terram sanctam.
units.tr: You shall not hand over to his master a fugitive slave who dwells outside the holy land.

units.la: Non falles servum istum.
units.tr: You shall not deceive that slave.

units.la: Ne fit fcortatrix ex filiabus Israel, i. quæ adjungit fe viro fine matrimonio.
units.tr: There shall be no whore among the daughters of Israel, that is, one who joins herself to a man without marriage.

units.la: Non inferes mercedem scorti aut pretium canis in domum Jehovæ.
units.tr: You shall not bring the wages of a harlot or the price of a dog into the house of Jehovah.

units.la: Non dabis in usuram Ifraelitę.
units.tr: You shall not lend at usury to an Israelite.

units.la: Potes dare in usuram genti- bus vel extraneo.
units.tr: You may lend at usury to the gentiles or to a foreigner.

units.la: Non differes solvere votatua & promissa spontanea.
units.tr: You shall not delay paying your vows and voluntary promises.
574 You shall

units.la: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Observ. 574 Debes observare omne quod ex ore egreditur ad sacrificium vel Elemolynam.
units.tr: Observ. 574 You must observe whatever goes out of your mouth, for sacrifice or alms.

units.la: Observ. 575 Mercenarius edet ex fructu in quo laborat in tempore laboris sui.
units.tr: Observ. 575 A hired labourer shall eat of the fruit on which he works, during the time of his labour.

units.la: Observ. 576 Mercenarius non accipiet plusquam quod edit.
units.tr: Observ. 576 A hired labourer shall not take more than he eats.

units.la: Observ. 577 Mercenarius non edet ex illo fructu quem demetit.
units.tr: Observ. 577 A hired labourer shall not eat of that fruit which he reaps.

units.la: Observ. 578 Dabis uxori tuæ libellum re- pudii ex forma legis.
units.tr: Observ. 578 You shall give your wife a bill of divorce according to the form of the law.

units.la: Observ. 579 Nec iterum illam accipies si nupserit alteri viro.
units.tr: Observ. 579 Nor shall you take her back again if she has married another man.

units.la: Non 580 Immunis est sponsus ab omni obs. onere primo anno.
units.tr: Not 580 A bridegroom is exempt from every burden in the first year. obs.

units.la: Non 581 Lætetur sponsus cum sua uxo- obs. re primo anno.
units.tr: Not 581 The bridegroom shall rejoice with his wife in the first year. observed

units.la: Observ. 582 Non accipies alterius ollam aliave instrumenta quibus utitur ad vitæ necessitatem.
units.tr: Observ. 582 You shall not take another's pot or other instruments which he uses for the necessities of life.

units.la: N. obs. 583 Non eripies signa lepræ.
units.tr: N. obs. 583 You shall not snatch away the signs of leprosy.

units.la: Observ. 584 Non accipies manu propria pignus fratris sed judex vel arbiter hoc faciet.
units.tr: Observ. 584 You shall not take a pledge from your brother's hand yourself; a judge or arbiter shall do this.

units.la: Observ. 585 Non servabis usque ad mane quod accepisti ex fratre tuo, sed singulis noctibus rdddes. 586 Numer. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Observ. 585 You shall not keep until morning what you have received from your brother, but you shall return it every night. 586 Num. Praeceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: Observ. 586 Reddes pignus domino si ib. 13 pauper est.
units.tr: Observ. 586 You shall return the pledge to its owner if he is poor (ib. 13).

units.la: Observ. 587 Dabis mercedem mercena- ib. 15 rio in eo ipso die.
units.tr: Observ. 587 You shall give the hired labourer his wages on the same day (ib. 15).

units.la: Observ. 588 Non testimonium adhibebit 24. 16 propinquus contra proximum suum.
units.tr: Observ. 588 A relative shall not bear witness against his neighbour (24. 16).

units.la: Observ. 589 Ne pervertito iustitiam pu- ib. 17 pilli & peregrini aut alterius cujusquam.
units.tr: Observ. 589 You shall not pervert the justice due to the stranger, the fatherless, or anyone else (ib. 17).

units.la: Observ. 590 Ne pignori accipito vestem ib. 17 viduae.
units.tr: Observ. 590 You shall not take a widow's garment as a pledge (ib. 17).

units.la: N.obs. 591 Relinques manipulum messis ib. 19 pauperibus.
units.tr: N. obs. 591 You shall leave a sheaf of the harvest for the poor (ib. 19).

units.la: N.obs. 592 Non accipies vel colliges illum ib. 19 manipulum postea.
units.tr: N. obs. 592 You shall not take or gather that sheaf afterwards (ib. 19).

units.la: Observ. 593 Flagellabis impium. 25. 2
units.tr: Observ. 593 You shall beat the wicked (25. 2).

units.la: Observ. 594 Non flagellabis illum ultra ib. 3 statutum legis.
units.tr: Observ. 594 You shall not beat him beyond the statute of the law (ib. 3).

units.la: Observ. 595 Non obturabis os bovi tritu- ib. 4 ranti.
units.tr: Observ. 595 You shall not muzzle the ox that treads the grain (ib. 4).

units.la: Observ. 596 Glos non debet ire ad extra- ib. 5 neum nisi habet licentiam a leviro suo, i.e. a fratre mariti.
units.tr: Observ. 596 The wife of a dead man shall not go out to a stranger unless she has leave from her brother-in-law, that is, her husband's brother (ib. 5).

units.la: Observ. 597 Accipiet levir uxorem fratris ib. 5 sui.
units.tr: Observ. 597 The brother-in-law shall take his brother's wife (ib. 5).

units.la: Observ. 598 Exuet calciamentum ejus ib. 6 glos ex lege.
units.tr: Observ. 598 He shall loose her shoe, by the law of the halitzah (ib. 6).

units.la: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.
units.tr: Num. Præceptor. Cap. VI.

units.la: 599 Mulieris manus amputabitur quæ defensura virum suum apprehendit pudenda alterius, nec excusabit illam quod liberaret virum.
units.tr: 599 The hand of a woman shall be cut off who, to defend her husband, seizes the private parts of another man; nor shall she be excused on the ground that she was rescuing her husband.

units.la: 600 Non habebis misericordiam supra illum qui aliquid male facturus est, sed in ipsa via ad malum interficies illum.
units.tr: 600 You shall show no pity toward one who is about to do evil, but you shall kill him on the very road of his evil deed.

units.la: 601 Pondus & Epha sint tibi justa.
units.tr: 601 You shall have just weight and just measure.

units.la: 602 Recordaberis semper quod fecit tibi Amalechita.
units.tr: 602 You shall always remember what Amalek did to you.

units.la: 603 Exscindes semen Amalechi- tarum & delebis ipsorum memoriam.
units.tr: 603 You shall blot out the seed of Amalek and their memory.

units.la: 604 Diligenter recordaberis ne aliquando oblivisci quod Amalech tibi fecit.
units.tr: 604 Be diligent not to forget what Amalek did to you.

units.la: 605 Debes profiteri Jehovæ supra primitias fructus tui.
units.tr: 605 You must declare to Jehovah over the first fruits of your produce.

units.la: 606 Debes etiam profiteri Jeho- væ supra decimas.
units.tr: 606 You must also declare to Jehovah concerning the tithes.

units.la: 607 Non comedes in luctu deci- mam secundam.
units.tr: 607 You shall not eat the second tithe in mourning.

units.la: 608 Nec pollutas contaminatas- ve edes decimas dum redimantur pecuniis.
units.tr: 608 Nor shall you eat tithes that are polluted or defiled while they are being redeemed with money.

units.la: Pecunias decimarum secundianni consumes edendo & bibendo.
units.tr: You shall spend the money of the second tithe in the year on eating and drinking.

units.la: Sequi oportet Deum in viis suis.
units.tr: It is fitting to follow God in his ways.

units.la: Congregabis populum ut audiant statuta Dei in festis tabernaculorum & in fine septimi anni intermissionis.
units.tr: Gather the people that they may hear the statutes of God at the feast of tabernacles and at the end of the seventh year, the year of release.

units.la: Universi scribant sibi ipsis legem.
units.tr: Let everyone write the law for himself.

units.la: Ne bibas vinum libaminis Ethnicorum. Modo volunt Rabbini quia non sunt jam libamina, ne omnino bibant Judaei cum Christianis, ne contrahant post hanc familiaritatem matrimonium & ita veniant ad fidem eorum.
units.tr: Do not drink the wine of the libation of the Gentiles. Now the rabbis intend that, since these are no longer libations, Jews should not drink at all with Christians, lest after such familiarity they contract marriage and so come over to their faith.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Confitentur ultro se patria extorres, templo carentes Hierosolymitano, non universa sexcenta tredecimque praecepta observare, quod aliqua terram concernant Canaan, aliqua in templo sint peragenda, hinc ad praecepta, quę hodie observari non possunt, vidimus appositam notam: Non observatur, subsistentes interim alia, ut intermissorum defectum ćtum compensent; Confitentur pariter, fœminas cum viris omnibus obligari præceptis Negativis, negantes fœminas ad Affirmativa teneri præcepta nisi ad illa tria de fluxu sanguinis menstrui, de pane coquendo, accendisque lucernis circa vesperam Sabbathi, ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum, Part. V. cap. 4. Quicquid ratione præceptorum negativorum viris prohibitum est, idem quoq; in mulieres quadrat. Verum, quod ad præcepta affirmativa attinet, decrevere nostri, minime teneri fœminas ad præstandum illa, quæ certum requirunt terminum. Hæc ita ne frustra & dixisse & statuisse videri queant, provocant ad imbecillitatem sexus sequiorus ejusq; mollitiem, obsequium item, quo maritis suis obstrictisunt, nec non ad servitia iis ipsis præstanda. Tria proinde solum extant præcepta mulieribus in specie injuncta; vi primi, toto tempore fluxus sanguinis menstrui summa industria sibi a consuetudine maritali cavere debent, neque ad maritos suos accedere, nisi prius aqua probe fuerint abluta. Alterum vult, ut cum in subigendo & coquendo pane occupatæ sunt, placentam unam conficiant, quæ sacerdoti antiquitus dono dabatur, hodie vero igne absumitur. Ultimum huc tendit, accendant nempe circa vesperam Sabbati proximi accedentem lampades.
units.tr: They freely confess that, being exiles from their homeland and lacking the Jerusalem temple, they cannot observe all the six hundred and thirteen precepts, since some concern the land of Canaan and some must be performed in the temple. Hence, for the precepts that cannot be observed today, we have seen the note placed beside them: "Not observed"; meanwhile they keep the others, so that they make up for the lack of those that have lapsed. They likewise confess that women are bound by all the negative precepts together with men, but they deny that women are bound by the affirmative precepts, except those three concerning the flow of menstrual blood, baking bread, and kindling lamps near the evening of the Sabbath, according to Rabbi Leo of Modena, On the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part V, chapter 4. Whatever is forbidden to men by the negative precepts is equally binding on women. As for the affirmative precepts, however, our people have decided that women are by no means bound to perform those that require a fixed time. Lest these statements and decisions seem to have been made and laid down in vain, they appeal to the weakness and inferiority of the female sex and its softness, and likewise to the obedience by which women are bound to their husbands, and to the services they must render to them. Therefore only three precepts exist that are enjoined on women in particular. By the first, for the whole time of the flow of menstrual blood they must take the greatest care to refrain from marital intercourse, and not approach their husbands unless they have first been thoroughly washed in water. The second requires that, when they are busy kneading and baking bread, they set aside one cake, which in ancient times was given as a gift to the priest, but today is burned in the fire. The last precept aims at this: that they kindle lamps near the evening of the coming Sabbath.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Gloriantur Legem Mosis servatu esse facilem, ex Deuteron.cap.30. verf.14. Quod Judice Rabbi Mole Maimonide, in More Nevochim, Part. II. cap.39. nullus in Legibus Mosaicis sit excessus, defectusque, quodque in magno versentur errore, remque non bene intelligant, qui existiment, illas esse laboriosas, molestas, taediosasque, imo, quod homines profani, qui vitiis dediti sunt, eas habeant odio, cum sic loquitur pag.302. Quia tales continent cultus, in quibus nulla est defatigatio, nullusque excessus, sicut in cultu eorum, qui in montibus & locis desertis degunt, qui a carne, vino, & aliis rebus ad fragile corpus nostrum sustentandum necessariis abstinent, qui cultus divini causa hinc inde vagantur, & molestas peregrinationes suscipiunt, vel denique simile quippiam facere cogutur. Nullus etiam est in illis defectus, qui incitare possit homines ad contemtum, vel ad se in vitiis & flagitiis immergendum, ut quibusvis sceleribus fenestram quasi aperiat, atque ita hominem in moribus, virtutibus, & speculationibus suis imperfectum relinquat, sicut Leges aliarum gentium profanarum; Ajunt praeterea de gravitate & facilitate Legis Mosaicae non esse judicandum ex affectibus pravis, sed ex intelligentia hominis perfectissimi, uti rursus inquit Rabbi Maimonides, nides; pag. 303. Quocirca de levitate, vel gravitate Legis non est judicandum secundum cujusvis hominis mali, temerarii, vitiisque pessimis dediti affectus concupiscentiamque, verum secundum intellectum perfectissimi alicujus inter homines, cujus similes, secundum legem, omnes reliqui esse debe-rent.
units.tr: They boast that the Law of Moses is easy to keep, citing Deut. 30:14. According to Rabbi Moses Maimonides, in the More Nevochim, Part II, ch. 39, there is no excess or defect in the Mosaic laws. Those who think them laborious, troublesome and tedious, or who suppose that profane men given to vices hate them, are in great error and do not rightly understand the matter. He speaks thus at p. 302: Because such laws contain forms of worship in which there is no fatigue and no excess, as in the worship of those who dwell on mountains and in desert places, who abstain from flesh, wine and other things necessary for sustaining our fragile bodies, who wander here and there for the sake of divine worship and undertake troublesome pilgrimages, or who are compelled to do something similar. Nor is there in them any defect that could incite men to contempt, or to plunge themselves into vices and crimes, as if opening a window to every wickedness, and so leave a man imperfect in his conduct, virtues and speculations, as the laws of other profane nations do. They further say that the weight or lightness of the Mosaic Law is not to be judged from depraved affections but from the understanding of the most perfect man, as Rabbi Maimonides again says, p. 303. Therefore the lightness or gravity of the Law is not to be judged according to the affections and lusts of any wicked, rash man given to the worst vices, but according to the understanding of some most perfect man among men, to whom all the rest ought to be like according to the law.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Jactant hinc Judæi, persuadentque Rabbini infimæ multitudini, quod non solum decem Dei præcepta, sed totam Mosaicam observare possint legem, imitantes Adolescentem Judæum, apud Matth. cap. 19. vers. 20. qui gloriabatur se omnia mandata a juventute sua impense observasse nominantes hos מ'צ'ו Justos, referentesque, quod & totius orbis sint corona, imo ipsam coronam Creatoris imponant capiti, quodque Deus ipsos non tantum liberet a septem Gehennæ conclavibus, verum septem coronet coronis, hæredesque constituat septem conclavium in horto Eden.
units.tr: Hence the Jews boast, and the rabbis persuade the lowest multitude, that they can keep not only the ten commandments of God but the whole Mosaic law. They imitate the young Jew in Matt. 19:20, who boasted that he had diligently observed all the commandments from his youth. They call these men Justi [מ'צ'ו], and say that they are the crown of the whole world; indeed, that they place the very crown of the Creator upon their heads, and that God not only frees them from the seven chambers of Gehenna but crowns them with seven crowns and appoints them heirs of the seven chambers in the garden of Eden.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Jactant præterea, se aliquid amplius posse efficere, operaque supererogationis, seu potius superarrogationis præstare, extollentes valde suos Chasidim, חסידים sanctitate incomparabili & supererogatoria inclytos, de quibus Rabbi David Kimchi in Commentario ad
units.tr: They further boast that they can accomplish something more and perform works of supererogation, or rather super-arrogation, greatly extolling their Chasidim [חסידים], famed for their incomparable and supererogatory holiness. Of them Rabbi David Kimchi, in his commentary on

units.la: Psalm.103. vers.17. Chasid est, quifacit plus boni, quam præceptum est; Ex nimia arrogantia plus oneris super humeros recipientes, quam Lex imponebat Mosaica, milellæque plebis cervicibus jugum injicientes gravissimum, cum Legi addiderunt Augmenta, Additamenta pari pietatis affectu observanda, placita illa, dictaraque Rabbinorum, circa preces, phylacteria, eleemosynas, decimas, ablutiones, jejunia, festa, sabbataque, מועדים appellata, referentes de his præceptorum reliquiis, quod retardent, impediantque calamitates, designantes per reliquias, vel quod residuum manet præcepto jam perato, vel quod reliquum sibi quisque facit supra legis dimensum, ac sine ulla obligatione, seu tantum ex abundanti perficere vult; De his Magistrorum appendicibus, quas singulis præceptis attexuerunt, passim aguntin libris vulgaribus, legique potest Rabbi Leo Mutinensis in Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum, quibus jungi meretur Antonius Hulsius in egregiis notis ab Abhkat Rochel, quando de Festorum & Sabbathi Adjectionibus pag.314. sic loquitur: משנה תוספתא Additamentum Sabbathi, ritus & preces sunt, quas matutino si exercitio superadduntur, & sacris ad meridiem usque, quæ supererogationis opera sunt, immorantur, ideo vocantur שמים EpiEpimetra, quod ad ea ritibus של יצר matutinis, uti decet, peractis, non obligentur. Unde mirum quod homines isti conquerantur, se Sabbathum non rite observare, & hoc in causa esse, quod Messias adventum suum tamdiu differat, cum tamen plus, quam tenentur, praestare videri velint. Caeterum non Sabbathum tantum sed & omnia alia festa sua habent מוספין, veluti לראש חדש מוסף additamentum Novilunii, מוסף לראש השנה additamentum novi Anni, מוסף לכפור additamentum Festi Expiationis &c. Conveniunt his quae habet Buxtorfius in incomparabili Lexico Talmudico, p.964. מוסף Additamentum, Additio, Auctarium, Supererogatio. Judaei eam temporis partem, quae est inter שחרית matutinum tempus & meridiem, solent festis suis addere, quam precando & laudando Deum, quasi ex abundanti & opere supererogatorio, ut loquuntur, consumunt. Id appellant in libris precum מוסף Musaph, quasi Epimetron, Auctarium, cui certa preces & alia sectiones sacra destinata sunt.
units.tr: Psalm 103:17, says: A Chasid is one who does more good than is commanded. In excessive arrogance they take upon their shoulders more burden than the Mosaic Law imposed, and they lay a most grievous yoke on the necks of the common people. To the Law they have added Augmenta, Additamenta, to be observed with equal devotion of piety: those decisions and sayings of the Rabbis concerning prayers, phylacteries, alms, tithes, ablutions, fasts, feasts and sabbaths, called מועדים [moadim]. They refer to these as the remnants of the precepts, which they say delay and avert calamities, understanding by remnants either what is left over of a precept already performed, or what each person does beyond the measure of the law, without any obligation, or what he wishes to perform merely out of abundance. Concerning these appendices of the Masters, which they attached to the individual precepts, there is discussion everywhere in common books. One may read Rabbi Leo of Modena on the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, to which Antonius Hulsius deserves to be joined, in his excellent notes from Abhkat Rochel, where at p. 314 he speaks thus about the additions to the feasts and the Sabbath: the Mishnah and Tosefta [משנה תוספתא] say: The addition to the Sabbath consists of rites and prayers which are added to the morning exercise and which, lasting until midday, are works of supererogation; therefore they are called epimetra [שמים], because, once the morning rites of the yetzer [של יצר] have been duly performed, one is not bound to them. Hence it is strange that these men complain that they do not keep the Sabbath properly, and that this is the reason the Messiah delays his coming, when they wish to seem to do more than they are bound to. Moreover, they have a musaph [מוספין] not only for the Sabbath but for all their feasts: for example, the additional service for the new moon, the additional service for the New Year, the additional service for the Festival of Atonement, and so on. This agrees with what Buxtorf has in his incomparable Talmudic Lexicon, p. 964: musaph [מוסף] means addition, supplement, augmentation, supererogation. The Jews are accustomed to add to their feasts that portion of time which lies between the morning service [שחרית] and midday, and they spend it, as they say, in prayer and praise of God, as in something over and above and a work of supererogation. In their prayer books they call this Musaph, as if an epimetron, an augmentation, to which certain prayers and other sacred sections are assigned.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Sed quamvis Judaei nostri in Praeceptorum suorum glorientur multitudine, imo licet universorum praeceptorum inculcent, commendentque observantiam, illorum depraedicantes facilitatem, jactentque inaniter opera sua supererogatoria, non tamen versantur in ea opiopinione, quasi observatio omnium praece-ptorum semper necessaria fit ad vitam obti-nendam æternam, quod, teste Rabbi Jofepho Albo,lib.1.de Fundamentis,cap.25. Perfectio humana,quæ vita est æterna,unico Legis Mo-saicæ, præcepto aliquando acquiratur, lecus Lex Mosis alienaret hominem à vita æterna; Imo quod ille, qui multa commiserit peccata toto vitæ suæ tempore, si in fine dierum suo-rum vel unum exequatur præceptum, vel u-nam aliquam actionem faciat, sicut oportet, & moriatur in illo statu rectitudinis, alfequa-tur gradum aliquem e gradibus futuri lecul; Quodque secundum multitudinem præcep-torum augeantur gradus hominis in futuro seculo; Hinc disputatum inter Refch Lekisch, & Rabbi Jochannan , num homo per unius præcepti observantiam acquirere possit vitam futuri seculi? Uti patet ex Rabbi Iliaco Abar-banele de Capite Fidei,cap. 13. Atque inde difficultatem moverunt Refch Lekisch,& Rabbi Jochannan,in Tractatu Sanhedrin,cap.ult.sol.111.exverfu Efai.cap.5.verf.14.Idcirco expandit infernus animam suam, ac aperit os suum ei, qui sine statuto est, & commentatus est ad illud: Etiamsi vel unicum omiserit statutum legis: respondet autem ad illud Rabbi Johannes. Non placet Domino illorum, ut dicas tale quid: Sed sic potius; Modo observave-rit rit unum statutum legis. En Refch Lekisch existi-mavit omnia præcepta necessaria esse ad sanationem anima & perfectionis acquisitionem, atq; idèo ait hoc est, gehennam dilatare os suum contra eum, qui omisit vel unum præceptum legis; Rabbi vero Jochanan judicavit, per liberam præstationem unius præcepti vel statuti, prout decet, sanari animam perfecta curatione.
units.tr: Yet although our Jews boast of the multitude of their precepts, and even urge the keeping of all of them, extolling their ease and vainly boasting of their supererogatory works, they do not hold the opinion that keeping all the precepts is always necessary for obtaining eternal life. Rabbi Joseph Albo, in his book De Fundamentis, book 1, chapter 25, testifies that human perfection, which is eternal life, is sometimes acquired by a single precept of the Mosaic Law, lest the Law of Moses should estrange a man from eternal life. Indeed, a man who has committed many sins throughout his whole life, if at the end of his days he fulfils one precept or performs one action as he ought, and dies in that state of uprightness, attains some degree of the future world. And the degrees of a man in the future age increase according to the number of precepts. Hence Resh Lakish and Rabbi Johanan disputed whether a man can acquire the life of the future age by keeping a single precept, as is clear from Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel, De Capite Fidei, chapter 13. From this they raised a difficulty, Resh Lakish and Rabbi Johanan, in the tractate Sanhedrin, last chapter, folio 111, on the words of Isaiah 5:14: "Therefore hell has enlarged its soul and opened its mouth to him who is without statute." Resh Lakish commented on this: "Even if he has omitted even one statute of the law." Rabbi Johanan answers this: "It does not please the Lord that you should say such a thing; rather say this: provided he has observed one statute of the law." Behold, Resh Lakish thought that all precepts are necessary for the healing of the soul and the acquisition of perfection, and therefore he says that hell opens its mouth wide against him who has omitted even one precept of the law; but Rabbi Johanan judged that by the free performance of one precept or statute, as is fitting, the soul is healed by a perfect cure.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Commendant cum Decalogi præceptis, tum Leges Ceremoniales, appellatas, tum Leges Forenses, Judicialesve, nominatas, negantes omnes has, picturas, typosque fuisse Messiæ, has figurasse ipsius mortem, beneficiaque, inficiantes Messiam Legis fuisse finem, ex Isaco Orobio, in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag. 115. In ultima quæstione petebam, ut assignaretur textus in Veteri Testamento, in quo Deus prædixerit, quod tota divina Lex, præter moralia, fuerat umbra, typus, & figura eorum, quæ tempori Messiæ futura erant; Inficiantes Leges has fuisse convictiones, argumentaque insignia infirmitatum, mortis, condemnationis, intermi-nantia maledictionem, sed Leges has caussas esse justitiæ, remissionis, vitæque æternæ, latas in eum finem, ut per earum observantiam mercedem acquirerent æternam, coramque Deo justificarentur, ex Rabbi Josepho Albo, lib. 3. de Fundamentis, cap. 28. Lex dividitur in tres partes, in Articulos Fidei, qui sunt in Decalogo, in Statuta, & Judicia, sicuti exposuimus cap. 24. hujus libri, completeque sunt singula Præcepta Affirmativa & Præcepta Negativa, ut unaquæque illarum partium exhibeat viam asequenda perfectionis, aut partis perfectiisimus; Ut etiam discerne-rentur, & disterminarentur a mundi gentibus; Utque essent Naturæ & Philosophiæ compendium, sanitatique conducerent humanæ, uti Philosophatur Rabbi Moses Maimonides in More Nevochim.
units.tr: They commend both the precepts of the Decalogue and what are called the Ceremonial Laws, and what are named the Forensic or Judicial Laws. They deny that all these were pictures and types of the Messiah, that they foreshadowed his death and benefits, and they deny that the Messiah was the end of the Law. So Isaac Orobio, in his conference with Limborch, page 115: In the last question I asked that a text be pointed out in the Old Testament in which God foretold that the whole divine Law, apart from the moral precepts, was a shadow, type and figure of the things that were to come in the time of the Messiah. They deny that these laws were proofs, remarkable arguments of weakness, of death and of condemnation, threatening curse; but that these laws are the causes of righteousness, of forgiveness and of eternal life, given with this aim, that through their observance men might acquire eternal reward and be justified before God. So Rabbi Joseph Albo, De Fundamentis, book 3, chapter 28: The Law is divided into three parts: the articles of faith, which are in the Decalogue; the statutes; and the judgments, as we explained in chapter 24 of this book. The individual affirmative and negative precepts are complete, so that each of these parts may present the way of attaining perfection, or the perfection of a part. This was also so that they might be distinguished and set apart from the nations of the world, and so that they might be a compendium of nature and philosophy, and serve human health, as Rabbi Moses Maimonides philosophises in the More Nevochim.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Credunt Leges Mosaicas æternas, immutabiles, non distinguentes inter Morales, universorum hominum mentibus inscriptas, in monte Sinai repetitas, duabusque insculptas tabulis, quas ultro æternas, immutabilesque fatemur, cum ad naturam pertineant universam, continentque vitæ; officiorum, morumque erga Deum & hominem regulam perfectissimam; Legesque inter Ceremoniales, Judiciales, quæ non ea naturali nituntur æquitate, sed tanquam Juris Positivi, ex mero Institutoris arbitrio dependent, proinde mutabiles, atque temporariæ; Credunt omnes has Leges sine exceptione æternas, temporibusque Messiæ sine mutatione observandas, quod latæ sint, ex testimonio nio Scripturarum, לעולם In omnem æternitatem, לדורותם In generationes eorum; Quod semper recordari debeant Legis Mosis, ex præcepto Malachiæ, vaticinia sacra claudentis, deque extremo agentis judicio, c.4. ꝟ.4.5. Quod id conveniens sit, cum Legum divinarum naturæ & perfectioni, cui nihil addendum vel detrahendum, ex Deuteron. cap.1. tum Dei Legislatoris constantiæ & immutabilitati; Quodque quatuor adfuerint requisita, quæ legem aliquam in perpetuum esse latam dicitant, & non in certum aliquod tempus; Scilicet primo quod perfecta fuerit Lex Mosaica, tam quo ad Ceremonias, quam quo ad Juris, moraliaque præcepta; Secundo, quod cum data fuerit, cuncta concurrerint, quæ fuerint necessaria, præcesseritque apparatus; Tertio, quod præparati fuerint animi eorum, qui illam accepturi essent, cum Israelitæ per id tempus ad accipiendam legem essent idonei; Quarto denique, quod is, per quem data fuerit, aptus extiterit, sicuti hæc patent ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, qui in Conciliatore ad Leviticum, Quæst.7. non solum illa firmare conatur rationibus, ipsaque Scripturæ auctoritate, sed simul aggreditur Rabbi Josephum Albo, qui in libro de Fundamentis, de æternitate Legis fluctuat, dubitat-que; que; Hinc quoque Judæi inter Fidei suæ Articulos Legis æternitatem commendarunt, teste Articulo nono: Legem Mosis nunquam mutandam, abolendamque, nec aliam ullam tradendam a Creatore, cujus nomen sit benedictum; Hinc quoque Rabbi Moles Maimonides in Libro de Fundamentis Legis, cap. 9. §. 1. Expositum & declaratum est in Lege, fore præceptum fixum infeculasfeculorum, neque obnoxium futurum variationi, nec diminutioni, neque augmento, sicuti dicitur Deuteron. cap. 12. verf. 32. Omne verbum quod ego præcipio vobis, servabitis, ut faciatis, non addes ad illud, neque diminues ab eo; Et sicut dicitur Deuteron. cap. 29. verf. 29. Revelata sunt nobis & filiis vestris, ut semper faciatis omnia verba hujus Legis; Hinc etiam intelligis, omnia verba Legis præcepta nobis esse, ut semper faciamus ea; Et sic ipse ait Levit. cap. 23. verf. 14. Statutum æternum manebit apud vestras generationes; Sic pariter Judæus Anonymus apud Coccejum in Consideratione Responf. Judaic. cap. 31. Quomodo demonstrant Legem Mosis ad certum tantum modo tempus datam esse, cum Deus non sit sicut homo, qui mutatur & pœnitentia ducitur, cum tam multis Scriptura locis expresse dicatur Legem esse æternam; Et cap 8. pluribus enarrat, quomodo Lex Mosis absque ulla mutatione Messiæ temporibus sint observanda; Ita quoq; R. Isac Abarbanel de Capite Fidei, cap. 13.
units.tr: They believe that the Mosaic Laws are eternal and unchangeable, and they do not distinguish between the Moral laws, which are written on the minds of all men, were repeated on Mount Sinai, and were engraved on two tablets, and which we freely confess to be eternal and unchangeable, since they pertain to all nature and contain the most perfect rule of life, of duties and of morals toward God and man; and the laws among the Ceremonial and Judicial laws, which do not rest on that natural equity but depend, as laws of positive right, on the mere will of the Lawgiver, and are therefore changeable and temporary. They believe that all these laws, without exception, are eternal and to be observed without change in the times of the Messiah, because they were given, as the testimony of the Scriptures shows: "for ever" (לעולם), "throughout their generations" (לדורותם). They must always remember the Law of Moses, by the command of Malachi, who closes the sacred prophecies and speaks of the final judgment, chapter 4, verses 4 and 5. They say this is fitting, since the nature and perfection of the divine Laws, to which nothing is to be added or taken away (Deut. 1), and the constancy and unchangeableness of God the Lawgiver, require it. They also say that four requisites were present which show that a law has been given for perpetuity and not for some fixed time. Namely: first, that the Mosaic Law was perfect, both as to the ceremonies and as to the judicial and moral precepts; second, that when it was given, all things necessary came together and preparation went before; third, that the minds of those who were to receive it were prepared, since the Israelites were at that time fit to receive the law; and fourth, that he through whom it was given was suitable. These things are shown by Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, who in his Conciliator on Leviticus, question 7, not only tries to confirm these points by reasons and by the authority of Scripture itself, but at the same time attacks Rabbi Joseph Albo, who wavers and doubts about the eternity of the Law in his book De Fundamentis. Hence also the Jews among the articles of their faith commended the eternity of the Law, as witnessed by the ninth article: "The Law of Moses is never to be changed or abolished, nor is any other to be given by the Creator, whose name be blessed." Hence also Rabbi Moses Maimonides in his book De Fundamentis Legis, chapter 9, section 1: It is set forth and declared in the Law that it will be a fixed precept for ages of ages, not liable to variation, nor to diminution, nor to increase, as is said in Deut. 12:32: "Every word which I command you, you shall observe to do; you shall not add to it, nor diminish from it." And as is said in Deut. 29:29: "The things revealed are for us and our children, that we should always do all the words of this Law." Hence you also understand that all the words of the Law are commanded to us, that we should always do them. And so he himself says in Lev. 23:14: "It shall be an eternal statute among your generations." Likewise the Jewish Anonymous author, quoted by Coccejus in his Consideratio Responsorum Judaicorum, chapter 31: How do they show that the Law of Moses was given for only a certain time, since God is not as a man, who changes and is moved to repentance, when in so many places of Scripture the Law is expressly said to be eternal? And in chapter 8 he explains at greater length how the Law of Moses is to be observed without any change in the times of the Messiah. So too Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel, De Capite Fidei, chapter 13.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Credunt non tantum Leges Mosaicas æternas, temporibus Messiæ observandas, sed ipsas pariter Majorum suorum Traditiones, Magistrorumque suorum placita perennia statuunt, negantes reliqua Prophetarum, Hagiographorumque scripta, Messiæ temporibus ullum habitura ulum, sed abolenda, excepta Eftheris historia, ex Rabbi Mose Maimonide in Hilchot Megilla, cap. 2. §. 18. Omnes libri Prophetarum & Hagiographorum abolendi sunt diebus Messiæ, praeter historiam Estheris, quidem æque stabilis est, quam Pentateuchus, & Constitutiones Legis Oralis, quæ in æternum non cessabunt.
units.tr: They believe that not only the Mosaic laws are eternal and to be observed in the days of the Messiah, but that the traditions of their ancestors and the decrees of their teachers likewise stand as perpetual. They hold that the remaining writings of the Prophets and the Hagiographa will have no use in the days of the Messiah but are to be abolished, except the story of Esther, citing Rabbi Moses Maimonides in Hilchot Megilla, ch. 2, §18: All the books of the Prophets and Hagiographa are to be abolished in the days of the Messiah, except the story of Esther; indeed it is as stable as the Pentateuch, and the constitutions of the Oral Law, which will never cease.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Afferunt speciatim Legem Cibariam, de cibis mundis, immundisque esse moralem, perpetuamque, iplamque immunditiem ciborum ex se Deo esse abominationi, quippe repugnantem naturæ, sanctitatique divinæ, non recordantes semper Veterum Sapientum Hebræorum effati apud Rabbi Isacum Abarbanelem de Capite Fidei, cap. 13. Quare vocatur nomen ejus חזיר, hoc est, porcus?
