Quia Deus reducturus est אתיהם eum ad Israelem; Afferunt Legem hanc latam, tum sanitatis causa, ut ipsorum consuleret valetudini, prout genio regioregionis, & naturæ foli, quod incolebant, conveniebat, utque ianos illos ac incolumes præstaret, tum ut à cæteris gentibus discriminarentur, imprimis Ægyptiis, & externæ mundiciei redderet observatores, inficiantes illam mere fuisse positivam, typicam, tum spiritualem peccati impuritatem significantem, tum Messiæ victimam mundam offerendam adumbrantem, judicantes, reprehendentesq; nos in cibo, potu, in parte diei festi, Neomeniæ, Sabbathorumque, cum tamen umbræ fuerint futurorum, & mundis omnia sint munda, Regnumque Novi Testamenti non sit esca & potus, præterea-que hæc dæmoniorum sit opinio.
units.tr: They particularly assert that the Law concerning food, the distinction between clean and unclean foods, is moral and perpetual, and that the very uncleanness of foods is in itself an abomination to God, as being contrary to nature and to the holiness of God. They do not remember the saying of the ancient Hebrew sages, cited by Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel, De Capite Fidei, ch. 13: Why is its name called swine [חזיר], that is, pig? Because God will one day restore [אתיהם] him to Israel. They maintain that this Law was given partly for the sake of health, so as to look after their well-being, as suited the character of the region and the nature of the soil they inhabited, and so as to keep them sound and whole; and partly so that they would be distinguished from the other nations, especially the Egyptians, and would make them observers of an external cleanness. They deny that it was merely positive, typical, and signifying the spiritual impurity of sin, and foreshadowing the clean sacrifice of the Messiah to be offered. They judge and rebuke us for food and drink, for part of the festival day, for the New Moon and the Sabbaths, although these were shadows of things to come, and "to the pure all things are pure," and the Kingdom of the New Testament is not food and drink. Moreover, they say, this is the opinion of demons.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Credunt Judæi paucos de salute, vitaque æterna posse hic esse certos, quod in propria conscientia abunde convicti sint de operum suorum imperfectione, quodque post hanc vitam ob peccata commissa ad Infernum pariter possint trahi, hinc sæpe vel ad divinam confugiunt misericordiam, eamque implorant unicam, ut relarciret imperfectionem, vel aliquando de extrema dubitarunt salute, uti patet ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, qui libr. 2. de Resurrectione mortuorum, pag. 230. de Rabbi Jochannan Ben Zacay testatur, quod immiimminente fatali hora fleverit: rogatus causam à discipulis, responderit, duas se videre ante oculos suos vias; vidi unam, quae recta ad Infernum; alteram, quae in Paradisum euntes ducat; Et nescire se, quā ducendus sit; Hinc quoque Rabbini incertitudinem salutis inter leptem res collocant, quae homini sunt abscondita, recensentes diem mortis, diem consolationis, profunditatem judicii, quod nesciat quamnam compensationem sit accepturus, quid in corde proximi sui, quando Regnum Davidis sit restituendum, & quando peccatores sint consumendi; Hanc quoque vitae aeternae incertitudinem confessi mihi aliisq; fuerunt diversi temporis nostri Rabbini; Nec profecto mirum. Quomodo quaeso aliter sentire possent? Cum non nitantur Messiae immutabili justitia, sed operum suorum propria, quae valde est imperfecta.
units.tr: The Jews believe that few can be certain here of salvation and eternal life, since they are abundantly convinced in their own conscience of the imperfection of their works, and since after this life they can likewise be dragged down to Hell on account of the sins they have committed. Hence they often either flee to the divine mercy alone and implore it to make good their imperfection, or at times have doubted their final salvation, as appears from Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, who in book 2 on the Resurrection of the Dead, p. 230, reports of Rabbi Jochanan ben Zakkai that when the fatal hour was imminent he wept; asked by his disciples for the reason, he replied that he saw two ways before his eyes: one he saw, which leads straight to Hell; the other, which leads those going to Paradise. And he did not know which he was to be led by. Hence also the rabbis place uncertainty of salvation among the seven things that are hidden from man, enumerating the day of death, the day of consolation, the depth of judgment, what reward one is to receive, what is in the heart of one's neighbour, when the Kingdom of David is to be restored, and when sinners are to be destroyed. Various rabbis of our own time have also confessed to me and to others this uncertainty of eternal life. Nor is it surprising at all. For how, I ask, could they think otherwise, since they do not rest on the immutable righteousness of the Messiah, but on their own works, which are very imperfect?

units.la: CAPUT XV. De Ecclesia.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV. Concerning the Church.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: CRedunt Ecclesiam Judaicam, unicam, divinam Ecclesiam, quod antiquissima, à Di-
units.tr: They believe that the Jewish Church is the one, divine Church, because it is the most ancient, and was established by the divine

units.la: Divino instituta Numine, in fœdere Dei sit æterno, solaque Leges observet Mosaicas, antiquamq; teneat doctrinam, cœteras tum repudiantes, propriam tum extollentes, partim à summa antiquitate, & sanctitate, partim à privilegiis, prærogativis, aliisque titulis, gloriantes continuo majorum laudes, virtutesque, quod filius Dei sint primogenitus, Exod. c. 4. verl. 22. Quod vocentur populus sanctus, populusque peculiaris, Deuteron. cap. 7. verl. 6. Habitatio Dei, Plalm. 76. vers. 3. Quod appellentur Regnum Sacerdotale, Exod. c. 19. ṿ. 6. Sponsa Dei, Hos. cap. 2. ṿ. 19. Hæreditas Dei, dilestaque anima, Jerem. cap. 12. vers. 7. Jactantes magnifice, quod parentibus prognati sint illustrissimis, Abrahamo, Isaco, Jacobo, numerantes in avis, proavisque duodecim Patriarchas, tot Reges, vates, tot excelsos, & divina virtute viros, quorum nomina cœlo sunt consecrata; Crepantes urbem sanctam, terramque sacram brevi restituendam; Non distinguentes interim tempora diversa, nec considerantes admirandam rerum suarum conversionem, mutationemque, qua post contemptum, trucidatumq; Messiam, à divino abdicati, spretique Numine, non amplius electum Dei sint genus, sed jurati, infensique hostes, Abrahamique facti sint Posteri præ-posteposteri, proindeque non veram Mosaicam formant Ecclesiam, sed falsam, Apostaticam, miserandamque.
units.tr: Power. It stands in God's eternal covenant and observes only the Mosaic Laws, holding to the ancient doctrine. It rejects all other churches and exalts its own. Boasting of its great antiquity and holiness, and of its privileges, prerogatives and other titles, it constantly praises the virtues and glories of its forefathers. They say that it is the firstborn son of God (Exod. 4:22); that it is called a holy people and a peculiar people (Deut. 7:6); the dwelling of God (Ps. 76:3); a kingdom of priests (Exod. 19:6); the bride of God (Hos. 2:19); the inheritance of God and the beloved soul (Jer. 12:7). They boast proudly that they are descended from the most illustrious ancestors, Abraham, Isaac and Jacobi, and they count among their grandfathers and great-grandfathers the twelve Patriarchs, so many kings, prophets, and men of high and divine virtue, whose names have been consecrated in heaven. They chatter that the holy city and the holy land will soon be restored to them. Meanwhile they do not distinguish the different times, nor do they consider the remarkable change and reversal of their affairs. After they despised and slaughtered the Messiah, they were cast off by God and rejected by the divine Power. They are no longer the chosen race of God, but have become sworn and hostile enemies, and they are the descendants of Abraham only in name, generation after generation. Therefore they do not form the true Mosaic Church, but a false, apostate and pitiable one.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Gloriantur Ecclesiam Judaicam, unicam divinam esse Ecclesiam, quod soli vindices acerrimi sint gloriæ, majestatisque divinæ, veritatis cœlestis sint Assertores, unicique Patroni, in præceptis incedant Mosaicis, Prophetarumque observent monita, quod jure hæreditario quatuor speciales possideant præ aliis gentibus prærogativas, Terram Canaan in ipe, postliminio repetendam, Legem Mosaicam, Prophetias, & mortuorum Resurrectionem, ex Rabbi Bechai in Kad Hakkemach, sol. 8. Quatuor sunt speciales Israelis dignitates, quas in reliquis gentibus reperire non est, ut sunt, Terra Canaan, Lex, Prophetia, & mortuorum Resurrectio; Ex eodem in Commentario ad Deuteron. cap. 18. Quatuor sunt res, quibus non fuit dignus ullus populus, nisi Israel, nempe Prophetia, Lex, Terra Israel, & vivificatio mortuorum; Hinc in quotidianis precibus, in Ritualibus obviis, superbe satis clamant: Benedictus tu Domine, qui nos elegisti præ omnibus populis, præceptis tuis sanctificasti, & Legem nobis dedisti; Hinc in Sabbathi die ingenti deblaterant saltu: Tu es unus, & nomen tuum unum est, quisnam populus similis est populo tuo Israel. Et, o vos beatos de domo Israel? Vos enim Deus elegit, & Legem pro hæreditate vobis dedit in monte Sinai; Hinc quoq; gratias Deo agunt in precibus matutinis, quod formati sint Judæi, non gentes: Benedictus tu Deus, Deus noster, Rex mundi, quod me genetilem non fecerus; Hinc pariter in Catechesi Judaica, ad Quæst. 1. qua quæritur: Quis tu es, mi Fili? Respondetur: Servus tuus sum, & Dominum Deum cœlestem timeo, eumque laudo, & extollo, quod me hominem condiderit, Judæumque fecerit.
units.tr: They boast that the Jewish Church is the one divine Church, because they alone are the most zealous defenders of divine glory and majesty, the advocates and sole patrons of heavenly truth. They walk in the Mosaic precepts and observe the admonitions of the prophets. They claim that by hereditary right they alone possess four special prerogatives beyond other nations: the land of Canaan, to be recovered by right of return; the Mosaic Law; the Prophecies; and the resurrection of the dead. This is from Rabbi Bechai in Kad Hakkemach, fol. 8: There are four special dignities of Israel, which are not to be found among the other nations: namely the land of Canaan, the Law, the Prophecy, and the resurrection of the dead. From the same author, in his Commentary on Deuteronomy ch. 18: There are four things for which no people was worthy except Israel: namely Prophecy, the Law, the land of Israel, and the quickening of the dead. Hence in their daily prayers and their common rituals they cry out quite arrogantly: Blessed are you, O Lord, who have chosen us above all peoples, sanctified us by your precepts, and given us the Law. Hence on the Sabbath day they leap about in great exultation: You are one, and your name is one; what people is like your people Israel? And O you blessed of the house of Israel! For God has chosen you and given you the Law as your inheritance on Mount Sinai. Hence also they give thanks to God in their morning prayers that they were made Jews and not Gentiles: Blessed are you, God, our God, King of the world, who has not made me a Gentile. Likewise in the Jewish Catechism, at Question 1, which asks: Who are you, my son? The answer is given: I am your servant, and I fear the Lord God of heaven, and I praise and extol him, who made me a man and made me a Jew.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Gloriantur Ecclesiam Judaicam unicam divinam esse Ecclesiam, quod Sabbatha sancta colant, per quæ liberentur ex gravissimis periculis atque calamitatibus, ex Tractatu Talmudico Schabbath, sol. 118. Quicunque stabilit vel observat tria epula in Sabbatho, is liberatur ex tribus afflictionibus. A doloribus Messiæ, a judicio Gehennæ, & a bello Gog & Magog; Quorumq; observantia æquiparari debeat observantiæ totius Legis Mosaicæ, & per quæ distinguantur ab aliis populis, quibus Lex de observatione Sabbathi non fuerit lata, ex Catechesi Judaica, Responsione ad Quæst. 13. Propterea de Sabbatho, quod signum memoriale creationis est, dicit. cit Scriptura Exod.cap 31. verf.17. Inter me& filios Israel, signum hoc æternum est, hoc est, signum hoc principium est, & fundamentum magnum inter me & filios Israel, in cujus populi corde lex mea est, Esai.cap.51.verf.7. quo ab omnibus cæteris populis & linguis distinguuntur. Et ob hanc causam Sabbathum totam legem pondere æquat; Hinc tritum illud Hebræorum, Qui negat Sabbathum, est, ac si neget legem integram; Hinc quoque in precibus Sabbathinis inter alia exclamant: Domine Deus noster non dedisti illud Sabbathum gentibus terra, neque hereditate illud dedisti Rex noster idololatris, & requie ejus non habitabunt incircumcisi, quoniam Israeli populo tuo dedisti illud ex amore erga semen Jacobi, quod elegisti; Quod ex nuperrimo illorum Doctore, Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, quam maxime patet, qui in libello de Creatione, Problemate 8. ad Quæstionem: An observatio Sabbathi tantummodo locum habuerit inter Hebræos, an vero ea etiam communis fuerit omnibus gentibus? Respondet, quod non solum ex Antiquis Sapientibus nonnulli in diversis locis, inprimis ad verba Exod. cap.16. v.19. commemorent, Sabbathi observationem solis Israelitis jussam fuisse; Imo Viri Synagogæ magnæ, qui vixerunt temporibus Esdræ, idem in Sabbathinis inculcaverint precibus; verum etiam illud manifeste ex ipsa appareat Scriptura, quod Exod. cap.31. vers.13. dicatur: Loquere filiis Israelis, & dic illis, videte, ut Sabbathum meum colatis: quia signum est inter me & vos, in generationibus ve-stris, ut sciatis me Dominum esse, qui sanctifico vos. Similiter quoque Ezech. dicat cap. 20. vers 12. Insuper & Sabbatha mea dedi illis, ut essent signum inter me, & illos, & scirent quod ego sum Dominus sanctificans eos. In quibus vocibus nihil aliud innuatur, quam quod Dominus Deus Israelitis dederit Sabbathum veluti signaculum, quo eos sibi sanctificavit, populumque suum fecit. Tandem ut sententiam suam firmaret Menasseh, subjungit pag. 34, 35. Hæc opinio firmari etiam potest ex eo, quod inter præcepta veterum septem ponantur, ad quæ observanda obstricti sunt filii Noachi, per quos intelliguntur omnes reliquæ nationes mundi. Præcepta autem ista hæc sunt: Ne committant Idololatriam, ne occidant, ne adulterio se inquinent, ne furentur, ne blasphement nomen Domini, ne vescantur membro vivi animalis, ut constituantur judices, qui curent, ut hæc præcepta observentur. At inter illa nullam Sabbathi mentionem fieri videmus. Sed vero licet isti omnes non obligentur ad cultum Sabbathi: nihilominus tamen omnes tenentur credere illud, quod Sabbathum significat, atque idcirco etiam recordari illius diei. Nam propterea arbitror, cum præceptum SabSabbathi datur, duas diversas voces usurpari in Decalogo: in Exodo enim dicitur, זכור Recordari diei Sabbathi: sed in Deuteronomio, שמור Observare diem Sabbathi: nam Israelitae sunt obligati ad observandum Sabbathum: reliquae vero nationes, ut ejus recordentur, & hujus recordationis respectu est generale praeceptum.
units.tr: They boast that the Jewish Church is the one divine Church, because they keep the holy Sabbaths, through which they are freed from the gravest dangers and calamities. This is from the Talmudic Tractate Shabbath, fol. 118: Whoever establishes or observes three meals on the Sabbath is delivered from three afflictions: from the birth pangs of the Messiah, from the judgment of Gehenna, and from the war of Gog and Magog. Its observance is to be equated with the observance of the whole Mosaic Law, and by it they are distinguished from other peoples, to whom the Law concerning the observance of the Sabbath was not given. This is from the Jewish Catechism, the answer to Question 13: Therefore concerning the Sabbath, which is the memorial sign of creation, Scripture says (Exod. 31:17): "Between me and the children of Israel this is a sign forever," that is, this sign is the beginning and the great foundation between me and the children of Israel, in whose people my law is in the heart (Isa. 51:7), by which they are distinguished from all other peoples and tongues. For this reason the Sabbath weighs equal to the whole Law. Hence the familiar saying of the Hebrews: He who denies the Sabbath is as if he denied the whole Law. Hence also in their Sabbath prayers they cry out among other things: O Lord our God, you did not give this Sabbath to the nations of the lands, nor did you give it as an inheritance, our King, to idolaters, and the uncircumcised shall not dwell in its rest; but you gave it to your people Israel out of love for the seed of Jacob, whom you chose. This is made very clear by their most recent teacher, Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, who in his little book On the Creation, Problem 8, answers the question: Was the observance of the Sabbath confined to the Hebrews only, or was it common to all nations? He replies that some of the Ancient Sages in various places, especially on the words of Exod. 16:19, record that the observance of the Sabbath was commanded to the Israelites alone. Moreover, the men of the Great Synagogue, who lived in the time of Ezra, inculcated the same thing in their Sabbath prayers. Indeed, it also appears plainly from Scripture itself that it is said (Exod. 31:13): Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: See that you keep my Sabbath, because it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you. Likewise Ezekiel says (20:12): Moreover I gave them my Sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them. In these words nothing else is implied than that the Lord God gave the Sabbath to the Israelites as a seal by which he sanctified them to himself and made them his people. Finally, to strengthen his opinion, Menasseh adds (pp. 34, 35): This opinion can also be confirmed by the fact that among the seven precepts of the ancients, which the sons of Noah were bound to observe, and by whom all the remaining nations of the world are meant, these precepts are listed: that they should not commit idolatry, nor kill, nor defile themselves with adultery, nor steal, nor blaspheme the name of the Lord, nor eat the limb of a living animal, and that judges be appointed to see that these precepts are observed. Yet we see that no mention of the Sabbath is made among them. But although all these peoples are not bound to the worship of the Sabbath, nevertheless all are bound to believe what the Sabbath signifies, and therefore also to remember that day. For this reason, I think, when the precept of the Sabbath is given, two different words are used in the Decalogue: in Exodus it is said zakhor [זכור], to remember the Sabbath day; but in Deuteronomy shamor [שמור], to observe the Sabbath day. For the Israelites are obliged to observe the Sabbath, while the other nations are to remember it, and with respect to this remembrance there is a general precept.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Jactant Ecclesiam Judaicam, unicam, perfectam esse Ecclesiam, quod populus Dei sint circumcisus, proinde perfectus, praeputium vero vitium sit maximum, imo pejus omnibus reliquis vitiis, ex Rabbi Eliesere in Pirke c. 29.
units.tr: They boast that the Jewish Church is the one and perfect Church, because the people of God are circumcised and therefore perfect, while the foreskin is the greatest vice, indeed worse than all other vices, according to Rabbi Eliezer in Pirke, ch. 29.

units.la: Octava tentatio fuit: Cum Abram natus esset nonaginta novem annos, dixit ei Sanctus Benedictus, Genes. cap. 17. vers. 1. Ambula coram me, & esto perfectus. Dixit illi: Nondum es perfectus coram me nisi circumcideris carnem praeputii tui, quod in te est. Ambula coram me, atque esto perfectus: quia praeputium impurius est omnibus sordibus. Sicut dicitur Jesai. cap. 52. vers. 1. Non veniet in te amplius circumcisus & pollutus. Praeputium enim vitium est pejus omnibus vitiis. Circumcide carnem praeputii, tu ambula coram me, atque sis perfectus; Quod Abrahamus in praeputio fuerit sordidus, abominabilis, nullosque bonos protulerit fructus, post praeputii vero amputationem purus ac perfectus fuerit reditus, ditus, tuncque bonos producere inceperit fructus, ex citato Rabbi Eliefere in Pirke, cap. 29. Sic quoque Pater noster Abraham, cum nondum circumcisus erat, fructus quem proferebat, non erat bonus in operibus illius, & prophanus fuit habitus super altare, postquam vero circumcisus fuit, fructus, quem producebat, erat elegans in operibus ejus, & selectum erat vinum super altare, tanquam libaminis. Quod incircumcisi aeterno exitio sint devoti, ex Rabbi Bechai in Kat Hakkemach, sol. 43. Omnes praeputiati descendunt in Gehennam: Contra vero circumcisi ab hoc supplicio sint immunes; Quod circumcisi in sanguine suo vivant, ex Ezech. cap. 16. verf. 6. Id est, per circumcisionis sanguinem vitam acquirant aeternam, sicuti pluribus enarrabimus capite sequenti, de Sacramentis Ecclesiae Judaicae.
units.tr: The eighth temptation came when Abram was ninety-nine years old. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him (Gen. 17:1): "Walk before me and be perfect." He said to him: "You are not yet perfect before me unless you circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, which is in you. Walk before me and be perfect, for the foreskin is more unclean than all filth." As it is said (Isa. 52:1): "There shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean." For the foreskin is a vice worse than all vices. Circumcise the flesh of the foreskin; you walk before me and be perfect. Abraham, while he was in his foreskin, was filthy and abominable and brought forth no good fruit; but after the removal of the foreskin he returned pure and perfect, and then he began to bring forth good fruit, according to the Rabbi Eliezer cited in Pirke, ch. 29. So too our father Abraham, when he was not yet circumcised, the fruit he produced was not good in his works, and it was held profane upon the altar; but after he was circumcised, the fruit he produced was choice in his works, and the wine upon the altar was selected, as a libation. That the uncircumcised are devoted to eternal destruction, according to Rabbi Bechai in Kat Hakkemach, fol. 43: "All the uncircumcised go down into Gehenna." On the contrary, the circumcised are exempt from this punishment; that the circumcised live in their own blood, according to Ezek. 16:6. That is, through the blood of circumcision they acquire eternal life, as we shall explain more fully in the following chapter, on the Sacraments of the Jewish Church.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Jactant Ecclesiam Judaicam esse unam, sanctam Ecclesiam, extollentes Israelitas perfectos Justos, Sanctos, gloriantes multa de sanctitate, virtutibus, miraculis illustrium membrorum Ecclesiae Judaicae, non negantes interim, sed maxime quoque deplorantes inter Ecclesiae suae membra Intermedios, quorum opera bona cum malis haerent pendeantque in aequilibrio; Et נמורים רשעים Plene malos, improbosque, quorum opera mala multis parasangis superant pauca bona, quorumque flagitiis non solum templum secundum sit destructum, sed hodie quoque adventus impediatur Messiæ; Jactant multi Ecclesiæ sua membra sancta ipsis Angelis esse sanctiora & puriora, quod non solum diversis Rabbinorum, ex quorum ore sæpius sæpiusque audivi, probari posset testimoniis, sed in ipso confirmatur Zennorenna, qui de Jacobo fingit Patriarcha, Angelum ipsi propterea haud prævalere potuisse, quod nullum in ipso reperierit peccatum, pag. 42.
units.tr: They boast that the Jewish Church is one holy Church, extolling the Israelites as perfect, just and holy, and boasting much of the holiness, virtues and miracles of the illustrious members of the Jewish Church. Meanwhile they do not deny, but rather especially deplore, among the members of their Church the "Intermediates" [בינונים], whose good works hang in equilibrium with their bad ones; and the completely wicked and depraved [נמורים רשעים], whose evil works far outweigh the few good ones, and by whose crimes not only was the Second Temple destroyed, but even today the coming of the Messiah is hindered. Many boast that the holy members of their Church are holier and purer than the angels themselves. This could be proved not only by various testimonies of the rabbis, from whose mouth I have heard it often and again, but it is also confirmed in Zennorenna, who, of the patriarch Jacob, imagines that the angel could not prevail against him because he found no sin in him, p. 42.

units.la: Warumb sind die Engel für ihm (dem Jacob) hinweg gegangen / und haben ihn nicht gehütet / daß ihm solt nichts geschehen? Der Tiruz (Auflösung ist: GOtt der hat gewolt weisen / daß die Zaddikim (Fromme) seynd besser / als die Engel; als wir gefunden / daß Jacob hat sich geschlagen mit dem Engel / und hat ihm nichts können thun / und hat geherschet über den Engel; Et pag. 43. Der Malach Engel von Esau suchte / was für Afira (Ubertrettung) er hatte gethan / ob er könte Jacob wehthun zu zerschlagen ihn. Da gefand er keine Afira, nur daß zwo Schwestern hat Jacob genommen bey ihrem rem Lebeu. Das ist Deutsch der Pafuk aß her: vayar, kilo jacholl o, als wolt er sagen: er hat gesehen/der Malach er sonte kein A fira gesinden bey Jacob/ da kunte er ihm nichts thun. Imo multis ostendit Rabbi Menaleh Ben Israel, quomodo facile ex sacris daemonstrari possit literis, homines inprimis sanctos, dignitate superare angelos cum libello de Creatione, Problemate 29, pag. 122. inquit: Sed quod homines dignitate superent Angelos, illud facile ex Scriptura probatur. Nam Justi in Angelos imperium habent tanquam in subditos: uti ex exemplo Jacobi patet, Genes. c. 32. Et Angeli Dei obviam facti sunt: Et paulo post ; Jacobus misit מלאכים Angelos ad fratrem Esavum, id est, Jacobus jussit illos Angelos Dei, qui sibi apparuerant, ire ad fratrem suum Esavum. Deinde ex lucta Jacobi cum Angelo, qui tetigit femur ejus, quoniam offensus erat eo, quod Jacobus duas uxores simul superstites connubio sibi junxisset. Refertur denique Angelum a Jacobo superatum esse, & ab eo veniam abeundi petiisse, quae ostendunt homines supra Angelos esse. Quid quod Deus dicat, Exod. cap. 23. Ecce ego emittens Angelum meum, qui te custodiat in via tua. Item Psalmista David, Angelis suis praecipiet de te, ut te custodiant in omni itinere tuo. Quis est dignior (quaerunt Sapientes in Berefit Raba, Paraf. 78.) משמר ... custos, an vero is, qui custoditur? Certe, qui custoditur. Nam apparitores astant Regi, ejusq; curam gerunt; Sic quoque pergit Rabbi Menasseh, pag. 123. Ex his Antiqui inferunt in Sanhedrin, cap. 11. גדולים צדקים יותר ממלאכי השרת Praestantiores sunt Justi, quam Angeli ministerii. Et alio in loco, Holin cap. 6. חביבין ישראל יותר ממלאכי השרת Israel dignior est Angelis ministerii. Et in Pirque R. Eliezer ait, Angeli invidserunt homini, quod non omnium animalium nomina scirent, sicut Adamus. Et in B. Raba, cap. 8. Cum creati sunt, ilico se ei submissere, considerantes eorum dignitatem. Sic etiam R. Gerundensis dixit, animas hominum magis spirituales esse, & excellentiores, quam Angelos, quatenus libero arbitrio praeditae sunt, & operibus suis in altum se tollunt. Caeterum duo argumenta in sacris sunt, quantum mihi videtur, quae idipsum satis evidenter evincunt, primo, quod solus homo dicatur factus ad imaginem Dei. Deinde, quod homo ante, & post omnia (uti alias diximus) creatus est, id est, quatenus anima primum in creatione mundi condita; deinde corpori juncta est, ut vita in hoc mundo frueretur. Rationes vero, quas adversarii in contrarium afferunt, facile solvi possunt; Sed de his alio tempore.
units.tr: "Why did the angels go away from him (Jacob) and not guard him, so that nothing should happen to him? The Tiruz (explanation) is: God wanted to show that the Zaddikim (the pious) are better than the angels, as we have found that Jacob wrestled with the angel and could do nothing to him, and prevailed over the angel." And p. 43: "The Malach (angel) of Esau sought what Afira (transgression) he had committed, whether he could hurt Jacob, to beat him. Then he found no Afira, only that Jacob had taken two sisters during their lifetime. In German the Pasuk says: vayar, kilo jacholl o, as if to say: he saw that the Malach could find no Afira in Jacob, so he could do nothing to him." Moreover, Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel shows at length how easily it can be demonstrated from the sacred letters that men, especially the holy ones, surpass the angels in dignity, in his little book On the Creation, Problem 29, p. 122. He says: "But that men surpass the angels in dignity is easily proved from Scripture. For the just have dominion over the angels as over their subjects, as is clear from the example of Jacob, Gen. ch. 32: 'And the angels of God met him.' And shortly after: 'Jacob sent messengers [מלאכים] to his brother Esau,' that is, Jacob ordered those angels of God who had appeared to him to go to his brother Esau. Then from Jacob's wrestling with the angel, who touched his thigh, because he was offended that Jacob had joined two wives to himself in marriage at the same time. Finally it is related that the angel was overcome by Jacob and asked him for permission to depart, which shows that men are above the angels. What of the fact that God says, Exod. ch. 23: 'Behold, I send my angel, who shall keep you in your way.' Likewise the Psalmist David: 'He shall give his angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways.' Who is more worthy (the Sages ask in Bereshit Rabbah, Parashah 78) of the custodian [מִשְׁמָר] ... the guard, or he who is guarded? Surely he who is guarded. For the attendants stand before the King and take care of him." Rabbi Menasseh continues in the same way, p. 123: "From these things the Ancients infer in Sanhedrin, ch. 11: 'The just are greater than the angels of ministry' [גדולים צדקים יותר ממלאכי השרת]. And in another place, Chullin ch. 6: 'Israel is dearer than the angels of ministry' [חביבין ישראל יותר ממלאכי השרת]. And in Pirke, R. Eliezer says, the angels envied man, because he did not know the names of all animals, as Adam did. And in Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 8: when they were created, at once they submitted to him, considering his dignity. So too R. Gerundensis said that the souls of men are more spiritual and more excellent than the angels, inasmuch as they are endowed with free will, and by their works raise themselves on high. Moreover, there are two arguments in the sacred writings, as it seems to me, which prove this quite clearly: first, that man alone is said to be made in the image of God; second, that man was created both before and after all things (as we have said elsewhere), that is, in that the soul was first formed at the creation of the world, and then joined to the body, that it might enjoy life in this world. But the arguments which the adversaries bring to the contrary can easily be solved; but of these at another time."

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Crepant Ecclesiam Judaicam mira doctrinae concordia illustrem, non Sectis distinctam, non discordem in Articulis Fidei fundamen-talibus, quamquam in Ritualibus, pro Regio-num diversarum ratione, ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi, in Opusculo de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum hodiernorum, Part.I.cap.I. Omnia ista, quæ hodie inter Judæos usitata sunt, ejusdem non sunt momenti, nec ab omnibus pari modo observantur; commode quoque illa ipsa tribus assignantur classibus; quarum prima ambitu suo complectitur præcepta legis scripta, id est, illa, de quibus præcipit Pentateuchus; Eadem diffpefcuntur commode in 248 Affirmativa, & 365 Negativa præcepta, quæ ulterius in fe invicem du-cta, & in unam summam collecta efficiunt 613. Vocantur alias præcepta legalia. Altera comprehenditur Lex ore tradita; nomen conveniens cum commentariis à Rabbinis & Doctoribus olim super Pentateuchum exstructis, tum quoque infinita multitudini regularum & constitutionum, quas appellare solent Doctorum placita, quæ collecta extant in grandi quodam volumine, Talmude nempe, de quo sigillatim agetur inferius cap. 2. Part. II. Ultima complexu suo tenet res, quibus usus diverso tempore, varius in locis authoritatem conciliavit, aut quæ nuper modo invaluere, hinc consuetudines nuncupantur. Ex hisce jam duo priores ordines continentes legem per Mosen literis consignatam, & oralem illam à Doctoribus bus traditam, æqualem apud omnes Judæos obtinent authoritatem, quamvis dispersi etiam per totum terrarum orbem sint; adeo ut hac quidem ex parte, nulla insignis detur differentia; uti id ipsum modo allegatum Talmud planum facere poterit. Sed quod ad Tertiam, ultimamque classem, quæ simpliciter circa mores versatur, negari sane nequit, ingens occurrere discrimen; unde & Judæi hic inde dispersi ab ista ceremoniarum differentia nomen, rationemque agendi, vivendique diversam sortiti sunt; Præcipue autem elucet illa ceremoniarum dissimilitudo Orientales inter, Germanos & Italos. Orientalibus merito accenseo hoc loco quoque Judæos Peloponnesiacos, Græcia item, Barbariaque, nec non illos, qui Hispanorum nomine veniunt in istis regionibus. Ad Judæos Germanos autem referuntur, quotquot Bohemiam, Moraviam, Poloniam, Moscoviam, aliasque incolunt regiones. Hoc proinde ordine, distinctione neque servata, conabor, quoad me fieri poterit, hoc opusculo demonstrare ista, quæ petita sunt ex Lege tam Scripta, quam orali, tum, quæ consuetudinibus solum ortum debent. Cæterum in antecessum moneo, quod ubicunque inter Judæos disparitas detur, illa non nisi negotium consuetudinum attingat, quibus tamen vim mandati inesse, aut nomen præceptorum convenire, neque ipsi sibi persuaderi patiuntur; iis interea, quæ constituunt primi & secundi ordinis jussa, vim obligandi omnino inesse concedunt, ac pro certo habent; Sed licet dogmatum fidei miram crepent unitatem, mutuumque jactent lententiarum consensum, revera tamen, si aperte loquendum, pleni sunt infinitis Magistrorum disputationibus, discordiisque, non solum libri Mischnici, Gemaricique, sed quotquot fere sunt hodiernorum Rabbinorum: Hujus rei testimonium sunt Hillelis & Schammai disensiones triennales illustres, quae nullo alio potuerunt componi modo, quam per Revelationem Bathkol, filiam vocis, ex Tractatu Talmudico Erubhin; Satisfaciet pariter Conradus Fronmullerus, in Epistolis Hebraicis, ad Judaeum Amicum Rabbi Henoch, Ben Levi, exaratis, de dissensionibus multiplicibus Rabbinorum inter se agens, & de lententiis eorum discrepantibus & contrariis, etiam in rebus circa cultum Dei.
units.tr: They boast that the Jewish Church is distinguished by a remarkable harmony of doctrine, that it is not divided into sects, and that it is not at odds over the fundamental articles of faith, although in ritual matters it differs according to the custom of each region. So Rabbi Leo of Modena, in his little work on the ceremonies and customs of the Jews today, Part I, chapter I: All those things that are now in common use among the Jews are not of the same importance, nor are they all observed in the same way. They can conveniently be assigned to three classes. The first, in its scope, embraces the precepts of the written law, that is, those commanded in the Pentateuch. These are conveniently divided into 248 affirmative and 365 negative precepts, which, when multiplied further among themselves and gathered into a single sum, make 613. These are also called legal precepts. The second class comprises the oral law handed down, a name that fits the commentaries built by the rabbis and teachers over the Pentateuch, and also the endless multitude of rules and regulations that the teachers usually call their decrees, which are collected in a great volume, namely the Talmud, of which a separate account will be given below in Part II, chapter 2. The last class holds those things which, varying in different places and at different times, have gained authority through custom, or which have only recently taken hold, and for this reason are called customs. Of these, the first two classes, containing the law written down through Moses and the oral law handed down by the teachers, hold equal authority among all Jews, although they are scattered throughout the whole orb of the lands; so that in this respect no striking difference appears, as the Talmud just cited will make plain. But as to the third and last class, which concerns mere manners, it cannot be denied that a great difference appears; and for this reason the Jews, dispersed here and there, have received from this difference in ceremonies a name and a manner of acting and living that differ. This difference in ceremonies stands out especially between the Eastern Jews, the German Jews, and the Italian Jews. To the Eastern Jews I rightly count here also the Jews of the Peloponnese, likewise those of Greece and the Barbary lands, and those who go under the name of Spanish in these regions. The German Jews are those who inhabit Bohemia, Moravia, Poland, Muscovy, and other regions. Accordingly, in this order, and without keeping to a strict distinction, I shall try, as far as I can, to show in this little work those things that are drawn from the written law, from the oral law, and those that owe their origin only to custom. Meanwhile I give notice beforehand that wherever disagreement exists among the Jews, it touches only the matter of customs, which they nevertheless do not allow to be persuaded to have the force of a command or to deserve the name of precepts. Meanwhile, they fully concede that the orders of the first and second classes have full binding force, and they hold them as certain. But although they vaunt a remarkable unity of articles of faith and boast of agreement in opinions, in truth, to speak openly, they are full of endless disputations and discords among the masters, not only in the books of the Mishnah and Gemara, but almost in all the writings of the rabbis of today. Witnesses to this are the famous three-year disputes of Hillel and Shammai, which could not be settled in any other way than by the revelation of a bath kol, the daughter of a voice, as recorded in the Talmud tractate Erubin. Conrad Frommüller will likewise satisfy the reader, in his Hebrew letters written to Rabbi Henoch ben Levi, a Jewish friend, where he treats of the manifold dissensions of the rabbis among themselves, and of their conflicting and contrary opinions, even on matters concerning the worship of God.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Crepant Ecclesiam Judaicam perennem, ad mundi finem duraturam, nunquam deficibilem, sed perpetuo visibilem, in ipsis vinculis hostium illustrem, quod mundus sine Israelitis subsistere non posset, quodque propter tres res firmiter staret, ex Capitulis Patrum, cap. 1. Simeon justus fuit ex reliquiis Synagogae magnae. Ille dixit: super tres res mundus consistit: super Legem, super cultum, & super restitutionem beneficiorum.
units.tr: They boast that the Jewish Church is everlasting, will endure until the end of the world, can never fail, but is always visible, and is glorious even in the chains of its enemies; that the world could not stand without the Israelites; and that it stands firm on account of three things, as in the Sayings of the Fathers, chapter 1: Simeon the Just was one of the remnants of the Great Synagogue. He said: the world rests upon three things: upon the Law, upon worship, and upon the restoration of benefits.

units.la: Per Legem, intelligentes Legis cognitionem, per cultum, Religionem in orationibus maxime conspicuam, & per retributionem beneficiorum, itudium proximo benefaciendi; Quod soli Legem Mosaicam habeant hæreditariam, ex Rabbi Bechai in Kad Hakkemach, sol. 8. Et in Commentario super Deuteron. cap.18. Ex vulgatis precum libellis, uti patet ex §.2. hujus capitis.
units.tr: By the Law they understand the knowledge of the Law; by worship, religion, most evident in prayers; and by the restoration of benefits, the zeal for doing good to one's neighbour. That only they have the Mosaic Law as their inheritance: from Rabbi Bechai in Kad Hakkemach, sol. 8, and in his commentary on Deuteronomy, chapter 18. From the commonly used prayer books, as is clear from §2 of this chapter.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Venditant Ecclesiam Judaicam perfectam docere salutem, certissimaq; vitæ æternæ adipiscendæ media ex Mose continuo inculcare, referentes summi boni fruitionem omnimodam in sola Judaica repertiri Ecclesia, hinc suos contribules valde dehortantes, ne se à Mosaica separent Ecclesia, ex Capitulis Patrum, cap.2. Non segregabis te ab Ecclesia; Ex Rabbi Isaco Abarbanele in Nachalath Abhot, f.204. col.1. Qui separat se ab Ecclesia, non videbit quoque refocillationem Ecclesiæ; Quod qui separet se ab Ecclesia, sit ex iis, qui nullam habent partem in seculo futuro; Dehortantes suos, ne ullis miraculis, prodigiisque seduci se patiantur, persuaderique sub speciosō prætextu, quod Lege Mosaica detur Lex perfectior, ex Judæo Isaco Orobio, in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag. 109. Hæc via est Lex Domini per Mosem sem Israeli præstita, per quam voluit, quod Israel sem- per incederet, ut ad Deum suum sine errore pervenire possit. Quicunque igitur, qui cum miraculis, & prodigiis nos ab hac Lege, seu via distrahere conatur, aliam viam securiorem, perfectiorem, aut breviorem esse, docens: præsertim si simul ad Deos alienos nos provocaverit, est Pseudo-Propheta in hoc capite à Deo damnatus, & nullatenus credendus.
units.tr: They proclaim that the Jewish Church teaches a perfect salvation and constantly inculcates from Moses the most certain means of obtaining eternal life, referring the full enjoyment of the highest good to be found only in the Jewish Church. Hence they earnestly warn their fellow countrymen not to separate themselves from the Mosaic Church, from the Sayings of the Fathers, chapter 2: Do not separate yourself from the congregation. From Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel in Nachalath Abhot, f. 204, col. 1: He who separates himself from the congregation shall not see the refreshment of the congregation; and that whoever separates himself from the congregation is among those who have no portion in the world to come. They warn their people not to allow themselves to be seduced by any miracles or prodigies, or to be persuaded under a specious pretext that a more perfect law is given by the Law of Moses. From the Jew Isaac Orobio, in his Conference with Limborch, p. 109: This is the way, the Law of the Lord given to Israel through Moses, through which he wished that Israel should always walk, so that it might reach its God without error. Whoever, therefore, tries to draw us away from this Law or way with miracles and prodigies, teaching that another way is safer, more perfect, or shorter, especially if he at the same time provokes us to strange gods, is a false prophet condemned by God in this chapter, and is in no way to be believed.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Admittuntad Ecclesiam Judaicam quosvis terrarum homines, quos גרים Proselytos, Advenas nuncupant, nullos removentes, quod Lex Mosaica data sit in deserto, quod omnibus fuit commune, ut ita omnes, qui vellent, salvarentur, ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel in Conciliatore ad Leviticum, Quæst.7. pag.192. Quippe data Lex est in deserto, loco omnibus communi; quo significatur, posse, quicumque vellent, per eam salutem suam obtinere, tametsi præcipue Israelitis data foret; Recipiebant olim Proselytum in Ecclesiæ communionem tribus ceremoniis, מילה Circumcisione, טבילה Baptismo, & קרבן Sacrificio; Hodie vero, cum templo sint orbati, in quo sacrificia offerebantur, per Circumcisionem & Baptismum ingrediuntur Israelis fœdus, uti patet ex Rabbi Mose Maimonide in Tractatu Issure Biah, cap.13. Tribus rebus Israelitæ ingrediuntur fœdus, circumcisione, Baptismo & Korban. Eodem quoque modo si Gentilis vel Christianus ad fœdus admitti voluerit, & hospitari sub aliis majestatis divinæ, & propterea receperit in se jugum legis, necesse habet, ut circumcidatur, ut baptizetur, ut afferat korban. Si fœmina est, baptismus & korban sufficiunt, quia dicitur Numer. cap. 15. vers. 15. Sicut vos, ita peregrinus. Quod per circumcisionem, baptismum, & korban vos estis, id etiam secundum generationes per circumcisionem, baptismum, & korban est proselytus. Korban autem illud est holocaustum jumenti, vel duorum turturum, vel duorum pullorum columbæ, & par alterutrius est unum holocaustum. Sed quoniam hodierno tempore, templi defectu, korban offerri nequit, necessaria tantummodo sunt circumcisio, & baptismus; Examinant quoque Candidatum fidei Mosaicæ, num lucri spe, aut honorum intuitu, num amore virginis, aut metu compulsus, sacra desideret Judaica? excitato Rabbi Maimonide in Illure Biah, cap. 13. Cum venerit proselytus aut proselyta, ut amplectatur Judaismum, inquisitione instituta pervestigant, qua de causa hoc faciat? Num forte divitias indesperet, vel hanc putet esse viam perveniendi ad dignitates, vel an faciat ex metu? Et si vir est, inquirunt, an amore puellæ Israelitidis sit captus? Si fœmina, idem faciunt & quærunt, an amore juvenis alicujus ex Israelitis flagret? Proponunt insuper Candidatum didato, Mosaicam Legem rigidissimam esse, hujusque Sectatores hodie inter abjectissimos & vilissimos numerari homines, uti loquitur Rabbi Leo Mutinensis in Opusculo de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judaeorum, Part. V. cap. 3. Quando quidam in Judaeorum numerum cooptari desiderant, Doctorum tres, vel alii viri auctoritate praestantes quaestionibus vexare, probeque examinare Candidatum tenentur, ut innotescat, quid ipsum induxerit, atque commoverit, ejusmodi quid sibi proponere: Arcenda namque sunt ab hoc negotio sacro & pio, omnia & desideria & consilia, quae carnem spirant & sanguinem; quod si exploraverint, humani quid subesse, missum ipsum faciunt, addendo insuper rigidissimam esse Legem Mosaicam, ejusque sectatores hodie numerari abjectissimos inter & vilissimos homines penes omnes gentes: quare tandem hortantur hominem, permaneat in avita, in qua natus & educatus est, religione. Si tamen inhaereat firmiter sententia semel propositae, admittitur sic tandem ad initiationis Sacramentum; inde sanatus totus aqua obruitur, praesentibus tribus examinatoribus ipsius. His peractis verus ab omnibus habetur & censetur Judaeus; De his Proselytis suis, tum Justitiae, tum domicilii, multa crepant magnifica, numerantes inter ipsos, Imperatores, Reges, Principes, viros, foeminasque illustres, omnium ordinum, aetatum tumque homines, iplos Monachos pariter Jesuitas, Augustinianos, Dominicanos, Franciscanos, exJudæoOrobio, inCollatione cum Limborchio, pag. 102. In hac civitate, (Amstelodami) & plurimus aliis regionibus, Monachos habemus, qui Idololatriam rejecere, Augustinianos, Franciscanos, Jesuitas, Dominicanos. Sunt in Hispania Episcopi, & gravissimi Monachi, quorum parentes, fratres & sorores, in hac, & aliis civitatibus, ut Judaismum servare possent, inhabitant; Imo ipse OrobiusJudæus ead. pag. fatetur, quod toties genua Baali flexerit, dum sic loquitur: Et quomodo ego de hoc suaderi possem, qui toties miser genua Baali flexi? Peccatum meum ego recordor, ut dicebat Jervus Pharaonis.
units.tr: They admit into the Jewish Church any men of the earth whatever, whom they call גרים [gerim] Proselytes, that is, Strangers, excluding none. The reason is that the Mosaic Law was given in the wilderness, a place common to all, so that anyone who wished might be saved by it. Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, in his Conciliator on Leviticus, Question 7, p. 192: Indeed the Law was given in the wilderness, a place common to all, which signifies that whoever wished could obtain his salvation through it, although it was given chiefly to the Israelites. Formerly they received a Proselyte into the communion of the Church by three ceremonies: מילה [milah] Circumcision, טבילה [tevilah] Baptism, and קרבן [korban] Sacrifice. Today, however, since they have been deprived of the Temple in which sacrifices were offered, they enter the covenant of Israel through Circumcision and Baptism alone, as is clear from Rabbi Moses Maimonides in the Treatise Issure Biah, chap. 13: Israelites enter the covenant by three things: circumcision, baptism and korban. In the same way, if a Gentile or Christian wishes to be admitted to the covenant and to dwell under the other majesty of the divine Name, and so takes upon himself the yoke of the Law, he must be circumcised, be baptized, and bring a korban. If the candidate is a woman, baptism and korban suffice, because it is said in Numbers chap. 15 vers. 15: As you are, so the stranger shall be. That is, as you are through circumcision, baptism and korban, so the proselyte is, throughout the generations, through circumcision, baptism and korban. The korban is a burnt offering of a beast, or of two turtledoves, or of two young pigeons, and the pair of either is one burnt offering. But since in the present age korban cannot be offered, for want of the Temple, only circumcision and baptism are required. They also examine the candidate for the Mosaic faith, whether he desires Jewish rites from hope of gain, or from regard for honours, or from love of a maiden, or compelled by fear. Rabbi Maimonides is cited in Issure Biah, chap. 13: When a male or female proselyte comes to embrace Judaism, they institute an inquiry and investigate why he does it: perhaps he despairs of riches, or thinks this is the way to attain dignities, or does it out of fear? And if he is a man, they ask whether he has been captivated by love of an Israelite girl; if a woman, they likewise ask whether she burns with love for some young Israelite. Moreover, they set before the candidate that the Mosaic Law is most severe, and that its adherents today are counted among the most abject and worthless of men, as Rabbi Leo of Modena says in his little work on the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part V, chap. 3: When certain persons desire to be enrolled among the Jews, three of the Teachers, or other men eminent in authority, are bound to harass them with questions and to examine the candidate well, so that it may become known what has induced and moved him to propose such a thing to himself. For all desires, plans and purposes which breathe flesh and blood must be kept far from this holy and pious undertaking. If they find that some human motive lies beneath, they dismiss him, adding moreover that the Mosaic Law is most severe, and that its adherents today are counted among the most abject and worthless of men among all nations. Finally they urge the man to remain in the ancestral religion in which he was born and brought up. If, however, he firmly holds to the resolution once proposed, he is then admitted to the sacrament of initiation; there he is wholly immersed in water, in the presence of his three examiners. When these things are done, he is held and reckoned by all as a true Jew. Concerning these proselytes of theirs, both of righteousness and of settlement, they boast loudly, counting among them emperors, kings, princes, and men and women of distinction of every rank and age, including monks, Jesuits, Augustinians, Dominicans and Franciscans. Orobio the Jew, in his Collation with Limborch, p. 102: In this city (Amsterdam) and in many other regions we have monks who have rejected idolatry: Augustinians, Franciscans, Jesuits, Dominicans. In Spain there are bishops and very serious monks, whose parents, brothers and sisters live in this and other cities, so that they may be able to keep Judaism. Indeed Orobio the Jew himself, on the same page, confesses that he had so often bent his knees to Baal, when he says: And how could I be persuaded of this, I who so often, wretched, bent my knees to Baal? I remember my sin, as the servant of Pharaoh said.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Credunt, non omnes damnari, qui extra Judaicam vivunt Ecclesiam, aliamque fidei suæ, Religionisque habent communionem, docentes, pios ex qualibet gente Probos ex mundi gentibus, quadantenus salvari, partem in Resurrectione habere mortuorum, vitæque æternæ suo sensu participes fore, si modo sint Filij Noachi, observent solum Septem præcepta filiorum Noachi, vitentq; quam maxime Idololatriam, maledictionem Numinis divini, Homicidium, Adulterium, Furtum, Judicia curent, &c.
units.tr: They believe that not all are damned who live outside the Jewish Church and have a communion of faith and religion other than theirs. They teach that the pious of any nation, the upright among the nations of the world, are saved to some degree, have a share in the resurrection of the dead, and will partake of eternal life in their own way, provided only that they are sons of Noah, observing just the Seven Precepts of the sons of Noah, and avoiding above all idolatry, blaspheming the divine Name, murder, adultery, theft, and they take care to establish judgments, and so on.

units.la: LI de vivo animalis membro non comedant, de quibus Rabbi Moses Maimonides in Tractatu de Regibus, cap.9.num.1. Sex res sunt primo hominis mandata, de Idololatria, de benedictione nominis divini, de effusione sanguinis, de revelatione turpitudinum, de rapina, de judiciis; Septima est Noacho addita, nempe de membro vivi, & ita famina sunt praecepta in universum septem; Et in eodem libro cap. 6. num. 11. Quicunque suscipit septem praecepta, & ea etiam facit, ecce is est unus de sanctis gentilium, & habet partem in seculo futuro; Dummodo ea propterea servet, quod Deus Benedictus illa primum Noacho, per Mosen praecepit. Nam si ideo servat, quod ea naturalis ratio dictat, non est proselytus domicilij, nec unus ex sanctis gentilium hujus mundi; Ad quae verba Keseph Mischna, ex cap. Chelec k annotat: Controversia inter Rabbi Eliefer est, & inter Rabbi Jehoschuam; Rabbi Eliefer ait: populi hujus mundi non habent partem in futuro seculo; Rabbi Jehoschua ait: habent; Et decisio est secundum Rabbi Jehoschuam; Credunt, pios ex quacunque gente fuerint gente, vitam adepturos aeternam, quod Deus nullam creaturam sua fraudet mercede, ex Schevoth Jehuda versionis Gentianae, pag. 282. In hac ipsa etiam fuit sententia Sapiens quidam cum Rege Cosrae controversiam habens, cujus verba haec sunt: Nos nulli mortalium, nulli genti, sive sive nationi bonorum suorum operum præmia negamus atque subtrahimus; Ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel in Conciliatore in Deuteron. Quæst.2. Septem præcepta, ut traditur in Gemara Sanhedrin, cap.7. omnes gentes observare tenentur, quæ idcirco vocata sunt, שבע מצוות בני נח Septem præcepta filiorum Noachi. Ex his (quemadmodum in Seder Olam cap.V. & apud R. Mosen in Jada-Hazaqua legimus) sena Adamo data sunt: nimirum ut abstineret 1. ab idololatria: II. maledictione nominis divini: III. cæde: IV. adulterio: V. furto: VI. ut judices institueret, quorum esset curare ut illa præcepta observarentur. Super hæc Noacho septimum additum fuit, ne membrum vivo animali amputatum comederet: hus verbis Genes. 9. 7. Carnem cum anima & sanguine suo ne comedas. Hæc sunt præcepta, ob quorum violationem ut ex S. Scriptura ibidem in Sanhedrin probatur, etiam gentes mundi à Deo punitas constat. Eum vero, qui illa observat, vocarunt. גר תושב peregrinum habitantem, quia in Israele morari poterat. Illi autem, qui ea non colit, quia natura sic suadere videtur, sed quoniam Lege præcipiuntur, & Moses tradidit ore Noachi filiis tradita, illi inquam, si R. Mosem Sepher Melachim, cap.8. audimus, sors erit in futuro sæculo. Unde & Veterum Sapientia extat dictum hujusmodi, Sanhed. cap. 11. יש חסידי אומות העולם להם חלק לעולם הבא Pijs ex nationibus mundi, pars est in mundo altero. Idem quoque R. Moses, Comment. ad Misnaiot, colligit ex Misna, cujus exordium est: Quatuor idiota non habent partem in altero mundo: quos inter repónitur Bilham gentilis; idque ne haberetur unus e pijs gentium, quibus fors erit in futuro seculo. Etiam varius locus magni & egregij operis Mishne Tora; Hilchot Tefuva, c.3. Ifure Biah, cap.14. Hedut cap.11. Et in Directione Lib. III. cap.XVIII.ait, nullum bonum opus mercede apud Deum carere, juxta dictum Pesahim cap. 10. אין הקדוש ברוך הוא מקפח שכר כל בריה Deus benedictus nulli creaturae praemium suum denegat. Hinc in Semot Raba cap.31. legas Deum jussisse canicadaver objici, quia adversum Israelitas non latrasset: alia ejusdem generis exempla praetermitto. Etiam R. Jehuda Levita, Cuzari lib. 1. art. 111. ait, Hebraeos dicere nulli e gentibus mercedem negari operum suorum; quamvis non aequent peregrinum sibi ipsis, eo quod Propheta evadere nequeat. In sacro quoque libro Zoar, Par. Picude. traditur, Regibus, omnibusque adeo magistratibus, qui justa exercent imperia, & Hebraeos in ditione sua habent, certum in Paradiso gradum esse assignatum; quemadmodum eosdem, si male Hebraeos habeant, poena certa manet; Quod pii ex gentibus resurrecturi sint ad participandam futuri seculi beatitudinem, uti pluribus, capite de Resurrectione, enarrabimus ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, de Resurrectiorectione mortuorum, lib. 2. cap. 9. Quod beneficiorum redemptionis futuri sint participes, ex Judaeo Orobio, in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag. 12. Verum pij ex gentibus, sive ex Israele oriundi, sive non, qui verum Deum coluerint, qui Israelis mirabilem redemptionem adjuverint, Deo, & populo inservientes, Dei amore, & timore allliciti, redemptionis beneficiorum erunt participes: Eorum corda, ut Israelis, circumcidentur, ut ament Dominum Deum suum toto corde suo, & tota anima sua, ut vivant, divina gratia omnes affluentes.
units.tr: That they should not eat a limb cut from a living animal, as Rabbi Moses Maimonides says in the Treatise on Kings, chap. 9, num. 1: There are six things commanded to man from the beginning: concerning idolatry, concerning the blessing of the divine Name, concerning the shedding of blood, concerning the uncovering of nakedness, concerning robbery, and concerning judgments. The seventh was added for Noah, namely concerning the limb of a living animal; and so there are seven precepts in all. And in the same book, chap. 6, num. 11: Whoever accepts the seven precepts and also performs them, behold, he is one of the righteous of the Gentiles, and has a share in the age to come. Provided he keeps them because God, blessed be he, commanded them first to Noah, through Moses. For if he keeps them because natural reason dictates them, he is not a proselyte of settlement, nor one of the righteous Gentiles of this world. On these words the Keseph Mischna, from chap. Chelec, notes: The controversy is between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Jehoshua. Rabbi Eliezer says: the peoples of this world have no share in the future age; Rabbi Jehoshua says: they have. And the decision is according to Rabbi Jehoshua. They believe that the pious of whatever nation will obtain eternal life, because God, blessed be he, will defraud no creature of its reward; from the Schevoth Jehuda, in the Latin version of Gentianus, p. 282: In this very matter there was a certain wise man who had a dispute with King Chosroes, whose words are these: We deny and withhold the rewards of their good works from no mortal, no people, no nation whatever. From Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel in the Conciliator on Deuteronomy, Question 2: The seven precepts, as handed down in the Gemara Sanhedrin, chap. 7, all nations are bound to observe, and for this reason they are called שבע מצוות בני נח [sheva mitzvot bnei Noach] the seven precepts of the sons of Noah. Of these (as we read in Seder Olam, chap. 5, and in Rabbi Moses in Jad-Chazaka), six were given to Adam: namely, that he should abstain 1. from idolatry; 2. from blaspheming the divine name; 3. from murder; 4. from adultery; 5. from theft; 6. that he should appoint judges whose duty it was to see that those precepts were observed. To these a seventh was added for Noah, that he should not eat a limb cut from a living animal; by these words, Genesis 9:7: You shall not eat flesh with its life, that is its blood. These are the precepts for whose violation, as is proved from Holy Scripture in the same place in Sanhedrin, the nations of the world are known to be punished by God. But him who keeps them they called גר תושב [ger toshav], a resident alien, because he could dwell in Israel. But as for him who does not observe them because nature seems to suggest them, but because they are commanded by the Law, and were handed down by Moses to the sons of Noah through Noah's mouth, that man, I say, if we listen to Rabbi Moses in Sepher Melachim, chap. 8, will have a lot in the future age. Hence also a saying of the ancient wisdom has come down, Sanhedrin, chap. 11: יש חסידי אומות העולם להם חלק לעולם הבא [yesh chasidei umot ha-olam lahem chelek la-olam ha-ba] The pious of the nations of the world have a share in the world to come. Rabbi Moses also, in his Commentary on the Mishnah, gathers the same from the Mishnah, whose beginning is: Four ignorant men have no share in the other world; among whom is set the Gentile Bilam; and this lest he be thought one of the pious of the Gentiles, to whom there will perhaps be a lot in the future age. Also various passages in the great and excellent work Mishne Tora: Hilchot Teshuvah, chap. 3; Issure Biah, chap. 14; Hedut, chap. 11. And in the Directio, Book III, chap. 18, he says that no good work lacks its reward with God, according to the saying in Pesachim, chap. 10: אין הקדוש ברוך הוא מקפח שכר כל בריה [ein ha-kadosh baruch hu mekaphe sechar kol beriah] God, blessed be he, denies the reward of no creature. Hence in Shemot Rabba, chap. 31, you may read that God ordered a dog's carcass to be thrown out because it had not barked against the Israelites; I pass over other examples of this kind. Also Rabbi Judah Halevi, Cuzari, Book 1, art. 111, says that the Hebrews say that the reward of their works is denied to no one of the Gentiles, although they do not make the stranger equal to themselves, because the Prophet cannot be evaded. In the sacred book Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, it is taught that kings, and indeed all magistrates who exercise just rule and have Hebrews in their domain, have a certain assigned grade in Paradise, just as, if they treat the Hebrews badly, a certain punishment awaits them. That the pious of the Gentiles are to rise again to share in the blessedness of the future age, we will set out in several places in the chapter on the Resurrection, from Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, On the Resurrection of the Dead, Book 2, chap. 9. That they will be partakers of the benefits of redemption, from Orobio the Jew, in his Collation with Limborch, p. 12: But the pious of the Gentiles, whether born of Israel or not, who have worshipped the true God, who have helped the wonderful redemption of Israel, serving God and the people, drawn by the love and fear of God, will be partakers of the benefits of redemption. Their hearts, like those of Israel, will be circumcised, so that they may love the Lord their God with all their heart and with all their soul, and live, all abounding in divine grace.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Afferunt ex modernis plurimi, ipsos Christianos cum Judaeis salvari, meliorem- que post hujus vitae difficultates, expectare vitam, ita Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, in Epistola dedicatoria libri primi de Resurrectione mortuorum: Unum enim Deum colimus, ejus praeceptis nos subjicimus, & post hujus vitae difficultates meliorem vitam expectamus; ita Rabbinus Vindebonensis, Christianos salutis caelestis fieri participes, asseruit Wagenseilio, in Sota, p. 753; Sic multos Christianos, pietati & aequitati operam dantes, salvatum quoque iri, ex diversis Rabbinis saepius atque saepius audivi; Sed, profecto, omnes fucum nobis faciunt, nec candide, nec sincera fide nobiscum agentes, sed, vel ex metu loquentes, vel ex adulatione, ut gratiam in oculis inveniant; Cum contrarium ex propriis fluat principiis; Si enim vita æterna acquiritur per obíervantiam Legis Mosaicæ, & quidem Circumcisionis merito, sane Christiani salvari non possunt, quod per ipsos Circumcisio cum reliquis ceremoniis sit abrogata, ipsaque pristina Mosaica Religio valde mutata; Imo si pii ex gentibus mundi quadantenus salventur, secundum leptem Noachidarum præcepta viventes, profecto Christiani non poterunt salvari, cum sint ex mente Judæorum Idololatræ, statuentes Jesum hominem, Dei fuisse filium æternum, Deo æqualem, ipsumque pro Deo colentes; cum sanguinem comedant, sicque Noachica transgrediantur mandata; Præterea si Principes, aliique magistratus, justa exercentes imperia, Judæosque beneficiis afficientes, certum in Paradiso assignatum habebunt gradum, sequitur ultro, damnari illos, qui vel male tractant Judæos, vel illis in regionibus suis destituuntur.
units.tr: Many modern writers maintain that Christians are saved together with the Jews and expect a better life after the difficulties of this one. So Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, in the dedicatory epistle of the first book of his work on the Resurrection of the Dead: For we worship one God, we submit to his precepts, and after the difficulties of this life we expect a better life. So the Viennese rabbi asserted to Wagenseil, in Sota, p. 753, that Christians become sharers in heavenly salvation. I have often and repeatedly heard from various rabbis that many Christians who practise piety and justice will also be saved. But they certainly all deceive us, dealing with us neither frankly nor with sincere good faith. They speak either out of fear or out of flattery, so that they may find favour in our eyes, whereas the opposite follows from their own principles. For if eternal life is acquired by observing the Mosaic Law, and indeed by the merit of circumcision, then Christians certainly cannot be saved, since among them circumcision has been abrogated along with the other ceremonies, and the original Mosaic religion has been greatly changed. Moreover, if the pious among the Gentiles are saved to some extent by living according to the seven precepts of the sons of Noah, then Christians surely cannot be saved, since in the judgment of the Jews they are idolaters, who hold that Jesus was a man, the eternal Son of God, equal to God, and who worship him as God; and since they eat blood, they transgress the Noachide commands. Furthermore, if princes and other magistrates, who exercise just rule and bestow benefits upon the Jews, will have an assigned place in Paradise, it follows of course that those are condemned who either treat the Jews badly or are deprived of them in their own regions.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Credunt Ecclesiam Christianam esse Idololatricam, ex Commentario Manuscripto Rabbi Davidis Kimchii in Esai. cap. 2. vers. 18. apud Procokium in Notis Miscellaneis ad Sortam Mosis, pag. 322. Sunt tamen & adhuc in parte parte Orientis Idololatræ, quin etiam habendi sunt etiam Christiani pro Idololatris, quod incurvent se, ac adorent imaginem Jesu Nazareni. Et ad verf. 20. ex eodem Kimchii Manuscripto, quod fallacias nondum experta fuit manus, cum in Codicibus impressis hæc fere desinunt; Sicut explicavimus, quoniam ad hunc usque diem in quibusdam regionibus Orientalibus colunt idola argenti & auri, atque ita Christiani faciunt imaginem figura Jesu Nazareni, & figura crucis, ex argento & auro; Ex Rabbi Maimonidis Codice Manuscripto, Jad Chalaka, Tractatu de Idololatria, cap. 9. §. 4. apud Wulferum in Animadversionibus ad Salomonis Zevi Theriacam Judaicam, pag. 137. Christiani Idololatræ sunt, & diem septimanæ primum festum agunt, ideoque prohibitum est, die quinto & sexto uniuscujusque septimanæ, in Terra Sancta, cum iis negotiari. Nec opus est, ut de ipso Solis die quicquam dicamus, siquidem eodem negotiari velle nunquam non prohibitum est. Eadem autem omnium eorum festorum est ratio; Sic Rabbi Bechai in Cad Hakkemach pag. 62. Christianos accusat idololatriæ, quod y hominem pro Deo colant; Sic Rabbi Asac Abarbanel in Maschmia Jeschua, pag. 5. ad verba Numer. cap. 24. verf. 25. Verba hæc procul omni dubio ita exponi debent: Væ quis vivet in diebus illis, quando homo mortalis, ex muliere natus, tus, se ipsum in Deum ponet? quo quidem Jesus Na-zarenus innuitur, qui ipse Deum se esse, dixerat, aut de quo alij minimum idem dicebant: nec quippe prater eum quisquam repertus est alius, qui se ipsum Deum fecerit. Etsi enim Nebucadnezar dixerit: Assimulabo me Altissimo, &c. non tamen id de Deitate intelligendum est, quasi ejus respectu Deo similis fieri voluerit; nulla enim comparatio instituì ea propter potest; quin imo etsi is Deum blasphemarit ac opprobrio affecerit, oculorumq; celsitudinem contra Sanctum Israelis extulerit, nunquam tamen Causam primam se esse, dixit, mundiq; Creatorem venditavit, quemadmodum Jesus fecit, aut Assecla ejus minimum voluerunt; Sic ex maximi pretii Machfor Manuscripto Bibliothecae Norimbergensis, a nobis pariter viso, multis deducit Optimus Wulferus in perdoctis suis Animadversionibus ad Theriac. Jud. pag. 140. qua ratione in precibus Deum efflagitent, ut idola regni superbi funditus evertat, tollatque: Fac o bone Deus, ut annus redemptionis brevi illucescat! tunde perfidos, idola in regno superbo confringe, & dejice ac praecipites age profanos! Et in alia ad Deum precatione sic ingemiscunt: Quomodo quasi intueberis, & tacebis, qui in nominis tui ignominiam ac contemtum coeunt, seque conjungunt, & flexo corpore truncum ligni colunt, ac adorant? Cur quasi respicies ad perfidos? Et ex eodem Co-
units.tr: They believe that the Christian Church is idolatrous, on the basis of the manuscript commentary of Rabbi David Kimchi on Isaiah 2:18, cited by Prokisch in his Miscellaneous Notes on the Book of Moses, p. 322: Nevertheless there are still idolaters in parts of the East; indeed the Christians too are to be regarded as idolaters, because they bow down and worship the image of Jesus of Nazareth. And on verse 20, from the same manuscript of Kimchi, which the hand of the deceivers had not yet touched, since in the printed codices these words mostly disappear: As we have explained, to this day in certain eastern regions they worship idols of silver and gold, and so Christians make an image of Jesus of Nazareth and a figure of the cross, of silver and gold. From the manuscript codex of Rabbi Maimonides, the Jad Chalaka, Treatise on Idolatry, ch. 9, §4, cited by Wülfer in his Animadversions on Salomon Zevi's Jewish Theriac, p. 137: Christians are idolaters, and they keep the first day of the week as a festival; therefore it is forbidden to trade with them on the fifth and sixth days of each week in the Holy Land. There is no need to say anything about the day of the Sun itself, since it has always been forbidden to wish to trade on that day. The reason for all of their feasts is the same. Thus Rabbi Bechai, in Cad Hakkemach, p. 62, accuses Christians of idolatry because they worship a man as God. So also Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel, in Maschmia Jeschua, p. 5, on the words of Numbers 24:25: These words without doubt must be explained thus: Woe, who shall live in those days, when a mortal man, born of a woman, shall place himself in God's stead? By this is indicated Jesus of Nazareth, who said that he himself was God, or of whom others said the same thing at least; for indeed no other was found beside him who made himself God. For although Nebuchadnezzar said, "I will be like the Most High," etc., yet this is not to be understood of the Deity, as if he wished to be made like God in respect of him; for no comparison can be made in that respect. Indeed, even though he blasphemed God and reviled him, and lifted up the pride of his eyes against the Holy One of Israel, he never said that he was the first cause, nor did he proclaim himself the Creator of the world, as Jesus did, or as his followers at least wished. So the most excellent Wülfer, in his learned Animadversions on the Theriac of the Jews, p. 140, deduces from the manuscript Machfor of the Nuremberg Library, which I too have seen, by what reasoning they beseech God in their prayers that he would utterly overthrow and remove the idols of the proud kingdom: Grant, O good God, that the year of redemption may dawn soon! Smite the faithless, break the idols in the proud kingdom, and cast down and drive headlong the profane! And in another prayer to God they groan thus: How is it that you look on as if you did not see, and keep silent, while they assemble to the dishonour and contempt of your name, join themselves together, and with bent body worship and adore the trunk of a tree? Why do you look away, as if at the faithless? And from the same

units.la: Codice Manuscripto in alia Oratione: Qui clavo suffixum adorat, consilium mihi dedit, ut a te, o Deus omnipotens! deflecterem, stipitemque ligni adorarem; Rursus in eodem libro precantur: Deleantur e libro vitae Edomitae & Moabitae super-bi, qui truncum ligni adorant, eique se incurvant, & in Deum jus cipiunt; Et tandem in precibus instant: Accinge te ad vindictam, irascere iis, qui sulcum prolongant, & in te praevaricati honorem divinum simulacro hominis mortalis exhibent, qui ipse ob scelera sua punitus est. Via eorum ducunt ad haeresin; Vocant Religionem Christianam horrendam Idololatriam, ita Lumbroro Judaeus Illyricus in Propugnaculo Judaismi ad articulum Grotii xvi. lib. v. de Veritate Religionis Christianae, apud Limborchium in Collatione cum Orobio Judaeo, p.217. His adde horrendam Idololatriam, quae ab ipsis Judaeis adinventa fuit & suscitata in Jerusalem, videl. Christianismus, per quem tota Lex divina ut insupportabile jugum deleta fuit & exterminata, quem non pauci Judaeorum amplexi fuerunt, & per tot secula usque in praesens eodem errore misere inficiuntur.
units.tr: manuscript codex, in another prayer: He who adores what is fixed with a nail has counselled me to turn away from you, O almighty God, and to worship the trunk of a tree. Again in the same book they pray: Let the proud Edomites and Moabites be blotted out of the book of life, who adore the trunk of a tree, bow themselves before it, and ascribe to it the right of God. And at last they press in their prayers: Gird yourself for vengeance, be angry with those who lengthen the furrow, and who, transgressing against you, give divine honour to the image of a mortal man, who himself was punished for his crimes. Their ways lead to heresy. They call the Christian religion a horrible idolatry. So Lumbroso the Illyrian Jew, in the Bulwark of Judaism, on the article of Grotius, book 5, ch. 16, On the Truth of the Christian Religion, cited by Limborch in his Collatio with the Jew Orobio, p. 217: To these add the horrible idolatry which was devised and set up in Jerusalem by the Jews themselves, namely Christianity, through which the whole divine Law, as an intolerable yoke, was abolished and destroyed, and which not a few of the Jews embraced, and which for so many centuries down to the present they have wretchedly been infected with by the same error.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Appellant Ecclesiam Christianam, errorum matrem foecundam, ex qua omni tempore innumerae prognatae sint Sectae, & ex qua quotidie gravissima oriantur bella, venditan-tes.
units.tr: They call the Christian Church a fruitful mother of errors, from which countless sects have been born at all times, and from which the gravest wars arise every day, boasting

units.la: tes contra, Ecclesiæsuæ per totum orbem ter- rarum dispersæ, admirabilem fidei, Religio- nisque unitatem absque ulla aliqua aut sesta, aut hæresi, ex Judæo Anonymo, Quæst 39. Si Christiana Religio est vera, qui fit ut inter ipsos tanta fit Religionum & Sectarum se mutuo dam- nantium diversitas? Ex Judæo Orobio in Col- latione cum Limborchio, pag. 57,58. Nunquam usque ad Evangelium verbum divinum tot difficul- tates, tot dubia, tot varias intelligentias perpessum fuit: Unde enim tot sectarum differentiæ exortæ, nisi ex Veteris, & Novi Testamenti diverso intelle- ctu? Cum antea sacra scripta sincere ab Israele fue- rint intellecta; nulla nova secta in populum inve- cta (præter aliqua ad Dei cognitionem neq; ad Legis essentiam pertinentia, quæ depravato jam sæculo emersere, & paulo post per divinam misericordiam penitus evanuere,) conservatur, populus per totum orbem dispersus adeo in Religione unitus, ut jam nulla secta, nulla hæresis, sine Rege, sine judice, sine punitione pro transgressoribus; Sed unica ubique facies ecclesiæ, unus intellectus, una fides. Sed à na- scente ecclesia Christiana, quod fuerunt sibi contra- ria Evangelia, ex quibus plurima jam diu fuere re- jecta? Nec defecere dissidia inter Apostolos, neque hæreses sequentibus, usq; ad nostrum sæculis: Non quidem in rebus parvi momenti, sed quæ ad Religio- nis essentiam pertinebant: Circa Trinitatem, Chri- sti Iti divinitatem, æqualitatem, & consubstantialitatem cum Patre, personalitatem, humanitatem, corporalem, aut sacramentalem præsentiam in eucharistia, in Sacramentorum numero, & essentia, in baptismate, an de necessitate salutis, an non ita? Inde Ebionitæ, Arriani, Anabaptistæ, Manichei, Sociniani, & alij plurimi Sectarij, quorum hoc tempore non modica propago: sed quid de Idololatria Papistica, quam ab Apostolis traditam totus Christianismus plus quam per mille & tercentos annos defendit, & nunc in potiore Christianismi parte perseverat, cæteros de hæresi convictos asseverans. Unde igitur tot discrimina, tot sectæ, nisi ex Veteris & Novi Testamenti adeo diversa intelligentia, ut hos amaros fructus peperit.
units.tr: in contrast of the admirable unity of faith and religion of their own Church, spread throughout the whole world, without any sect or heresy. From the Anonymous Jew, Question 39: If the Christian religion is true, how does it come about that there is such a great diversity of religions and sects among them, each condemning the others? From the Jew Orobio, in his Conference with Limborch, pp. 57, 58: Never until the Gospel has the divine word suffered so many difficulties, so many doubts, so many different interpretations. For whence have so many differences of sects arisen, except from the different understanding of the Old and New Testaments? Before, when the sacred writings were understood sincerely by Israel, no new sect was introduced among the people (apart from some matters pertaining to the knowledge of God, not to the essence of the Law, which emerged in a corrupt age and shortly afterwards vanished entirely by divine mercy), and the people, scattered throughout the whole world, is so united in religion that no sect or heresy exists without a king, without a judge, without punishment for transgressors; rather, the face of the Church is everywhere one, one understanding, one faith. But from the rise of the Christian Church, how did the Gospels come to be in conflict with one another, many of which have long since been rejected? Nor have disagreements failed among the Apostles, nor heresies among those who followed, down to our times: not indeed on matters of little moment, but on those which pertained to the essence of religion: concerning the Trinity, the divinity of Christ, his equality and consubstantiality with the Father, his personality, his humanity, the bodily or sacramental presence in the Eucharist, the number and essence of the sacraments, and baptism, whether it is necessary for salvation or not. Hence the Ebionites, Arians, Anabaptists, Manicheans, Socinians, and many other sectaries, whose offspring are not small in this age. But what of the Papistical idolatry, which the whole of Christendom has defended for more than thirteen hundred years as handed down from the Apostles, and which still persists in the greater part of Christendom, asserting that others are convicted of heresy?
