Whence then so many discords and sects, except from so different an understanding of the Old and New Testaments, which has borne these bitter fruits?

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Accusant, repudiantque quam maxime Ecclesiam Romanam, quod Ecclesia sit Idololatrica, à Gentium Idololatria non multum distincta, quam, Deorum, Dearumque nominibus duntaxat mutatis, fuerit amplexa, uti loquitur Judæus Orobius in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag. 68,69. Cum igitur (Gentiles) Veteris Testamenti essent ignari, Evangelio facile credidere, & cultum pietate plenum admisere: cum antea summa cum barbarie plurimos homines mortuos ut Deos adorandos amplecterentur, multis fabulis contextis lumini rationis plane repugnangnantibus : quid mirum, quod melius instructi Deum Israelis admitterent, quem fortasse non crediderint nisi suo modo ipsis proponeretur humanatus, ex muliere natus, pulcherrimus, innocentissimus, mortuus, resurrectus, & in cœlis ad dextram Patris sedens inter divos collocatus: Erant similibus populi terra satis assueti. Paulo post vel statim a Christianismi exordio, paucis labentibus annis eadem gentium idololatria perstitit, divorum nominibus, atque dearum, duntaxat mutatis, quibus eadem antiqua templa fuere dicata, & in quibus non minus idololatricus cultus celebratur, & adhuc pro majore parte in Christianismo consistit. Cum igitur ego dixi ea argumenta suffecisse gentibus, non sic debet Doctissimus Vir intelligere, quasi dicere velim, ea argumenta pro statuendo Evangelio, utpote valida, & vera, suffecisse pro gentibus: sed quod ea ignara ob sui inscitiam potuerunt is facile convinci, & fidem praestare: nec enim habebant principia, quibus novis repugnarent, & sua antiqua sustinere possent, ideo Occidentales & Orientales Indi facillime non solum religionem, sed Papistica idola admisere, & alia quæcunque admitterent, si proponerentur, non ita Chinenses, utpote suis ritibus, quantumvis falsis, rationabilibus instructi; Etp. 140. Fecerunt profecto pariter ac Christiani Pontificii, qui suam evidentem Idololatriam cum Evangelica doctrina componunt, quamvis ei evidenter contrariam. riam. Credunt quod verum est omnibus Christianis; Sed vero falsitatem addidere, vano suae traditionis praetextu, quae non de patribus ad filios ortum habuit; Sed ab uno, vel altero incepta, & confecta, & ab aliorum credulitate recepta, tandem de una in alteram nationem inter plurimos homines propagata; Et pag. 141. Quod Papistis contigit, qui primitivae Ecclesiae sinceris actibus abutentes, in idololatricas, & sultas superstitiones, paulatim degenerarunt.
units.tr: They accuse the Roman Church most strongly and repudiate it, on the ground that the Church is idolatrous, not much different from the idolatry of the Gentiles, which it has embraced, the names of gods and goddesses alone having been changed, as the Jew Orobio says in his Conference with Limborch, pp. 68, 69: Since the Gentiles were ignorant of the Old Testament, they easily believed the Gospel and admitted a worship full of piety. Previously, with great barbarity, they had embraced very many dead men as gods to be worshipped, with many fables woven together, plainly repugnant to the light of reason. What wonder, then, that better instructed they should admit the God of Israel, whom perhaps they would not have believed unless he had been presented to them in a human manner, born of a woman, most beautiful, most innocent, dead, risen, and seated in heaven at the right hand of the Father, placed among the gods. They were fairly accustomed to similar things from their own land. Shortly after, or immediately from the beginning of Christianity, within a few years, the same idolatry of the Gentiles persisted, the names of the divinities and goddesses alone having been changed, to whom the same ancient temples had been dedicated, and in which no less idolatrous worship is celebrated, and which for the most part still consists in Christianity. Therefore, when I said that those arguments sufficed for the Gentiles, the most learned man ought not to understand it as if I wished to say that those arguments, being valid and true, sufficed for the Gentiles in establishing the Gospel; but that, being ignorant, they could easily be convinced by them on account of their lack of knowledge and give assent. For they had no principles by which they could resist new things and sustain their old ones; therefore the Western and Eastern Indians very readily admitted not only the religion but also Papistical idols, and would have admitted whatever else was proposed to them, but not so the Chinese, who, being instructed in their rites, however false, are reasonable. And p. 140: They have certainly done the same as the Papist Christians, who reconcile their manifest idolatry with the Evangelical doctrine, although it is manifestly contrary to it. They believe what is true, as all Christians do; but they have added falsehood, under the empty pretext of their tradition, which did not arise from fathers to sons, but was begun and completed by one or two men, received by the credulity of others, and at last propagated from one nation to another among very many people. And p. 141: This has happened to the Papists, who, abusing the sincere acts of the primitive Church, have gradually degenerated into idolatrous and superstitious practices.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Accusant Romanam Ecclesiam, quod cultum religiosum Angelis Sanctisque exhibeant, ex Maimonide, Albo, Abarbanele, Catechesi Judaica, aliisque, cap. 8. § 17. 18. Theologiae nostrae Judaicae; quod vitam commendent Monasticam, quae beluarum moribus magis sit congrua, quam hominum, ex Saadia Gaon, Maimonide, Orobio, cap. 13. § 9. Theol. Jud. Quod lignum adorent, crucemque, ex Maimonide, Kimchio, Bechai, Machsor Manuscripto, hoc cap. 15. § 12. Quod genua Baali flectant, ex Orobio, hoc eod. cap. § 9. Quod faciant simulacra contra Decalogi praeceptum, ex Judaeo Anonymo, Quaest. 10. Quo jure gloriantur Christiani, quasi Decalogum in pretio habeant, facientes simulacra; Quod Jesum Nazarenum dicant esse in pane, ex Lipmanno, cap. 16. Quod lectionem sacrae Scripturae proprohibeant, ex Judaeo Anonymo, Quaest. 40. Cur plebejis Scripturarum lectione interdicitur? An quia non sunt satis apti aut industrij intelligendis Scripturis? Cur Judaei hoc sive impedimentum sive incommodum non similiter verentur? Quod Papa le Dei proximum appellet, ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, lib.3. de Resurrectione mortuorum, cap.5. pag.290. Vel potius de Papa Romano capiendum est, qui se pastorem & proximum a Deo appellat, & Dei Vicarius in terris audire vult. Contra illum similesq; illi, qui potestate sunt inferiores, Deus bellum suscitabit; quod traditiones jactent incertas, confiastasque, ex Orobio, hoc cap. §.14. Quod crepent innumera miracula falsa, ex Orobio, in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag.15. Sic nostro tempore Pater Avianus Capucinus miraculis claret, populos, & principes decipit, ut sanctissimus impostor; Quod contra naturale Dei praeceptum Sacerdotibus suis non permittant uxores, ex Judaeo Anonymo, Quaest.32. Cur Sacerdotibus suis non permittunt Christiani ut uxores ducant, quod cum naturali Dei praecepto pugnat, dicentes: Crescite & multiplicamini: quae verba toti mundo dicta sunt? Et Quaest.33. Cur Sacerdotes Christianorum non ducunt uxores, cum Paulus ipsemet velit episcopum unius conjugis virum esse, 1.Tim.3:2.idemq; de Diaconis ait. Et cap. 4. ejusdem epist. monet venturos nonnonnullos, qui in hypocrisi mendacia loquentur, quorum conscientia velut cauterio adusta est, prohibentes matrimonium; Quod Sacrificuli, licet publice & licite matrimonia neutiquam contrahant, nihilominus tamen clam suis indulgeant libidinibus, ex Nizzachon veteri edito per Wagenseilium, pag. 43; Quin igitur potius sic accipienda Scriptura, ut loquatur de ea usatione, qua Monachi vestri & Sanctimoniales uruntur libidinibus, ac calescunt, & venerem appetunt, nec desideria possunt explere. Atque haec est illa usatio, quam Deus abominatur, oditq. Nam libido, in libro minorum Prophetarum, usatio vocatur, uti apud Hoseam cap. 7. verf. 4. Omnes adulterantur, similes fornaci ardenti: ignem urentem intra vos habetis. Scriptum quoq; Cant. cap. 8. verf. 6. Prunae ejus, prunae sunt ignis, flammaq; divina. Quin & in libro errorum ipsorum, hoc Pauli legitur dictum: Melius est uxorem ducere aliquam, quam adversus eam exardescere; Et pag. 241. Si Monachi in locum Sacerdotum successerunt, quare non ducunt uxores, & generant prolem, ceu Aaron Amrami filius summus Pontifex fecisse deprehenditur? Adde, quod primum omnium praeceptorum, quae Adamo protoplasto data fuerunt, ad sobolis procreationem pertinuit. Vos autem a conjugio abstinetis, & non fornicationibus tantum, sed & vino ac mero dediti estis, quibus corda vestra obruuntur; Quod Sacrificuli crificuli domum domui jungant, opes corra-dant immensas, terrasque ad fe rapiant, ex Nizzachon Veteri, pag.82. ad verba Efai.c.5. ¶.8. Va conjungentibus domum domui &c. Etiam hunc locum de cultoribus Jesu licet interpretari: ut nimirum significentur Monachi rasi, & Flamines, qui manibus suis omnes terras arripiunt, jungunt ades adibus, & agros agris, ut nullus locus illorum rapacitatem evadat. Et sedebitis foli in medio terra. Hae sunt mansiones illorum in Monasteriis; Accusant Ecclesiam Romanam, quod contendat Papam, Dei Vicarium, solvendi ligandique habere potestatem, cum nemo, praeter solum Deum, peccata possit dimittere & condonare, ipseque Moses hac facultate neutiquam fuerit praeditus, ex Nizzachon veteri, pag.250,251. Quia enim contenditis, Pontificem Dei Vicarium esse, eum ligandi & solvendi habere potestatem, quare non Sanctimonialibus jus concedit, ut foemina eas adeant, atque illis peccata exponant? Magis enim conveniens & honestius utique foret, ut foemina foeminis, viri viris confiteantur, quo fcortationum & adulteriorum evitentur occasiones. Interim, fi dicendum quod res est, aeque parum iste modus ac alter proficit; nemo enim dimittere & condonare peccata potest, praeter solum Deum: ac ne Moses quidem omnium Prophetarum maximus, facultate peccata remittendi ac condonandi gaudebat.
units.tr: They accuse the Roman Church of offering religious worship to angels and saints, citing Maimonides, Albo, Abarbanel, the Jewish Catechism, and others, ch. 8, §§ 17–18 of our Jewish Theology; of commending the monastic life, which is more suited to beasts than to men, citing Saadia Gaon, Maimonides, and Orobio, ch. 13, § 9 of the Jewish Theology; of adoring wood and the cross, citing Maimonides, Kimchi, Bechai, and the manuscript Machsor, this ch. 15, § 12; of bowing the knee to Baal, citing Orobio, this same ch., § 9; of making images contrary to the precept of the Decalogue, citing the anonymous Jew, Question 10: By what right do Christians boast, as if they held the Decalogue in esteem, while they make images? Of saying that Jesus of Nazareth is in the bread, citing Lipmann, ch. 16. Of forbidding the reading of Holy Scripture, citing the anonymous Jew, Question 40: Why are the common people forbidden to read the Scriptures? Is it because they are not apt or diligent enough to understand the Scriptures? Why do the Jews not fear this hindrance or inconvenience in the same way? Of the Pope calling himself the neighbour of God, citing Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, book 3 on the Resurrection of the Dead, ch. 5, p. 290: Or rather, it must be understood of the Roman Pope, who calls himself shepherd and neighbour of God, and wishes to be heard as God's Vicar on earth. Against him and those like him, who are inferior in power, God will raise up war. Of boasting of uncertain and fabricated traditions, citing Orobio, this ch., § 14. Of trumpeting countless false miracles, citing Orobio, in his Conference with Limborch, p. 15: So in our own time Father Avianus the Capuchin is famous for miracles, and deceives peoples and princes, like a most holy impostor. Of refusing their priests wives, contrary to the natural precept of God, citing the anonymous Jew, Question 32: Why do Christians not allow their priests to take wives, which fights against the natural precept of God, saying: "Increase and multiply"? Words spoken to the whole world. And Question 33: Why do the priests of the Christians not take wives, when Paul himself wishes a bishop to be the husband of one wife, 1 Tim. 3:2, and says the same of deacons? And in ch. 4 of the same epistle he warns that some will come who speak lies in hypocrisy, whose conscience is seared as with a hot iron, forbidding marriage; Of the priests, although they never contract marriage openly and lawfully, nevertheless indulging their lusts secretly, citing the old Nizzachon, published by Wagenseil, p. 43: Why, then, should Scripture not rather be taken as speaking of that burning by which your monks and nuns are inflamed with lusts, grow hot, and crave sexual intercourse, and cannot satisfy their desires? And this is that burning which God abominates and hates. For in the book of the Minor Prophets lust is called "burning," as in Hosea ch. 7, v. 4: "They are all adulterers, like a burning oven; you have a consuming fire within you." It is also written in Song of Songs ch. 8, v. 6: "Its sparks are sparks of fire, a divine flame." Indeed, in their own book of errors this saying of Paul is also read: "It is better to take a wife than to burn with desire for her." And on p. 241: "If the monks have succeeded the priests in their place, why do they not take wives and beget offspring, as Aaron, son of Amram, was found to have done as high priest? Add that the first of all the precepts given to Adam the first-formed was for the procreation of offspring. But you abstain from marriage, and are given over not only to fornication but also to wine and strong drink, by which your hearts are overwhelmed." Of the priests who join house to house, heap up immense wealth, and seize lands for themselves, citing the old Nizzachon, p. 82, on the words of Isaiah ch. 5, v. 8: Woe to those who join house to house, etc. This passage too may be interpreted of the worshippers of Jesus, namely to signify the shaven monks and flamens, who seize all lands with their hands, join house to house and field to field, so that no place escapes their rapacity. "And you will sit alone in the midst of the land." These are their dwelling places in the monasteries. They accuse the Roman Church of maintaining that the Pope, God's Vicar, has the power of binding and loosing, although no one but God alone can forgive and pardon sins, and Moses himself, the greatest of all the prophets, was not endowed with this faculty, citing the old Nizzachon, pp. 250–251: For since you contend that the Pontiff is God's Vicar and has the power of binding and loosing, why does he not grant to nuns the right that a woman may approach women and lay their sins before them? For it would surely be more fitting and more honourable that women confess to women and men to men, so that occasions of fornication and adultery may be avoided. Meanwhile, if the truth be told, this method profits no more than the other; for no one can forgive and pardon sins except God alone, and not even Moses, the greatest of all the prophets, possessed the faculty of remitting and pardoning sins.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Extollunt Unitarios, Arianos, Socinianos, Trinitatis hostes acerrimos, ex Rabbi Iiaco, Bar Abraham, in Munimine Fidei, pag 119. cap. 4. §. 6. Theol. Jud. Utentes hinc, non solum Socinianorum argutiis, ad nostram infringendam fidem, verum ipsos quoque solos æternæ beatitudinis participes pronuncian‐tes, uti testatus nuper est ArchiSynagogus Amstelodamensis apud Wulfferum in Animadversionibus ad Theriacam Judaicam Salomonis Zevi, pag. 248; Quare quoque Servetum, qui Genevæ combustus ob seditionem & blasphemias, Excellentem & Sapientem appellant, teste Rabbi David Gans, in Tzemach David, ad An. Mundi 5514, qui à nato Christo est 1554: Hoc quoque anno in urbe Geneva combustus est excellens sapiens Servetus, qui negaverat Deitatem Messiæ ipsorum, & cogitaverat renovare religionem Arianorum.
units.tr: They extol the Unitarians, Arians and Socinians, the bitterest enemies of the Trinity, citing Rabbi Isaac Bar Abraham, in Munimen Fidei, p. 119, ch. 4, §6, Theol. Jud. They use him not only to draw on the Socinians' subtleties in order to undermine our faith, but also to pronounce that they alone share in eternal blessedness, as the Amsterdam Archsynagogue recently testified in Wülfer's Animadversions on the Jewish Theriac of Solomon Zevi, p. 248. For the same reason they call Servetus, who was burned at Geneva for sedition and blasphemies, an "excellent and wise man," as Rabbi David Gans attests in Tzemach David, at the year of the world 5514, which is 1554 after the birth of Christ: In this year also the excellent sage Servetus was burned in the city of Geneva, who had denied the Deity of their Messiah and had planned to renew the religion of the Arians.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Damnant Apostatas, Mosaicæ fidei desertores, appellantes hos probrosis nominibus, mox Rejectos à Divino Numine, seu Perditos, ob Legem desertam, ejuratamque Religionem, ex confessione Judæorum unanimi, ipso pariter Rabbi Elia Levita in Lexico Thisbi, ad vocem Schamid: Hinc est, quod nos Judæi Judæi eum qui desciscit à Religione sua משומד voca-mus. Ab eo videlicet quod homines Apostatæ-cerunt tempore persecutionis, hinc est quod voca-runt eos משומדים, quasi dicas permutarunt legem propter persecutionem. Modo autem cum sua sponte nulla adacti persecutione à religione sua de-sciscunt, nihilominus tamen remansit eis hoc no-men; Mox illos nominantes מלשינים Calumnia-tores, Detractores, quod falsis criminibus one-rent Judæos; Mox מוסרים Proditores, quod fidei secreta prodant Christianis; Non solum diras imprecantes, extremamque maledictio-nem, ex quotidianis precationum libellis: Et omnibus Apostatis nulla sit spes: omnes hæretici quasi momento pereant: omnesque inimici populi tui cito exscindantur: regnum superbiæ eradicato, confrin-gito & destruito: subigito eos omnes cito in diebus nostris; Sed aqua igne que interdicentes, imo ad ipsam necem, si sine periculo fieri posset, omnibus modis rapientes, ex Rabbi Maimo-nidis Codice Manuscripto Avoda Sara, c. 10. Proditores Israelis, & Hæreticos, & Epicuræos, jussi sumus, manu nostra trucidare, & ad inferos usque persequi, quia Israelem affligunt, populumque seduncunt, ut Jesus Nazarenus cum discipulis suis, & Zadocus, ac Baithosus, cum asseclis eorum. Nomen autem imporum horum putrescat? Conquerun-tur quoque de multitudine Apostatarum, præpræsertim in Hispania & Portugallia, ex Judæo Orobio in Collatione cum Limborchio, pag. 102. Post vero Idololatriam Papisticam magnus Judæorum numerus in diversis regionibus amplectebatur, & à Lege divina defecit; nostrisq; temporibus id ipsum experimur. Neapolitana Synagoga persecutionem perferre non potens ad Papismum conversa: Bareinonica, & quotquot erant in tota Catalonia, diris tormentis, præter eos, qui martyrium sustinuerunt, & eos qui mature aufugerant, religionem abnegarunt, & idololatriam admisere. Quid dicam de Hispania, & Portugalia? Ubi ex Judæis Apostatis fere omnes & principes, nobiles, & populares originem ducunt: quod in iis regionibus adeo notum ut nemo dubitaverit: quamvis pro insignis nobilitatis, & dignitatibus, præsertim Ecclesiasticis obtinendis Judaismum abjurare oportet, & informationes exhibere, quod ab Israele oriundi non sunt: quod falsis testibus adhibitis, ut in regia, auro etiam juvante, facile consequuntur. Ideo omnium Monachorum claustra, atq; monialium Judæorum plena. Canonici, Inquisitores, Episcopi, plurimi ex Judæis procedunt: non pauci in corde judaizant, & propter ea bona temporalia, Christianismum fimmulant: ex quibus aliqui respiscunt, & ut possunt, effugiunt.
units.tr: They condemn apostates, deserters of the Mosaic faith, calling them by shameful names, first rejected by the Divine Majesty, or lost, because they have deserted the Law and abjured the religion. This is the unanimous confession of the Jews, as Rabbi Elijah Levita also says in the Lexicon Thisbi, under the word Shamad: Hence it is that we Jews call one who falls away from his religion meshumad [מְשֻׁמָּד]. This is because men who apostatised in a time of persecution were called meshumadim, as if to say they changed the law on account of persecution. Yet now, when people fall away from their religion of their own accord, with no compulsion of persecution, the name has nonetheless remained for them. Then they call them malshinim [מַלְשִׁינִים], calumniators and detractors, because they burden the Jews with false accusations; then moserim [מוֹסְרִים], betrayers, because they disclose the secrets of the faith to the Christians. Nor do they only utter dire curses and the most extreme malediction in their daily prayer books: And let there be no hope for any apostates: let all heretics perish in an instant: and let all the enemies of your people be quickly cut off: uproot, crush and destroy the kingdom of pride: subdue them all quickly in our days. They also forbid them water and fire, and indeed, if it could be done without danger, they seize them by every means for the very killing itself, according to the Manuscript Code of Rabbi Maimonides, Avoda Sara, ch. 10: We have been commanded to slaughter with our own hand the betrayers of Israel, the heretics and the Epicureans, and to pursue them even to hell, because they afflict Israel and lead the people astray, as Jesus of Nazareth did with his disciples, and Zadok and Baithos with their followers. May the name of these impious men rot! They also complain of the multitude of apostates, especially in Spain and Portugal, according to the Jew Orobio in his Conference with Limborch, p. 102: Indeed, after Papist idolatry, a great number of Jews in various regions embraced it and fell away from the divine Law; and in our own times we see the same thing. The Neapolitan synagogue, unable to bear persecution, turned to Papism. The synagogue of Barcelona, and all those in the whole of Catalonia, under dreadful torments, apart from those who endured martyrdom and those who fled early, renounced their religion and admitted idolatry. What shall I say of Spain and Portugal? There almost all the princes, nobles and commoners trace their origin to Jewish apostates. This is so well known in those regions that no one doubts it, although to obtain distinguished nobility and dignities, especially ecclesiastical ones, one must renounce Judaism and provide sworn statements that one is not descended from Israel. With false witnesses brought forward, they easily obtain this, aided even by gold, as is well known at court. Hence the cloisters of all the monks and nuns are full of Jews. Canons, inquisitors and bishops, very many of them, come from Jews; not a few secretly still favour Judaism, and for the sake of temporal goods they feign Christianity. Some of them repent and, as far as they can, escape.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Damnant Judæos Sadducæos, Animarum & Rerumpublicarum pestes, ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, in Epistola Dedicatoria Libri I. de Resurrectione Mortuorum: Atque hucuniversaprimi libri opera tendit, ut cunctiintelligant, in doctrina hac tam necessaria omnes nos contra Zaducæos, animarum, & Rerumpublicarum pestes, penitus convenire; Probantes operose contra Sadducæos Animarum immortalitatem, mortuorumque Resurrectionem, uti patet ex Rabbi Menasseh, qui tres libros de mortuorum resurrectione consignavit; Quorum numerus valde licet decreverit, reperiuntur nihilominus tamen in Turcia, Italia, maxime vero in Hispania, maluntque ob odium publicum, cum periculosum valde esset apud populum in publico seculum negare futurum, magis latitare, quam in omnium vivere oculis; Inter hos Sadducæos seculo nostro percelebris fuit Uriel Acosta, qui edito libro demonstrare conatus est, Legem Mosaicam nihil aliud observantibus & transgredientibus proponere, quam præmium aut pœnam temporalem; Sed non solum nastus Adversarium Judæum, Samuelem de Sylva, qui contrario libello Animarum demonstravit immortalitatem, verum quoque, postquam flagris esset percussus à Synagoga Amstelodamensi, incidit in desperationem, miserabilemque, se ipsum globo transverberans, obiit mortem, uti refert Limborchius in Praefatione Urielis Acostae Exemplaris vitae humanae.
units.tr: They condemn the Sadducees, the Jews, as pests of souls and commonwealths, citing Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, in the Dedicatory Epistle to his first book on the Resurrection of the Dead: And the whole aim of this first book is that everyone should understand that in this doctrine, so necessary, all of us are wholly agreed against the Sadducees, the pests of souls and of commonwealths. He labours to prove against the Sadducees the immortality of the soul and the resurrection of the dead, as is clear from Rabbi Menasseh, who wrote three books on the resurrection of the dead. Although their number has greatly dwindled, nevertheless some are still found in Turkey and Italy, and above all in Spain. They prefer to lie hidden, because of public hatred, rather than live in the sight of all, since it would be very dangerous to deny the future age in public before the people. Among these Sadducees, in our own century, Uriel Acosta was very famous. He published a book attempting to show that the Mosaic Law offers to those who keep or transgress it nothing but temporal reward or punishment. But not only did he, having been opposed by the Jewish adversary Samuel da Silva, who in a counter-book demonstrated the immortality of the soul, fall into despair; also, after he had been flogged by the Amsterdam Synagogue, he tormented himself, beating his head with a ball, and died, as Limborch reports in the Preface to Uriel Acosta's Exemplar of Human Life.

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Damnant, Judaeos Samaritanos, odium continuantes cum Samaritanis Vatinianum, multisque hos proscindentes convitiis, contumeliisque, quod Idolo Hemathaeorum Afschima, de quo 2. Reg. cap. 17. gloriam tribuant creationis, illudque pro vero colant Numine, pro verbis Genes. cap. 1. vers. 1. In principio creavit Deus coelum & terram; ponentes: In principio creavit Afschima coelum & terram, ex Rabbi Aben Esra in Proœmio ad librum Esther: Cuthaei scripserunt pro In principio creavit Deus, creavit Afschima; Cum tamen Samaritani suos ab omni dehortentur idololatria, credantque unum Deum Israelis, Deum Abrahami, Isaci, & Jacobi, ex literis novissimis Samaritanorum ad Illustrem Virum, Jobum Ludolfum, fautorem maximum; Credunt praeterea Samaritani hodierni le puros atque sanctos, se Legis Mosaicae observatores, pro norma Religionis non alios admittentes libros, quam quinque Mosis, nec legentes libros Prophetarum Judaicorum, ex Epistolis Samaritanis ad Ludolfum; Quicquid continetur in Lege Mosis, observant, non omittentes CirCircumcisionem masculi, die octavo; Observant septem festa solennia, ex Epistolis Samaritanorum ad Ludolfum; Negant Mesliam adhucdum venisse, ex Samaritanorum literis ultimis ad Ludolfum; Gloriantur se Sanctorum, Prophetarumque servare sepulchra, inservireque, ex iisdem literis; Conqueruntur de odio & iniquitate Judæorum Rabbinorum, ex iisdem literis; Extollunt montem Garizim, locum Dei electum, domum Dei, glorificantes flatis festis in monte Garizim, ex relatione Jacobi Levi Tomeritæ, Judæi Hebronensis apud Ludolfum in Præfatione Epistolarum Samaritanarum; Precaturi mane & vesperi in suis locis, maxime in urbe Sichem, facies versus montem Garizim vertunt, ex citatis literis; Confitentur se Sabbathum valde stricte observare, non egredientes die Sabbathi de loco suo, nisi ad domum Domini orandi causa, ex literis Samaritanorum ad Anglos exaratis; Gloriantur, quod habeant Sacerdotes, ex filiis Levi & ex filiis Aaronis atque ex Sinchali filiis oriundos; Confitentur se in Gaza quoque habitare, ex literis Samaritanorum ad Anglos; Sed de his plura in libris Samaritanorum ad Scaligerum, quæ nuper publici juris quoque sunt factæ.
units.tr: They condemn the Jews, who keep up the Vatinian hatred against the Samaritans and assail them with many reproaches and insults, because the Samaritans ascribe the glory of creation to the idol of the Hemathites, Afschima, mentioned in 2 Kings chapter 17, and worship it as the true deity. For the words of Genesis 1:1, "In the beginning God created heaven and earth," they substitute "In the beginning Afschima created heaven and earth," according to Rabbi Aben Ezra in the preface to the book of Esther: The Cuthaeans wrote, for "In the beginning God created," "Afschima created". Yet the Samaritans dissuade their people from all idolatry, and believe in one God of Israel, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, according to the most recent letters of the Samaritans to the illustrious man Job Ludolf, their greatest patron. Moreover, the Samaritans of today believe that they are pure and holy, observers of the Mosaic Law, and admit no books as the rule of religion other than the five books of Moses; they do not read the books of the Jewish Prophets, according to the Samaritan letters to Ludolf. They observe whatever is contained in the Law of Moses, not omitting the circumcision of males on the eighth day. They observe the seven solemn feasts, according to the Samaritan letters to Ludolf. They deny that the Messiah has yet come, according to the Samaritans' latest letters to Ludolf. They boast that they keep and serve the tombs of the saints and prophets, according to the same letters. They complain of the hatred and injustice of the Jewish rabbis, according to the same letters. They extol Mount Gerizim, the place chosen by God, the house of God, and glorify the festivals celebrated on Mount Gerizim, according to the report of Jacob Levi Tomeritae, a Jew of Hebron, given to Ludolf in the preface to the Samaritan letters. When they pray morning and evening in their own places, especially in the city of Shechem, they turn their faces towards Mount Gerizim, according to the letters cited. They confess that they observe the Sabbath very strictly, not leaving their place on the Sabbath day except to go to the house of the Lord to pray, according to the letters written by the Samaritans to the English. They boast that their priests are descended from the sons of Levi, from the sons of Aaron, and from the sons of Sinchal, according to the letters written by the Samaritans to the English. They confess that they also dwell in Gaza, according to the letters of the Samaritans to the English. But more on these matters is found in the books of the Samaritans addressed to Scaliger, which have recently also been made public.

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: Damnant Judæos Karraitas, caneque pejus & angue fugiunt,imo inferiori & deteriori,quam aut Christianos, aut Gentiles habent loco, appellantes Karraitas diversis contumeliosis appellationibus, mox םינמרה Hæreticos, mox Epicuræos, Sadducæos, Cuthæos, Spuriosque; Dira quævis ipsis imprecantes; Nulla cum ipsis ineuntes connubia, nullum commercium, nullamque cum ipsis contrahentes conversationem, ex confessione Judæorum Rabbinorum, non diffitente Rabbi Leone Mutinensi in Opusculo de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum, Part. V. cap. 1.
units.tr: They condemn the Karaite Jews and shun them worse than a dog or a snake. They hold them in lower and worse regard than either Christians or Gentiles, and they call the Karaites by various abusive names: now Heretics [םינמרה], now Epicureans, Sadducees, Cuthites, and bastards. They pray all manner of curses upon them. They enter into no marriages with them, have no dealings or fellowship with them, and make no contracts with them. So confesses the Jewish rabbis, as Rabbi Leone of Modena does not deny in his little work on the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part V, chapter 1.

units.la: Hi Rabbanistæ seu Magistrales capitali odio persequuntur Karraitas, nolentes cum ipsis ullam contrahere affinitatem conjunctionemve, aut cum ipsis conversari, reputantes eos ממזרים idest, Spurios, eo quod in rebus matrimonialibus, repudio, & purificationibus fœminarum, nullas Rabbinorum constitutiones observent; Et certe tanta in Karraitas Rabbanistarum exacerbatio est, ut si quis Karraita ad Rabbanistarum transfire vellet sacra, arceretur, & ab omni aditu intercluderetur; Quod confirmat pariter Postellus, qui linguarum, consuetudinumque diversarum gentium egregiam habuit notitiam, cum in Alphabeto 12. Linguarum sic loquitur: Ditissimum hominum genus nus, (Karraitæ)sed usque adeo cæteris invisum, ut bona pars virginum illorum, quia per affinitatem & paucitatem, non sibi satis sunt, innupta maneat. Asserunt insuper communis opinionis Judæi, si accideret ut Christianus & Caraimus unus demergerentur una, pari utriusque salvandi potestate, pontem se effecturos corpore Caraimi adsalvandum Christianum. Damnant autem Karraitas Judæos, non propterea, quod negent animarum immortalitatem, paradisum, infernum, mortuorum denique resurrectionem, cum omnibus his veritatibus assentiantur, uti contra ipsos Judæos sincere & candide refert Rabbi Leo Mutinensis in citato Opusculo Part. V.cap.1. Negari alias nequit, Sadducaos fetiam pestiferam, animæ immortalitatem, & consequenter paradisum, infernum, purgatorium, resurrectionem, aliaque sanctæ credenda, pessime olim negasse. Karraitæ contra omnibus istis veritatibus hodie assentiuntur; Sed quod Legem Moysis Oralem, Talmudecomprehensam, divinam, authenticam, a Deoque profectam esse, negent, repudiantes Pharisæorum fictas, fabulosasque traditiones, solo scripturæ sensu literali contenti, uti aliquo modo liquet ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi, Part. V.cap.1. Fundamentum denominationis Karraitarum in eo situm, quoniam tantum quinque libros Moysaicos agnoscunt, atque am- plectanplectuntur, eos〈q;〉 juxta literam accipiunt, & interpretantur, neglectis Doctorum expositionibus, paraphrasibus, & constitutionibus; Caeterum credunt Karraitae, Religionis, fideique Regulam, non esse Mosis Legem Oralem, sed scriptam, in Codice Veteris Testamenti comprehensam; Credunt non quinque Libros Mosis tantum pro fidei norma amplectendos, uti ipse Rabbi Leo Mutinensis ex errore putavit, sed reliquos quoque Veteris Testamenti libros pari pietatis affectu excipiendos, quod inde quam manifeste patet, quia eadem Bibliorum habent exemplaria, ipsumque Vetus Testamentum a numero librorum appellant XXIV Viginti quatuor; Credunt hominem per Legis Mosaicae observantiam salvari; Credunt Resurrectionem mortuorum, Animarum immortalitatem, vitam aeternamque, reliquaque fidei Judaicae Essentialia; Aestimant quoque traditiones, sed non ut Oracula amplectuntur divina; Credunt puncta vocalia esse a Mose ex literis Peringeri, testis auriti, ad Ludolfum, in Celeberrimi Tenzelii nostri menstruis Colloquiis, An. 1691. pag. 574; Distincti interim sunt a Judaeis Rabbanitis, seu Pharisaeis, tum circa gradus consanguinitatis in conjugiis, circa divortia; tum circa usum Anathematum, circa immunditiem, mulierum rumque purificationes, circa cibos vetitos & licitos, non adhibentes in mensis diversa mantilia, ollas, patinas, cultrosque; Non Zizith in vestibus portantes, sed Synagogae alligantes; Dissentientes à Rabbanistis in figendo Novilunio, in ratione intercalandi, in observandis festis; Non legentes pro Jehova Adonai, sed Jave; Improbantes nimias Rabbanistarum usuras; Hinc suas peculiares habent libros Rituales, aliosque, quibus superbit Bibliotheca Lugduno Batava, interque quos caput efferunt sequentes: Libri Karraeorum. Liber Menachem Karraitae. Syntagma librorum Karraeorum. Bacca Cypri Judae filii Eliae Karraitae. Systema Ordinationis Karraitarum. Controversia Karraeorum cum Rabbanitis. Liber praeceptorum ex mente Karraitarum. Ritus Karraeorum. Epistola de dissensu Cabbalistico & Karraitico in materia Sabbathi. Constitutio Rituum Karraeorum. Levini Warneri Expositio Pentateuchi ex MSS. Karraeorum, Aaronis, Jelchuae, Japheti, &c. De Karraeorum dogmatibus, quibus dissentiunt à Rabbanitis, cum versione Warneri. Commentarius in S. Scripturam ex libris Karraeorum, cum versione Warneri; Modi explicandi Scripturam juxta mentem Karraeorum, cum versione Warneri; Sed de his, aliisque Karraitarum libris, rebusque reliquis, de eorum sedibus, prima origine atque separatione à Judaeis Rabbaniftis, dicemus aliquando pluribus, in Religione Karraitarum.
units.tr: These Rabbanites, or Magistrales, pursue the Karaites with deadly hatred. They refuse to form any marriage alliance or union with them, or to associate with them, and regard them as mamzerim [ממזרים], that is, spurious, because in matters of marriage, divorce, and the purification of women they observe none of the constitutions of the Rabbis. Indeed the Rabbanites' rage against the Karaites is so great that if any Karaite wished to pass over to the Rabbanites' rites, he would be kept out and shut off from every approach. Postellus, who had an excellent knowledge of languages and of the customs of various peoples, confirms this equally. In his Alphabet of Twelve Languages he speaks thus: The richest race of men (the Karaites), but so hateful to the rest that a good part of their virgins, because of the narrowness of kinship and their small number, are not enough for themselves and remain unmarried. Moreover the Jews of common opinion assert that if a Christian and a Karaite were to sink together, with equal power of each to be saved, they would make a bridge of the Karaite's body to save the Christian. The Karaites, however, do not condemn the Jews because they deny the immortality of the soul, paradise, hell, or finally the resurrection of the dead, since they assent to all these truths. Rabbi Leo of Modena sincerely and candidly reports this against the Jews themselves in the work already cited, Part V, chapter 1. It cannot otherwise be denied that the pestilent Sadducees once very wickedly denied the immortality of the soul, and consequently paradise, hell, purgatory, the resurrection, and other things holy to be believed. The Karaites today, on the contrary, assent to all these truths; but they deny that the Oral Law of Moses, contained in the Talmud, is divine, authentic, and proceeded from God. They reject the feigned and fabulous traditions of the Pharisees and are content with the literal sense of Scripture alone, as is somewhat clear from Rabbi Leo of Modena, Part V, chapter 1. The foundation of the Karaite denomination lies in this, that they acknowledge only the five books of Moses, embrace them, and take and interpret them according to the letter, neglecting the expositions, paraphrases, and constitutions of the teachers. Moreover, the Karaites believe that the rule of religion and faith is not the Oral Law of Moses but the written law, contained in the codex of the Old Testament. They believe that not only the five books of Moses are to be embraced as the norm of faith, as Rabbi Leo of Modena wrongly thought, but that the remaining books of the Old Testament too are to be received with equal affection of piety. This is clear enough from the fact that they have the same copies of the Bible, and they call the Old Testament itself by its number of books, Twenty-four. They believe that man is saved by observance of the Law of Moses. They believe in the resurrection of the dead, the immortality of souls, eternal life, and the other essentials of the Jewish faith. They also esteem the traditions, but do not embrace them as divine oracles. They believe the vowel points were devised by Moses, according to the letter of Peringer, the ear-witness, to Ludolf, in our famous Tenzel's Monthly Conversations, year 1691, p. 574. They are, however, distinguished from the Rabbanite, or Pharisaic, Jews: concerning degrees of consanguinity in marriage and concerning divorces; concerning the use of anathemas, uncleanness, and the purifications of women; concerning forbidden and permitted foods, not using different napkins, pots, dishes, and knives at table; not wearing zizith on their garments but fastening them to the synagogue; differing from the Rabbanites in fixing the new moon, in the method of intercalation, and in observing the feasts; not reading Adonai for Jehovah but Jave; and disapproving of the Rabbanites' excessive usury. Hence they have their own peculiar ritual books and others, of which the Library at Leiden boasts, and among which the following stand out: The Books of the Karaites. The Book of Menachem the Karaite. The Compendium of the Karaite Books. The Cyprus Berry of Judah son of Elijah the Karaite. The System of Ordination of the Karaites. The Controversy of the Karaites with the Rabbanites. The Book of Precepts according to the mind of the Karaites. The Rites of the Karaites. A Letter on the Cabbalistic and Karaite disagreement concerning the Sabbath. The Constitution of the Rites of the Karaites. Levi Warner's Exposition of the Pentateuch from the manuscripts of the Karaites, Aaron, Jelchua, Japheth, etc. On the dogmas of the Karaites, in which they differ from the Rabbanites, with Warner's translation. A Commentary on Scripture from the books of the Karaites, with Warner's translation. Methods of explaining Scripture according to the mind of the Karaites, with Warner's translation. But of these and other Karaite books, and of their remaining matters, their seats, first origin, and separation from the Rabbanite Jews, we shall some time speak at greater length, in the Religion of the Karaites.

units.la: CAPUT XVI. De Sacramentis.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVI. On the Sacraments.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: JActant Judæi nostri, Ecclesiæ suæ Sacramenta, Sacraficia puta, per Messiam Regem cum Templo Hierosolymitano restauranda, maxime Circumcisionem & Pascha, asserentes sua Sacramenta perennia, non mutanda, aut abolenda, quod fœderis divini signa sint perpetua, לעולם in æternitatem à Summo data Numine, per quæ tum à profanis distinguantur gentibus, tum vitam acquirerent æternam.
units.tr: Our Jews boast that their Church's sacraments, namely their sacrifices, are to be restored with the Temple of Jerusalem through the Messiah the King. They maintain that their sacraments are everlasting, not to be changed or abolished, because they are signs of the divine covenant, which the Supreme Deity gave for eternity [לעולם], and through which they are distinguished both from the profane nations and win eternal life.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Primum Ecclesiæ suæ Sacramentum ponunt Circumcisionem, quam Sacramentum vocant Initiationis, per quam Israelis ingrediantur fœdus, hæredesque futuri incipiunt
units.tr: They put circumcision first among their Church's sacraments. They call it the sacrament of initiation, through which Israelites enter the covenant and begin to be heirs of the age to come, since before circumcision they are by nature children of wrath. (From Rabbi Maimonides, in Hilchot Milah, ch. 3, §1.)

units.la: esse seculi, cum ante Circumcisionem a natura sint filii irae, ex Rabbi Maimonide in Hilchot Milah, cap. 3. §. 1. Et si nonnulli adstiterint Circumcisioni, dicunt- Quemadmodum initiasti eum fœdere: sic vovemus, inities eum Legi, & matrimonio, & bonis operibus; Ex Col Bo, in Constitut. de Circumcis. Sect. 75. Si non adfuerit pater pueri, tum adstantes benedicunt, ad initiandum eum; Et statim: Nihilominus in praxi hoc observant, ut susceptor benedicat, ad initiandum eum; Appellant Circumcisionem Signum fœderis sanctum, statutum in carne, תחומה Signaculum, Sigillum, quo caro, seu carnalis homo a Deo signatus, caro Dei est, Deoque soli dicatus, sicque a reliquis distinctus gentibus, imo per quam, tam in vita, quam in morte, permanens gerit fœderis signum, sacramentumque, cum reliqua, quae quaedam signa etiam sint, sed inferiora, ut Zizit, Tephillin, Mesura, sint extra hominem, neque semper illi praesentia, & ob oculos versentur continuo, ex Rabbi Maimonide in Hilchot Milah, cap. 3. §. 3. Postea benedicit pater filioli, aut qui circumcidit, aut aliquus ex adstantibus: Benedictus tu es, Domine Deus noster, Rex mundi, qui sanctificavit dilectum ab utero, & statutum in carne ejus posuit, & posteros ejus obsignavit per signum fœderis sanctum.
units.tr: And if some are present at the circumcision, they say: As you have initiated him into the covenant, so we vow that you will initiate him into the Law, and into marriage, and into good works. (From Col Bo, in the Constitutions on Circumcision, sect. 75.) If the father of the boy is not present, then those standing by bless, to initiate him. And straightaway: Nevertheless in practice they observe this, that the sponsor blesses, to initiate him. They call circumcision the holy sign of the covenant, established in the flesh, seal [חותם], seal, signet, by which the flesh, or the carnal man, is marked by God, is the flesh of God and dedicated to God alone, and so is distinguished from the other nations; indeed through it, both in life and in death, he bears the sign of the covenant and its sacrament, along with the other signs, which are also signs, but of lower rank, such as the Zizit, Tephillin and Mezuzah, which are outside the man and are not always present to him and before his eyes continually. (From Rabbi Maimonides, in Hilchot Milah, ch. 3, §3.) Afterwards the father of the little son, or the one who circumcises, or someone of those standing by, blesses: Blessed are you, Lord our God, King of the world, who sanctified the beloved from the womb, and placed in his flesh the statute, and sealed his offspring with the holy sign of the covenant.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Asserunt Circumcisionem omnium praeceptorum esse maximum, quod reliqua superet omnia, aequivalensque sit toti Legi Mosaicae, illudque patere satis ex verbis Mosis, Deuter. c. 30. v. 12. Quis ascendet nobis in caelum? In quibus responsio sit parata, nempe Circumcisio מילה, quae ex quatuor literis constat initialibus; Hinc qui per Circumcisionem Proselytus justitiae factus erat, omnia tenebatur servare praecepta, eratque legis universae debitor, non diffitente Apostolo Paulo, in Epistola ad Galatas cap. 5. vers. 3. Testor enim rursum omni homini, qui circumciditur, eum esse debitorem totius legis servandae; Ex Rabbi Davide Kimchio in Libro Schorascim, ad vocem אר. Est praterea, qui proselytus perfectus fit, & cooptatur omnino; ille est, quem lex ad servanda praecepta obligat, Levit. cap. 18. vers. 26. Indigena & proselytus, &c. Et Numer. cap. 9. vers. 14. Statutum unum erit vobis, & proselyto &c.; Hinc quoque docent, quod propter omnia praecepta, tres excisiones Israeli sint denunciatae, seu qui omnia & singula transgrediuntur divina praecepta, triplici multentur excisione; Ille vero qui unicam Circumcisionis Legem violet, carnem praeputii sui non circumciden-do, tredecim mereatur excisiones, utiloquitur Rabbi Maimonides, in Hilchot Milah, cap. 3. §. 9. Caeterum propter omnia & singula praecepta gravia decreta sunt Israelitis tres excisiones, quia dictum est: Haec sunt verba foederis, quod praecepit Dominus, praeter id, quod pepigit cum illis in Choreb. Iterum vero dicit alibi: Vos stantes estis hodie omnes, ut transeatis in foedus Domini Dei tui. Ecce isti sunt tres excisiones. Verum enim vero super circumcisione decreta sunt tredecim excisiones, scilicet cum Abrahamo patre nostro. 1. Et dabo foedus meum inter me & inter te. 2. Ego, ecce foedus meum tecum. 3. Et erigam foedus meum inter me, & inter te. 4. In foedus aeternum. 5. Et tu foedus meum servabis. 6. Et foedus meum quod servabitis. 7. Et erit in signum foederis. 8. Et erit foedus meum in carne vestra. 9. In foedus aeternum. 10. Foedus meum irritum fecit. 11. Et erigam foedus meum cum eo. 12. In foedus aeternum. 13. Et foedus meum erigam cum Isaco.
units.tr: They assert that circumcision is the greatest of all the commandments, that it surpasses all the rest and is equivalent to the whole Mosaic Law, and that this is clear enough from the words of Moses, Deut. ch. 30, v. 12: Who will ascend into heaven for us? To this the answer is ready, namely that circumcision [מילה], which consists of four initial letters. Hence whoever became a proselyte of righteousness through circumcision was bound to keep all the commandments, and was a debtor to the whole Law, the Apostle Paul not denying it, in the Epistle to the Galatians, ch. 5, v. 3: For I testify again to every man who is circumcised that he is a debtor to keep the whole law. (From Rabbi David Kimchi, in the book Schorashim, under the word [אר].) There is moreover one who becomes a perfect proselyte and is wholly admitted; he is the one whom the Law obliges to keep the commandments, Lev. ch. 18, v. 26: The native and the proselyte, etc. And Num. ch. 9, v. 14: There shall be one statute for you, and for the proselyte, etc. Hence they also teach that on account of all the commandments three excisions are threatened to Israel; that is, those who transgress all and each of the divine commandments are punished with a threefold excision. But whoever violates the single law of circumcision, by not circumcising the flesh of his foreskin, deserves thirteen excisions, as Rabbi Maimonides says in Hilchot Milah, ch. 3, §9. Moreover, for all and each of the grave commandments three excisions have been decreed for the Israelites, because it is said: These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded, besides what he covenanted with them in Horeb. And again he says elsewhere: You stand here today all of you, that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God. Behold, these are the three excisions. But truly, with regard to circumcision, thirteen excisions have been decreed, namely with Abraham our father: 1. And I will give my covenant between me and between you. 2. Behold, my covenant is with you. 3. And I will establish my covenant between me and between you. 4. For an everlasting covenant. 5. And you shall keep my covenant. 6. And my covenant which you shall keep. 7. And it shall be a sign of the covenant. 8. And my covenant shall be in your flesh. 9. For an everlasting covenant. 10. He has broken my covenant. 11. And I will establish my covenant with him. 12. For an everlasting covenant. 13. And I will establish my covenant with Isaac.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Crepant Circumcisionis merita, quod hominem liberet e fovea, ex Rabbi Maimonide in Hichot Milah, cap. 3. §. 3. Ideo per meritum hoc Deus vivus, portio nostra, petra nostra, praecepit liberare dilectas carnis nostrae e fovea, propter foedus suum, quod posuit in carne nostra; Et ex Auctore Libri Col Bo, in Expositione benedictionis nis super circumcisione, Sect. 73. Praecepit eri-pere dilectas carnis nostrae e fovea, sicut scriptum est: Etiam tu per sanguinem foederis tui emisisti vinctos tuos e fovea, in qua non sunt aquae. Nimi-rum, qui participes sunt foederis hujus circumcisio-nis, liberantur a judicio inferni per meritum Abrahami; excepto eo, qui congreditur cum gentili, & qui rursus attrahit praeputium suum; Quod homo qui ante circumcisionem est lordidus & abominabilis in oculis Dei, incipiat post praeputii amputationem purus & perfectus esse, ex Rabbi Eliezeris Pirke, cap. 15. §. 4. Theol. Jud.
units.tr: They extol the merits of circumcision, because it frees a man from the pit (From Rabbi Maimonides, in Hichot Milah, ch. 3, §3). Therefore through this merit the living God, our portion, our rock, commanded that the beloved of our flesh be freed from the pit, on account of his covenant which he placed in our flesh. And from the author of the book Col Bo, in the exposition of the blessing over circumcision, sect. 73: He commanded that the beloved of our flesh be snatched from the pit, as it is written: Also you, by the blood of your covenant, have sent forth your prisoners from the pit in which there is no water. Namely, those who share in this covenant of circumcision are freed from the judgment of hell through the merit of Abraham; except the one who has intercourse with a Gentile woman and who again draws back his foreskin. (And that a man who before circumcision is filthy and abominable in the eyes of God begins after the removal of the foreskin to be pure and perfect: from Rabbi Eliezer's Pirke, ch. 15, §4.) (Theol. Jud.)

units.la: Quod per Circumcisionem vitae aeternae accipiat haereditatem, ex Tractatu Talmudico Sanhedrin, cap. II. Quaeritur, quando infans particeps esse possit futuri saeculi, &c? Rabbi Nachmam filius Isaaci respondet: statim atque circumcisus est, juxta illud Psalm. 88. verf. 16. Afflictus ego sum, & moribundus ab adolescentia mea portavi terrores tuos: timebo; Quod in sanguine circumcisionis vitam vivant aeternam, Ezech. c. 16. v. 6. ex R. Eliezere in Pirke, c. 29.
units.tr: That through circumcision he receives the inheritance of eternal life: from the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, ch. II. The question is, when can an infant be a sharer in the age to come, etc.? Rabbi Nachman son of Isaac answers: as soon as he is circumcised, according to that passage in Psalm 88, v. 16: I am afflicted and dying from my youth; I have borne your terrors, I shall be dismayed. That in the blood of circumcision they live an eternal life: Ezek. ch. 16, v. 6, from R. Eliezer in Pirke, ch. 29.

units.la: Die isto, quo egressi sunt Israelitae Aegypto, circumcisi sunt omnes a magno usque ad parvum, juxta illud Josef. cap. 5. verf. 4. Circumcisi enim erant omnes de populo, qui egressi erant. Sumserunt autem sanguinem circumcisionis & sanguinem paschatis, eumque collocarunt super liminare, adium suarum, ut cum cum transiret Sanctus Benedictus & videret san-guinem fœderis, & sanguinem paschatis, implere-tur misericordia supra Israelitas, sicut dicitur Ezech. cap. 16. vers. 6. Transiens per te, vidi te conculcatum in sanguine tuo. Et dixi tibi: In sanguine tuo vive. Dixit Rabbi Eliefer: Quod autem vides Scripturam hic dicere, In sanguine tuo vive, quasi Sanctus Benedictus dixisset: Merito sanguinis fœderis circumcisionis, & sanguinis paschatis liberavi vos ex Aegypto; merito quoque illorum vos liberaturus sum sub finem regni quarti, hinc hic dicitur: In sanguine tuo. Et ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi in Opusculo de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum, Part. iv. cap. 8. Circumcisor craterem vino plenum in manus suas accipit, eoque benedictio aliam adhuc, quam imperti-tur recens circumciso, pronunciat benedictionem, eius nomen, quod quidem jussit parens, imponit, re-citans simul ista Ezechielis: Dixi tibi in sanguine tuo vive, &c. Quod Pater Abraham ad inferni ledeat portas, omniq; impediat modo, ne circumcisi per eam ingrediantur, præpu-tiatis liberum concedens transitum, ex Libro Rituali & Juridico Arba Turim, Part. II. quæ inscribitur Jore Scah, numer. 260.
units.tr: On that day, when the Israelites went out of Egypt, all were circumcised, from the greatest to the least, according to that passage in Joshua ch. 5, v. 4: For all the people who had come out were circumcised. They took the blood of circumcision and the blood of the Passover and placed it upon the lintel of their houses, so that when the Holy Blessed One passed through and saw the blood of the covenant and the blood of the Passover, mercy would be poured out upon the Israelites, as is said in Ezek. ch. 16, v. 6: Passing by you, I saw you trodden in your blood. And I said to you: In your blood, live. Rabbi Eliezer said: But that you see Scripture saying here, In your blood, live, is as if the Holy Blessed One had said: On account of the blood of the covenant of circumcision and the blood of the Passover I freed you from Egypt; on account of them also I will free you at the end of the fourth kingdom; hence it is said here: In your blood. And from Rabbi Leo of Modena, in the little work on the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part IV, ch. 8: The circumciser takes in his hands a cup full of wine, and over it pronounces the blessing, and then the newly circumcised child is given his name, which the father has ordered, while reciting at the same time those words of Ezekiel: I said to you, In your blood, live, etc. That Father Abraham stands at the gates of hell and in every way prevents the circumcised from entering through them, granting free passage to the uncircumcised: from the ritual and legal book Arba Turim, Part II, which is entitled Jore Dea, number 260.

units.la: Præceptum affirmativum est omni homini de Israe-le, ut circumcidat filium suum, & majus est reliquis præceptis affirmativis, in quibus est aliquis reatus exciexcisionis: quandoquidem super eo pacta sunt tredecim foedera in sectione de circumcisione Genes. 17. Neq; vocatus est Abrahamus perfectus, antequam circumcisus esset. Per meritum quoque hujus circumcisionis pactum cum illo est foedus super donatione terrae Canaan. Haec circumcisio praeterea est, quae liberat a judicio inferni; quemadmodum dixerunt Sapientes nostri, quod Abraham pater noster sedeat ante portam inferni, & non permittat ingredi in eum quenquam, qui circumcisus est. Turpe certe est praeputium, propter quod ignominia notata sunt gentes: Dictum enim est, quia omnes gentes sunt praeputiatae. Quisquis vero irritum reddit foedus Abrahami, patris nostri, ita aut non circumcidatur, aut, ut attrahat sibi praeputium, si maxime scripturam diligenter manibus suis tractet, habeatque bona opera, attamen non habebit partem in futuro seculo; Quod propter sanguinem foederis in circumcisione effusum & caeli conservantur & terra, ex Rabbi Maimonide in Hilchot Milah, cap. 3. §. 4. Qui circumcidit proselytos benedicit ita: Benedictus tu es, Dominus Deus noster, Rex mundi, qui sanctificavit nos per praecepta sua, & praecepit nobis circumcidere proselytos, & stillare facere sanguinem foederis ex illis: nam nisi foret sanguis foederis, non conservarentur caeli & terra, quia dictum est: si non foedus meum interdiu & noctu, statuta caelorum & terrae non posuisem.
units.tr: The affirmative precept lies on every man of Israel, that he circumcise his son, and it is greater than the other affirmative precepts, in which there is a liability to excision. For thirteen covenants were made concerning it in the section on circumcision, Gen. 17. Abraham was not called perfect until he had been circumcised. Also, by the merit of this circumcision, the covenant concerning the gift of the land of Canaan was made with him. Moreover, it is this circumcision that delivers from the judgment of hell, as our Sages said, that Abraham our father sits before the gate of hell and does not allow anyone who has been circumcised to enter. Certainly the foreskin is a shameful thing, on account of which the nations were marked with infamy; for it is said that all the nations are uncircumcised. But whoever renders void the covenant of Abraham our father, either by not being circumcised or by drawing his foreskin back over himself, even if he diligently handles the Scripture with his hands and has good works, he will nevertheless have no portion in the world to come. That heaven and earth are preserved on account of the blood of the covenant shed in circumcision is taken from Rabbi Maimonides, Hilchot Milah, ch. 3, §4: "He who circumcises proselytes blesses thus: Blessed are you, Lord our God, King of the world, who has sanctified us by his precepts, and has commanded us to circumcise proselytes and to cause the blood of the covenant to drip from them; for unless there were the blood of the covenant, heaven and earth would not be preserved, because it is said: 'If I had not appointed my covenant day and night, I would not have set the ordinances of heaven and earth.'"

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Negant audacter Circumcisionem fuisse typicam, seu Circumcisionem in manifesto, quae externis peragebatur ceremoniis, designasse Circumcisionem in occulto, qua nostra corda ab impuritate spirituali per Messiam circumcidenda, quaeque intus in corde hominis a Spiritu Dei perficiebatur; Inficiantur Circumcisionem externam denotasse naturae impuritatem, significasse originis labem, resectaque carnis particula totum hominem morte dignum esse pronunciasse; Inficiantur sanguinem circumcisionis praefigurasse sanguinem Messiae, effundendum in peccatorum remissionem; Negant praeputii resectionem & abjectionem obsignasse hominis sanctificationem & regenerationem per carnalium concupiscentiarum ablationem, Negant denique Circumcisionem denotasse ipsam glorificationem, seu praefigurasse perfectam depositionem peccatorum in morte & resurrectione per exutionem corporis peccati;
units.tr: They boldly deny that circumcision was typical, or that the circumcision in the open, which was performed with external ceremonies, prefigured the circumcision in secret, by which our hearts are to be circumcised from spiritual impurity through the Messiah, and which is accomplished inwardly in the heart of man by the Spirit of God. They deny that external circumcision denoted the impurity of nature, signified the stain of origin, and by the cutting away of a piece of flesh declared that the whole man deserved death. They deny that the blood of circumcision prefigured the blood of the Messiah, to be shed for the remission of sins. They deny that the cutting off and casting away of the foreskin sealed the sanctification and regeneration of man through the removal of carnal lusts. Finally, they deny that circumcision denoted glorification itself, or prefigured the perfect putting off of sins in death and resurrection through the stripping off of the body of sin.

units.la: Sed contra asserentes, in sanguine circumcisionis, & in resectione vilissimae pelliculae fuisse & pretium, & peccati expiationem, aut remedium esse externum contra corruptionem naturalem, facientes quin imo Circumcisionem merum opus legis, imo ipsam foedaris. ris essentiam, quæ data sit in fœdus perpetuum, non vero, quæ fœdus Dei obsignabat, & cuncta ejus beneficia, ut justificationem, sanctificationem & glorificationem, & ita fœderis gratiæ, fideique sigillum erat.
units.tr: But, on the contrary, those who assert that in the blood of circumcision and in the cutting away of that most base little skin there was both a price and an atonement for sin, or an external remedy against natural corruption, and who make circumcision a mere work of the law, indeed the very essence of the covenant, which was given as an everlasting covenant, and not that which sealed God's covenant and all its benefits, such as justification, sanctification and glorification, and so was the seal of the covenant of grace and of faith.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Afferunt præterea Circumcisionem in eum esse latam finem, ut populus Israelis ab aliis distingueretur gentibus, sicque hoc Sacramento Israelis innotesceret dignitas, non considerantes propterea Judæos à Gentilibus distinctos, ut cognosceretur ex quo populo, & ex qua Ecclesia Messias debuerit nasci & prodire; Ajunt quoque propterea Circumcisionem à divino fuisse institutam Numine, ut illi, qui hujus sunt fidei, habeant unum quoddam signum, quod illos conjungat, imo ut mutuo se amarent, & adjuvarent, ex Rabbi Maimonide in More Nevochim, Part. III. cap. 49. Insuper constat, quam intense mutuo fe-ament & adjuvent ejusmodi homines, qui commune aliquod signum habent, quod fœderis formam habet; Exinde imant præterea, propter hanc rationem instítutam fuisse Circumcisionem, ut carnales infirmaret cupiditates, & remedio naturali seu physico coeundi debilitaret appetitum, ex Maimonide in More Nevochim lib. & cap. cit. Porro, Circumcisio etiam, meo judicio, propter hanc rationem instituta est, ut libido hominum diminuatur, & membrum hoc, quantum fieri potest, ad actum istum debilitetur; Et paulo post pergit: Damnum enim illud, quod membro isti infertur, est illud ipsum, quod intenditur, quo nulla actio corrumpitur, in quo effentia viri consi-stit, neque etiam facultas generandi adimitur, sed superfluus tantum appetitus coeundi diminuitur. Quod autem Circumcisio virtutem intensivam membri illius voluptatem debilitet, id extra omnem dubitationem est. Nam cum membrum illud statim in ipsa natitate sanguinem suum effundit, tegumentumque amittit, sine omni dubio exinde debilitatur. Hinc dixerunt Sapientes nostri, mulierem cum viro incircumciso matrimonio junctam difficulter ab ipso posse abstrahi. Atque hac est principalis ratio, meo quidem judicio, in circumcisione; Referunt quoque ex Judæis aliqui, propterea Legem de Circumcisione datam, ut id, quod in pellicula superfluum abscinderetur, ex Col Bo, qui tamen dubitanter loquitur, in Expositione benedictionis super circumcisione, Sect.73. Statutum in carne ipsius posuit. Expositio; Hac est circumcisio, quae data est in carne ejus in statutum perpetuum. Aut significabit residuum hominis, & abundans quid in eo: nam præputium est superfluum quid in homine; Sed hanc Judæorum sententiam refutat futat Rabbi Maimonides, cum in More Ne-vochim, Lib. III. cap. 49. ficinquit: Quidam existimarunt, Circumcijionem istam esse perfectio-nem defectus nativitatis; prout quilibet contra-dicendi avidus facillime materiam invenire potest, dicendum autem illis, qua ratione res naturales ita imperfectæ esse possint, ut exterius perfici opus habeant? præter id, quod afferri potest de utilitate, quam pellicula illa membro isti adfert. Præceptum itaque istud non est datum ad supplendum defectum Creationis, sed ad corrigendum defectum morum. Cœterum de ritibus, qui hodie observantur in Sacramento Circumcisionis, pluribus consuli potest Rabbi Leo Mutinensis in Opusculo de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus Judæorum, Part. IV. cap. 8.
units.tr: Moreover, they claim that circumcision was instituted for this end, that the people of Israel might be distinguished from other nations, and that by this sacrament the dignity of Israel might become known; not considering that the Jews were on this account distinguished from the Gentiles, so that it might be known from what people and from what Church the Messiah was to be born and come forth. They also say that for this reason circumcision was instituted by the divine Majesty, so that those who are of this faith might have one sign which would join them together, and indeed so that they might love and help one another; from Rabbi Maimonides, More Nevochim, Part III, ch. 49: "Moreover, it is evident how intensely men who have a common sign, which has the form of a covenant, love and help one another." Thence they further think that circumcision was instituted for this reason, that it might weaken carnal desires and, by a natural or physical remedy against intercourse, enfeeble the appetite; from Maimonides, More Nevochim, the book and chapter cited: "Furthermore, circumcision, in my judgment, was instituted for this reason, that the lust of men may be diminished and this member, as far as possible, be weakened for that act." And a little later he goes on: "For the injury that is inflicted on that member is the very thing that is intended, by which no action is corrupted, in which the essence of the man consists, nor is the faculty of generating taken away, but only the superfluous appetite for intercourse is diminished. That circumcision weakens the intensive power and pleasure of that member is beyond all doubt. For since that member at once in earliest infancy sheds its blood and loses its covering, it is without any doubt thereby weakened." Hence our Sages said that a woman joined in marriage to an uncircumcised man can with difficulty be drawn away from him. "This is the principal reason, in my judgment, for circumcision." Some of the Jews also report that the law concerning circumcision was given so that what was superfluous in the skin might be cut away, from Col Bo, who however speaks doubtfully, in the Exposition of the blessing over circumcision, sect. 73: "He placed a statute in his flesh. Exposition: This is the circumcision which was given in his flesh as a perpetual statute." Or "it will signify the remnant of man and what is excessive in him, for the foreskin is something superfluous in man." But Rabbi Maimonides refutes this opinion of the Jews, when in More Nevochim, Book III, ch. 49, he says: "Some have thought that this circumcision is the perfecting of a defect of birth; as anyone eager to contradict can very easily find material, but to them it must be said: by what reason can natural things be so imperfect that they need an outward work of perfection? Besides what may be said about the usefulness which that skin brings to that member. This precept, therefore, was not given to supply a defect of creation, but to correct a defect of morals." As for the rites which are observed today in the sacrament of circumcision, more may be consulted in Rabbi Leo of Modena, in his little work on the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part IV, ch. 8.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Alterum Ecclesiæ suæ Sacramentum, vel potius ridiculam Sacramenti veteris imaginem, constituunt Agnum Paschalem, seu Epulum Paschale, in agni paschalis locum per Judæorum Magistros substitutum, quod Lege divina prohibitum sit comedere agnum paschalem extra terram sanctam; ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi in Opusc. de Cerem. & Consuet. Jud. Part. III. cap. 3. Loco ceremoniarum antiquitus observatarum, de quibus præcipit cap. 12. Exod. ubi jubentur Judæi comedere agnum & panes azyazymos cum herbis amaris &c. Hodie in catino aut corbula exigua partes quasdam agni & haedi capra dissectas asservant, additis azymis ac herbis amaris, ex.gr. apio Italico, intybo, aut lactuca, una cum vasculo, in quo conditura, quibus sibi in memoriam revocant laborem operosum fatis calcis ac laterum, quos Majores nostri in Aegypto coquere aut conficere cogebantur. Idem porro manibus suis pocu-lum vino repletum tenent, recitantes integram historiam plagarum, quas Patres ab Aegyptiis inflictas sibi ferre & sustinere adigebantur; miracula idem & prodigia in ipsorum gratiam a Deo, ut liberaren-tur a jugo ista perquam difficili, facta ac perpetrata non negligunt, sed juxta ordine recensent, totumque hunc actum concludunt, pro omni sibi exhibito favore, quadam gratiarum actione; Propterea incinunt Psalm. 113. cum sequentibus, qui veniunt nomine הללו. Coenam deinceps apponunt, qua absoluta, ad superiorem redeunt pietatem, recitando, quae adhuc residua sunt ex Psalmis ante laudatis, aliasve solennitati praesenti vel maxime convenientes gratiarum actiones.
units.tr: The second sacrament of their Church, or rather a ridiculous image of the old sacrament, they set up in the Paschal Lamb, or Paschal Feast, which the Jewish masters have substituted in place of the paschal lamb, since the divine Law forbade eating the paschal lamb outside the holy land; from Rabbi Leo of Modena in the Opusculum on the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews, Part III, chap. 3. In place of the ceremonies observed of old, which chap. 12 of Exodus prescribes, where the Jews are ordered to eat the lamb and unleavened bread with bitter herbs, etc. Today they keep in a dish or a small basket some pieces of the lamb and of the kid cut up, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs added (for example Italian celery, endive, or lettuce), together with a little vessel in which there is a paste (charoseth), by which they call back to mind the laborious toil of making lime and bricks, which our forefathers in Egypt were forced to bake or make. Next, they hold in their hands a cup filled with wine, reciting the whole history of the plagues which the Fathers were compelled to bear and endure, inflicted by the Egyptians; they also do not neglect the miracles and prodigies done and wrought by God for their sake, that they might be freed from that very hard yoke, but recount them in their order, and they conclude this whole act with a certain thanksgiving for all the favour shown to them. For this reason they sing Psalm 113 with the following psalms, which begin with the word הללו [Hallelu]. Then they set out the supper, and when it is finished they return to their earlier devotion, reciting what remains of the psalms mentioned above, or other thanksgivings especially suited to the present solemnity.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Credunt hoc Ecclesiae suae Sacramentum fore aeternum, ex Exod. cap. 12. vers. 14. monente Rabbi Maimonide in More Nevochim, Part. III. cap. 46. cum de ritibus & consuetudinibus loquitur Paschalibus: Ut autem in sempiternum ista observentur, ideo praecepit, ut sempiterna quoque illius rei esset memoria, sicut dicitur Exod. cap.12. verf. 24. Observabis itaque rem istam pro statuto tibi & filiis tuis in saeculum; Negantes audacter Agnum Paschalem denotasse Messiam, Agnum illum Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi, praefigurasseque Agnum incul-patum, ab initio mundi in sacrificiis occisum, & in extremitate dierum in proprio corpore mactatum; sed tantum significasse vel naturalia, moraliaque, ipsamque attulisse vitam aeternam.
units.tr: They believe that this sacrament of their Church will be eternal, from Exodus chap. 12 verse 14, as Rabbi Maimonides warns in the More Nevochim, Part III, chap. 46, when he speaks of the Paschal rites and customs: "That these things may be observed for ever, God therefore commanded that there should be an everlasting memory of the thing, as is said in Exodus chap. 12 verse 24: 'You shall observe this thing as a statute for you and your sons for ever.'" They boldly deny that the Paschal Lamb signified the Messiah, that Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world, or that it foreshadowed the spotless Lamb, slain in sacrifices from the beginning of the world and sacrificed in his own body at the end of the days; but that it signified only natural and moral things, and brought eternal life itself.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Arcent ab hoc Sacramenti ludo omnem a Sacris alienum Judaicis, nullos admittentes nisi per Circumcisionem initiatos, putantes, quod sicut in Circumcisionis vivant sangui-ne, ita pariter per sanguinem paschalem secu-li futuri fiant haeredes, uti non tantum patet ex Rabbi Elieseris Pirke,cap.29.citat.§.4. hujus cap. Sed ex Rabbi Maimonide in More Nevochim, Part.III.cap.46. Praeputium habentibus sive Incircumcisis cur prohibitus fuerit ejus esus, ejus rei causam reddiderunt Sapientes no-stri, dicentes: Ipsi intermiserunt praeceptum Circum-cisionis, cum prolongaretur commoratio ipsorum in Aegypto, ut similes fierent Aegyptiis. Ideo cum injunctum fuit nobis praeceptum Paschatis, hanc ei conditionem annexit Deus, ut nemo illud maflaret, nisi post quam se ipsum, suos filios & domesticos circumcidisset, atque ita tum demum accederet ad agnum Paschalem comedendum. Circumciderunt se omnes, & tantus circumcisorum fuit numerus, ut sanguis circumcisionis miscetur cum sanguine Paschatis: quemadmodum hujus rei vestigium habemus apud Prophetam Ezech. cap. 16. verf. 6. dicentem: Et vidi te conculcatum in sanguinibus tuis, hoc est, in sanguine Circumcisionis & sanguine Paschatis; Et ex Nizzachon Veteri autoris incerti, editi per Wagenseilium in Telis Igneis Satanae, pag. 34-35. ad Exod. cap. 12. verf. 22. Dicendum, illud significasse Deum: Ob triplicem sanguinem illas vos praestabo, cum sanguinem in portis vestris intuebor; ob sanguinem nimirum circumcisionis Abrahami, ob sanguinem quem ligando filium, in ejus mactatione effundere volebat, & ob sanguinem paschalis agni. Huc omnino pertinet illud Ezech. cap. 16. verf. 6. Cum viderem teprabentem conculcandam te in sanguine tuo; Ecce sanguinem unum. Dixi tibi in sanguine tuo vive. Ecce alterum. Iterumque dixi tibi in sanguine tuo vive. Ecce tibi tertium; Sed plura de hoc Pafchatis Sacramento, qui ex Judaeis Magistris scire desiderat, conferre potest Tractatum Talmudicum Pesachim seu de Paschate; Rabbi Maimonidem in Hilchot Chamez umazumazzah;Orach Chajim anum.469.Precum libellos; aliosque.
units.tr: They exclude from this sacramental play every person alien to Jewish rites, admitting none except those initiated by circumcision, thinking that just as they live by the blood of circumcision, so likewise by the paschal blood they become heirs of the age to come; as is clear not only from Rabbi Eliezer's Pirke, chap. 29, cited in § 4 of this chapter, but from Rabbi Maimonides in the More Nevochim, Part III, chap. 46: "The reason why eating it was forbidden to those having foreskins, or the uncircumcised, our Sages give, saying: They had neglected the precept of circumcision, since their sojourn in Egypt was prolonged, so that they might become like the Egyptians. Therefore, when the precept of the Passover was enjoined on us, God attached this condition to it, that no one should slaughter it unless he had first circumcised himself, his sons and his household, and so only then should he approach to eat the paschal lamb. All of them circumcised themselves, and the number of the circumcised was so great that the blood of circumcision was mixed with the blood of the Passover"; as we have a trace of this thing in the prophet Ezekiel chap. 16 verse 6, saying: "And I saw you trampled in your blood," that is, in the blood of circumcision and the blood of the Passover; and from the old Nizzachon, of uncertain author, published by Wagenseil in the Telum Ignitum Satanae, pp. 34-35, on Exodus chap. 12 verse 22: It must be said that God signified this: "Because of a threefold blood I will spare you, when I shall look upon the blood at your doors: namely, for the blood of Abraham's circumcision, for the blood which he was willing to shed in the slaying of his son when he bound him, and for the blood of the paschal lamb." To this very thing pertains that passage of Ezekiel chap. 16 verse 6: "When I saw you lying trampled in your blood, behold one blood. I said to you, Live in your blood. Behold another. And again I said to you, Live in your blood. Behold a third for you." But whoever desires to learn more about this Paschal sacrament from the Jewish masters may consult the Talmudic tractate Pesachim, or On the Passover; Rabbi Maimonides in Hilchot Chametz u-Matzah; Orach Chayim, no. 469; the prayer books; and others.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Rident, subsannantque Ecclesiae nostrae Christianae Sacramenta divina, maxime tamen Pontificiae, vocantes per summam blasphemiam aquas Baptismi מים טמאים Aquas foetidas, putridasq;, מים זורמים Aquas Superbas, ex Rabbi Bechai in Kad Hakkemach, pag. 61. Vocat David Regnum Edomiticum מים הזדונים aquas superbas, quia fidei articulus apud eos est, ut aqua baptizentur; Ex Rabbi Mosefe Israel Demercato in Commentario ad Psalmos, pag. 104. Et contra prolixum hoc exilium ait: Tunc transfiiffent super animam nostram aquae superbae &c. quia regnum hoc, Christianorum puta, vocatur מלכות זדון Regnum superbum; Et ex Rabbi Isac Abarbanel in Praefatione libri Sebach Pesach; Et ex Nizzachon Veteri, p. 150; Vocantes Aquas Baptismi מים טמאים aquas immundas, quae immundorum spirituum sint sedes & receptacula, non diffitente Rabbi Salomone Zevi, sed vocibus benigniorem sententiam tribuente, cum fucum nobis facit in Theriaca Judaica, cap. 2. §. 25. Cum igitur Pontificij, sine ullo discrimine, homines aquaaspergant, ut olim sepulchra, aliaque quaevis, ipsosque infantes aqua baptizent, quos, peccato originali contaminat. minatos, purgandos esse, inquiunt, non injuria דמא ןד vocantur, id est: Aqua immundorum, quibus ij ipsi abluisolent: Ipsa tamen aqua immunda non est, cum & eodem jure aqua nostra in Tabernaculo, & Sanctuario, immunda fuisset; Appellantes Baptismum nostrum nefandum, in Nizzachon Veteri, pag. 70. ad Jerem. cap. 31. v. 31: Hoc loco abutuntur infideles, ajuntq; de Jesu vaticinari Prophetam, quod is cum natus fuerit, daturus sit ipsis Legem novam, & nefandum baptismum pro Circumcisionis foedere, & celebrationem diei primi hebdomadis sive diei Solis pro Sabbathi cultu sit introducturus; Appellantes Aquas Baptismi aquas impuras ex citato Nizzachon Veteri p. 74. ad Ezech. cap. 16. verf. 9.
