Now the image and likeness of God is the divine law, delivered to the people through Moses; for that law, as the Cabalists observe, is full of divine names. Just as the law consists of 248 affirmative precepts and 365 negative ones, so also the whole structure of the human body consists of 248 members and 365 sinews. This seems to indicate nothing other than that the whole perfection and consummation of man lies in the careful observance of the precepts.

units.la: Et mox pauca interjecta pergit Rabbi Menafleh: Cum igitur fieri non posset, quin homo partim ob materiam, ex qua constatus est, in observanda lege aliquando ceciderit, ac labatur, vel aliquid mali cogitet, juxta illud Jobi, Memento quaeso quod sicut lutum mefecisti, & alibi, Homo natus de muliere, & illud Davidis, & memininit quod caro illis partim ob vitam breviorem, ut sufficiat, ad tot ac tam varia praecepta legis praestanda: idcirco Deus pro sua erga eum misericordia, statuit ei dare, ac concedere alia quaedam, eaque aptiora media, quibus adjutus perfectionem iltam consequatur. Id est, constituit hominibus corpora largiri, non coalita ex con-
units.tr: And after a few intervening words Rabbi Menasseh goes on: Since, therefore, it cannot be but that man, partly because of the matter of which he is made, sometimes falls and slips in observing the law, or thinks something evil, according to that saying of Job, "Remember, I beg you, that you made me as clay," and elsewhere, "Man born of woman," and that of David, "He remembered that they were flesh," and partly because his life is too short to suffice for performing so many and so varied precepts of the law, therefore God, in his mercy towards him, resolved to give and grant him certain other and more suitable means, by which, aided, he might attain that perfection. That is, he resolved to bestow on men bodies not compounded

units.la: Ex R. Menafleh. Ben Israel, sed ea que ad Recitationis tomo conjunctione maris, & fœmina, quæ natura sua ad vitia, & turpitudinem sunt proclivia: sed ex terra facta, quale fuit <bl>Adami</bl> corpus; ut ita tanquam Dei creatura à Deo immediate creata aptiores & magis dispositæ essent ad bene agendum, ac gratia Dei, qua tum largissime perfunduntur, ad totam legem ejus perfecte observandam;
units.tr: From Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel: not compounded from the union of male and female, which by nature are prone to vices and baseness, but formed out of earth, as was the body of Adam; so that, as creatures created immediately by God, they might be more fit and better disposed to act well, and to observe his whole law perfectly, being then richly bathed in the grace of God.

units.la: XXI.
units.tr: XXI.

units.la: Supererat, ut de Resurrectionis loco notaremus, quomodo communis Rabbinorum fere sit sententia, mortuorum Resurrectionem in terra Canaan futuram, idque non tantum ipsis constare ex diversis Scripturæ locis, Exod. cap. 6. vers. 4. Numer. cap. 18. vers. 28. Deuter. cap. 11. vers. 9. Et cap. 31. vers. 16. Esai. cap. 26. vers. 19. Ezech. cap. 36. vers. 20. Et cap. 37. vers. 9. Verum illud quoque patescere ex terræ Israelis dignitate, quod primus homo conditus sit & vivificatus in terra sancta, quod Isacus typus resurrectionis in ea ligatus, quod filius Sareptanæ & Sunamitidis, item vir, qui tetigit ossa Elisæ, in ea sint resuscitati, quod patres maximo desiderio flagraverint in ipsa terra sepeliri, quod terra sit sancta; Supererat pariter, ut ex communi sententia Rabbinorum describeremus, qua ratione corpora, extra terram sanctam sepulta, volvenda sint per cavernas subterraneas in terram Israelis, ut in ea resuscitentur simul; Imo à Icopo nostro non fuisset alienum, si de tempore resurrectionis, ex mente Hebraeorum, mentio quoque facta fuisset; Sed quae ob nimiam omissa sunt festinantiam, curis, si Deo placuerit, reservabuntur secundis.
units.tr: It remains for us to note the place of the resurrection, and how the common opinion of the rabbis is almost this: that the resurrection of the dead will take place in the land of Canaan. This they hold not only from various passages of Scripture (Exod. 6:4; Num. 18:28; Deut. 11:9; Deut. 31:16; Isa. 26:19; Ezek. 36:20; Ezek. 37:9), but also from the dignity of the land of Israel: that the first man was created and quickened in the holy land; that Isaac, a type of the resurrection, was bound there; that the son of the Sarepta widow and of the Shunammite woman, and likewise the man who touched the bones of Elisha, were raised there; that the fathers burned with the greatest desire to be buried in that very land; and that the land is holy. It likewise remained for us to describe, according to the common opinion of the rabbis, by what means bodies buried outside the holy land are to be rolled through subterranean caverns into the land of Israel, so that they may be raised together there. Indeed, it would not have been out of place for our author to have also mentioned the time of the resurrection, according to the mind of the Hebrews. But what has been omitted through excessive haste will, God willing, be reserved for a later occasion.

units.la: CAPUT XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: De extremo judicio, vita & morte aeterna.
units.tr: On the Last Judgment, eternal life and death.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: POst Resurrectionem considerant Extremum Judicium, quod Deus in humanum fit instituturum genus, distinguentes illud, tum ratione temporis, tum ratione magnitudinis & subjectorum, a duobus antecedaneis Judiciis, quorum prius corpus tantum respiciat, peragaturque quam maxime quotannis ipsis calendis Tishri seu Septembris, & quidem in hac terra; Posterius vero animam solum concernat, quando per mortem a corpore suo manet separata, cum per illud vel absoluta fertur in Paradisum, vel damnata ad infernum. num relegatur, ut in eo debitas luorum peccatorum luat poenas; Probantes triplex illud famosum Judicium divinum, non tantum ex Jobi cap. 33. veri. 29,30: Ecce omnia haec operatur Deus fortis bisque terque cum homine; Reducendo animam ejus à fovea; ut illustretur lumine hujus vitae; Sed ex ipsis antiquorum Hebraeorum dictis, & communi omnium Judaeorum consensu, uti liquet ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, libr. II. de Resurr. mort. cap. 20: Sed ut hoc melius intelligatur, cogitandum est, quod homo non semel, aut bis, ter judicandus sit; juxta illud Jobi cap. 33. (eo enim respexisse videtur.) Ecce omne illud operatur Deus tribus vicibus cum homine. Primum Judicium proprie ad solum corpus pertinet, & exercetur repetiturque quotannis ipsis Calendis Tishri, qui respondet menti Septembri. Tum enim condita est universi mundi machina (uti in Conciliatore & Problematibus nostris de Creatione comprobavimus.) Quare par est, ut tum quoque quotannis de homine judicium fiat. Praeterea cum planeta per id tempus influentius & zyzigiis suis, varios morbos & calamitates generant in mundo elementari: puta in genere, famem, pestem, corporis languorem & debilitatem, mortem, bella, & clades, &c. In specie vero, quae vel huic aut illi homini noxia sunt. Propterea ab Hebraeis dies Judicii appellatur. Quia vero ii, quibus Lex divina cordi est, ab ista syderum efficacia liberi sunt: hinc placuit Deo, ut ille dies festus a popu-lo suo haberetur: & dicitur Num.cap.XXIX.dies Jubilæus, quia tunc tubis & buccinis clangebat pop-ulus: qui significabat bellum sibi esse cum affectibus, ad subjiciendum illos imperio rationis, velad excitandum sese, atq; expergefaciendum oblivionis somnio. Atq; idcirco isti rei vitæ exequendæ constitutum erat spatium decem dierum: decimo vero die festum erat Expiationis peccatorum, quo pecca-ta sua Deo confitebantur omnes illi, qui ea agnosce-bant, & eorum feria poenitentia ducebantur: alioqui subditi manebant imperio ac dominio planetarum, eaq; illus infortunia exspectanda erant, quæ syderum affectus denuntiabant. Hujus primi diei, quod ad corpus attinet, meminere antiqui, cum ajunt. Quatuor temporibus de mundo judicium fertur. Primum in Festo Paschatis super terra proventibus. Deinde in festo Pentecostes, super fructibus arborum. Tertio in Rosa Sana jeu principio anni, super omnibus rebus humanis. Quarto in festo Tabernaculorum, super aquis. Addunt vero etiam futurum, ut tres libri aperiantur in Rosa-Sana, seu principio anni: primus perfectorum, qui sanctissime vixerunt; alter flagitiosorum, qui pessime vixerunt; tertius eorum, qui medium tenuerunt, & nec pessimam, neq; optimam vitam duxerunt. Optima vitæ homines, inquiunt, confestim scribuntur in li-bro bro vitæ; pessimæ vitæ homines in libro mortis; qui mediam vitam egere, illorum judicium suspendi-tur, usque ad diem expiationis; Dealtero judicio, quod post hanc vitam, solam concernit animam, sic, post quædam subjecta, loquitur R. Menalseh Ben Israel: Alterum Judicium anima est, quod eam post separationem a corpore manet, quod vel absoluta fertur in paradisum, vel damnata in tartarum detruditur, ut ibi peccatorum suorum pœnas luat. Hujus judicii variis in locis meminere veteres. De R. Johanan Ben Zacay refertur, quod imminente fatali hora fleverit: rogatus causam a discipulis, responderit, duas se videre ante oculos suos vias; vidi unam, quæ recta ad infernum; alteram, quæ in paradisum euntes ducat; & nescire se, qua ducendus sit. Quam plurima etiam commemorant de utraque hac via Cabalistæ per totum Zoar: ubi etiam multis agitur de præmio, & pœna animarum a corpore sejunctarum.
units.tr: After the Resurrection they consider the Last Judgment, which God will hold over the whole human race. They distinguish it, both in time and in scale and in its subjects, from two earlier judgments. The first concerns the body alone and is carried out every year, especially on the calends of Tishri, that is, of September, and in this land. The second concerns only the soul, when after death it is separated from its body, and is either carried off absolved into Paradise or condemned and consigned to hell, so that there it may pay the due penalties for its sins. They prove this threefold famous divine judgment not only from Job 33.29–30, "Behold, God works all these things twice or thrice with man, bringing back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life," but also from the sayings of the ancient Hebrews and the common agreement of all Jews, as is clear from Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, book 2 of On the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 20: But so that this may be better understood, it must be considered that a man is not judged once, or twice, but three times, according to that passage of Job 33 (for he seems to have had it in view): Behold, God works all that with man three times. The first judgment pertains properly to the body alone; it is carried out and repeated every year on the calends of Tishri, which corresponds to our month of September. For then the machinery of the whole world was set up (as we have shown in our Conciliator and in our Problems on the Creation). Therefore it is fitting that a judgment on man also be made then every year. Moreover, since at that time the planets, by their influence and their conjunctions, generate various diseases and calamities in the elementary world, namely in general famine, plague, weakness and weariness of the body, death, wars and slaughters, and so on, and in particular those things which are harmful to this or that man, for this reason the day is called by the Hebrews the Day of Judgment. But because those whose hearts are set on the divine Law are free from this influence of the stars, it pleased God that this day should be kept as a festival by his people. In Numbers 29 it is called the Jubilee day, because then the people sounded with trumpets and horns, signifying that they were at war with the passions, to subject them to the rule of reason, or to rouse and awaken themselves from the dream of forgetfulness. And for this reason a space of ten days was set apart for carrying out this business of life; on the tenth day was the feast of the expiation of sins, on which all those who acknowledged their sins confessed them to God, and that day was counted as a day of repentance for them. Otherwise they remained subject to the rule and dominion of the planets, and those misfortunes were to be expected which the influences of the stars foretold. The ancients also mention this first day, as far as the body is concerned, when they say: judgment on the world is passed at four seasons. First, at the Passover, over the produce of the earth; second, at Pentecost, over the fruit of the trees; third, at Rosa-Sana, that is, the beginning of the year, over all human affairs; fourth, at the feast of Tabernacles, over the waters. They add moreover that three books will be opened at Rosa-Sana, that is, at the beginning of the year: the first of the perfect, who lived most holily; the second of the wicked, who lived most wickedly; the third of those who held the middle course and lived neither the worst nor the best life. The people of the best life, they say, are at once written in the book of life; the people of the worst life in the book of death; those who lived a middling life have their judgment suspended until the day of atonement. Concerning the second judgment, which after this life concerns the soul alone, Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel speaks thus, after certain preliminaries: The second judgment is of the soul, which awaits it after its separation from the body; the soul is either carried off absolved into paradise, or condemned and thrust down into Tartarus, there to pay the penalties of its sins. The ancients mention this judgment in various places. It is related of Rabbi Johanan ben Zakkai that when his fatal hour was near he wept; asked by his disciples the reason, he replied that he saw two ways before his eyes: one he saw leads straight to hell, the other leads those going into paradise; and he did not know by which he was to be led. The Cabalists also record very many things about each of these ways throughout the whole Zohar, where much is also said about the reward and punishment of souls separated from their bodies.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Tertium Judicium est Extremum sive ultimum Judicium, exercendum a divino Numine, in ultimis mundi temporibus, cum mortui resurgent, estque illud magnum & universale Judicium, quod non tantum animam, corpusque concernet, piorum, sed ad universum spectabit orbem terrarum, uti demonstrat Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel, in Nachalath lath Abhoth, rad. 13. Ecce hac ratione nec Judicium magnum nec universale futurum erit, nec secundum praescriptum juris omnibus communis. Praeterea si foli justi resurgent, quomodo tres ordines die judicij erunt, scilicet perfecte justorum, perfecte malorum, & mediorum, juxta autores Baraitha? Patetque quam dilucide ex Rabbi Menalfeh Ben Israel, libr. 11. de Resurrectione mortuorum, cap. 20: Deniq; tertium judicium erit anima & corporis, cum mortui resurgent, atq; illud magnum, & extremum judicium dicitur, quo universus orbis terrarum judicabitur; De hoc ultimo judicio, ejusq; executione ita porro pronunciat Rabbi Menalfeh Ben Israel, citato cap. 20, pag. 233, 234: Hic aequa lance ac trutina cunctorum facta expendentur, & examinabuntur. Et multi isti boni probiq;, quiin hac vita saepe magnis miseriis & infirmitatibus corporis obnoxii vixerunt; tum demum omnibus bonis ipsis, quibus hic caruerant cumulabuntur. Mali vero & improbi homines, qui in star herba hic floruerunt, omnibusq; vita bonis, & deliciis abundarunt, expergiscentur, & ad illud judicium resurgent, quod denuntiat illis Esaias, Et sallent & venient in corporibus virorum, qui in me rebelles fuerunt, quia vermis eorum non morietur, neq; ignis eorum extinguetur. Rationi etiam consentaneum hoc est, & ab omnibus est creditur: hinc Canonista dicunt, quicunque foci criminis, vel alicujus culpæ, meriti, aut demeriti, participes fuerunt, æquum & par est, ut ejusdem quoq; præmii vel pœnæ participes fiant; Confirmat hæc Rabbi Leo Mutinensis, quando de universali judicio sic loquitur in Opusculo de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus hodiernorum Judæorum, Part. v. cap. ii. Similiter certo persuasi sunt Judæi, Deum univer-sale in omnes homines, qua corpus & animam, judicium exercitum esse, juxta illud Danielis Prophetæ cap. 12. vs. 2. Multi ex dormientibus in pulverulenta terra expergiscentur; hi ad vitam æternam; illi ad opprobria & contemptum æternum.
units.tr: The third judgment is the Last or ultimate Judgment, to be carried out by the divine Power in the final times of the world, when the dead will rise. It is the great and universal Judgment, which concerns not only the soul and body of the pious but extends to the whole circle of the earth, as Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel shows in Nachalath lath Abhoth, rad. 13. Thus in this way the Judgment will be neither great nor universal, nor according to the prescribed law common to all. Moreover, if only the just rise, how will there be three orders on the day of judgment, namely of the wholly just, the wholly wicked, and the intermediate, according to the authors of the Baraitha? And how clearly this is set out by Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, in book 11 on the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 20: Finally, the third judgment will be of soul and body, when the dead rise, and it is called the great and final judgment, by which the whole circle of the earth will be judged. Concerning this last judgment and its execution, Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, in the chapter cited, pages 233 and 234, further pronounces thus: Here all will be weighed and examined with an equal balance and scale. And those many good and upright people, who in this life were often subject to great miseries and bodily infirmities, will then be heaped with all the good things of which they were deprived here. But evil and wicked men, who flourished here like grass and abounded in all the good things and delights of life, will wake and rise for that judgment which Isaiah announces to them: And they shall go forth and look upon the carcasses of the men who rebelled against me; for their worm shall not die, nor shall their fire be quenched. This also agrees with reason and is believed by all. Hence the canonists say that whoever shared in a crime, or in some fault, merit or demerit, it is fair and right that they also share in the same reward or punishment. Rabbi Leo Mutinensis confirms this when, speaking of the universal judgment in his little work on the Ceremonies and Customs of today's Jews, Part v, chapter ii, he says: Likewise the Jews are firmly persuaded that God exercises universal judgment over all men, both body and soul, according to that of the prophet Daniel, chap. 12, vers. 2: Many of those sleeping in the dusty earth will awake; these to eternal life, those to eternal reproach and everlasting contempt.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Tradunt universos judicandos בין הגוים in Judicio illo magno, in tribus distinctos classibus coram divino comparituros Numine: Prima erit perfectæ piorum צדיקים גמורים illico ad vitam obsignandorum æternam; Secunda Improborum perfectorum רשעים גמורים, obsignandorum pariter illico in Gehenna; Tertia erit Intermediorum, quorum iniquitates & justitiæ pares sunt, quique descensuri in Gehennam, ibique ejulaturi, tandemque rursum inde ascensuri, quod non tantum probare conantur ex Zachar. cap. 13. v. 9. 1. Sam. cap. 2. verf. 6. Sed ex traditione domus Schammai, in Tractatu Talmudico Rosch HaHafchana, firmant, uti liquet ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, libr. II. de Resurrectione Mortuorum, cap.20. pag.232: Academia Sammay inquit, quod tres hominum classes atq; ordines judicanda sistentur; unus impiorum ac pessimorum, alter optimorum, tertius mediorum. Illi qui perfectissime justi sunt, sine mora fruentur vita futuri seculi. Isti qui plane mali atq; improbi fuerunt, confestim in infernum detrudentur; juxta illud: Multi ex dormientibus in terra pulvere expergiscentur; hi ad vitam æternam, illi ad pudorem & opprobrium æternum. Intermedii descendent, & precabuntur, & hinc ascendent, juxta illud Zachar. cap.13. vers.9. Et inducam tertiam partem per ignem. Et de his loquitur Hana, 1.Sam. c.2. vers.6. Dominus occidit, & vitæ restituit, facit descendere ad sepulchrum, & facit ascendere. Cæterum Academia Hillelis ait, Deus est gratiosus, & propensus ad misericordiam; uti loquitur David, cum ait Psalm. 116. vers.1. Dilexi, quoniam exaudiet Deus vocem deprecationum, &c. usq; ad, attenuatus sum, & me servavit.
units.tr: They teach that all who are to be judged, among the nations [בין הגוים], will appear before the divine Power at that great Judgment, distinguished into three classes. The first will be of the wholly pious [צדיקים גמורים], who are at once to be sealed for eternal life. The second will be of the wholly wicked [רשעים גמורים], who are likewise at once to be sealed in Gehenna. The third will be of the intermediate, whose iniquities and righteousness are equal, who will go down into Gehenna and lament there, and at last will come up again from there. They try to prove this not only from Zechariah chap. 13, vers. 9, and 1 Samuel chap. 2, vers. 6, but also from the tradition of the house of Shammai, in the Talmudic Tractate Rosch HaHafchana, where they affirm, as is clear from Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, book II on the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 20, page 232: The Academy of Shammai says that men will be presented for judgment in three classes and orders: one of the impious and most wicked, another of the best, and a third of the intermediate. Those who are most perfectly just will at once enjoy the life of the age to come. Those who were plainly evil and wicked will immediately be thrust down into hell, according to that: Many of those sleeping in the dusty earth will awake; these to eternal life, those to eternal shame and reproach. The intermediates will go down, and will pray, and from there will go up again, according to Zechariah chap. 13, vers. 9: And I will bring the third part through the fire. And Hannah speaks of these in 1 Samuel chap. 2, vers. 6: The Lord kills and makes alive, he brings down to the grave and brings up. But the Academy of Hillel says: God is gracious and inclined to mercy, as David says when he says in Psalm 116, vers. 1: I love, because God will hear the voice of my supplications, etc., down to: I was brought low, and he saved me.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Credunt vitæ, mortisque æternæ doctrinam, fidei articulum esse fundamentalem hinc jure merito non tantum tredecim fundamentalibus fidei Judaicæ articulis fuit insertus, uti ex autore liquet Rabbi Moseh Maimonide. nide,in Commentario ad Tractatum Talmu-dicum Sanhedrin,cap.11. Fundamentum undecimum est, quod Deus retributurus sit bonam mer-cedem observantipræcepta ejus, & puniturus sit ea-dem violantem, & qui non præstiterit ea; atq; retri-butionem maximam esse futurum seculum, & pœ-nam gravissimam exterminium. Et jam declara-vimus in hoc capite, quantum isti sufficit. Docet autem Scriptura de hoc fundamento, Exod.cap.32, vers.32,33. Et jam si reputaveris peccata eorum: Et si non, dele me quaso e libro tuo, quem scripsisti. At respondit ei Deus: Eum, qui provocaverit mihi, ego delebo ex libro meo. Atque hæc est proba-tio de præmio justi & pœna impii; Verum in quo-tidianis commemoratur precibus hac se-quenti formula compositis: Ego credo fideli perfecta, quod Creator, cujus nomen sit benedi-ctum, retribuat bonum illis, qui custodiunt præcep-ta ejus; & puniat istos, qui transgrediuntur eadem. Apparetq; quin etiam in suo npʰ Catechismo Judaico, ut Juventus Judaica immobile hoc discat fundamentum, obviamque possit ire Sadducæis, qui constantem insiciantur veritatem, uti patet ex Responsione discipuli ad Magistri sui Quæstionem so: Fundamentum undecimum, quod Deus nemini præmium sit denegaturus, sed retributurus mercedem iis qui præceptaservant, & delinquentes multaturus pœna, vel in hoc seculo, vel in futuro, vel in utroque, prout praece-pti delictorum gravitas exegerit. Summa vero retributio erit post mortem in futuro seculo, summa punitio.
units.tr: They believe that the doctrine of eternal life and eternal death is a fundamental article of faith. Hence, rightly, it was inserted not only among the thirteen fundamental articles of the Jewish faith, as is clear from the author Rabbi Moses Maimonides in his Commentary on the Talmudic Tractate Sanhedrin, chapter 11: The eleventh foundation is that God will reward with a good recompense those who observe his precepts, and will punish those who violate them and who have not kept them; and that the greatest recompense will be in the future age, and the most grievous punishment, destruction. And we have already declared in this chapter how much this suffices. Scripture teaches about this foundation in Exodus chap. 32, vers. 32, 33: And now, if you will forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray, out of your book, which you have written. But God answered him: Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot out of my book. This is the proof of the reward of the just and the punishment of the wicked. Indeed, it is also recalled in the daily prayers, composed in this formula: I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, blessed be his name, will repay good to those who keep his precepts, and will punish those who transgress them. It appears also in their Jewish Catechism, that Jewish youth may learn this unshakeable foundation and be able to confront the Sadducees, who deny this firm truth, as is clear from the disciple's answer to his master's question: The eleventh foundation: that God will deny reward to no one, but will repay the wage to those who keep the precepts, and will fine the offenders with punishment, either in this age, or in the future, or in both, as the gravity of the precept's violation demands. The greatest reward will be after death in the future age, the greatest punishment.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Credunt æternam transigendam vitam In seculo venturo, In horto Eden seu Paradiso, ex testimonio novissimo Rabbi Menasfis Ben Israel, libr. III. de Resurr. Mortuorum, cap. II. pag. 343: Quare cum antiquis concludimus eos, qui resurgent, non morituros esse: sed post multos annos, quibus vixerint, cum corpore & anima in terrestrem paradisum vel in cælum translatum iri, instar Hanochi & Eliæ, ut ibi sine ulla actione, aut passione humana felicissime vivant; Et Problemate 17. de Creatione, pag. 71, 72: Veteres Sapientes quoque simpliciter secundum literam acceperunt paradisum, dixerunt quoque esse locum, in quo animæ piorum hominum, defuncto corpore, fruuntur præmiis suorum bonorum operum: quemadmodum etiam traditum est variis in locis Zoar. Similiter refertur in Pirque Abot discipulis Abrahami Patriarchæ, obtigisse paradisum; discipulus autem Biliam, infernum. Et alio in loco dicitur, servantibus legem paradisus paratus est, infernus vero legis prævaricatoribus. Et c. Secundo tractatus Temura legitur quoque Mosem M. cum per paradisum proficisceretur, dixisse Jehova.
units.tr: They believe that eternal life is to be spent in the coming age, in the garden of Eden or Paradise, on the latest testimony of Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, book 3 of On the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 2, p. 343: Therefore, with the ancients, we conclude that those who rise will not die, but after many years of life they will be translated, body and soul, into an earthly paradise or into heaven, like Enoch and Elijah, there to live most happily without any human action or suffering. And in Problem 17 on the Creation, pp. 71-72: The ancient sages also took paradise simply according to the letter; they also said it is a place in which the souls of pious men, once the body has died, enjoy the rewards of their good works, as is also taught in various places in the Zohar. Similarly, it is reported in Pirqe Avot that paradise fell to the disciples of Abraham the Patriarch, but the disciple Balaam fell to hell. And in another place it is said that paradise is prepared for those who keep the law, but hell for the transgressors of the law. And in the second chapter of the tractate Temurah it is also read that Moses our teacher, when he set out through paradise, said to Jehovah.

units.la: Hmm sua, propone nunc omnia dubia quacunque habes. Et in Midras Theylim, quotiescunque in sacris literis reperitur terra vita, uti in Psalm. 116.9. ambulabit coram Domino, in terra vita, & similia loca, semper antiqui sapientes exponunt ea de paradiso quia ille est, terra ista in qua aeternum vivitur. Ita etiam eleganter Abigail locum illum vocat צרור החיים fasciculum vitae, cum David loquens 1. Sam. 25.29. Erit anima Domini mei ligata in fasciculo vitae apud Dominum Deum tuum: porro inimicorum tuorum anima rotabitur, quasi in impetu & circulo funda. Quo versu admirabilia, quaedam continentur. Primo, animas esse immortales, & incorruptibiles, quia in illis non est causa efficiens corruptionis. Quod indicatur eo, quum dicitur, anima Domini mei erit ligata in fasciculo vitae: nam sic paradisus vocatur, quoniam illic continuum & indissolubile vitae gaudium est; Et eodem Problemate, pag. 75: Sed ut ad propositum revertamur, certissimum est vere & non figurate locum extare, qui dicitur paradisus, in quo antiqui nostri M. M. referunt septem habitationes esse, sive gradus felicitatis, quos divini Theologi in Zoar הכלות Palatia, appellarunt. In iis quilibet juxta eos potest per opera sua cuiusque gradus felicitatis gaudia & delicias consequi, quemadmodum abunde satis de eo agitur in libro Midras a-Nehelam. Rabbi Jehuda Levita etiam asserit Cuzari lib. 1. gentiles, omnes quotquot scripserunt de paraparadiso, omne illud ex Scriptura S. hausisse. Quare concludimus locum aliquem esse, in quo omnes qui sapienter, pie, honesteque vixerint, praemio operum suorum fruuntur.
units.tr: Well then, my friend, now set out all the doubts you have. In the Midrash Tehillim, whenever the sacred writings speak of the land of the living, as in Psalm 116:9, "I will walk before the Lord in the land of the living," and in similar passages, the ancient sages always explain these words of paradise, because that is the land in which one lives forever. Abigail too elegantly calls that place "the bundle of life" [צרור החיים, tzror ha-chayim], when David says in 1 Sam. 25:29, "The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord your God; but the souls of your enemies he shall sling out, as from the hollow of a sling." Several admirable points are contained in this verse. First, that souls are immortal and incorruptible, since in them there is no efficient cause of corruption. This is indicated when it says, "the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life," for paradise is so called because there is continuous and indissoluble joy of life there. And in the same discussion, p. 75: "But to return to our purpose, it is most certain that there truly and not figuratively exists a place called paradise, in which our ancient Masters report that there are seven dwellings, or degrees of happiness, which the divine theologians in the Zohar called palaces [הכלות, hekhalot]. In these, each person, according to them, can obtain the joys and delights of each degree of happiness through his own works, as is sufficiently discussed in the book Midrash ha-Neelam. Rabbi Jehudah Levi also asserts in the Cuzari, book 1, that the Gentiles, all who have written about paradise, drew all of that from Holy Scripture. Therefore we conclude that there is some place in which all who have lived wisely, piously and honorably enjoy the reward of their works."

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Contendunt omnes Judaeos, si paucos excipias, vitae aeternae futuros haeredes, quod Judaei sint populus Dei Justus, qui jure haereditario terram in perpetuum debeat possidere, ex Esaia cap. 60. verf. 21. Et populus tuus omnes justi sunt, in perpetuum hereditabunt terram, germen plantationis meae, opus manus meae ad glorificandum; Quod Veterum Sapientum fit effatum, Israelem futuri seculi fore participem, ex Tractatu Talmudico Sanhedrin, cap. 11: Totus Israel partem habet futuri seculi; Hinc, non tantum ꝑ'ꝑ'ꝑ justos, statim a morte deliciis frui paradisiacis, sed ipsos Intermedios, impiosque Judaeos, postquam infernalibus flammis per ignem purgatorium spatio duodecim mensium, aut tempore quandoque breviori, ob peccata sua fuerint excruciati, Ilicque purgati, partem suam in vita consequi aeterna, quamvis non ita magnam, quam piorum justorumque; Excludentes unice Judaeos perfecte improbos, qui Deum prorsus abnegant, vel a fide deficiunt Judaica, ampletentes alienam, uti patet ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi in
units.tr: All the Jews, with a few exceptions, contend that they will be heirs of eternal life, because the Jews are the just people of God, who by hereditary right ought to possess the land forever, from Isaiah 60:21: "And your people are all just; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, for my glorification." There is also the saying of the ancient sages, that Israel will have a share in the age to come, from the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, chapter 11: "All Israel has a share in the age to come." Hence they hold that not only the tzaddikim [צדיקים], the just, at once from death enjoy paradisal delights, but also the intermediate and wicked Jews, after they have been tormented in the infernal flames by purgatorial fire for a period of twelve months, or sometimes for a shorter time, on account of their sins, and have been purged there, obtain their share of eternal life, though not as great as that of the pious and just. They exclude only the Jews who are utterly wicked, who deny God altogether or fall away from the Jewish faith, embracing a foreign one, as is clear from Rabbi Leo of Modena in

units.la: Opusculo de Ceremoniis & Consuetudinibus hodiernorum Judaeorum, Part.v. cap.10: Sic & pro certo habent, Judaeos haereji non infectos, nec discedentes a traditionibus majorum diutius uno anno in purgatorio haud detineri: & horum numerum non exiguum esse censent. Paucissimis namque contingere putant, neque nisi gravissimis peccatoribus, in perpetuum poenas experiri & subire infernales.
units.tr: his little work On the Ceremonies and Customs of the Jews of Today, part 5, chapter 10: They also hold for certain that Jews not infected with heresy, nor departing from the traditions of their elders, are not detained in purgatory for longer than one year; and they consider that the number of these is not small. For they think that only the very few, and only the gravest sinners, undergo and suffer the infernal punishments forever.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Pronunciant Proselytos vitae futurae cohaeredes, sed in inferni ignem prius deturbandos, perqué menses duodecim purificandos, quod Israeli sint saepe sicut scabies, quoque in Tractatu Talmudico Nidda, sol. 13. impedient Messiae adventum, teste Rabbi Moseh Maimonide, cap.11. Sanhedrin, sol. 18: Cum homo credit fundamenta illa omnia, & inclaresçit in fide suo per illa, congregatur cum universo Israel & praecepto, ut amemus eum; & misericordiam exhibeamus illi, & conversentur cum illo in omnibus, quae unicuique praecepit Deus Benedictus charitatem & fraternitatem concernentibus &c. Talis eadem punitur pro ratione peccatorum suorum; est tamen et pars in futuro seculo; sic Piis ex mundi gentibus vitam tribuunt aeternam, si modo septem Noachi praecepta diligenter observaverint, uti liquet ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, libr.
units.tr: They pronounce proselytes co-heirs of future life, but first to be cast down into the fire of hell and cleansed for twelve months, because they are often like a scab to Israel, and, as in the Talmudic tractate Niddah, folio 13, they delay the coming of the Messiah, as witnessed by Rabbi Moses Maimonides, chapter 11 of Sanhedrin, folio 18: When a man believes all those fundamental principles, and is illuminated in his faith through them, he is joined with all Israel, and the precept is that we should love him, show mercy to him, and deal with him in all matters that the Blessed God has commanded concerning charity and brotherliness, etc. Such a person is punished according to the measure of his sins; yet he also has a share in the age to come. So too, for pious persons from the nations of the world, they assign eternal life, if only they have diligently observed the seven precepts of Noah, as is clear from Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, book 3 On the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 2, p. 345:

units.la: libr.III.deRefurrectioneMortuorum,cap.II. pag.345: Nihilominus tamen, qui sese exgentibus aggregaverint populo Dei, vel septem praecepta Noachi diligenter observaverint, ex sententia R. Hanina, iisdem privilegiis atq; Israelitae fruentur; juxta illud, quod ante etiam retulimus: Piae nationes mundi partem obtinebunt in futuro seculo; Pluribusque videri potest ex Theologia Judaica, cap.15. §.9. & 10; Sic quoque inter Recentiores reperiuntur Judaeos, qui Christianos ad vitae aeternae trahunt communionem; sed quam candide agant, & sincere, diximus cit. cap.15. §.11. apparebitque ulterius ex moxadducendis Hebraeorum testimoniis.
units.tr: Nevertheless, those who have joined themselves to the people of God from the nations, or who have diligently observed the seven precepts of Noah, according to the opinion of R. Hanina, shall enjoy the same privileges as the Israelites; in accordance with what we also related before: the pious nations of the world shall obtain a share in the age to come. It may be seen more fully from the Jewish Theology, chapter 15, §§ 9 and 10. Thus among the more recent writers too are found Jews who draw Christians into fellowship of eternal life; but how frankly and sincerely they act, we said in the cited chapter 15, § 11, and it will appear further from the testimonies of the Hebrews to be adduced below.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Altercantur vehementer Judaei de vitae beatae post mortuorum resurrectionem conditione & statu: An resuscitati cibo & potu usuri, generationi prolis operam daturi, aliasque animales actiones exercituri sint? Hinc in diversas abeunt partes. Qui negantium castra sequuntur, illi constanter asserunt, quod in vita aeterna neque fit commessatio, nec compotatio, nec generatio, nec multiplicatio, nec odium, nec invidia, sed quod justi fruituri sint splendore praesentiae Dei, uti legitur in Tractatu Talmudico Berachot, cap.2: Dictum celebre fuit in ore magistri: Seculum futurum non ita ita se habet ut seculum præsens. In seculo futuro non est esus, nec potus, nec liberorum procreatio, nec venditio, nec emptio, nec invidia, nec odium, nec contentio, sed justi sedent coronas in capitibus gerentes, & voluptatem capiunt e splendore majestatis divinæ, sicut dicitur Exodi cap. 24. vers. 11. Et viderunt Deum, & comederunt, & biberunt; quod cibus, potus, generatio, & quæ non alia, turbent gaudium illud perfectum in fidelibus vitæ beatæ, qui sic relegarentur rursus in mundum hunc turbidum, vilem, molestiisque plenum, teste Rabbi Jehuda Zabara in Michtaf Techija, cap. 6: Cum seculi futuri particeps fiat unusquisque justus, statim ac ex hoc mundo excesserit, adeo ut splendore majestatis divinæ fruatur, & deliciis summis, quibus nulla æquandæ sunt: quare credamus reversurum justum quemlibet in hunc mundum, anima & corpore reunitus, mundum hunc turbidum, vilem, molestiis plenum, atque ipsi adeo Gehennæ proximum relicto gaudio perfecto, cui nihil deest? Quod fideles in altera vita purissimi ipsa luce divina sint cibandi, cum in deserto Manna fuerint cibati, cibo e luce suprema generato, uti ratiocinatur R. Meir Ben Gabbay in Afodat Haccodesch, sol. 54: Jam vidimus, quod corpora illorum, qui puram habent animam, conserventur rebus valde tenuibus, & qui pra cæteris purus est & magis spiritualis, alantur re magis tenui & pura. Nam qui in deserto vivebant, conservabantur cum Man absorpto in membris, quod erat generatum a luce & splendore supremo, qui descendit corpore veflitus ad necessitatem eorum, ut eveheret animas eorum, & tunc evecta fuit anima eorum pro eo, atque assecuti sunt, ad fontem, quo digni fuerunt habiti. Dominus autem Prophetarum Moses, qui magis fuit evectus & singularis in cognitione creatoris sui, non indiguit eo, quod lux generarat, sed conservatus fuit luce ipsa, quae erat splendor majestatis divinae. Etiam nos firma fide credimus, resuscitandos conservatum in illa luce ista in perpetuum, perpetuitate scilicet voluntatis divinae, ut spiritus ejus sit in illis futurus, eos conservans; Quod post hanc vitam resurgentes voluptatem in mente & corpore sint percepturi ex splendore majestatis divinae, ita R. Nachman Gerundensis apud Rabbi Isacum Abarbanelem in Nachalath Abhoth, rad. 14: Resurgentes non esse esuros, nec bibituros, nec voluptatibus corporeis indulturos, sed e splendore majestatis divinae corpore simul & anima voluptatem, percepturos; Nec solum haec Nachmanidis fuit sententia, sed multorum quoque Galliae & Hispaniae Doctorum, uti citato loco testatur Rabbi Isac Abarbanel: Haec est sententia Rabbi Nachmanidis piae memoriae, cum quo faciunt multi Doctores Galliae, & multi Sapientes Hispaniae credi illud illud volunt; Sic quoque animam & corpus subsistere sine cibo & potu ait Rabbi Joseph Albo Fundamentorum sol.145: Tunc unaquaque subsistere corpus & animam sine cibo & potu; Ita beatorum gloriam dicunt, solum consistere in beatifica Dei visione, teste Rabbi Leone Mutinensi in Opusculo de Ceremoniis Judæorum, Part.v.cap.10: Dari itaque Paradisum nostri credunt, quem vocant פרדס Hortum deliciarum, ubi beati fruuntur gloria; solum in beatifica Dei visione consistente.
units.tr: The Jews dispute vigorously about the condition and state of the blessed life after the resurrection of the dead: will the raised ones eat and drink, beget offspring, and carry on the other animal activities? Opinions divide in different directions. Those who follow the camp of the deniers consistently maintain that in eternal life there is no feasting, no drinking-party, no begetting, no multiplying, no hatred, no envy, but that the righteous will enjoy the splendour of God's presence. This is taught in the Talmudic tractate Berachot, chapter 2: A famous saying was heard from the mouth of the master: the future age is not as the present age is. In the future age there is no eating, no drinking, no procreation of children, no buying and selling, no envy, no hatred, no strife, but the righteous sit with crowns on their heads and take their delight in the brightness of the divine majesty, as it is said in Exodus 24.11: And they saw God, and they ate and drank. Food, drink, generation, and such things, they argue, would disturb that perfect joy of the faithful in the blessed life, which would thus be sent back again into this troubled, base world, full of troubles. So teaches Rabbi Jehuda Zabara in Michtaf Techija, chapter 6: As soon as every righteous person has departed from this world, he becomes a partaker of the future age, so that he enjoys the splendour of the divine majesty and the highest delights, to which nothing can be compared. Why then should we believe that any righteous person will return into this world, reunited in soul and body, to this troubled, base world full of troubles, and be brought close to Gehenna itself, leaving behind a perfect joy that lacks nothing? That the faithful, in the other life, most pure, are to be fed with the divine light itself, since in the desert they were fed with manna, a food generated from the supreme light, as Rabbi Meir ben Gabbay reasons in Afodat Haccodesch, fol. 54: Now we have seen that the bodies of those who have a pure soul are preserved by very subtle things, and that one who is purer and more spiritual than the rest is nourished by a more subtle and pure thing. For those who lived in the desert were sustained by the manna absorbed into their limbs, which had been generated from the light and supreme splendour, which descended clothed in a body to meet their need, so that it might raise up their souls; and then their soul was raised up accordingly, and they reached the fountain, for which they were judged worthy. But the lord of the prophets, Moses, who was more exalted and unique in the knowledge of his Creator, did not need that which the light had generated, but was preserved by the light itself, which was the splendour of the divine majesty. We too, with firm faith, believe that those who are raised will be preserved in that light for ever, by the perpetuity of the divine will, so that his Spirit shall be in them, keeping them. That, rising after this life, they will perceive delight in mind and body from the splendour of the divine majesty: so Rabbi Nachman of Gerona, as quoted by Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel in Nachalath Abhoth, rad. 14: Those who rise will neither eat nor drink, nor indulge in bodily pleasures, but from the splendour of the divine majesty they will perceive delight with both body and soul. Nor was this only the opinion of Nachmanides, but also of many teachers of France and Spain, as Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel testifies in the passage cited: This is the opinion of Rabbi Nachmanides of blessed memory, with whom many teachers of France agree, and many wise men of Spain wish that this be believed. Likewise Rabbi Joseph Albo says in the Fundamenta, fol. 145, that soul and body subsist without food and drink: Then each body and soul subsists without food and drink. So too they say that the glory of the blessed consists solely in the beatific vision of God, as Rabbi Leo of Modena testifies in his little work on the ceremonies of the Jews, part 5, chapter 10: Therefore our people believe in a Paradise which they call Pardes [פרדס], the garden of delights, where the blessed enjoy glory, consisting solely in the beatific vision of God.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Qui Affirmantium suscipiunt partes, defendentes fideles post resurrectionem esuros, bibituros, & corporeis fruituros voluptatibus, non tantum varia producunt argumenta ex Sacra Scriptura, verum ex ipsa quoque ratione, imo Veterum Sapientum non omittunt authoritatem, uti liquet ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, libr.III.de Resurrectione mortuorum, cap.9.pag.320: Ex eo quod hactenus constituimus de novo mundo, videlicet eum plane ejusdem futurum perfectionis atque excellentiæ cum primo mundo, in quo Adamus fuit, antequam peccaverat, consequitur, eos qui in isto mundo resuscitabuntur, iisdem animalibus ac naturalibus actionibus vacaturos & operam daturos esse, Hinc varios opinionis laudat Patronos, Saadiam Gaonem, nem, Molen Maimonidem,& Ifacum Abarbanelem; Contra Rabbi Molen Nachmanidem seu Gerundenfem aggreditur, qui a negantium stat partibus, demonstrans, quod Deus nihil faciat frustra; Quod corpus reluscitatum eadem debeat gaudere qualitate; Adducens quoque quod qui ab Elia,Elifaeo & Ezechiele fuerint resuscitati, cibum sumserint & potum, uti rursus patet ex cit.cap. 9. pag.322,323,324: Hoc ipsum ex eo quoq; confirmari potest, quod resuscitati ab Elia, Elifaeo, Ezechiele, ederint, & uxores duxerint. Cur itaq; idem non fiet in seculo resurrectionis? Haec fuit opinio R. Sehadya Gaon, R. Mosis Aegyptij, R. Simhon Bar Semah in libro suo Maguen Abot, & Ifac Abravanel. Eam quidem refutat Gerundensis, in opere suo Saar a-gemul, qui existimat in futuro seculo nulli actio-ni corporeae locum fore. Caeterum, quod ad me attinet, hoc mihi verisimile, non videtur. Primo, quia Deus nihil frustra facit: at si idverum esset, tum frustra forent fructus, arbores, plantae, quae nutriendo & justentando homini serviunt. Secundo, corpus nostrum resuscitatum, eadem qualitate, ac conditione, qua ante praeditum erit. Quare necesse etiam est, ut eosdem habeat affectus & inclinationes; aut ut membra corporis frustra esse dicantur. Ad hoc Gerundensis respondet, corpus humanum adeo exacta atque perfecta compositionis esse, ut in se mirabilia quaedam secreta contineat; ac proinde non implicare contradictionem, si idem numero, iisdemque qualitatibus praeditum corpus, resuscitatum non eadem officia ac munia quae solet, per membra ista praestet. Verum responsio hac nemini facile satisfaciet: nam corpus hominis, eadem secreta etiam nunc habet, cum officium suum facit; & quis dicat, rem tum aliter se habituram esse? Certe ex sententia doctissimi, ac nobilissimi viri Isaac Abravanel, omnino id sequendum est, quod verisimillimum videtur. Quare cum homines resuscitandi sint iisdem corporibus materialibus induti quod fatentur omnes, licet non aeque compactis, & terrestribus: fieri profecto nequit, ut ii qui corporei sunt, non exerceant actiones corporales. Quid? an fidei ei natura est, ut nos cogat credere id quod ratioui repugnat? Nequaquam. Itaque resuscitatorum actiones & functiones erunt eadem cum istis, quae nunc exercentur, etsi earum longe major erit moderatio ac continentia. Si lubet etiam propius expendere sententiam antiquorum, apparebit eam plane cum hac nostra convenire: nam uti primo libro huius operis diximus, Aaroni, cum resuscitabitur, decima (uti scriptura ait) dabuntur, & Patriarchis terra Palaestina, id est eorum singulis sua terra istius portio adsignabitur. At vero si cibi ac potus nullus tum usus erit, quorsum dabuntur decimae, & portiones sua Levitis & Sacerdotibus? Accedat dat huc testimonium Esaiæ Prophetæ, qui postquam egit de innovatione, atq; instauratione mundi, ait cap. 65.21. Et ædificabunt domos, & habitabunt, & plantabunt vineas, & comedent fructum earum. Et deinde cap. 66.10. Latamini cum Jerusalaim, & exultate in ea omnes, diligentes eam gaudete cum ea gaudio universi lugentes super eam. Ut sugatis, & saturemini ab ubere consolationum ejus, ut mulgeatis, & delectemini a splendore gloriæ ejus. Hinc tribus versibus post rursum, Et videbitis, & gaudebit cor vestrum, & ossa vestra tanquam herba germinabunt. Ecce Propheta promittit hic gaudium corporale illis, qui super Hierosolymis luxerunt. Atque hæc quidem argumenta, partim a ratione, partim a S. Scriptura, & antiquorum auctoritate petita sufficiant, ad sententiam nostram comprobandam.
units.tr: Those who take up the side of the affirmers, maintaining that the faithful after the resurrection will eat, drink, and enjoy bodily pleasures, produce not only various arguments from Holy Scripture but also from reason itself. Indeed, they do not omit the authority of the ancient sages, as is clear from Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, book 3, On the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 9, page 320: From what we have hitherto established about the new world, namely that it will be entirely of the same perfection and excellence as the first world, in which Adam was before he sinned, it follows that those who are raised up in this world will be occupied with the same animal and natural actions and will busy themselves with them. Hence he praises various advocates of this opinion: Saadia Gaon, Moses Maimonides, and Isaac Abarbanel. Against Rabbi Moses Nachmanides, or of Gerona, who takes the side of the deniers, he argues, showing that God does nothing in vain; that the raised body must rejoice in the same quality; and he also adduces that those who were raised by Elijah, Elisha, and Ezekiel ate and drank, as again appears from the cited chapter 9, pages 322, 323, 324: This can also be confirmed from the fact that those raised by Elijah, Elisha, and Ezekiel ate and took wives. Why then should the same not happen in the age of the resurrection? This was the opinion of Rabbi Saadia Gaon, Rabbi Moses the Egyptian, Rabbi Simhon bar Semah in his book Maguen Abot, and Isaac Abravanel. Gerona indeed refutes it in his work Sha'ar ha-Gemul, where he thinks that in the future age no place will be left for any bodily action. For my part, however, this does not seem probable to me. First, because God does nothing in vain; but if this were true, then the fruits, trees, and plants, which serve man by nourishing and sustaining him, would be in vain. Second, our body, raised with the same quality and condition in which it was before, must also have the same affections and inclinations; otherwise the members of the body would be said to be in vain. To this Gerona replies that the human body is of such exact and perfect composition that it contains within itself certain marvellous secrets; and therefore it does not involve a contradiction if a body that is the same in number and endowed with the same qualities, once raised, does not perform through those members the same offices and functions that it usually does. But this answer will hardly satisfy anyone: for the human body has these same secrets even now, when it performs its office; and who would say that the matter would then be otherwise? Certainly, in the judgement of that most learned and most noble man, Isaac Abravanel, one must altogether follow what seems most probable. Therefore, since men are to be raised clothed in the same material bodies, which all admit, though not equally compact and earthly, it is surely impossible that those who are corporeal should not exercise bodily actions. What then? Is it the nature of faith to compel us to believe what is repugnant to reason? By no means. Therefore the actions and functions of the raised will be the same as those that are now exercised, although their moderation and restraint will be far greater. If it pleases us to weigh more closely the opinion of the ancients, it will appear that it plainly agrees with this view of ours. For, as we said in the first book of this work, tithes (as Scripture says) will be given to Aaron when he is raised, and the land of Palestine to the Patriarchs, that is, to each of them a portion of that land will be assigned. But if there is then no use of food and drink, to what purpose will tithes and portions be given to the Levites and priests? Let there be added the testimony of the prophet Isaiah, who, after speaking of the renewal and restoration of the world, says in chapter 65.21: And they shall build houses and dwell in them, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit. And then in chapter 66.10: Rejoice with Jerusalem, and exult in her all you who love her; rejoice with her in joy, all you who mourn over her; that you may suck and be satisfied from the breast of her consolations, that you may milk and be delighted with the splendour of her glory. Three verses later he says again: And you shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall sprout like grass. Behold, the prophet here promises bodily joy to those who mourned over Jerusalem. These arguments, drawn partly from reason, partly from Holy Scripture, and from the authority of the ancients, are enough to confirm our opinion.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Sic Rabbi Ifac Abarbanel, inter Affirmantes minime postremus, non tantum constanter asserit, post resurrectionem homines eluros, bibiturosque, sed rationibus quoq; nonnullis evincere omni studet modo, uti liquet ex Nachalath Abhoth, rad 14: Quod si docea-mus, resurrecturos nil esse acturos membris & sensi-bus suis, & in æternum sua offa retenturos: Ecce non sorent illi ipsi, qui erant morientes, quoniam non is-dem corporibus & membris gauderent, quippe qua erant naturâ passibilia, pro temperamenti con-ditione ditione agentia, ratione materiæ corruptibilia. At corpora resurgentia erunt alterius naturæ incorruptibilis, impassibilis, nec facultatibus suis & sensibus utentis, ac proinde à natura morientis discrepantis, ut discrepat corpus cadaveris ab corruptibilibus hisce. Itaque foret nova creatio, non resurrectio mortuorum. Altera Rabbi Abarbanelis ratio hæc est: Præterea licet voluptas, qua ibi fruentur, sit à splendore majestatis divinæ spiritualis, qua delectari posset anima rationalis, corpora tamen plane non delectabuntur, cum unusquisque sensus sensibili proprio oblectetur, non aliquo, quod cum eo non spectet, imo nec genere conveniat; uti odoratus è sonis musicis voluptatem non capit, nec gustus è formis pulchris. Si ergo tunc voluptatibus sensitivus non afficietur homo, qua tandem re gaudebit corpus, cum majestas divina sensuum ejus objectum non sit? Tandem tertiam adducit rationem Abarbanel: Adhæc obstat huic sententiæ dubium, quod hac de re movit magnus Doctor Maimon, quod sensus & facultates frustra essent; Sic in suffragantium classe apparet Rabbi Moses Maimonides, cum in Epistola de Resurrectione Mortuorum ita scribit: Illi, quorum animæ in corpora redibunt, edent, bibent, concumbent, gignent & morientur post vitam valde diuturnam ad instar ejus, quæ Messiæ tempore erit; Sic inter affirmantes conspicitur Rabbi Saadias Hag-gaon. gaon in Sepher Emuna, sol. 36. Sexta quaestio est, an sint comesturi, bibituri, uxores ducturi? dico utique, sicut filius Sareptanae, quem vivificabat Deus per Eliam, et filius Sunamitidis, quem per Elisam, comederunt, biberunt, et procul dubio uxores duxerunt; Sic Rabbi Molche de Trana, in Beth Elohim, sol. 112. Et Rabbi Aben Esra, ad Daniel. cap. 12. verf. 2. Aliique plures Affirmantium sequuntur captra.
units.tr: Thus Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel, not the least among the Affirmers, not only firmly asserts that after the resurrection men will eat and drink, but also tries by several arguments to prove it in every way, as is clear from his Nachalath Abhoth, rad 14: But if we were to teach that those who rise will do nothing with their limbs and senses, and will keep their bones for ever, then those very persons who were dying would not be the same, since they would not rejoice in the same bodies and limbs, which by their nature were passible and acted according to the condition of their temperament, and were corruptible by reason of their matter. But risen bodies will be of another nature, incorruptible and impassible, and not using their faculties and senses. Accordingly they would differ from the nature of the dying, just as a corpse differs from these corruptible bodies. So it would be a new creation, not a resurrection of the dead. Abarbanel's second argument is this: Moreover, although the pleasure which they will enjoy there comes from the splendour of the divine majesty, such as a rational soul could take delight in, the bodies will not take delight at all, since each sense is delighted by its own proper sensible object, and not by something which does not relate to it, nor even belongs to its kind. Thus the sense of smell takes no pleasure from musical sounds, nor taste from beautiful forms. If then man is not affected by sensory pleasures in that state, by what means will the body rejoice, since the divine majesty is not the object of its senses? Lastly, Abarbanel adduces a third argument: Besides, there is a difficulty against this opinion, which the great teacher Maimonides raised on this matter, namely that the senses and faculties would then be in vain; So among the company of those who agree appears Rabbi Moses Maimonides, when he writes thus in his Epistle on the Resurrection of the Dead: Those whose souls return to bodies will eat, drink, marry, beget children and die, after a very long life, like that which will be in the time of the Messiah; So among the Affirmers is seen Rabbi Saadia Haggaon, in his Sepher Emuna, p. 36: The sixth question is whether they will eat, drink and take wives? I say indeed, just as the son of the widow of Zarephath, whom God revived through Elijah, and the son of the Shunammite woman, whom He revived through Elisha, ate, drank and, without doubt, took wives; So also Rabbi Moses of Trani, in Beth Elohim, p. 112; and Rabbi Aben Ezra, on Daniel ch. 12 v. 2. And several others of the Affirmers follow these lines.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Sed licet multis inter Judaeos haereat mens, homines post resurrectionem futuros, bibituros, liberosque procreaturos, non tamen hi omnes in ea versantur opinione, quod semper, in omni aeternitate, & in seculo futuro sint comesturi & bibituri, distinguunt quippe inter mundum resuscitatorum, & coelum beatorum, indicantes, quod in illo, cibo & potu sint fruituri, non vero in hoc, seu seculo futuro, uti exipsis liquet affirmantibus, maxime ex Rabbi Saadia Haggaon, cum in Sepher Emuna, sol. 36. Hic inquit: Septima est quaestio, quomodo transferantur in seculum futurum, ubi esus & connubium exulant, quibus in hoc seculo erant assuefacti, & tamen vivant? Dico, sicut Moses Magister noster, super quem fit pax, erat assuefactus usui, bitioni, & connubio; nihilo tamen minus sine illis subsistebat in monte Sinai quadraginta diebus tribus. bus vicibus,& vivebat ceu narratur in lege; Et ex Rabbi Mosche de Trana in Beth Elohim, sol. 111. Præterea Mosi æquiparatur Israel à Saadia. Licet autem ille substiterit in monte quadraginta diebus sine cibo & potu, ecquis tamen ad tantam ut ille sanctitatem corporis ascendit? Itaq; tempore resurrectionis quo concupiscentia prava maximam partem carebunt homines resurgentes, poterit unusquisq; mundare corpus suum, ut finito suo tempore transferatur ad seculum futurum, ubi sine esu, potu, & cæteris corporis præsidiis subsistat; Ita Rabbi Moses Maimonides asserit, solas animas seculum ingressuras futurum, suaque corporea deposituras membra, per consequens illas non necesse habituras cibo, potuque, uti patet ex Jad Chazalia, Tractatu de Pœnitentia, c. 8. In seculo autem futuro non est corpus, neque corporale quid, sed anima solummodo justorum, & quidem absq; corpore, perinde ut angeli ministerii, quandoquidem itaque nihil in eo corporale est, ideo etiam in eo neque cibus est neque potus, aut quicquam eorum, quibus corpora hominum hoc in seculo habent opus. Neque ibi aliquid eorum contingit, quæ hoc in seculo evenire corporibus solent, cujusmodi sunt, sessio, statio, mutatio, mors, dolor, risus, & quod hùs est simile; De mundo resuscitatorum referunt Rabbini, quod per mille duret annos, ex eoque in seculum futurum transferantur, post exactos mille annos in terra, illi, qui vitam merentur æternam.
units.tr: But although many among the Jews are persuaded that men after the resurrection will eat, drink and beget children, not all of them hold the opinion that they will eat and drink always, in all eternity and in the future age. For they distinguish between the world of the risen and the heaven of the blessed, indicating that in the former they will enjoy food and drink, but not in the latter, or future age, as is clear from the affirmers themselves, especially from Rabbi Saadia Haggaon in his Sepher Emuna, p. 36. He says here: The seventh question is, how are they transferred into the future age, where eating and marriage cease, to which they were accustomed in this age, and yet they live? I say that, just as Moses, our teacher, upon whom be peace, was accustomed to food, drink and marriage, yet nonetheless he stayed without them on Mount Sinai for forty days, three times, and lived, as is related in the Law; and from Rabbi Moses of Trani in Beth Elohim, p. 111: Moreover, Israel is compared by Saadia to Moses. Yet although he remained on the mountain for forty days without food and drink, who has ever attained such holiness of body as he did? Therefore at the time of the resurrection, when men who rise will be largely free of depraved desire, each man will be able to cleanse his body, so that at the end of his time he may be transferred into the future age, where he may subsist without eating, drinking, and the other supports of the body; Thus Rabbi Moses Maimonides affirms that only souls will enter the future age, laying aside their bodily limbs, and consequently will have no need of food or drink, as appears from the Jad Chazaka, in the Treatise on Repentance, ch. 8: In the future age there is no body, nor anything bodily, but only the souls of the just, and indeed without a body, just like the angels of ministry. Since therefore nothing in it is bodily, there is neither food nor drink in it, nor any of those things for which human bodies have need in this age. Nor do any of those things happen there which usually happen to bodies in this age, such as sitting, standing, change, death, pain, laughter, and the like. The Rabbis relate of the world of the risen that it lasts a thousand years, and after that those who merit eternal life are transferred from it into the future age, after the thousand years spent on earth.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Credunt alterum de mortuorum, resuscitatorumque hominum fore miserum, doloro-sumque, afferentes, improbos, damnatosque suas in Inferno exquisitas passuros pœnas, hinc ut conditionem qualitatemque describerent damnatorum, simulque pœnarum indigitarent locum, variis hunc ex Scriptura Sacra appellarunt nominibus, mox Infernum, Sepulchrumque; Perditionem; Puteum perditionis; mox Fovcam sonitus; Lutum cœni; Umbram mortis; Terram inferiorem; mox voce usitatissima, Gehennam; Thopheth; Lacum Inferorum; Siccitatem, uti de septem prioribus appellationibus liquet ex Tractatu Talmudico Erufin, cap.4, sol.19: Dixit Rabbi Jehosua, Bar Levi: Septem sunt nomina quibus appellatur infernus: Scheol, Abaddon, Beer Schachat, Bor Schaon, Tit haijaven, Tzalmaveth, Eretz thachthith; Scheol appellatur, quia scriptum Jonæ cap.2. verf.3: A ventre inferni clamavi, vocem meam exaudivisti; Abaddon vocatur, quia scriptum Psalm. 88. verf.12, Numquid narrabitur in sepulchro benignitas tua, veritas tua in perditione? Nominatur Beer Schachat. chat, quia scriptum Psalm.16. vers.10: Quoniam non derelinques me in inferno, nec dabis pium tuum, ut videat corruptionem. Vocatur Bor Schaon, & Tit haijavcn, quia scriptum Psalm.40.vers.3. Et eduxit me ex puteo strepitus, ex luto cœni. Dicitur Tzalmaveth, quia scriptum Psalm.107.vers.10: Habitantes tenebras & umbram mortis: Vocatur quoque Eretz thachthith.
units.tr: They believe that the other state of the dead and of resurrected men will be wretched and full of pain, asserting that the wicked and the damned will suffer the exquisite punishments prepared for them in Hell. Hence, in order to describe the condition and nature of the damned and at the same time to name the place of punishment, they have called it by various names taken from Holy Scripture: first Hell, and Sepulchre; Destruction; Pit of destruction; then Pit of noise; Miry clay; Shadow of death; Lower earth; and then, by the most common term, Gehenna; Tophet; Lake of the dead; Dryness. This is clear about the first seven of these names from the Talmudic tractate Erubin, chapter 4, folio 19: Rabbi Jehoshua ben Levi said: There are seven names by which hell is called: Sheol, Abaddon, Be'er Shachat, Bor Sha'on, Tit ha-yaven, Tzalmavet, Eretz tachtit. It is called Sheol, because it is written in Jonah chapter 2, verse 3: Out of the belly of hell I cried, and thou heardest my voice. It is called Abaddon, because it is written in Psalm 88, verse 12: Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? or thy faithfulness in destruction? It is named Be'er Shachat, because it is written in Psalm 16, verse 10: For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thy holy one to see corruption. It is called Bor Sha'on and Tit ha-yaven, because it is written in Psalm 40, verse 3: He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay. It is called Tzalmavet, because it is written in Psalm 107, verse 10: Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. It is also called Eretz tachtit.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Credunt, homines, tum intermedios, impiosque, tum perfecte improbos, ad infernum omnes descensuros, pœnasque subituros infernales; hanc tamen addentes differentiam, quod intermedii, impiique ex Judæis, tandem post duodecim menses ex hoc carcere sint liberandi & ad vitam perducendi æternam, perfecte vero improbi tum Judæi, tum gentiles, tum Christiani nullam ex inferno liberationis habeant (pem reliquam, nulloque modo ad superas possint evadere auras, uti patet ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi in Opusculo de Ceremoniis hodiernorum Judæorum, Part. V. cap.10: Quod ad infernum, qui Judæis dicitur ᵴᵴᵴ, sentiunt, impiorum animas igni illic, alisque supplicijs vehementissime excruciari, qua aliæ damnatorum sine spe redemptionis; alij vero ad certum tempus sustinere tenentur. Ad ultimum pœnarum genus optime nomen purgatorij quaquadrat; neq; enim hoc ab inferno ratione loci, sed tantum ratione durationis distinguitur; Et ex R. Menasseh Ben Israel, libr. II. de Resurrectione Mortuorum, cap.8.p.180,181: Probi adjuum commodum ac bonum ut recipiant praemium virtutis. Improbi, ad incommodum & malum sluum, ut corpore atq; anima simul puniantur, ac miserè crucientur. Idcirco a Psalmista dicitur Psalm.1.5: Ideo non consistent impij in judicio. Idest, resurgent quidem: sed non consistent; quippe resurrectio illa, non fiet eorum bono, ac commodo: sed ad gravissimam eorum poenam. Hinc Chaldaeus Paraphrastes pro יקפ' א'ל ponit יכי' א'ל non merebuntur; atque illud est, quod diximus. Intermedii expiantur suo bono: nam aliquamdiu quidem puniuntur: sed postea puri atq; immaculati facti, recipiuntur in ordinem bonorum, ut cum illis parti felitate fruantur.
units.tr: They believe that all men, both the intermediate and the wicked, and also the utterly wicked, will descend into Hell and undergo infernal punishments. They add this difference, however: the intermediate and the wicked among the Jews will at last, after twelve months, be freed from this prison and brought to eternal life; but the utterly wicked, whether Jews, Gentiles or Christians, have no remaining hope of deliverance from Hell and can by no means escape to the upper air. This is clear from Rabbi Leo of Modena in his little work on the ceremonies of the Jews of today, part 5, chapter 10: "As for the hell which the Jews call Sheol, they hold that the souls of the wicked are tormented there most severely by fire and other punishments, while the souls of other damned persons are held there for a fixed time. Purgatory is the best name for this last kind of punishment, for it is distinguished from hell not by its place but only by the length of its duration." And from R. Menasseh ben Israel, book 2 on the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 8, pages 180–181: The good rise so that they may receive the reward of virtue; the wicked rise to their own harm and evil, so that they may be punished and wretchedly tormented in body and soul together. Hence the Psalmist says (Psalm 1:5): Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the judgment. That is, they will indeed rise, but they will not stand; for that resurrection will not be for their good and advantage, but for their most grievous punishment. Hence the Chaldee paraphrast puts [יקפ' א'ל] for [יכי' א'ל], "they shall not be worthy"; and that is what we have said. The intermediate are cleansed for their own good; for they are indeed punished for a while, but afterwards they are made pure and spotless and are received into the order of the good, so that they may enjoy the same happiness. ## XIV.

units.la: XIV.

Asserunt, Judaeos Intermedios, priorem in inferno constituentes clausem, non aeternas perpessuros poenas, sed temporarias, non damnandos in tempiternum, sed expiandos, hinc in bonorum ordinem ad vitam recipiendos aeternam, nitentes hoc immoto atque irrefragabili Talmudistarum fundamento: Quod omnis Israelita particeps futuri sit seculi, id est, quod si Judaeus unicum tantum parret bonum opus, hæres futurus sit vitæ æternæ; per consequens, quod pauci ex Judæis, illa sint privandi felicitate; Quod 1.Sam.cap.25.v.29. hoc expresse innuatur, cum dicitur: Porro animicorum tuorum anima rotabitur, quasi in impetu, & circulo funda; teste Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, Problemate 17. de Creatione, pag.73:
units.tr: They assert that the Jews who are intermediate, while they place the former in Hell as a prison, will not suffer eternal punishments but temporary ones; that they will not be condemned forever but cleansed, and hence received into the order of the good to eternal life. They rest this on the firm and unshakeable foundation of the Talmudists: that every Israelite is a partaker of the world to come, that is, that if a Jew performs even one single good work he will be an heir of eternal life; and consequently that only a few of the Jews are to be deprived of that happiness. That this is clearly hinted at in 1 Samuel 25:29, when it is said: Yet the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out, as out of the middle of a sling; as Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel testifies, Problem 17, on the Creation, page 73:

units.la: Quinto punitri malos & impios, cum animæ ejusmodi hominum nunquam quietis fiant participes, sed semper inquietentur, non aliter quam in funda lapillus, antequam ejiciatur, nunc huc, nunc illuc agitatur: nam sursum ascendere conantes, deflituuntur alis virtutis, & bonorum operum, & ad corpus redire cupientes, non inveniunt illud: quare perpetua inquietudine & turbatione assidua in & cum eo vexantur, instar Sisyphi, vel Tantali, de quibus Homerus in Odyssea sua. Sexto deniq; animas impiorum aliquando pœnis, & cruciatibus liberatum iri, quia eorum tormenta non sunt perpetua. ideo enim dixit in circulo funda; quoniam ejusmodi animæ nondum sunt abjectæ in locum longinquum & remotum, sicut petræ funda projici solent, sed sine emissione quasi in fundo & centro funda hærent, usque dum vitia eluerint & purgaverint; Et pag.74: Nam Deum non omnino perdere animam, eamque annihilare: sed cum mortua est, id est, cum privata & destituta est præsentia Dei, sive orbata omni spiritualitate sua, Deum con constituisse eam, non penitus & plane à se depel-lere atque abjicere: sed ad tempus donec tantum sese à vitiis peccatisque suis purgaverit, tum vero deinde eam velle reducere, & remittere altera vice in mundum per μετεμψύχωσιν seu animarum transmigrationem, uti Cabbalistæ opinantur. Ex quo manifestum fit, animam in æternum non privari divinitate.
units.tr: Fifthly, the wicked and the impious are punished, since the souls of such men never become partakers of rest but are always disturbed, just as a little stone in a sling, before it is cast out, is moved now here, now there. For when they try to rise upward they are deprived of the wings of virtue and good works; and when they desire to return to the body they do not find it. Therefore they are vexed with perpetual unrest and constant disturbance in and with it, like Sisyphus or Tantalus, of whom Homer speaks in his Odyssey. Sixthly, finally, the souls of the impious will at some time be freed from punishments and torments, because their torments are not perpetual. For that reason he said "in the circle of a sling": since such souls have not yet been cast into a distant and remote place, as stones are usually flung from a sling, but without being released they hang as it were in the bottom and centre of the sling, until they have washed away and purged their vices. And on page 74: For God does not utterly destroy the soul and annihilate it; but when it is dead, that is, when it is deprived and destitute of the presence of God, or bereft of all its spirituality, God has established it, not wholly and plainly to cast it away and reject it from himself, but for a time, until it has cleansed itself from its vices and sins; and then he wills to bring it back and send it again into the world by [μετεμψύχωσις], that is, by the transmigration of souls, as the Cabbalists suppose. From this it is made manifest that the soul is not deprived of divinity for ever.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Non credunt Judæi, Purgatorium ab Inferno esse sejunctum, verum Purgatorium in ipso collocant Inferno, statuentes pœnam infernalem, quam, qui in priore sunt classe, sustinere necesse habent, nihil esse aliud quam Purgatorium, proinde Purgatorium ab inferno neque distingui ratione loci, neque ratione expiationis, repudiantes propterea Pontificiorum Purgatorium, Limbumq; appellantesq; hoc totum meram fabulam, uti patet ex R. Menasseh Ben Israel, cum Problemate 11. de Creatione, ad Quæstionem: An præter duo ista loca proœmii & pœnæ, sint ea quæ vulgo dicuntur limbus, & purgatorium? Sic respondet pag. 84, 85: Verum hoc totum mera est fabula. Itaque primo negamus apud inferos esse locum, quem vocant sinum Abrahami: nam certo credendum est, Patriarchas, & eos qui fuerunt ju-sti, fti, ut Hanochum & Noachum, fi in vita, quando anima eorum conjuncta adhuc erat corpori immundo, fruerentur spiritu & gratia Dei, tanto magis postquam mortui sunt, iisdem frui. Multa etiam loca passim inveniuntur, ex quibus hæc confirmari queunt. Nam Deus varius in locis promittit observantibus legem, vitam & bonum; contra vero mortem & malum legem non observantibus. Dicit enim David Psalm. 116. 9. ambulabo coram Domino, in terra vita. Atque ita etiam Abigail futura prænuncians ait, & erit anima Domini mei ligata in fasciculo vitæ. Valde præterea ridiculum est credere limbum esse, in quem conjiciantur infantes, propter peccatum originale: quod confirmari facile a nobis potest rationibus multis. Denique non est necessarium, ut ponamus purgatorium: nam ponimus varios gradus esse in inferno, pro ratione multorum aut paucorum peccatorum, quæ quis commisit. Quid quod in sacris literis nullum vestigium eorum locorum reperire est? & gentiles qui locuti sunt de præmio & pœna animarum, non plura pufuere loca, quam infernum & paradisum, quorum hunc vocarunt Elysios campos, illum Tartarum; Sic pluribus describunt duplicem animarum viam post hanc vitam, unam tendentem ad paradisum, alteram ad infernum, teste Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, libr. II. de Resurrectione Mortuorum, cap. 10 pag. 230: Alterum judicium animæ est, quod eam post separationem à corpore manet, quod vel absoluta fertur in paradisum, vel damnata in tartarum detruditur, ut ibi peccatorum suorum pœnas luat. Hujus judicii varius in locis meminere veteres. De R. Johanan Ben Zacay refertur, quod imminente fatali hora fleverit: rogatus causam à discipulis, responderit, duas se videre ante oculos suos vias; vidi unam, quæ recta ad infernum; alteram, quæ in paradisum euntes ducat; & nescire se, qua ducendus sit. Quam plurima etiam commemorant de utraque hac via Cabalistæ per totum Zoar.
units.tr: The Jews do not hold that Purgatory is separate from Hell. They place Purgatory within Hell itself, holding that the infernal punishment which those in the first class must undergo is nothing other than Purgatory. Purgatory and Hell therefore differ neither in place nor in purpose of cleansing. For this reason they reject the Papists' Purgatory, and they call Limbo and all of this a mere fable, as is clear from Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, in his Problem 11 on the Creation, where he asks whether, besides these two places of reward and punishment, there are those that are commonly called limbo and purgatory. He answers thus (pp. 84, 85): Indeed, all of this is a mere fable. Therefore, first, we deny that there is in the underworld a place which they call the bosom of Abraham. For it must be firmly believed that the patriarchs and those who were righteous, such as Enoch and Noah, while they lived, when their souls were still joined to an unclean body, enjoyed the Spirit and grace of God, and all the more so now that they are dead. Many passages are also found everywhere from which these things can be confirmed. For God in many places promises life and good to those who keep the law, but death and evil to those who do not keep it. David says in Psalm 116:9: "I will walk before the Lord in the land of the living." And Abigail, foretelling the future, likewise says: "The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life." Moreover, it is very ridiculous to believe that there is a limbo into which infants are cast on account of original sin, which we can easily confirm by many arguments. Finally, it is not necessary for us to posit a purgatory, for we posit various degrees in Hell, according to the number of few or many sins that a person has committed. Moreover, in the sacred writings no trace of those places can be found.
