And the Gentiles who spoke of the reward and punishment of souls did not name more places than Hell and Paradise, of which they called the one the Elysian Fields and the other Tartarus. Thus they describe, in many ways, a twofold path of souls after this life, one leading to Paradise and the other to Hell, as witnessed by Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, in Book II of On the Resurrection of the Dead, ch. 10, p. 230: There is a second judgment of the soul, which remains after its separation from the body; the soul is either carried away, absolved, into Paradise, or, condemned, is thrust down into Tartarus, there to pay the penalties of its sins. The ancients mention this judgment in various places. It is related of Rabbi Johanan ben Zakkai that when his fatal hour was at hand he wept; when his disciples asked the cause, he replied that he saw two ways before his eyes, one that leads straight to Hell and another that leads those going to Paradise; and that he did not know by which he was to be led. The Cabbalists also record very many things about each of these ways throughout the whole Zohar.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Docent, Judæos perfecte improbos, sed tamen paucos, posteriorem Inferni, ultimamque formantes classem, ad Superos nunquam revocandos, sed æternum pœnis infernalibus cruciandos, referentes inter hos singulariter improbos, Judæos Apostatas, Epicureosque, qui fidem deserunt Judaicam, legi Mosaicæ derogant divinitatem, mortuorumque non agnoscunt resurrectionem, probantes illud ex Exod. cap. 32. v. 32: Et nunc si auferes peccatum eorum, & si non, dele me nunc de libro tuo. Et dixit Dominus ad Moïse: Quisquis peccavit mihi, delēdelebo eum de libro meo ; Uti patet ex Theol. Judaic. cap. 15. §. 17. Et pluribus videri potest ex Tractatu Talmudico Sanhedrin, cap. Chelek, sol. 90: Hi sunt, qui non habent partem in futuro seculo, nempe qui dicit, quod revivificatio mortuorum non sit ex lege, & quod lex non sit data e coelo, & Epicurus ; Ex Rabbi Mose Maimonide in Sanhedrin, cap. Chelek, pag. 17: Dictum quoque 1. Sam. cap. 25. verf. 29: Vivat anima Domini mei, & ligata sit in fasciculo viventium ; Ecce omnis qui eligit, ut quiescat in voluptatibus corporis, & avertatur veritatem, & diligit mendacium, exscisus est ab illa dignitate; Ex Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, libr. II. de Resurrectione Mortuorum, cap. 8. pag. 181: Excepto triplici illo hominum genere, primum qui negant Deum esse, deinde qui legi Mosaicae divinitatem derogant, denique qui non agnoscunt resurrectionem mortuorum; tales enim etiamsi honeste ac probe in caeteris vixerint: nihilominus tamen beatitudinis participes non erunt: sed expergiscentur, ac resurgent, ut in aeternum cruciantur: juxta verba Esaiae, cap. 66. 24. Et egredientur & videbunt cadavera virorum praevaricantium in me, quia vermis eorum non morietur, & ignis eorum non extinguetur, & erunt nausea omni carni; Xx
units.tr: They teach that the Jews who are utterly wicked, yet few in number, form the last and lowest class of Hell, and are never to be recalled to the upper world, but are tormented forever with infernal punishments. Among these especially wicked ones they count Jewish apostates and Epicureans, who abandon the Jewish faith, deny the divinity of the Mosaic law, and do not acknowledge the resurrection of the dead. They prove this from Exodus 32:32: "Now, if you will forgive their sin, well; but if not, blot me, I pray, out of your book." And the Lord said to Moses: "Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot out of my book." As is clear from the Jewish Theology, ch. 15, §17. And it may be seen more fully from the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, chapter Chelek, fol. 90: These are they who have no part in the world to come, namely he who says that the resurrection of the dead is not from the law, and that the law was not given from heaven, and Epicurus. From Rabbi Moses Maimonides, in Sanhedrin, chapter Chelek, p. 17: Also, it is said in 1 Samuel 25:29: "The soul of my lord shall live, and be bound in the bundle of the living." Behold, whoever chooses to rest in bodily pleasures, and turns away from truth, and loves falsehood, is cut off from that dignity. From Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel, Book II of On the Resurrection of the Dead, ch. 8, p. 181: Excepting that threefold kind of men: first, those who deny that God exists; next, those who deny the divinity of the Mosaic law; and finally, those who do not acknowledge the resurrection of the dead. For such, even if they have lived honestly and uprightly in other respects, nevertheless will not be partakers of blessedness, but will awake and rise again to be tormented forever, according to the words of Isaiah 66:24: "And they shall go forth and see the carcasses of the men that have transgressed against me; for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh."

units.la: Ex Rabbi Leone Mutinensi, in Opusculo de Ceremoniis hodiernorum Judæorum, Part. V. cap. 10; Aliisque sine numero.
units.tr: From Rabbi Leone Modena, in the little work on the ceremonies of the present-day Jews, Part V, ch. 10; and from others without number.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Collocant in Inferni posteriore ultimaq; classe non tantum Judæos Apostatas, Epicureosque, sed pari quoque modo, omnes extra Judaicam viventes Ecclesiam, הערל Præputiatos, non circumcisos, maxime tamen Christianos, quod & patet, ex adductis Talmudis & Rabbi Maimonidis dictis, §. præced. quæ omnes concernunt, sive negantes ex Judæis, sive ex Christianis, sive ex alterius religionis hominibus; Et clarius liquet ex particularibus Rabbinorum testimoniis, confessionibusque; Si quippe illi in æternum damnantur, qui affirmant resurrectionem mortuorum non esse à Lege, id est, qui dicunt, quod vita æterna non contingat propter solius Legis Mosaicæ, & sexcentorum & tredecim præceptorum observationem; Necessario Christiani æternas infernales subire debent pœnas, cum hoc expresse valde negent; Atqui tales, ipsis fatentibus Judæis, in æternum damnantur, quia beneficio legis non consequuntur vitam tam æternam; Ita quippe verba Talmudica explicat Rabbi Ifac Abarbanel, cum in Nachalath Abhoth, cap. 6. sol. 93. inquit: Nunc commemoravi, quod sermo hic adductus fuerit ad explicandum a nobis magnitudinem legis, quæ dat vitam in futuro sæculo illis, qui faciunt eam; Et cum sol. 94. pergit: Et adducit Rabbi Jose probationem, si quis consequatur vitam æternam, fieri id beneficio legis & bonorum operum: & quod lex ducat ac rectificet opera, constat e verbis Salomonis, super quo fit pax, in libro Proverbiorum, cap. 6. verf. 20, 21, 22, 23; Et initium versiculorum tale est: Custodi, fili mi præcepta patris tui, nec desere legem matris tuæ: Liga ea super corde tuo assidue, annecte super fistulas gutturis tui. In ambulando te ducet te, &c. quia lucerna præceptum, & lex lux; Præterea, si illi damnantur, qui legi Mosaicæ derogant divinitatem, necesse est, ut quam maxime flammis infernalibus perpetuis crucientur Christiani, quia Legem Oralem תורה שבעל פה, non asse-runt esse legem divinam, Mosi de nocte in monte Sinai datam, sed merum putidumque humanum dicunt esse opus; Sed adsunt alia Judæorum clariora hac de re testimonia, uti apparet ex autore Veteris Niz-zachon, zachon, cum pag. 40. de Christianis sic loquitur : Quanto magis vos torquebit ignis inextinguibilis, & in ima inferni descendetis, qui errore vestro eo prolabimini, ut dicatis rem sanctam intrasse fœminam, per locum tam obscœnum ? Ex Rabbi Bechai in Parașcha קדושים in fine: Tanta gentium oculos caligine laborare, ut lucem legis non videant, quia nullam legem habent: sed in meris tenebris ambulant, sicut dicitur : Et sunt in tenebris opera eorum &c. Quapropter & ad Gehennam destinati sunt, quæ obtenebratio vocatur, juxta illud: Omnes tenebræ absconditæ sunt in occultis ejus &c. Ex Josepho Jachiade, Psalm. 140. vers. 11. cum de Christianis & Turcis ita inquit: Declinabunt &c. id est, in infernum tandem detrudentur, & declinabunt super eos prunæ ; in ignem enim conjiciet eos Deus, & in profundas inferni foveas, e quibus nunquam, ne in Resurrectione quidem mortuorum, emergent.
units.tr: They place in the lowest and last class of Hell not only Jewish apostates and Epicureans but, in the same way, all who live outside the Jewish Church: the uncircumcised [הערל], the non-circumcised, and above all Christians. This is clear from the passages of the Talmud and Rabbi Maimonides cited in the preceding section, which all concern those who deny it, whether Jews, Christians or people of another religion. It is made even plainer by the particular testimonies and confessions of the rabbis. If those are damned forever who affirm that the resurrection of the dead does not come from the Law, that is, who say that eternal life is not obtained by the observance of the Mosaic Law and its six hundred and thirteen precepts alone, then Christians, who expressly deny this, must necessarily undergo eternal infernal punishments. Yet, as the Jews themselves admit, such people are damned forever, because by the benefit of the Law they do not attain eternal life. Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel explains the Talmudic words in this way, when in Nachalath Abhoth, chapter 6, folio 93, he says: "Now I have recalled that this saying was cited by us to explain the greatness of the Law, which gives life in the future age to those who keep it." And when, at folio 94, he goes on: "Rabbi Jose also brings the proof that if anyone attains eternal life, this comes by the benefit of the Law and good works; and that the Law guides and directs works is evident from the words of Solomon, 'upon which peace rests,' in the book of Proverbs, chapter 6, verses 20, 21, 22, 23." The beginning of those verses is: "Keep, my son, the precepts of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother. Bind them continually upon your heart, tie them about your throat. When you walk, they will lead you, etc., for the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light." Moreover, if those are damned who deny the divinity of the Mosaic Law, it must be that Christians are tormented by perpetual infernal flames all the more, since they do not hold that the Oral Law [תורה שבעל פה], given to Moses by night on Mount Sinai, is divine, but say it is a mere human and rotten work. There are also other clearer Jewish testimonies on this matter, as appears from the author of the Old Nizzachon, who speaks of Christians thus at page 40: "How much more will the unquenchable fire torment you, and you will descend to the depths of hell, you who by your error have come to the point of saying that a holy woman entered through so obscene a place?" From Rabbi Bechai on the parashah Kedoshim, at the end: "The eyes of the Gentiles labour under such darkness that they do not see the light of the Law, because they have no law, but walk in pure darkness, as it is said: 'And their works are in darkness,' etc. Therefore they are also destined for Gehenna, which is called obscuration, according to that saying: 'All darkness is hidden in its secrets,' etc." From Joseph Jachiade on Psalm 140, verse 11, where he speaks thus of Christians and Turks: "They shall fall, etc., that is, at last they shall be thrust down into hell, and burning coals shall fall upon them; for God will cast them into fire and into the deep pits of hell, from which they will never emerge, not even in the resurrection of the dead."

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Digladiantur Judæi, de damnatorum animis, posteriorem Gehennæ classem constituentibus, an perpetuis sint torquendæ dæ pœnis infernalibus, an dissolvendæ, abolendæ, annihilandæ, sicque puniendæ? Qui priorem fovent sententiam, glorian- tur non tantum in consentientium multitu- dine, verum his quoque se tuentur ratio- nibus, quod animæ sint immortales, per- consequens nunquam possint mori aut dis- solvi; Quod vermis improborum non mo- riatur, quodque ignis impiorum sit inex- tinguibilis, ex Esaiæ cap. 66. vers. 24. Pro hac sententia stat Rabbi Isac Abarbanel, cum in Commentario ad Legem, Numer. cap. 15. vers. 30. duos aggreditur Moses, Maimonidem, Nachmanidemque, oltendens ex hac sententia, dubia & absurda consequi multa; Stat quoque pro communi sententia, quam maxime Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel, pluribus animarum demonstrans immortalitatem, & libr. II. de Resurrectione Mortuorum, cap. 8. pag. 181. brevibus sic loquens: Expergiscentur, ac resurgent, ut in æternum crucientur; Stat pariter Rabbi Leo Mutinensis in Opusculo de Ceremoniis hodiernorum Judæorum, Part. V. cap. 10. Paucissimis namque contingere putant, neque nisi gravissimis peccatoribus, in perpetuum pœnas experiri, & subire infernales ; Sed juvabit quoque audire Rabbi Isacum Abarbanelem ad Num. cap. 15. vers. 30: Hac de causa venit hæc pœna nomine חמ hoc est, excidii, quod proprie competit ramo, qui exscinditur ab arbore, à qua accipit nutrimentum & vitam, quamdiu ei conjunctus manet: Sic anima exscinditur ex illo fasciculo vitæ superioris, neque recipit splendorem majestatis divinæ, quæ est voluptas & merces animalis. Hæc tamen non est privatio animæ mera, aut destructio totalis: est enim substantia spiritualis, per se subsistens, & natura sua incorruptibilis: Sed חמ sive excidium est pœna & dolor magnus animæ, recipiens magis & minus: & postquam accepit pœnam, recipit etiam oblestationem & voluptatem, sicut dicitur Jobi cap. 14. vers. 7. Est enim deo arbore spes, si præcisa fuerit, & adhuc pullulabit, & propago ejus non deficiet; Pro sententia posteriore pugnant imprimis Rabbi Moses Maimonides, & Rabbi Moses Nachmanides, uti non tantum testatur Rabbi Isac Abarbanel ad Numer cap. 15. vers. 30: Ex quibus vides, quod duo isti Sapientes, Maimonides & Nachamanides, consentiant in excidio animali, quod consistit in privatione animæ, & corruptione vel destructione ejus totalis; tum in excidio illo, quod dictum est in Idololatram & blasphemantem, quod est corporis & animæ; Verum ex ipso patet Rabbi Mose Maimonide, cum in Tractatu de Pœnitentia, cap. 8. sic inquit: Quicunque non meretur, ut vivat vitam istam, ille moritur, & nunquam reviviscit, sed exscinditur in impietate sua, & perit, ut jumentum. Et hæc excisio illa est, de qua in lege scriptum, ubi dicitur: Exscindendo exscindetur anima illa. Ex quo illud disci potest, quod anima duplici excisione fit exscindenda, quarum una ad præsens seculum, altera ad futurum pertineat. Perinde enim est, ac si dicat, quod anima a corpore separata in hoc seculo, non amplius habeatur digna, quæ vivat in seculo futuro, sed jam de seculo quoque futuro fit excisa; Et in libro Madda ita loquitur: Ultio impiorum est, quod illorum memoria non fit futura ad vitam, sed quod moriantur & exscindantur; & quicunque non est dignus vita, ille mortuus est, qui non vivit in seculum, sed in impietate sua exscinditur, & perit instar jumenti. Et hoc est excidium commemoratum in Lege, quando dicitur; Exscindendo exscindetur anima illa; Imo ex ipso quoque Rabbi Mose Nachmanide liquet, cum in Thorath Haadam, in illa ejus parte, quam שער הגמול Portam Retribu-tionis vocat, sequentem scribit in modum: Qui obnoxii sunt pœnæ, judicantur in Gehen-na duodecim menses, unusquisque prout conve-nit ipsi, post duodecim autem menses anima ejus comburitur, & fit instar cineris, hoc est, de-perit forma ejus, ut sit veluti res exusta.
units.tr: The Jews dispute concerning the souls of the damned, who form the last class of Gehenna: are they to be tormented with infernal punishments forever, or are they to be dissolved, abolished, annihilated, and so punished in that way? Those who favour the former opinion boast not only of the agreement of a great multitude, but also defend themselves with these arguments: that souls are immortal and consequently can never die or be dissolved; that the worm of the wicked does not die, and that the fire of the impious is unquenchable, from Isaiah 66:24. Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel stands for this opinion, when in his Commentary on the Law, at Numbers 15:30, he attacks two men, Maimonides and Nachmanides, showing that many doubtful and absurd consequences follow from their opinion. Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel also stands for the common opinion, most of all, demonstrating the immortality of souls by many arguments, and in book II of his On the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 8, page 181, speaks briefly thus: They will awake and rise again, to be tormented for eternity. Rabbi Leo of Modena likewise stands for it, in his little work on the ceremonies of the present-day Jews, Part V, chapter 10: For they think that very few, and only the gravest sinners, undergo and suffer infernal punishments in perpetuity. But it will also help to hear Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel on Numbers 15:30: For this reason this punishment comes under the name חמ, that is, excision, which properly belongs to a branch that is cut off from a tree, from which it receives nourishment and life as long as it remains joined to it. So the soul is cut off from that bundle of higher life, and does not receive the splendour of the divine majesty, which is the delight and reward of the animal. Yet this is not a mere privation of the soul, nor a total destruction: for it is a spiritual substance, subsisting in itself, and by its nature incorruptible. But חמ, or excision, is a punishment and great pain of the soul, admitting of more and less; and after it has received the punishment, it also receives refreshment and delight, as is said in Job 14:7: For there is hope for a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and its shoot will not fail. For the latter opinion, Rabbi Moses Maimonides and Rabbi Moses Nachmanides chiefly contend, as not only Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel testifies at Numbers 15:30. From these you see that these two wise men, Maimonides and Nachmanides, agree on an animal excision, which consists in the privation of the soul and its corruption or total destruction; and on that excision which is said of the idolater and the blasphemer, which is of body and soul. Indeed, from Rabbi Moses Maimonides himself it is clear, since in his Treatise on Repentance, chapter 8, he says thus: Whoever does not deserve to live this life dies, and never revives, but is cut off in his impiety, and perishes like a beast. And this is that excision of which it is written in the Law, where it is said: That soul shall be utterly cut off. From this it can be learned that the soul is to be cut off by a double excision, of which one pertains to the present age, the other to the age to come. For it is just as if he said that the soul, separated from the body in this age, is no longer considered worthy to live in the age to come, but is now also cut off from the age to come. And in the book Madda he speaks thus: The punishment of the wicked is that their memory will not be preserved for life, but that they die and are cut off; and whoever is not worthy of life is dead, who does not live forever, but is cut off in his impiety, and perishes like a beast. And this is the excision mentioned in the Law, when it is said: That soul shall be utterly cut off. Indeed, it is also clear from Rabbi Moses Nachmanides himself, when in the Torath Haadam, in that part which he calls שער הגמול, the Gate of Retribution, he writes in the following manner: Those who are liable to punishment are judged in Gehenna for twelve months, each according as is fitting for him; after twelve months, however, his soul is burned and becomes like ashes, that is, its form perishes, so that it is like a thing burnt up.
